<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Accruals | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Accruals/360005073918-Accrual-settings.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005073918-Accrual-settings -->

# Accrual settings

Accruals can be edited in **Worktime > Administration > Working Community / Setting Group settings** **> Work hours > Accruals. **Click on the accrual which settings you want to edit. The service's standard accruals have the settings that have been assigned to them (work time shortening leave and levelling period hours are accrued according to the earnings table, others do not have this table), all possible settings are available for new custom accruals, meaning they can be configured exactly as desired. 
## Accrual Settings
Every accrual has the following basic settings:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27996309197981)
**Name** The name given to the accrual and possible variations in different languages.
**Accrual unit type** can be either days or hours. Default setting is hours. NOTE: This setting is not visible for accruals that have an earning table, because the unit is defined with settings "Earn based on" and "Earned as".
**Visible in week tables** setting defines whether the accrual and it's value are shown in each users' calendar and table views. The accrual is shown on it's own row at the bottom of the day's activities. The value is shown in green if it's positive and in red if it's negative.
**Calculate future accrual predictions** setting defines, if the system should predict what the accrual value will be in the future. Defaults to 'Yes'. Events that directly affect accrual will be shown in the future, i.e., for example, accrual leave, or work exceeding the work obligation that has been directed to accrual. A mere obligation that fell short of a working day does not show negative hours in the future.
**Code** is the unique code given to the accrual, can be used in integrations to identify the accrual.
### Borrowing rules
The settings in this section can be used to determine in which situations unfilled work obligation is automatically borrowed from the accrual.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27996369184797)
**Accrual automatically borrows from balance if there's not enough work on the day** \- Whether or not time will be automatically borrowed from the accrual if the daily obligation isn't met.
**Do not borrow from balance if obligation has been manually set** \- Whether or not time will be borrowed from the accrual if the daily obligation has been manually set. The obligation can be manually set in the calendar view by setting 'Length of work day' to a different value.
**Borrow at the end of the week if weekly obligation not fulfilled** \- Whether or not time will be borrowed from the accrual at the end of the week, if the weekly obligation isn't met.
### Earning rules
The settings in this section determine in which situations and under what conditions value is earned to accrual.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27996369186205)
**Year start date** setting can be used to define the restart time for the earning table to be any other date than the default. The default reset is January 1st. Please note: When adding a new value to the setting, the year is shown as 2000 for technical reasons. This doesn't need changing, it is enough to set correct day and month.
**Earning table counts reset every** setting can be set to either year or month. If the earning period is year, the accrual earning is based on the earning table during the year. If the earning period is month, the earning happens during every calendar month as per the earning table. The default setting is a year.
**Earn based on** can be set either hours, days or months, the default being hours. 
If earn based on is set to months, the number of working days or the number of working hours from the calculation of annual leave will be used to see if accrual is earned for the month worked. Read more about the implementation of annual leave earning [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560698>).
If the earning basis is in hours, the earning threshold can be set to the minute.
Note! You cannot use months as the earning basis if the earning period is a month. If this is set, no accrual will be earned at all.
**Earned as** can be set to be earned as days or hours.
**Calculation method for part-time employees** setting lets you specify that earnings will be based on the person's worktime percentage. For example, if employees would earn 8 hours of accrued leave after 17 working days, with a 50% worktime percentage, the employee would earn 4 hours of accrued leave after 17 working days.
**Override earn percentage** In this section, you can specify that earnings will be based on a specific percentage, for example, if the earnings percentage needs to be different from the employee's worktime percentage.
**Do not earn leave unless this many months into contract** setting defines a minimum length of the working contract until leave is earned. This setting requires work contract start date to be filled in person's details.
**Earn from the beginning of employment** lets can specify that the accrual is earned from the beginning of the employment. If the value is "No" or the value is not set, the accrual will only start after the employment has lasted for the number of months specified in the setting Do not earn leave unless this many months into contract.
**Earned only from regular time** setting allows the accrual to be earned only from regular time, so not from over time or any other work time exceeding regular hours.
**Earn from time borrowed from accrual** defines, wheter accrual can be earned also from time that has been borrowed from another accrual, balance for example.
**Earning table** If accrued leave is earned after a certain amount of work has been done, the required working hours and the leave earned from them are filled in the earnings table. The table can be filled in either in working hours or working days.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27996309203229)
### Spending rules
The settings in this section can be used to determine in which situations value is deducted from the accrual and by how much.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27996369188637)
**Days of week that leave/holiday can spend balance** \- Which days of the week can compensate the user if they have recorded leave/holiday for those days. The other settings below can also influence whether the leave is paid. The default is Monday to Sunday.
**Only days with obligation counted as leave/holiday days** \- Whether the day must have a work day length/obligation or not to be considered as a compensated leave/holiday day.
**Leave/holiday ignored if work on day** \- If set to yes, then any work events on the day will prevent the accrual leave/holiday from paying the employee or deducting from their accrual balance. Defaults to no.
**Leave/holiday ignored if public holiday** \- If set to yes, then any work events on the day will prevent the accrual leave/holiday from compensating the employee or deducting from their accrual balance. Defaults to no.
**Leave/holiday paid as** \- How the employee should be compensated/paid for their leave. In reality this affects how the time is displayed in the calendar and exported out of the system to payroll systems. For example "Regular time" will display in the calendar and export as regular pay, but "Annual leave" will not display in the calendar and be exported as annual leave according to the integation rules. Note: Accruals that compensate as "Annual leave" will not currently show in Annual leave/holiday reports as customers should still be using the current Annual holiday system to track annual holiday days.
**Amount leave/holiday should pay (per day) and Amount to deduct from accrual balance (per day) when on leave/holiday** \- How much compensation is paid to the employee for a valid leave/holiday, and how much is deducted from the accrual to cover that pay respectively. Both settings share the same options listed below but are separated as it is sometimes desirable to compensate the user a different amount to what is deducted from their balance e.g. if the compensation is paid in hours and the balance is measured in days.
  * **Amount of obligation used** \- Compensation is paid to the employee that matches how much has been recorded up to their work day length/obligation e.g. On a workday, if you record 1 hour of leave, there will be 1 hour of pay, if you take 10 hours of leave, there will be 7.5 hours of pay (or whatever the work day length is set to). On a non-workday, there will be no pay, regardless of other settings.
  * **Percentage (0-1) of obligation used** \- Only available for the deduction setting. The amount deducted from the accrual is based on the percentage of the obligation you used during the day as a value between 0 and 1. For now it can only deduct 0, 0.5 or 1, and is useful if you have an accrual recorded in days and want to allow employees to record either half or full days. The threshold between whether it deducts a half day or a full day is if 60% of the day length has been used.
  * **Fixed amount per day** \- You can define how much the accrual leave should compensate the user and/or deduct from their accrual balance as a fixed amount on obligated and non-obligated days (see below).
  * **Work day length** \- Compensates the user and/or deducts from the accrual balance the amount that is defined as their work day length for the day.
  * **Fifth of work day length** \- Compensates the user and/or deducts from the accrual balance a fifth of their weekly obligation. This is useful for deducting on days where they are not expected to work but is otherwise defined as a day of the week that should pay accrual leave.
  * **Max work day length** \- Compensates the user and/or deducts from the accrual balance the amount that is defined as their work day length for the day.


**Amount on leave days with/without a work day length** \- These should be set when using "Fixed amount per day" to specify how much is compensated and/or deducted from the accrual on days where the user is expected to work and not expected to work respectively.
### Limits and adjustments
These settings allow you to define the minimum and maximum balance at the beginning or the end of the day and what should happen if you exceed it. It is recommended to use the default behavior that the limit _can_ be exceeded and only a warning is generated for the person and their supervisor.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27997463203741)
**Maximum negative/positive balance at the end/beginning of the day** settings define, what is the maximum/minimum value the accrual can reach at the end or beginning of the day.
**Behaviour of negative / maximum positive limit** defines what happens when that limit is reached. More on how to manage maximum and minimum limits [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360010514358>).
**Maximum balance that can be earned per day** sets a limit for daily accrual increase.
## Example - Balance
The most important settings for the balance accrual are the maximum daily accrual of the balance and the minimum and maximum amounts. It is generally not advisable to set a minimum amount because then it is not easily seen if the negative balance starts to accumulate larger than the set value.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27997474045469)
With the setting **Borrowed from default accrual contributes towards weekly obligation** , it is possible to determine that any balance deductions are to be made only on the last day of the workweek. If this setting is in use and it is desired to avoid reducing the balance when using certain event types, it can be defined in the section **Work hours > TES > ****Event types that contribute to work week** Event Types that are counted in the workweek.
  * **Yes** : The event type affects the formation of weekly overtime, and hours are not filled from the balance on the last day of the workweek.
  * **No** : The event type does not affect the formation of weekly overtime, and hours are filled from the balance on the last day of the workweek.
  * **Yes, but not to the formation of overtime:** The event type does not affect the formation of weekly overtime, but hours are not filled from the balance on the last day of the workweek.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20289288487965)
## Example - Use of holiday pay leave on Saturdays
If you want the holiday pay leave to be consumed as annual leave from Monday to Saturday, and you want the holiday pay leave days recorded for Saturdays to be included in the salary data along with other holiday pay leaves, there are four different options available in the service for this purpose.
**Option 1** \- Saturday does not rise to the salary data if the day’s work obligation (the length of the workday) is 0 hours. An exception can be set for Saturday in the [Length of Workday](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>) setting and an exception for the entire workweek in the [Length of Workweek ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558537>)setting, so that if the event ‘Holiday Pay Leave’ is recorded for the day, the length of the workday and the length of the workweek are automatically set to value X. This results in regular working hours being formed in the calendar for the holiday pay leave days, and the amount of work done during the week increases. Holiday pay leave creates interpreted working time for the salary data, but without increasing the length of the workweek, this does not happen if the length of the workweek has already been completed earlier in the week. For this reason, an exception is needed for both the length of Saturday’s workday and the entire workweek.
**Option 2** \- Set in the holiday pay leave accrual settings, to the**Amount to deduct from accrual balance (per day) when on leave/holiday** section, a fixed hour amount for **Amount on leave days with a work day length** and******Amount on leave days with zero work day length**. The setting determines how much the employee is compensated on a free/holiday day and how much the compensation is for days that have a set length of the workday and for days without the length of the workday. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20289288496541)
**Option 3** \- Forming a salary rule for holiday pay leave based on the marked working time (MarkedTime). The salary rule can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360008045337>), under the section ‘Holiday pay leave selected from Saturdays with no work obligation’. The rule takes into account that Sunday is not included in the data, even if holiday pay leave has been recorded for Sunday.
**Option 4** \- If you want the holiday pay leave to behave like annual leave, then the fourth option is to create a new, customized holiday pay leave event type in the service, which behaves like annual leave and the corresponding accrual for this event type. See below for instructions on creating a new accrual. Instructions for creating a new event type can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519157>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Accruals | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Accruals/360002481817-Accrual-value-transfer-to-another-accrual.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002481817-Accrual-value-transfer-to-another-accrual -->

# Accrual value transfer to another accrual

Sometimes you may encounter a situation where you want to transfer value from one accrual to another. Typically, for example, when the balance accrual reaches the maximum limit, some of the hours are transferred to bank accrual. There is a setting in the accrual settings that allows the value to be automatically transferred to another accrual when the limit is reached. However, if you want to make the transfer manually, below are instructions for doing so. Let's use a situation where you want to transfer 30 hours from balance to bank as an example.
## Example of moving hours from balance to bank
First, the hours to be transferred are subtracted from the balance. The subtraction is done as follows:
1\. Go to the desired person's calendar view and make the changes for the day you want to make the transfer.
2\. Create a new event "Balance change". Mark the amount to be transferred as a negative value. So in this situation, when you are transferring 30 working hours to the bank, the balance change is made with the value -30.
3\. You can add a comment to the event if you want to give a reason for the transfer.
4\. Save the event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27944423805981)
After this you see that on the day, the value you set to be subtracted has been deducted from balance. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27944438005149)
Next:
1\. Go to the person's calendar view and select the day you want to make the change for.
2\. Create new event "bank change". Enter the value of the change as positive. For example, if you are transferring 30 hours from balance to bank, give 30 as the value for bank change.
3\. You may also leave a comment for the event, to explain why hours have been deducted.
4\. Save.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27944423812509)
After this you see that on the day, the value you set to the change has been added to bank.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27944423813405)
The same steps can be taken to transfer hours to/from any accrual in use.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / New terminal setup | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/New-terminal-setup/360004790097-Activating-a-terminal.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004790097-Activating-a-terminal -->

# Activating a terminal

An administrator can activate a terminal into Nepton service with this guidance.
## New terminal behaviour after powering up
New terminals will automatically install after powering up. This should not take more than a couple of minutes. After the initial installation the terminals will wait for activation. Eventually there will be a notice similar to the following:
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8598215690397)
(Terminal may display its messages in Finnish or other language selected, see the exact Finnish messages in the [Finnish version of this guide](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004790097>).)
At the lower edge of the screen the "Online" notice and the green background indicate that there is a connection to the service.
The terminal ID is shown in the notice displayed. It can also be found near the lower right corner of the screen. The ID is the numeric code after the # sign. Write down the ID for activating the terminal.
If there is no connection to the service the terminal may display an error message about the connection problem. Also, if the terminal ID displayed is #0 or a negative number with minus (-) prefix, this will indicate that the terminal has not been connected to the Nepton service.
Check that the device cables are correctly connected and, if necessary, restart the device. If the connection problems continue, check with the IT representative of your organization that there is access from your network to the following addresses:
  * <https://go.nepton.com/>
  * <https://time.nepton.com/>


## Activating terminal in Nepton service
You can activate a terminal in the Employees section of Nepton service.
Select **Employees > Administration > Terminals.**
Click Add new terminal. Add the terminal ID in the field reserved for it. Select **Save**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33604393257117)
If the activation was successful, there will be a notice: "Terminal added". If the device has already been activated, there will be a notice: "Terminal X is already reserved. Please check the id and try again."
![mceclip22.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8599803311645)
Double-check the terminal id directly from the terminal screen. If the id is correct and the terminal does not display information of an activated terminal (see below), follow the instructions above at "if there is no connection to the service".
## Activated terminal appearance
When a terminal has been activated successfully, it will display a login screen after a connection check done when starting up. The appearence of the terminal depends on if the PIN code login is in use.
### PIN code login not in use
When the setting **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Current status > Log in possible with the recording terminal **value is "PIN-code login not in use" (default)
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33604365328925)
or "Only RFID-login in use"
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33604348653981)
an activated terminal will display: "Place your ID on the reader and wait for the signal".
![mceclip19.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8599734003997)
### PIN code login in use
When the setting **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Current status > Log in possible with the recording terminal **value is "PIN-code login in use"
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33604348654621)
an activated terminal will display: "Login with PIN Code or RFID Tag".
![mceclip20.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8599734856093)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Setting groups | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Setting-groups/360002557537-Add-or-copy-a-setting-group.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002557537-Add-or-copy-a-setting-group -->

# Add or copy a setting group

New setting groups can be added or copied from **Worktime > Administration > Setting groups > Add setting group**. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35364810356893)
There are many ways to add a new setting group.
## Add manually
**Name** : Setting group can be given any name. The name is recommended to be descriptive of the setting groups settings regarding work time calculations, e.g. "Levelling period 40hrs".  
  
**Parent group** : If parent group is set, the setting group will be added as a child to the parent setting group. The new child setting group can have distinct settings that override the settings in the parent group. The selection must be empty if the group to be added is a parent group itself.  
  
**Code** : Setting group code can contain numbers and letters and is mandatory. Code is used in person imports in case the import handles setting group information.  
  
**Description:** A brief description on what kind of settings the setting group consists of.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35364810358301)  
  
Adding the new setting group is finalized by clicking **Save** -button.
## Create from template
Setting groups can also be created based on existing groups or ready-made templates. We recommend that existing customers, however, create empty setting groups so that they always have all the desired settings. When using templates, it can be more difficult to get the desired interpretation of working hours when you cannot directly see what settings have been set.
### Basic templates
The service has ready-made templates for each environment, which have some TESs-compliant settings predefined. We recommend using templates only with the project manager during the service implementation phase!
When creating a new setting group from a template, you can choose whether to copy the subgroups of the selected template at the same time. This is done by selecting Copy subgroups. If this option is active, all groups that are subgroups of the settings group selected in Create from template will be copied as a subgroup when creating the setting group.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35364810359581)
### Copy an existing setting group
It is also possible to copy an existing setting group from your environment. All setting groups created in the environment are displayed in the "create from template" menu under the subheading "Existing setting groups".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35364810361117)
Unless the new settings group has a completely different parent group than the group being copied, it is recommended to create a new settings group from scratch and set it as a subgroup of the desired settings group instead of copying it.
### Copy from another customer environment
This option is only available if you have access to another client environment.
Use this option if you want to copy an existing setting group from another customer environment. You must know the system ID of that setting group to be able to copy it.
The system ID of a setting group is displayed in the setting group details. For more information, see [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558758>).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35364836061213)  
If "Create from system identifier" is selected, "Create from system identifier" - field appears below the "Create from template" field. The system identifier of the other customer's setting group is inserted into the "Create from system identifier" input field. Note that if a setting group is copied from another customer environment, the system will not copy settings that are related to custom event and absence types, or settings that are related to integration rulesets.  
  
![20210107-support-add-setting-group-en-3.PNG](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015672537)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management / Person details management | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/Person-details-management/360002425517-Add-or-manage-a-persons-RFID-tag.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002425517-Add-or-manage-a-persons-RFID-tag -->

# Add or manage a persons RFID tag

If RFID tags are used to record work hours in your working community, RFID tag identifier needs to be saved in each employee's information.
## Adding RFID tag identifier manually
RFID tag identifier can be saved in employee's information in **Employees** section through **Persons > Person's information > Identifiers**.  
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4412579295761)  
One user can have multiple RFID identifiers. To save more than one, separate the identifiers with pipe symbol (|). Once you have added the information, remember to save the changes from the Save-button at the bottom of the page. Please note, that the field is managed with [validity tools](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004856937>).
The same RFID tag identifier can only be saved for one person, so when an employee's contract ends, the RFID tag identifier needs to be removed from their information before [deactivating the user](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002424617>).
In some of the RFID tags the code that has been printed on the tag is actually not the identifier code. The right code can be seen when the tag is shown to the reader that's connected to a terminal. If the code is not set for another user, the terminal will inform that the code was not found, and will show the code on the screen. You can save this code into the user's details.
## Adding RFID tag identifier with reader
RFID tag identifier can also be added to the person's details by connecting a reader to the computer via USB port. By showing the person's RFID tag to the reader, the right code will be read straight from it to the person's information.
  1. Connect the reader to a computer via USB.


![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360009426478)
  2. Log in to Nepton.
  3. Open the right person's information.
  4. Click your mouse on the RFID tag identifier -field.


![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360008281197)
  5. Show the tag (picture below) to the reader.


![keyfob.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4402933069713)
  6. The code will appear on the field.


![mceclip4.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360008281237)
  7. Save the changes from the Save-button at the bottom of the page.


The tag identifier has now been added to the user's information.

# Add person

Please note that a returning person, whose username has already been deleted, can be restored and does not need adding again. A new user account for the service should not be created for a person who returns to employment. Instructions for restoring a person can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002424957>).
1\. Go to **Employees > Persons**
2\. Select **Add person**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29056296647325)
3\. Fill the person's basic details and click **Save**. More details about person's info fields can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004769718>).
4\. You are now presented with the options to: Add (another) person, return to the 'Persons' page, or view the newly created person's information.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29056281454877)

# Add person to a setting group

An employee must be added to a setting group to activate the calculation settings for working hours. The employee can be added to a setting group either in the **Employees section** under the person’s details or in the **Worktime section** under the setting group’s details.
Also, see the [instructions for updating or setting a setting group for multiple people at once](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019776498-Update-or-set-a-worktime-setting-group-for-multiple-people-at-once>).

Select **Employees > Persons > Persons**. Choose the desired person from the list and open their details using the magnifying glass icon.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/21393751571357)
Select **Employment information - Worktime Setting Group**. Click the **Value** field and choose **Add**. A search field will now be visible, where you can search for the desired setting group.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23505780637853)
After adding the desired setting group and clicking **Done, Save** the changes.
## Adding a person to the settings group in the Wortime section
Alternatively, the setting group can be set in the Worktime section. We recommend setting the person's setting group in the Employees section, as described in the instructions above.
Select **Worktime > Administration > Settings Group****s**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23505780641181)
Choose**Action > Setting group members**. (The selected setting group does not matter here.)![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23505780643613)
Person is shown in a **Person non-grouped users** section. First start by clicking calendar:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23505780646301)
Through the opening pop-up window, you can define the person's setting group. Add a setting group for the person by clicking the **Add** button.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23505766296477)
Select the desired settings group in the **Value** field
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23505780651933)
If necessary, you can set the desired dates in the **Valid from** and**Valid to** fields. By default, the current day is filled in as the Valid from date. (Validity starts at 00:00 and ends at 23:59.)
In a normal situation for a new person, both dates are left blank by clicking the date and selecting**Clear Date.**
If the employee changes the setting group, the **Valid from** date is set to the day from which the setting should start. In this case, the**Valid to** date must be set for the previous setting group.
Save your changes by clicking the **Save** button.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23505766304797)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Project management | path: en-gb/Support/Project-management/360002560877-Add-project.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560877-Add-project -->

# Add project

Projects can be for example project work with start and end times, or cost centers set up for targeting the work.
A new project can be created in **Worktime - > Projects -> Project Administration**. From the Action menu, select **Add Project**.
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4414927519505/mceclip2.png)
**Parent Project** defines where the project is shown in project tree.
**Name** defines the name of the project.
**Code** defines the project code, which doesn't have to be unique.
If [work shift planning](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360011258978>) is used as well, projects should not have duplicate codes with [units](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590317>).
**External Identifier** defines a unique project identifier, which is from or can be read to another system.
**Project type** defines [the project type](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002562338>).
**Project starts** and **Project ends** define the time period work hours can be recorded on the project.  
Fields can also be left blank. Work hours cannot be targeted for the project after it’s end date. When the project has ended, it is possible to record hours retrospectively for the time period the project was active.
If a project is set as the person's [default project](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002563098>), they will be able to record hours for the project even after it has ended.
**Description** field can be used to write down more details of the project. The field can also be left empty.
**Visible on the recording terminal** can be set if you want the project to be selectable in the recording terminal, in the current status view, or in mobile. By default, the project is only displayed in the mobile view and when creating a work event in the browser (events in calendar or events in table).
For a child project to be visible in the recording terminal, all of it's parent projects need to be visible in the recording terminal as well.
**Project Managers** can be assigned to every project. Project managers can view and approve hours recorded on the project. The left field shows the people that can be be selected, and the right field shows the people who have already been selected to be project managers. There can be several project managers. Read more about managing project managers [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360018588898>).
After saving the project, the new project will appear in the Project List under the Projects menu, where it is also possible to view the project tree in more detail.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management / Online work contracts | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/Online-work-contracts/360002590277-Adding-and-reviewing-work-contracts.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590277-Adding-and-reviewing-work-contracts -->

# Adding and reviewing work contracts

In the service, it is possible to manage the entire signature process related to work contracts. Information about the contract and its status is automatically conveyed to the employee, supervisor and administration. The contract may consist of several attached files, which the employee must approve at the time of signing. Once all parties have signed the contract and it has been approved by the administration, the completed information is automatically transferred to the employee’s personal information.
The feature’s implementation is done together with the service provider.
## Adding work contract for the employee
To add a work contract for an employee, the person must first be created in Nepton with the information that is available. The remaining information can be collected from the work contract. Before adding the work contract to the person, it is also necessary to define the [work contract template](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590217-Creating-and-managing-work-contract-templates>), which must be attached to the [work contract package.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590237-Work-contract-packages>)
Adding an work contract for a person is done as follows:
1\. Go to the**Employees** section and select the desired person from the list of people. Open the person’s details by pressing the magnifying glass icon.
2\. Move from the **Person's informatiom** view to the **Documents** view via the top menu.
3\. Adding a work contract for a person is done through the '**Create new work contract'** button. The button is visible when the file folder type is defined as ‘Work contracts’ and the user has rights to the folder. The contract package created earlier is selected as the contract. Read more about file folders [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/11443677456029-Implementation-of-online-work-contracts>).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20521581930269)
Through the ‘**Create new work contract** ’ button, the '**Creation of work contract** "’ view opens, where a work contract is selected for the employee. The view also provides the employee’s name and email address.
The desired work contract package is selected for the employee from the ‘**Adaptable work contract package** ’ dropdown menu. After selecting the work contract package, all the work contracts and contract attachments associated with the package will be listed under ‘**Template of work contract package** ’.
Finally, select ‘**Add work contract** ’. After this, the contract has now been added to the person.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20521598456861)
## Filling out and signing the work contract
The created work contract appears with a red background in the ‘Documents' tab of the person’s details. The employer is the first to fill out the contract, and the employee cannot see the template until the employer has filled it out.
1\. Select ‘**Fill’**. The template opens in a new tab in the web browser. Fill out the template.
2\. **Accept and save** from the bottom of the page.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20521991047581)
Once the employer has filled out the base, the contract moves to the employee for review, completion and approval. The contract appears gray to the employer until the employee has approved it.
When the employee logs into Nepton, they are immediately shown the work contracts and any attachments that need approval. At this stage, the employee can also fill in the fields for which they have been given the right to fill, such as contact details. The filled-in information is automatically updated in the person’s details in addition to the work contract.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20521991053853)
Finally, the contract is forwarded to the administration for approval. At this stage, the administration can no longer modify the contract. The work contract appears green in the view.
Administrators, human resources and payroll are able to approve contracts that are awaiting administrative approval.
Once all parties have approved the contract, the background color of the contract’s attachments turns white. The contract is now complete.
## Browsing employment contracts
All contracts assigned to individuals can be viewed in a single view by selecting the ‘**Contract List** ’ from the ‘**Employees** ’ section’s **Contracts** menu. Supervisors, administrators and management can browse work contracts. The view lists all contracts.
Work contracts can be searched by name or contract date or filtered by contract status. The list can also be sorted by column names. The contract can be examined through the ‘**Review** ’ icon in the **Information** column.
Contracts can also be viewed through individual persons’ documents, where the employee can also see their contract.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20523894997149)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Project management | path: en-gb/Support/Project-management/360002563098-Adding-default-project-to-a-person.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002563098-Adding-default-project-to-a-person -->

# Adding default project to a person

A default project can be added to a person in the Employees section. The default project is automatically attached to an event when creating a new event. The project can be changed to another one before saving the event.
If default project has been set it is automatically added to all new events. Automation can not be defined based on event type or absence type.
Default project can only be one of the projects person has [visibility ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360006776758>)to either through person or person group settings, if not all projects are visible to everyone.
## Adding or changing default project to a single person
1\. Go to **Employees > Persons**. Choose the correct person by searching with their name. Open that person's details from the magnifying glass. ![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/36220871121053)
The default project is set in the **Person’s information** tab in the **organization** section. Start entering the project name in the field “Default project” and select the correct project from the search results. Click **save** at the bottom of the page to save the information.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/36220871121949)
The default project field does not have a validity function. A person can only have one default project at a time, and it is always valid for the past and future. Changing the default project to another does not change the entries already made, only new events created after the change are offered the new default project.
## Adding or changing default project to multiple persons at once
The default project can be edited for multiple people at once.
  1. Go to**Employees > Persons > Persons.**
  2. Select **Export to importable Excel**. Open the file. In Excel, you'll see a **Default Project** column.
  3. Leave only the people whose default project you want to change to the list (completely remove all other people (rows) from the file).
  4. Only leave the columns ‘Employee Number', 'First Name', 'Last Name' and 'Default Project' in the list.
  5. In the 'Default Project' column, write the code for the project you want to assign to the persons.
  6. Save the file (name does not matter).
  7. Choose **Employee > Persons > Import Persons**. Upload the file you saved.
  8. The information has now been updated.


With this method, other person information can also be edited at the same time. More information about person import can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003762577>).
The update is valid for all columns from the moment the file is run.
An example file for updating default projects:
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4414989045137)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-recording/360002596797-Adding-events-in-calendar-view.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002596797-Adding-events-in-calendar-view -->

# Adding events in calendar view

Adding an event can be done in multiple ways. This article will walk you through adding an event in the calendar view.
You can either enter all the event details at once, or start the event with just the start time and later complete and end it.
## Starting an event
1\. Click on the date of the day you want to make an entry for. A new window will open next to the day, where you can see the day's information and add new events. Click **Add event**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30001021673117)
  
2\. The **Add Event** button will open a new pop-up window:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30001021675933)
3\. The [default event type](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558717>) is Work, unless otherwise specified. The event type to be recorded is selected from the drop-down menu using the arrow. The event types are divided into three categories; Work, Absence and administrative events. Administrative events are only visible to the administrator or another person who has been granted sufficient access rights.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34216683314205)
4\. By default, the event times are 08:00-16:00, unless[ otherwise specified](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360008777997>). The event can be started with just the start time, leaving the end time blank, in which case the event will roll as active until it is stopped, or it can be given an end time as well. By clicking on the green arrow next to the start time, the current time will be the start time of the event. If there is an event for the day already, Nepton suggest the end time of the previous event to the new event.
5\. It is also possible to write a comment for the event in the Note field. Additionally, depending on the settings, project allocation, overtime target, and possible supplements and attachments can be added to the event.
6\. Save the entry from the **Save** -button, after which it is visible in the calendar.
## Using Quick Events
If quick start buttons have been defined in the service, a specific event type can be started directly from such a button. Quick starts appear in the calendar and table view when you click on the date of the desired day and a window opens next to it:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30001021679133)
Quick starts can have predefined content, so the event can already have everything you need (such as project allocation, overtime target) ready. Therefore, event registration is faster when you just start the event. The quick start event starts in real time if you press the 'Start' button highlighted with an arrow, or the event editing window can be opened from the + sign in front of it if you want to make changes to the predefined content, or if you want to start the event in a time other than real time.
## Targeting work to project
The service allows you to enable work allocation to projects. Project is the service's generic name for an object, but projects can be used to target work for customers, orders, cost centers, and so on. The interpreted work time is targeted for the project on the event, and it is available in reporting and integrations.
An event can be targeted to one or more projects. The project targeting can specify the amount of work done either as a percentage or in hours. If no information is set, all worked time interpreted from the event is targeted to the project in question. It is also possible to record two or more projects, each with 100% project targeting. Please note that events can only be targeted to the lowest-level projects.
Internal and public notes can be written to projects. Notes set for projects are displayed in the user interface and in the Hours by Person report in project reporting. The Note field of the event is also displayed in the report in question.
Notes can be used, for example, to describe the content of the work or to record the billing basis for the work. The note fields of project lines are visible to everyone and their visibility cannot be specified. Notes can be fetched using rule sets in integrations.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34216683318557)
When targeting work to project, the projects that have been used most frequently in the last two months are displayed as a shortcut. This two-month time window is based on the day for which the event and the project targeting to it are performed. For example:
A Work event is created and the project targeting is Project A for the current day.
The most frequently used projects are displayed in a two-month time window, counting backwards from the current day.
The most frequently used projects are arranged so that the most frequently used ones appear first in the list. If there are more than 20 most frequently used projects, only the 20 most frequently used projects are displayed as a shortcut. All projects can be browsed or searched regardless of whether a project is displayed as a shortcut or not.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34216677155869)
## Overtime target
Depending on the rights and settings, it may be possible to choose overtime target for an event. The overtime target is selected under "Overtime". Clicking this opens a menu from which you can select the desired target for the event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34216683319709)
## Adding a supplement
[Supplements ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559637>)can also be added to an event. Supplements are allowances that are manually added to an event. The supplements drop-down menu opens a search for all available supplements. The supplement shows the unit for entering the value (euros, pieces, decimal, integer), a comment field, and a date field, based on supplement settings.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34265729301405)
## Adding an attachment
Attachments can also be added to the event. This function is used especially with the travel invoice event. We do not recommend saving medical certificates to Nepton. The attachment can be uploaded from the device to Nepton under the "Attachments" heading.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34265729306525)
Once an attachment has been added to an event, it is shown in calendar view with paperclip icon:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34265729309085)
**Attachment restrictions**
File size:
Maximum attachment size: 2 MB  
Maximum number of attachments per event: 20  
Maximum total attachment size per event: 8 MB
**File format**
Supported file formats are:
  * Excel
  * Html
  * Image
  * Pdf
  * Power Point
  * Text
  * Word
  * Zip


## Finishing an event
1\. In the calendar view or table view, click on an unfinished event and select Stop from the pop-up window or alternatively Edit, which allows you to select the end time in the window that opens.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30000994856605)
Different worktime roles can be defined with different [rights](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554338-Worktime-roles>) in Nepton. All functions in this article might not be in use in your environment in Nepton. Please contact your company Nepton administrator if you are not sure your company's practices.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-recording/360002603258-Adding-events-in-current-status-view.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002603258-Adding-events-in-current-status-view -->

# Adding events in current status view

The Current status view can be accessed in **Worktime** > **Work hours** > **Current status.**
## Starting an event
Event entry view in the Current Status view:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34272689476509)
To start recording, activate the desired event type. Press the Start button, and the event will start at the current time and will be active without an end time until it is stopped.
If you want to start another event, simply activate the desired event type and press the Start button. You don't need to stop the previous event, it will end automatically when a new one is started.
There must be at least 1 minute between events recorded in real time so that they are considered separate events.
## Adding project targeting
You can also target events for projects in the Current status view. Select the desired event type, for example Work. The event type is activated. Select Projects. Select the desired project from the menu, then start the event using the Start button. If a default project has been set for the person, it will always be offered as the default for events. You can change the project for each event in the Projects menu.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34272680588061)
When an event is started, the service will notify you of its successful start, including project targets:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34272680590621)
## Changing an event's overtime target
The overtime target for an event can be changed when the event is ended. When the event is active, the Overtime heading appears in the right-hand menu. Clicking this will open the overtime target options for that event. You can select the desired one from these, and then end the event with the Stop button.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34272680593437)
## Adding supplement to an event
Supplements can be added to an event when the event is ended. When the event is active, the Supplements heading appears in the right-hand menu. Supplements can only be added to an event in the current state if its unit is time (duration in days or minutes) or an integer. If a default value has been given for the supplement, this value is pre-selected for the supplement that is automatically added to the event. Set the desired value using the - and + signs, and use the X button to reset the field.
##  ![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34272689492125)  
Ending an event
To end an active event, open the current status view and press the End button. If you want to change the event type during the day, simply activate the desired event type and press the Start button, which will automatically end the previous running event. This means you don't need to end the event in between.
## Starting an event with an earlier start time / ending with a later end time
[In the settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560518>), the possibility to start the event with an earlier start time, and correspondingly end the event with a later end time can be activated. If this function is enabled, the Earlier Start Time option will appear in the right side panel before the event has been started. This allows you to set the start time to a time earlier than the current time. When the event is started, the event will start at this specified time instead of the current time.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34272680597021)
Similarly, when an event is running and is stopped, the option "Later end time" appears in the right-hand menu. Here, you can specify a desired end time for the event in advance, which is later than the current time. When the event is stopped, the end time is not registered as the current time, but as the end time specified in the setting.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34272680598557)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Mobile | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Mobile/360002602638-Adding-events-in-Nepton-mobile.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002602638-Adding-events-in-Nepton-mobile -->

# Adding events in Nepton mobile

Nepton mobile is accessed at https://go.nepton.com/. The same address is also used in the desktop version. The address can be saved, for example, to the bookmarks of your phone's web browser or as a shortcut, making it easy to use.
There are two ways to start an event on the mobile website. The **quick start** allows you to start basic events with a single button, and if you want to edit the event type, time or project, for example, this can be done via a separate **Add Event** button (orange +).
## Quick Start
When you open the Mobile page, the service offers [Quick Starts](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7074461491101>) by default. With Quick Start, you can start defined events with pre-filled informations. By default, work and lunch are offered as quick starts. To start the event, press the **Start** button.
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360018305017)
When an event is logged using quick start, the event start time will be the time the Start button is pressed. If the user has a default project, the event will automatically be logged to it.
If you want to start another event after starting an event, all you have to do is press the Start button in the Quick Start view. This will automatically end your previous event, meaning you don't have to stop the current event separately. At the end of the day, it is possible to end an active work event (or any other event) in the quick start view with the Stop button.
An event made in the past can also be continued quickly by clicking the Continue button next to it:![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19004301587741)
In this case, an event exactly the same as the one that was continued will be logged for the current day starting from that time. This can speed up logging events, for example, when the event is targeted to a project. When using the Continue function, all information from the event is also logged to the new event, including projects and supplements.
## Starting an Event by "Add Event"
The **Add event** button makes it possible to select different types of events, edit the time of the entry, change the project and, for example, add supplements to the event.
**Please note!** If you have only the permission to report own real time events (no permission to edit events), you can only start events with the quick start buttons. User permissions might also limit setting overtime options and adding supplements.
To add an event for the current day, select the orange 'plus' sign at the bottom of the page.
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360018305037)
The Add Event window will then open.
Select the event type, start and end times and, if necessary, projects, overtime target and / or supplements. It is also possible to write a comment in the Notes field. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35274399460509)
When pressing the green arrow, the start time will become current time and end time will be removed.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35274386689821)
When the correct information is entered, click **Save**.
Now that the work event has started, it will appear on the front page (the Quick Start page). In this view, it is possible to end the event with the Stop button.
![mceclip5.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360018305157)
## Starting an event from a work shift
If there is a work shift on the day, it is possible to start an event based on the work shift.
Starting a real-time event from the work shift can be done from pressing the Start button next to the shift.
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4927126142237)
Or by clicking the shift, an event edit window opens up. By default the start and end times are based on the planned shift. By saving the event, a work event based on the shift has been added.
![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4927169442717)

# Adding persons to a unit

A person is added to a unit in the Employment section under Units.
The desired unit's information is opened by selecting the magnifying glass icon next to the unit's name.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28216523336733)
The unit's information is divided into three tabs; Unit information, unit persons and additional functions.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28216529272477)
A list of persons in the unit is shown in "unit persons". 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28216529274781)
To add a person, enter the name of the person to be added in the **Search for person by keyword** field and select **Search**.
The person to be added appears as a search result and is added to the unit by selecting **Add**. The person can now be seen in the **Unit persons** listing.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management / Person details management | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/Person-details-management/360002430618-Adding-supervisor.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430618-Adding-supervisor -->

# Adding supervisor

Adding or replacing a supervisor for a user requires certain types of [roles](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002425637>) from the administrator. You can only choose a supervisor to be someone who has their employee number set.
Please note that supervisor sees his own subordinates. If you want to allow a supervisor to see other supervisors subordinates, the supervisor needs to be set to substitute this supervisor. Instructions can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430678>).
The easiest way to add a supervisor to a subordinate or edit supervisor information is through the person's information card in the **Employees** section. A person may have several supervisors, one of whom has been selected as the primary supervisor.
A supervisor can be assigned to an employee as follows:
Open the Employees section and choose Persons > **Persons**.  
Open the desired person's information from the magnifying glass.  
From the menu, select **Organization > Supervisors > Add**. Start typing the name of the supervisor and select the desired person as the supervisor from the results.
You can add more than one supervisor to a person. If more than one supervisor is added to the person, the service will indicate who is the primary supervisor. However, it is important to note that only the supervisor designated as the primary supervisor receives messages about the sensitive actions of his subordinates, such as sick leave, vacation leave and annual leave.
Once you have selected the supervisors, select **Done**.  
Always remember to save the changes from the **Save** button at the bottom of the page.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29075242646813)
Supervisor information can also be updated for multiple employees at the same time. Instructions for mass import of supervisors can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430658>).
Only the primary supervisor (and/or the primary supervisor's substitute) receives an email notification requesting approval for a subordinate's event request."

# Adding units

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event types and absence types | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-types-and-absence-types/360002519157-Adding-enabling-and-editing-event-types.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519157-Adding-enabling-and-editing-event-types -->

# Adding, enabling and editing event types

By default there are multiple different [Event types](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002520778-Event-types>) in Nepton. This article describes how to add, enable, and edit new event types directly in the service. A custom event type can be needed, for example, if the name of the event type needs to be changed. The article also describes how the visibility of the event types is managed.
There is also a separate article for[ Default and Assumed Event Types](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558717>).
## Adding a new event type
The configuration is made in the menu **Work time > Administration > Working community settings > Work hours > Event types**.
Click **Add Event Type**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34194975561117)
Enter a **name** for the new event type. Please make sure that the name is clearly different from the names of the service's default event types. This text will appear in the event list when a new event is added or an event is edited. The name can be up to 64 characters long. You can also provide a translation for the name in another language by clicking "Other languages". In this case, if Nepton is used in English, for example, the user will see the English name entered for the event type instead of the original Finnish name.
Enter a **code** for the event type. The code can be anything, but it must be unique. This makes it easier to handle the event type in, for example, rule sets for integrations and setting exception settings. The code can be up to 64 characters long.
Select the **behavior** for the event type, i.e. how the calculations with the new event type is performed. For example, if you select work as the behavior, the new event type behaves in the same way as the work event type. **NOTE:** If behavior is, for example Work time shortening leave, then Work time shortening leave [accrual](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005073918-Accruals>) needs to be in use. Otherwise visibility selection for this event type can't be set.
At the moment it is not possible in the service to create an event type from Travel invoice so that it would include the supplements and calculations of a Travel invoice.
When all the fields have been entered, click **Add**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/16686866347677)
Error is shown if event type with the same name and behavior already exists.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/16686895768349)
## Event type activation and visibility
When a new event type is added, it will appear in the list. The listing is in alphabetical order. The new event type must be activated at either the Working community settings level or the Setting groups level, depending on how widely the event type is used in the work community (i.e. the new event type can be visible and selectable to all or only to a specific group). Activation of the event type is done by ticking the selection (at the Working community settings level) or by selecting the "Yes" option from the menu (at the Setting groups level). Event types can be taken into use for example only for terminals, but not the calendar view.
When editing events = calendar view  
On terminal = recording terminals, current page and mobile  
From direct link = Not in use anymore
The setting is saved from the Save button at the bottom of the page.
Working community settings options:  

![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34194995292957)
Setting groups options:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34194995293469)
## Event type settings
The settings of the event types are shown in a table format. The event types are listed below and the settings for them are listed in rows. It is therefore possible to make event type-specific settings. Working community level settings are slightly wider than setting group level settings.
The first setting is "**Marked time total** ". If this setting is activated, the calendar view will have its own row, where the total time marked for this type of event is calculated daily and weekly. Below is an example of a situation where the marked time total has been activated for Remote work:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20871445760029)
After this comes the "in use" section, where you can specify on which devices the event type is used. This is explained in more detail in the text of the previous heading (Event type activation and visibility).
The next setting is "**Expose begin and end time on terminal** ". This is often used, for example, for annual leave or balance leave, when these event types should be able to be recorded in advance from the terminal. Options in the setting are Not exposed (default, same as Not set), Optional or Mandatory. The Optional selection enables, but does not force, the recording of start and end times. Selecting Mandatory forces the recording of start and end times.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34194975567133)
Activating "**Requested from supervisor in advance** " turns the event type into an [event request](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360017787717>).
By activating "**Show in planning view** " the event types are shown in the shift planning calendar. For example, if this is activated for the event type "Annual leave", and the person has recorded annual leave for the future in their calendar, the shift planner will see these Annual leave events when planning shifts for these days. All absences are displayed in the planning view with just "Absence". For example, here Vuoro, V. has recorded Annual leave for the period of 19.8.-25.8., and it appears in the planning view like this:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20873019670429)
Note! The event type is displayed in the planning view after the activation is  
done. Any events recorded before activation are not automatically updated  
in the planning view. If the old event is modified after activation, then it  
will be updated in planning.
## Removing event type from use
If an event type is out of date, and you no longer want it to appear in the event menu when adding a new event, it can be disabled either at the Working community level or Setting group level. In the event type row under "In use", set "NO" (or uncheck the box at work community level) to the options from which you want to remove it.
Removal of event type visibility is done by removing it from use. This does not affect history of created events but prevents new events being created with this event type.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34194995298333)
## Editing existing event type
If event type with behavior _Emergency Work_ was created before 18.04.2024, it currently has behavior _No change_. Salary calculations of this event type has not changed. If event type is saved again with behavior Emergency Work, it inherits behavior of standard Emergency Work event type (e.g. minimum compensation of 1 hour, is daily overtime).
At the working community settings level, the pen image in front of the event type indicates that this is a new event type added directly to the service, not a standard event type. At the setting groups level, this is indicated by the * sign. From the pen image, you can also edit event type information and behavior. Event types can only be edited at the Working community settings level.
![mceclip6.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407098482449)
![mceclip5.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407098476305)
Edit event type view contains fields for _original name_ and  _name_. The differences are:
  * Original name: Name which was used when the event type was created. This can't be changed and no new event type can be created with **this name and behavior**. If event type was created with multiple translations, original name is the translation which was set for language which was used in the service when creating the event. 
  * Name: Name of the event type which is shown, for example, in worktime calendar. It is possible to modify translations with Other languages action. If translations are not modified, original name and name can be the same. 


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/16686895772957)
Changes made here also have a retroactive effect - if you want the changes to take effect only from today, you must create an entirely new event type instead of editing it and change the deployment settings for both event types in both the working community settings and each of the setting groups.
