<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event types and absence types | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-types-and-absence-types/360020205977-Adding-enabling-and-editing-absence-types.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360020205977-Adding-enabling-and-editing-absence-types -->

# Adding, enabling, and editing absence types

Nepton has dozens of different standard event types. One of the event types is Absence, under which absence types can be defined. When absence types are set to absence event type, they are shown as list when adding new Absence event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32930535263517)
This article describes how you can add, enable and edit absence types in Nepton.
The entries made will remain in the service, even if the absence type is later deactivated.
### Default absence types
The service comes with a set of absence types that are available to everyone.
![Näyttökuva 2025-11-25 kello 15.42.39.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32057429974301)
### Adding absence types
Adding new absence types is done in Working community settings (**Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Work hours > Absence types**). 
Click **Add absence type**.
![Näyttökuva 2025-11-25 kello 15.43.25.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32057429975965)
Enter **Name** for the absence type. Name is shown in adding and editing window when event type is chosen as Absence. 
The name can be translated into every language used in the organisation. This way, the absence type is displayed according to the user's language preference. By clicking the **Other languages** button, you can add translations for different languages
Select the wanted **Compensation type default**. This defines, if absence type is paid, unpaid, or reduced salary as default. 
Select if absence type **Earns vacation days default**.
Click **Add**
![Näyttökuva 2025-11-25 kello 15.45.03.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32057429977245)
![Näyttökuva 2025-11-25 kello 15.45.20.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32057460992669)
When new absence type is added, it will be shown in listing. It also automatically generates a code. Code can be used to define [exceptions to settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560677-Configure-exceptions-to-settings>) or in [integration rulesets.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002489257-Setting-up-integration-rulesets>)
### Enabling absence types
Absence type can be enabled by selecting '**Yes** ' in the '**In use** ' column. By default, All listed absence types are in use and shown when adding new Absence event. 
![Näyttökuva 2025-11-25 kello 15.48.04.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32057460994973)
### Editing Absence type
Absence type calculator behavior can be edited. Editing is possible but editing values in columns '**Compensation type defaul** t' and '**Earn vacation days default** '. New value is valid once setting is saved. Default setting to each absence type listed can be found [here.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519937-Absence-type-management>)
Name of the new absence type created to Nepton can be edited as well as the translations of the name. Default absence type names cannot be edited. Editing is possible by clicking blue pen icon.
![Näyttökuva 2025-11-25 kello 15.50.02.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32057460996509)
New name is added to the name field. You can also edit other fields in this view.
![Näyttökuva 2025-11-25 kello 15.49.44.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32057460999965)
If person has rights to edit compensation type default or vacation days earning, it can be done when adding or editing the event. Work time role rights can be managed in the Worktime Roles - Worktime roles permissions menu.

---

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002559438-Additional-work-formation.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559438-Additional-work-formation -->

# Additional work, formation

Additional work is formed when working hours exceed regular time but do not exceed maximum work day length. Regular time can be based on local agreements, collective agreements or Working Time Act.
If work week length is exceeded, additional work is earned up to maximum hours of work per week limit. For example, a person working 37,5h per week could earn additional work after regular time up to 40h. Additional work would be 2,5h in a week.
If maximum hours of work per week is not exceeded, additional work is earned up to maximum work day length. For example, a person working 7,5h per day could earn 30 mins of additional work per day.
When daily or weekly maximum hours are exceeded, overtime is formed, except when working on hour to hour basis targeting work time balance. 
## Earning additional work and additional work rise
Addition work can be earned with or without rise percentage. Additional work rise percentage and thresholds after which rise is earned can be found in working community and setting group settings Work hours > TES.
Setting **Only earn after total daily hours** determines after how many daily hours earning of additional work rise starts. By default the value is work day length before the work time percentage is applied. 
Setting **Only earn after total weekly hours** determines after how many weekly hours earning of additional work rise starts. By default the value is work week length before the work time percentage is applied.  
  
Setting **Apply worktime percentage when a public holiday shortens the work week** , you can define whether the additional work rise percentage weekly threshold for a part‑time employee during a public‑holiday week is calculated in the same way as for a full‑time employee, or according to the employee’s work time percentage. By default, this setting is **“Yes”** , meaning that during a public‑holiday week, the additional work rise percentage weekly threshold is calculated according to the work time percentage.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34220981966237)
If person is a part-time worker with 6h work day length, maximum work day length of 8h and settings above are used, then earnings during 9h working day would be as follows (time after work day is marked as overtime):
  * 6h regular time
  * 1,5h 0% additional work
  * 0,5h 50% additional work
  * 1h 50% daily overtime


### Additional work rise and work time percentage
With following settings:
  * Length of work day 7,5h
  * Work time percentage 80%, which results to work day length of 6h


Work day length of 7,5h is used as a daily threshold after which additional work rise is earned.
## Considering weekly regular time before forming additional work
According to some collective agreements such as Kunnallinen yleinen virka- ja työehtosopimus (KVTES) and Avaintyönantajat AVAINTA ry työehtosopimus (Avaintes) additional work is earned weekly between time of work week length and maximum hours of work per week. This setting can be set on working community and setting group level.
Below is an example how to implement additional work settings to setting group which follows Avaintes collective agreement.
\- Work day length 7h 21min  
\- Maximum work day length 8h  
\- Work week length 36h 45min  
\- Maximum hours of work per week 38h 45min  
  
1\. From settings group settings choose TES  
  
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/6433965032349)  
  
2\. **Work week calculation mode** sets how work week and possible additional work and overtime is calculated:  
  
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/6433993863325)  
  
3\. Work week calculation mode: **Calculate regular time for whole week before calculating additional work and overtime**. Weekly hours are taken in consideration when calculating daily additional work. 
Example below illustrates how daily additional work cannot exceed 39 mins and weekly additional work cannot exceed 2 h. With this setting total amount of daily additional work cannot exceed maximum weekly additional work limit.
![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/6434402571805)
If calculation would be done on a daily basis, additional work would be 39 mins every weekday.
With the setting "Workweek calculation mode: **Calculate work hours on public holidays that shorten work week after work days** ", the working hours of the work week can be set to be calculated in such a way that:  
First, the hours of normal working days are calculated (days with a work obligation)  
Next, the hours of public holidays that shorten the workweek are calculated  
Last, the hours of working days that do not have a work obligation are calculated
The setting can be used, for example, in cases where overtime should be earned on public holidays only if the obligation of a shortened workweek has been fulfilled on other working days (including when the public holiday is on a Monday).
## Considering weekly accruals on weekend before forming additional work
Worktime setting Work hours > TES > Work week calculation mode > **KVTES** takes in consideration weekly accruals and regular time on weekend before forming additional work, according to TES Kunnallinen yleinen virka- ja työehtosopimus (KVTES). More detailed examples are shown below.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13825878926493)
For clarity, Saturday and Sunday represent weekend in this chapter. Setting "KVTES" works on weekday accruals on the second last and the last working day of the week. These days may be different depending on [work week starting time](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007557338-Defining-Work-week-starting-time>). 
Other relevant settings used in examples:
\- Length of work day: 7h 15min
\- TES maximum work day length: 8h
\- TES work week length: 36h 15min
\- TES maximum hours of work per week: 38h 15min
\- TES daily 50% overtime compensated hours: 2h
\- Earn 100% overtime after weekly overtime: After TES maximum weekly 50% overtime
\- TES maximum weekly 50% overtime hours: 5h
\- Borrowed from balance contributes towards weekly obligation: No
When work week calculation mode "KVTES" is in use, accumulated accruals during the week are taken in consideration on weekend. If accrual value is negative, same amount of regular time is earned on weekend before earning additional work and overtime. 
In the example below balance accrual from Monday to Friday is 2h 45min negative. Saturday work is marked as overtime to salary. Regular time of 2h 45min is earned on Saturday before earning additional work and overtime. This corresponds to the value of negative balance from Monday to Friday.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13825945269917)
Positive amount of accrual contributes only until work week length (e.g. 36h 15min) and does not reduce amount of additional work. In the example below balance accrual from Monday to Friday is 45min positive. Saturday work is marked as overtime to salary. Extra 45 min of work during the weekdays does not reduce amount of additional work (time between 36h 15min and 38h 15min, 2 hours).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13825934335901)
Because setting "KVTES" interprets weekday negative balance as regular time on weekend, it is recommended to [define length of work day](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417-Defining-the-length-of-work-day>) on weekend as a setting exception if there is work events. In this way daily overtime is earned in a consistent manner. Otherwise only regular time is earned on a long weekend working day if there is a large amount of negative accrual during the week. 
In the example below balance accrual from Monday to Friday is 14h 30min negative. Saturday work is marked as overtime to salary but there is no length of work day on Saturday. 14h 30min is earned as regular time due to absence of work day length.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13826063767325)
When length of work day is set to 7h 15min on Saturday, regular time is earned only until work day length after which daily overtime is earned.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13826130448285)
Exception to above-mentioned behavior when weekday accruals are taken in consideration on weekend, is the usage of event type weekly leave. If weekly leave is used, weekday accrual check is postponed accordingly. 
In the example below weekly leave is marked on Monday and Saturday has overtime. Saturday is interpreted as regular working day because one working day was skipped with the usage of weekly leave event. Regular time until work day length is earned on Saturday and daily overtime after that.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13826188532125)
If there wouldn't be any event on Monday, regular time on Saturday would be the amount of negative accrual between Monday and Friday. This is the default behavior of "KVTES" setting. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13826192593821)
In the example below weekly leave is marked on Monday and Tuesday, Saturday and Sunday have overtime. Saturday and Sunday are interpreted as regular working days because two working days were skipped with the usage of weekly leave event. Regular time until work day length is earned on Saturday and Sunday, and daily overtime after that.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13826231035037)
If there wouldn't be any event on Monday and Tuesday, overtime would be earned on Saturday and Sunday because weekly working hours are reached already in this case. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13826234037405)
## Addition work and public holiday on weekday
By default public holiday on weekday does not affect additional work formation.
Additional work can be formed in a different way if public holiday shortens work week length and maximum hours of work per week. More information about weekly working hours [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005058217>).
On public holiday regular time can be 0 minutes and additional work is paid up to maximum work day length. In this case additional work can be, for example, 8 hours when working on public holiday.
Setting group and working community levels have setting Work hours > Public holidays > **Treat working on public holidays that shorten the week as**. This setting controls work time calculations on public holiday. The options are:
**Normal day** : Regular time and additional work is formed like on any other work day.
**Additional** **work** : Additional work is formed whole day up to maximum work day length. Time after that is overtime.
**Daily / weekly overtime** : Overtime. Weekly overtime after maximum hours of work per week. No regular time or additional work is formed.
**Daily overtime** : Only daily overtime. No regular time, additional work or weekly overtime is formed.
## Additional work on planned holiday
Work on planned holiday can be either weekly overtime or additional work up to daily or weekly limit. This is controlled with setting Work hours > TES >**Earn weekly overtime on work days without a planned shift / obligation**. If the value is 'Yes' work on planned holiday is always weekly overtime and no additional work is formed. 
## Daily additional work contribution to weekly obligation
Setting Work hours > TES > **Daily additional earned over the additional rise threshold contributes to weekly additional rise threshold** controls whether daily additional rise contributes to weekly obligation or not. More information about this setting in article [Overtime calculation basic settings.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4417295059985>)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Reporting / Worktime reports | path: en-gb/Support/Reporting/Worktime-reports/360002548717-Annual-leave-reporting.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548717-Annual-leave-reporting -->

# Annual leave reporting

There are three different reports for tracking annual holidays;
Annual leave usage by month (former name "Annual leave, rolling month analysis")  
Annual leave usage by season (former name "Annual leave, usage follow-up") and  
Annual leave earning by month (former name "Annual leave, earned days")
All reports can be filtered by persons, and the reports can be exported to Excel. It is recommended that the annual leave reports are always taken for the period of the vacation year (April - March of the following year).
## Annual leave earning by month
The Earning by month report allows you to monitor a person's earned annual leave. It is recommended that reports always be taken for the period of the leave accrual year (April - March of the following year). The report shows earned days on a monthly basis up to the time of reporting, according to the settings configured in the service.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27424331281693)
Once the time period and the persons have been selected, click "show report". The report below is taken from a person whose employment relationship began in August 2023. According to the settings, she has accumulated annual leave days 2 days/month from August to March 2024. It has been agreed that she will be given two additional leave days, which have been added manually for September 2023. This is shown in the report under September with the text "Annual leave earnings change". The Total column shows the leave days earned during the entire holiday period, i.e. 18 days. Therefore, the person has 18 leave days to use in the holiday year 2024-2025.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27424331282333)
According to the settings, the person will start accruing annual leave of 2.5 days/month starting in April 2024. In September 2024, the annual leave earnings report for the year 2024-2025 will look like this:  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27424331283229)
## Annual leave usage by season
The leave usage report shows both earned days and their planned usage. Select the period for which you want to view the vacation entitlement. The report shows your accumulated vacation entitlement at the beginning of the period.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27424340931485)
The "Balance at the end of..." column shows the person's accumulated annual leave entitlement for the selected holiday period.
The "Planned annual leave days" column shows the annual leaves added to the person's calendar for that year, that reduce vacation entitlement. The figure takes into account annual leaves already used and those requested for future months.
The "Unused annual leave days" column shows the amount of annual leave the person has unplanned, i.e. still available, for the selected holiday year.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27424340932893)
## Annual leave usage by month
Rullaava kuukausierittely -raportti esittää henkilön käytettävissä olevat lomapäivät, milloin ne on suunniteltu käytettävän, ja kuinka paljon suunnitellun käytön jälkeen on vielä jäljellä käytettäviä vuosilomapäiviä. Raportti suositellaan otettavaksi aina lomavuosi kerrallaan. Alla olevassa esimerkissä on otettu raportti esimerkkihenkilöltä, joka oli ansainnut 18 lomapäivää lomavuonna 2023-2024. Päivät ovat siis käytettävissä lomavuonna 2024-2025, jolta tämä raportti on otettu. Raportista nähdään, että näistä 18:sta päivästä on tällä hetkellä suunniteltu pidettävän 12 päivää kahden viikon jaksossa kesäkuussa 2024 sekä neljä päivää elokuussa 2024. Tällöin henkilöllä on vielä 2 päivää pidettävänä myöhemmin lomavuonna.
The leave usage by month report shows the person's available vacation days, when they are planned to be used, and how many annual leave days are still available to be used after planned use. It is recommended to always take the report one holiday year at a time. The example below is taken from an example person who had earned 18 leave days in the holiday year 2023-2024. The days are therefore available in the holiday year 2024-2025, from which this report is taken. The report shows that of these 18 days, 12 days are currently planned to be taken in a two-week period in June 2024 and four days in August 2024. In this case, the person still has 2 days to take later in the holiday year.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27424331285917)
Approved leave days are shown in dark gray and unapproved leave days in light gray text. Days marked red are not counted as leave days and do not reduce annual leave accrual.

# Annual worktime - following

The simplest way to track annual worktime is to report the Realized work hours.
The same report also makes it possible to monitor total worktime.
The report can be found in the menu Worktime-Work hours-Reports->Realized work hours and can be run at any time.
In some cases, eg in teaching, the earnings of additional work and overtime are determined in steps according to the total amount of annual working time. In this case, monitoring requires the use of Levelling Period settings. If you are not familiar with them yet, you can find instructions [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559537>). 
## Setting up
1\. Enabling accrual: Worktime-Administration-Setting group settings-select setting group-Setting group settings-Work hours-Accruals and overtime hours -> Accruals in use-Levelling period hours
![Tasoittumisjaksot_5.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015046758/Tasoittumisjaksot_5.png)
2\. Set Period start dates: Worktime-Administration-Setting group settings-select setting group-Setting group settings-Work hours-Accruals and overtime hours-Calculation settings-Levelling period hours -> Period start date
![Tasoittumisjaksot_6.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360014972397/Tasoittumisjaksot_6.png)
3\. Set overtime limits for the period: Worktime-Administration-Setting group settings-select setting group-Setting group settings-Work hours-Levelling period -> Levelling period compensation
![Tasoittumisjaksot_9.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015046798/Tasoittumisjaksot_9.png)
## Compensation calculation
Compensation is always calculated on the last day of the period and is visible in the calendar view.
![blobid0.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015048578/blobid0.jpg)
Example image where the levelling period has ended on 31.12.2018 and hours exceeding regular time are shown on the last day of the period.
More information about the calculation, see the "Levelling Period Compensation - Additional work earned after total hours" section in the [Setting up a Levelling period](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559537>) article.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event management | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-management/360005378238-Approve-event-settings.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005378238-Approve-event-settings -->

# Approve event settings

General settings related to approving events can be defined in **Work time > Administration > Working community / Setting group settings > Work hours > Event locking and approval.**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35078388917021)
### Lock events automatically after
Time period after which days will be locked automatically. Automatic locking happens every day early in the morning after midnight.
Example: Lock events automatically after-setting is set to be 14 days. When it is 14th of February, events will be locked until 31st of January. The following day 15th of February events will be locked until 1st of February and so on.
### Approve full days instead of individual events
By default, events are approved individually on event level. With this setting approving can be done on day level.
### When editing an event removes its approval
Makes it possible to remove approval of other events automatically when editing an event and its approval is removed as a result. Enables removal of approval only for persons who have the right to modify already approved events.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35078388920605)
Note! The approval of an event is always removed if the person has the right to modify the event but does not have the right to approve it.
### Approving an event approves all attached projects
Defines if when events are approved also the targeted project hours are approved. **Travel invoice is an exception. Travel invoice project hours are** _**always**_**approved when travel invoice is approved.**
### Removing approval from an event removes the approval of attached projects
Defines if when approval is removed from events, also approval of targeted project hours are removed. **Travel invoice is an exception. Approval of travel invoice project hours is** _**always**_**removed when approval of travel invoice is removed.**
Note! Approval of projects related to an event is always removed when editing the event, unless the event remains approved and the approval of the event approves the projects associated with it.
### Approving all projects attached to an event approves the event
When project hours is approved, also all the work hours of the event are approved. **Travel invoice is an exception. Approval of travel invoice project hours can be done only by approving the travel invoice.**

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event management | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-management/360002519197-Approving-events-and-working-hours.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519197-Approving-events-and-working-hours -->

# Approving events and working hours

Events can be approved either in the calendar view or in the Approve hours view. See the approval-related settings [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005378238>).
The supervisor receives a notification (orange "!") in the Work hours top menu when they have hours to approve. The notification always appears if there are unapproved hours in the previous week. The notification is updated every 30 minutes, or every time the person logs in to the service again or approves hours.
An approved event is displayed in green. If all events for the day have been approved, the entire day is displayed in green. After approving the events, the supervisor has the option to remove the approval if the supervisor or employee needs to make changes to the events later.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245377128477)
Only the primary manager will receive a notification in the menu about unapproved hours, however, secondary managers can also approve hours in the same Approve hours view and calendar, even if they do not receive notifications.
## Approving events in calendar
In the **Events in Calendar** view, each employee's hours can be approved either individually or in batches. This view is the easiest way to review the hours before approval.
### Approving a single event
In the calendar view, you can approve individual events by clicking on the event and then **Edit**. In the Edit Event view, in the Approval field, select the event as approved, after which save the event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245363809821)
### Approving multiple events
Depending on the organization's policy, events can either be approved only, or approved and locked at the same time. Different approval options can be found in the menu under the Approval button. The service remembers the selection and displays the selection that was used last by default the next time.
Events can be approved in the calendar:
-One week at a time (from the weekly summary):
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245377132957)
-The whole calendar view at a time (from the bottom of the page):  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245377135133)
-By using bulk actions and selecting the events to be approved:  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245377136669)
Event approval via the Events in Calendar view also approves any travel invoices and event requests, if they are on the selected period.
Event approval can be removed by selecting **Remove approval** from the Approval menu.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245363823261)
If days are locked, the Approve button will disappear from the calendar view and the supervisor will not be able to reopen the events. By default, locking days upon approval is only possible for administrators.
After locking, a lock icon will appear in the calendar:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245377137949)
For example, supervisors can be separately granted the right to lock events via their worktime role rights. The Can lock event dates permission found in higher-level permissions gives the right to lock days when they are approved. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245363825053)
Unlocking is possible with the separate Can unlock locked dates permission. Unlocking can be done in calendar view under the Approval menu and with the [Lock events function](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002521158>).
## Approving events in hours approval view
Please note that travel invoices are not approved in approve hours view. Travel invoices can be approved either one by one, or when approving events in events in calendar view or separate approve travel expenses view. More info about approving travel invoices can be found [here.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005381337-Approving-travel-invoices>)
In **Approve hours** view all subordinates or deputies' subordinates are shown. Also in this view supervisor can choose if the hours will be only approved or the days also locked. 
If a supervisor has a lot of subordinates, there is a possibility to choose how many subordinates to view at once by selecting **Number of items per page.** Default is 25 per page. If Number of items per page is used, clicking **Approve and continue** takes automatically to the next page. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245377143197)
After approving events in this view, the approval/locking can also be removed from one or several employees.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245363828125)
By default, unapproved events from the previous week or earlier are given for approval. However, the time range of the view can be changed to also include events from the current week via the "Filters" button at the top.
Please note, if subordinates has previous unapproved hours, these hours will always be shown first in the table row, even though they are outside of the selected period of time. Unapproved hours are shown from maximum period of 12 months before the report ends.
Approved work hours before selected period of time are not shown, only unapproved hours. 
If there are event requests during the period, they will also be approved without separate notification.
### Colors and abbreviations of the view 
Color codes of the view and their definitions can be opened from the **Legend** button.
**All events clocked with a terminal** means that all events on the date have been added in real-time with a terminal device and their times have not been modified after they were created.
**All events clocked** means that all events on the date have been added in real-time regardless of the device used, and their times have not been modified after they were created.
Absences are shown with following letter codes in the day's info: 
SL = Sick leave  
A = Absence  
AH = Annual leave  
BL= Balance leave  
WSL = Work time shortening leave  
PH = Public holiday shortening the work week
Work time of the day is shown in day's info in hours and minutes in .0HH:MM form. If absence is paid, the letter code and work time of the absence is shown for example Paid 0 absence is shown as A 08:00. Unpaid would be without the worktime 07:30, only A.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35245377144733)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Travel invoices  | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Travel-invoices/360005381337-Approving-travel-invoices.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005381337-Approving-travel-invoices -->

# Approving travel invoices

Travel invoice functionality is included in the **Complete service level**.
Travel invoices can be approved the same way as other events. See instructions for event approval [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519197>).
The service will notify the supervisor with an orange "!" as soon as there are travel invoices to be approved. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33723066639005)
By selecting **Approve travel expenses** a view for approving travel invoices will open. The view presents each approvable travel invoice in rows, as well as the associated routes, reimbursements, and attachments. In the view you can select only the travel invoices you want to approve.
Approving is done with the 'Approve' button at the bottom. You can open and edit the travel invoice by clicking 'Open' on the correct row.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33723066640285)
If **Accept travel expenses** is not highlighted with an exclamation point, or if you select **Filters** in the approval view, a view opens where you can filter for which time period you want to search for approvable travel invoices.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33723059051933)
You can also choose if you want to search only for unapproved or all travel invoices. Searching for all travel invoices is handy when you need to remove an approval from a travel invoice.
By clicking **Select users** you can limit the search to limited persons. Filtering persons works in the same way as when approving hours and viewing worktime reports.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33723059053725)
The travel invoice approval view opens after you select users and press **View Travel expenses**.
When travel invoices are approved through the Approve Travel Expenses function, only travel invoices are approved. **Approving travel invoice** _**always**_**automatically approves also its project hours. Unapproving travel invoice** _**always**_**unapproves its project hours.** If you also want to approve other events or working hours, you must do so separately via either the Approve Hours view or the Calendar view.
When travel invoices are approved via the Events in Calendar view, both the events and working hours are also approved.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management / Person details management | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/Person-details-management/360002430678-Assigning-deputy.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430678-Assigning-deputy -->

# Assigning deputy

A person may be appointed as a deputy for someone, for example if a person is on a leave. This setting can be done by any person, either for themselves or for persons whose data they have the permission to manage. The person appointed as a deputy does not automatically receive notification of the substitution, i.e. he or she must be informed separately.
## What information does a deputy see?
You can't chain deputies, meaning if person A has person B as deputy and B has person C as deputy, person C does not get deputy rights to person A. Every person that needs to be a deputy to someone, has to be set as deputy to that person directly.
The deputy will be notified of the hours and event requests of the subordinates of the substitute in the same way as the primary supervisor. In addition to the notifications in the calendar view, a separate message about event requests will be sent to the substitute and primary supervisor by email.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33246984220189)
### Worktime
The deputy sees the event entries of the subordinates of the person being substituted in the worktime section. If the deputy is substituting for a person with administrator rights, the deputy will not see the events of all people, but only the event entries of the person's subordinates. For the duration of the substitution, the person designated as a deputy will have the same visibility to the person's subordinates' event entries, approvals and reports as the person being substituted. The deputy will see all the person's subordinates' worktime information during the substitution, i.e. also for the time when they are not acting as a substitute. In this case, the deputy can, for example, approve the hours that were entered before the substitution began. 
### Employees
The deputy cannot see persons' information in the Employee section. If you want to give the person visibility to persons' information in the Employee section, you must set the person as the supervisor of the desired person.
### Workshift planning
The deputy does not have the same visibility into shift planning as the person being substituted. If the deputy is to be able to plan shifts for the same locations as the person being substituted, they must be separately granted the necessary rights to shift planning. Instructions for this can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/19215744439965>).
## Assigning a deputy
Sijainen määritellään Työsuhde-osiossa. Avaa henkilön tiedot auki ja valitse Sijaiset.
The deputies can be added inn **Employees** section. Open the person information of the person you want to set a deputy to and open **Deputies** tab. If you are about to set a deputy to yourself the settings are found in **Own info** > **Deputies**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33246984221341)
To choose the deputy, start typing the beginning of the wanted deputy's last name to **Deputy** -field. You will get a list of persons who match that name and you can choose the right person from the list. The deputy can be anyone who has an active working contract in Nepton.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33246946866077)
You can set start and end times either by typing the dates to Start time and End time fields or by choosing the dates from calendar icons. Both these fields must have a valid date in order to save the deputy. 
After saving the settings, the creation date of deputy will be shown in **Created** -field.
There can be several deputies to one person and valid times can be overlapping.
You can edit settings by clicking the 'Pencil' icon or delete the deputy by clicking the 'X' icon.
### What happens when the employment of a person being substituted ends
When the employment of the person being substituted ends, it must be noted that the substitution and the rights it brings with it do not end with the termination of the employment. Even if the employment of the person being substituted has been terminated in Nepton, the substitution relationship continues until the person's (being substituted) Nepton account is also deactivated. When the substitution period expires, the deputy no longer has visibility into the data of the person's subordinates, even if the person being substituted account is still active.

# Assigning person groups to persons

Person group can be assigned to a person in two ways: In person's details in Employees section, or through Person grups in Worktime section.
Please note that the Person Group does not support validity.
## Assigning person group in Employees section
1\. Go to Employees > Persons > Persons.  
2\. Search for the right person with the search engine.  
3\. Click the magnifying glass in the beginning of the persons row to open their details.  
4\. In the organization section choose the right person group and then press save at the bottom of the page. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19456352983709)
## Assigning person group in Worktime section
  1. Select Worktime -> Administration -> Person Groups.
  2. From the Person Groups main view, select the person group to which you want to add a person.
  3. In the view that opens on the right-hand side, select the “Persons” tab.
  4. Search for and select the person you want to add to the chosen person group.
  5. Save the addition of the person to the person group by clicking the Save button. ![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469817965469)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Workshift planning and Work schedules / Work schedules | path: en-gb/Support/Workshift-planning-and-Work-schedules/Work-schedules/34102283785885-Assumed-Lunch-Reduction-for-a-Shift-Type.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/34102283785885-Assumed-Lunch-Reduction-for-a-Shift-Type -->

# Assumed Lunch Reduction for a Shift Type

This article explains how an assumed lunch reduction can be defined for a shift type in shift planning. The reduction can be set individually for each shift type. The assumed lunch reduction can only be defined for shift types in the work schedule.
## General rules for the assumed lunch reduction
The assumed lunch reduction can be defined only for event types that are listed under the **Work** category in the Event type list. If the event type is selected from the **Absence** category, the field used for setting the assumed lunch reduction will not be shown.
If no specific assumed lunch reduction is defined for a shift type, the reduction is determined as follows:
  * the shift’s assumed lunch reduction is taken from the Location settings under the**** Planning tab, or
  * from the Planning settings located under the Employees tab in the Administration section


If lunch break settings are defined both the assumed lunch reduction is always determined using the Location settings.
If no assumed lunch reduction should be applied to the shift type, the shift type’s reduction must be set to **0 minutes**. This ensures that no reduction is created.
## Defining the Assumed Lunch Reduction
The assumed lunch reduction is defined in the work schedule when creating a shift type. The reduction is set individually for each shift type, and the defined value affects all shifts created using that shift type.
The assumed lunch reduction is defined as follows:
  1. Create a new work schedule and schedule period, or open an existing work schedule.
  2. Create a new shift type or open an existing shift type.
  3. Add the desired **assumed lunch reduction** to the shift type.
  4. Save the changes.


![Screenshot 2026-02-20 105710.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34103435994909)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / HR API | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/HR-API/4406441875089-Authentication-in-HR-API.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406441875089-Authentication-in-HR-API -->

# Authentication in HR API

[HR API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360004855857>) functions have not yet been standardised and therefore have different types of authentication in use. In the future, all functions shall be migrated to the use of credentials tied to a person in the Nepton platform, and the access rights for the API will be the same as the person has configured in Nepton.  
For testing and automated use, we recommend setting up a dedicated person that is not used for other purposes. See [guidance for adding a person](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002427618>).
## Authentication
Many functions in the [HR API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360004855857>) are not yet standardised, please check the function description in the related articles for more information on the fields required to authenticate and make a request. You can also check the autogenerated documentation on the endpoint itself: <https://go.nepton.com/API/SOAPWebService.asmx>
For standardised functions, the elements of authentication are;
  * **Username** \- The username of a person configured in the Nepton service.
  * **UserPassword** \- The password of the above person. **ATTN: Password can not end with &-character. It breaks the XML-message.**
  * **DeploymentId** \- A numeric value identifying your working community. Please contact support for the correct value.
  * **WebServicePassword** \- A password related to the working community data. Please contact support for the correct value.


## Example
Here is an example of a GetUnits SOAP message using the authentication fields:
  * Method: POST
  * Endpoint: https://go.nepton.com/API/SOAPWebService.asmx
  * Headers:  

    * Content-Type: text/xml; charset=utf-8
  * Body:  

[code] <?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
        <soap:Envelope xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xmlns:xsd="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema" xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">
          <soap:Body>
            <GetUnits xmlns="http://tempuri.org/">
              <Request>
                <Username>Integration Account</Username>
                <UserPassword>e8bc7c00-17c8-4802-8962-c77e1071116c</UserPassword>
                <DeploymentId>285057</DeploymentId>
                <WebServicePassword>060b20fe-cd2a-4629-bdc5-7b896a1cebc6</WebServicePassword>
                <IncludeDeletedUnits>false</IncludeDeletedUnits>
              </Request>
            </GetUnits>
          </soap:Body>
        </soap:Envelope>
        
[/code]


API-calls are case-sensitive. Bear this in mind, when forming API calls - all upper case letters must be correct in order to make the API call work.

---

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / Worktime API | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/Worktime-API/360019983978-Authentication-in-Worktime-API.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019983978-Authentication-in-Worktime-API -->

# Authentication in Worktime API

All [Worktime API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360004861558>) messages require authentication with a person account to Nepton service. The access rights for the API are the same that the person has in Nepton service. For regular use we recommend setting up a dedicated person account with a username and a password for the API use in Nepton service. See [guidance for setting up a person](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002427618>). To authenticate a CallerAuthentication element must be supplied in the call as an SOAP element.
## CallerAuthentication
The CallerAuthentication element provides means for authentication. Values for the following fields should be provided:
  * CustomerId - A numeric value identifying the working community. You need to contact Nepton to get a value for the customer identifier.
  * Username - The username of the authenticating person account. A dedicated person account for the API is recommended.
  * Password - The password of the authenticating person account. **ATTN: Password can not end with &-character. It breaks the XML-message.**


Other fields listed in the API description of CallerAuthentication are for internal use only.
### Example
[code] 
    <CallerAuthentication>  
      <CustomerId>xxxxxxxxx</CustomerId>  
      <Username>xxxxxxxxx</Username>  
      <Password>xxxxxxxxx</Password>  
    </CallerAuthentication>
[/code]
API-calls are case-sensitive. When forming an API-call, make sure all the upper case letters are in their correct places to make the call work.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Travel invoices  | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Travel-invoices/360002559777-Automatically-filled-travel-allowances.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559777-Automatically-filled-travel-allowances -->

# Automatically filled travel allowances

Travel invoice functionality is included in the **Complete service level**.
If travel invoices feature is in use users can add travel invoices and their daily allowances. The service can automatically fill in daily allowance amounts based on the information entered to the travel invoice.
## Travel invoice settings
Travel allowance settings can be configured in the Worktime section: **Work Hours > TES > Travel Allowances.** ![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33721661354397)  
  
If Vero (tax) is selected in the configuration, the person will automatically receive the number of daily allowance according to the marked hours when using travel invoice event. Days of more than 6 hours will give out part-time allowance and days of more than 10 hours will give out full-time allowance. If the person has enjoyed one free lunch, the part-time allowance will be reimbursed in half and 2 free meals will halve the full-time allowance.
If you want to prevent daily allowance, you must add Meal reimbursement to expenses.
Automatic filling does not prevent editing the daily allowance on the travel invoice.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33721661356189)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / Example APIs and method descriptions | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/Example-APIs-and-method-descriptions/6869807559453-BeginActivity.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6869807559453-BeginActivity -->

# BeginActivity

Tästä metodista on uudempi versio. Mikäli käytät jo tätä metodia, niin suosittelemme että tarkastelet seuraavan version ohjeesta, mitä muutoksia vaaditaan uuden version käyttöönottamiseksi. Seuraavan version ohjeen löydät [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6869562936221>).
## Rajapinnan yleiskuvaus
Verkkopalvelua käytetään tapahtuman aloitukseen Neptonissa
Verkkopalvelu on suunniteltu käytettäväksi päätelaitesovelluksissa. Kaikki verkkopalvelun kautta aloitetut tapahtumat kirjataan kellotettuina tapahtumina.
Verkkopalvelun autentikoituminen eroaa muista verkkopalveluista sillä tavalla, että onnistuneesti käyttäjätunnuksella ja salasanalla autentikoitunut henkilö voi autentikoitua toisena henkilönä PIN-koodin tai RFID-koodin perusteella. Ensimmäisessä vaiheessa autentikoituneella henkilöllä täytyy olla oikeudet lukea henkilötietoja. Esimerkiksi:
[code] 
    <CallerAuthentication>
      <CustomerId>1234</CustomerId>
      <Username>PäätelaiteKäyttäjä</Username>
      <Password>KuvitteellinenSalasana123</Password>
      <PinCode>1234</PinCode> <!-- Päätelaitteella syötetty PIN-koodi -->
    </CallerAuthentication>
[/code]
Jos annetulla PIN-koodilla tai RFID-koodilla ei löydy henkilöä, autentikoituminen epäonnistuu.
Verkkopalvelun WSDL-skeema on julkisesti saatavilla [täällä](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). Rajapinnat ovat yleisellä tasolla kuvattuna [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>).
Kuvauksessa oleva sarake esiintymiskerrat määrittää sen onko jokin tieto pakollinen kutsussa vai ei. Esiintymiskerrat 0, tarkoittaa että kyseistä tietoa ei tarvitse siirtää kutsussa. Esiintymiskerrat 1 tarkoittaa, että tiedon tulee esiintyä kutsussa yhden kerran. Esiintymiskerrat 0..n tarkoittaa, että kyseinen tieto voi esiintyä kutsussa minkä tahansa määrän. Esiintymiskerrat 1..n tarkoittaa että kyseinen tieto tulee olla aineistossa ainakin kerran, mutta voi olla useamminkin.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / Example APIs and method descriptions | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/Example-APIs-and-method-descriptions/6869562936221-BeginActivityV2.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6869562936221-BeginActivityV2 -->

# BeginActivityV2

## Interface overview
The web service is used to start an event in Nepton.
The web service is designed to be used in terminal applications. All events started through the web service are recorded as clocked events.
Authentication in the web service differs from other web services in that a person who has successfully authenticated with a username and password can authenticate as another person based on a PIN code or RFID code. In the first step, the authenticated person must have the rights to view personal data. For example:
[code] 
    <CallerAuthentication>
      <CustomerId>1234</CustomerId>
      <Username>PäätelaiteKäyttäjä</Username>
      <Password>KuvitteellinenSalasana123</Password>
      <PinCode>1234</PinCode> <!-- PIN code given on the terminal -->
    </CallerAuthentication>
[/code]
If the person cannot be found with the provided PIN code or RFID code, authentication will fail.
The WSDL schema of the web service is publicly available [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). The interfaces are described in general [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).
The occurrences column in the description determines whether a piece of information is mandatory in the call or not. Occurrences 0 means that the information in question does not need to be passed in the call. Occurrences 1 means that the information must appear once in the call. Occurrences 0..n means that the information in question can appear any number of times in the call. Occurrences 1..n means that the information in question must appear in the data at least once, but can appear more often.
## Changes from the previous version ([BeginActivity](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6869807559453>))
### Structural changes
Old | New | Additional info  
---|---|---
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForBeginActivity>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForBeginActivity>
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForBeginActivityV2>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForBeginActivityV2>
[/code]
|  The name of the call root element has changed.
[code] 
    <tyo:ReturnValueForBeginActivity>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ReturnValueForBeginActivity>
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <tyo:ReturnValueForBeginActivityV2>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ReturnValueForBeginActivity>
[/code]
|  The name of the response root element has changed.
[code] 
    <StartedActivity>  
      <BeginDateTime>  
        2020-01-01 12:00:00  
      </BeginDateTime>  
      <EndDateTime>  
        2020-01-01 14:00:00  
      </EndDateTime>  
      <ModifiedDateTime>  
        2020-01-01 16:00:00  
      </ModifiedDateTime>  
    </StartedActivity>
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <StartedActivity>  
      <BeginDateTime>  
        2020-01-01T12:00:00  
      </BeginDateTime>  
      <EndDateTime>  
        2020-01-01T14:00:00  
      </EndDateTime>  
      <ModifiedDateTime>  
        2020-01-01T16:00:00  
      </ModifiedDateTime>  
    </StartedActivity>
[/code]
|    
In the response, the date and time elements are now of type datetime, which slightly affects the date format (BeginDateTime, EndDateTime, ModifiedDateTime)  
### Obsolete elements
The following elements were previously in the response twice, first under the Activity element and the second time under the PlannedWorkDetails element:
  * PlannedWorkCalculationUnit
  * PlannedWorkColor
  * PlannedWorkUseForWorkDayLengthCalculations
  * PlannedWorkCanBeCancelledUntil
  * PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetStartInMins
  * PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetEndInMins
  * PlannedWorkActivityGroupPublicInfo


From now on, these elements will only be found under the PlannedWorkDetails element.
RelatedActivityId was already reported as deprecated in the previous version, but now this element has been technically removed from the response.
### New features and elements
  * Possibility to define external identifiers to events
    * Added ExternalIdentifiers element to the call
    * Added ExternalIdentifiers element to the response
  * Response includes information about person's personnel number 
    * Added UserPersonnelNumber element
  * Response includes information about approver's personnel number  

    * Added ApproverPersonnelNumber element


## Sent data
LEVEL |  FIELD NAME |  FORMAT |  OCCURRENCES |  DESCRIPTION  
---|---|---|---|---

1 |  EndDateTime |  datetime |  0..1 |  The end date and time of the event. Data given in format `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`. Not mandatory. The event can be ended via another method.

1 |  OvertimeIncrementPartTargetedTo |  string |  0..1 |  Accrual, where overtime increment part is being directed to. See possible values [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6904407712413>).

2 |  ActivityToProjectRelation |  XML element |  0..n |

### Call example
[code] 
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">
      <soapenv:Header/>
      <soapenv:Body>
        <tyo:ParametersForBeginActivityV2>
          <CallerAuthentication /> <!-- Authentication is needed, but left out on this example --> 
          <ActivityTypeId>1</ActivityTypeId>
          <BeginDateTime>2021-05-28T07:35:34</BeginDateTime>
          <TerminalId>418</TerminalId>
          <ExternalIdentifiers>
            <ExternalIdentifier>
              <Identifier>ae2f6c97-104f-49e4-9cff-70951f00234e</Identifier>
              <IdentifierType>External</IdentifierType>
            </ExternalIdentifier>
          </ExternalIdentifiers>
        </tyo:ParametersForBeginActivityV2>
      </soapenv:Body>
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Rulesets | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Rulesets/25397332335773-Best-practices-for-ruleset-modifications.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/25397332335773-Best-practices-for-ruleset-modifications -->

# Best practices for ruleset modifications

This article describes how to manage rule sets correctly. The article provides tips that facilitate change management and the rapid implementation of a previous rule set, if for some reason you do not want to implement the new rule set as is. This article only touches rulesets for data extracted from Nepton (e.g. salary data, absences, holidays, PowerBI). Rulesets are generally built as high as possible in the setting group structure in Nepton: either at the Working Community settings level or in the highest setting groups. You can access rule sets via **Worktime > Administration > Working Community Settings > Integrations: Integration ruleset** or **Worktime > Administration > Setting groups, select the setting group you wanted and its settings > Integrations: Integration ruleset.**
## Changing a ruleset and keeping old ruleset rule in history
When changing a ruleset rule, it is important to note that the old rule, which has already been found to be working, is left "retained" in the history.
  1. Select the desired rule along the path mentioned above and copy the old rule in its entirety using the CTRL C key combination.
  2. Go to the rule validity function field from the button that looks like a calendar icon on the right side of the ruleset rule box  
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25559426027293)
  3. The Validity tool function opens a new view showing the currently valid rule. Set the **Valid to** date for the old rule (this should be either at the end of the month or at the end of the payroll period, so that the rule does not change in the middle of the payroll period). It is important that the validity of the old rule ends before the new rule starts. If the validity periods overlap, Nepton follows the validity period of the old rule.
  4. Press the **"Add"** button to add its own line for the new rule.
  5. Paste the old rule you copied in step 1 into the view that opens (for example, with the CTRL V key combination). Also make the desired changes to the rule here, if you are making changes in the user interface. If you are using another application to change the rule, paste the changed, new rule into this field directly from the other application.
  6. Set the **Valid from** date for the new rule. This date must be the day following the end date of the old rule, if the intention is that there will be no break between the old and new rules.  
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26177499481629)  
  

  7. Add a comment at the top of the new rule that contains a detailed description of **what** changes were made, **when** , at **whose request** , and **who** made the change. You can add a comment to a rule by using two dashes (--) at the beginning of the line, this prevents the comment from affecting the extraction rule itself. See an example of adding a comment below.  
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26177437803037)  
  

  8. When you are satisfied with the changes you have made, finally press the **Save** button in the validity function window to apply the changes you have made.
  9. After making the changes, it is also essential to test that the desired changes work correctly. You can test the new rule in its entirety by running the application in preview mode for selected test or example persons. Instructions for running working time applications can be found in our support service [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002492898-Worktime-integrations>)

---

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event management | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-management/360002521038-Bulk-actions.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002521038-Bulk-actions -->

# Bulk actions

If there is a need to edit or delete multiple events, **Bulk actions** -tool can be used. Go to Worktime > Work hours > Events in calendar.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35069362529053)
When bulk actions are activated, a check box will appear for each week, day, and event. Events can be selected for editing on a week, day, or event-by-event basis.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35069338127901)
When the events selected for editing are checked, the desired action is selected at the bottom of the view. The employee can delete the selected events, or edit their project allocation. The administrator or supervisor can also approve the events (without locking).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35069362529821)
If you edit the project targets of the selected events, the **Edit Projects** button will open a pop-up window where you can change the project targets.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35069338129181)
In the**Select projects** part project targets for events can be replaced with other projects, or new projects can be added to the event. Each project duration can be edited to the wanted length. 
In **Review events** part you can also separately select which events the project targeting will be changed to (check the box).  
  
Finally, you choose to either **Override existing projects** or **Add to existing projects** to the event in addition to existing projects.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Workshift planning and Work schedules / Work schedules | path: en-gb/Support/Workshift-planning-and-Work-schedules/Work-schedules/31936211362717-Bulk-Actions-for-Work-schedule-shifts.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/31936211362717-Bulk-Actions-for-Work-schedule-shifts -->

# Bulk Actions for Work schedule shifts

This instruction describes the use of bulk actions in planning view. Bulk actions are designed to make planning easier in situations where multiple shifts need to be managed simultaneously. With bulk actions, you can edit the details of several shifts, copy shifts, move shifts, or delete shifts all at once. Bulk actions are used in the planning view of shift scheduling. This instruction covers bulk actions for work schedule shifts. The use of bulk actions in detailed planning is described in a separate [article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/8271501506973-Bulk-actions>).
### Selecting shifts
When using bulk actions, shifts are first selected in the planning view. Start by clicking **Bulk Actions** and choose the shifts you want to edit.
![Screenshot 2025-12-02 120550.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32233367337629)
Shifts can be selected by clicking:
  * A single shift
  * A day cell
  * A week cell
  * A location cell at the location row
  * A resource cell at the person row
  * Select All function, additional options open from the downward arrow button


Once the shifts have been selected, continue by choosing the desired action.
![Screenshot 2025-12-02 120757.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32233398802333)
### Edit action
The Edit action allows you to modify the details of selected shifts in the planning view. The following details can be changed during editing:
  * Event type: The event type of a custom shift
  * Shift type: The event type of a calendar shift
  * Shift details / Note: A note to add or remove from the shift
  * Planner details: Custom shift information visible in the planning view
  * Shift abbreviation: Abbreviation for the custom shift
  * Start and end date and time: The timing of the shift can be changed
  * Task: Tasks to add to the shift
  * Person: The person to assign to the edited shift, to whom the selected shifts will be moved


When all editing selections have been made, click **Edit** at the bottom of the view.
![Screenshot 2025-12-02 120952.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32233398802973)
### Copy action
The Copy action allows you to duplicate selected shifts in the planning view. When copying, you must set the repetition and time interval. In addition, the following details can be modified:
  * Event type: The event type of a custom shift
  * Shift type: The event type of a work schedule shift
  * Shift information / Note: A note to add or remove from the shift
  * Shift information for planners: Shift information visible in the planning view
  * Shift alias: Alias for the custom shift
  * Task: Tasks to add to the shift
  * Location: The location of the custom shift (cannot be changed for work schedule shifts)
  * Person: The person to assign to the copied shift. If a person is added, the copied shifts will be moved to that person
  * Additional options


When all copy settings have been made, click **Copy** at the bottom of the view.
![Screenshot 2025-12-02 121245.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32233398804893)
### Move action
The Move action allows you to move selected shifts in the planning view. The following details can be changed during the move:
  * Date: The new date to which the shifts will be moved
  * Person: The person to assign to the moved shift. If a person is added, the selected shifts will be moved to that person


Shifts cannot be moved to another work schedule. When all move selections have been made, click **Move** at the bottom of the view.
![Screenshot 2025-12-02 121659.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32233367345437)
### Delete action
The Delete action allows you to remove selected shifts in the planning view. Before deleting, you will see a summary of the shifts to be removed. It is important to note that deletion is permanent and cannot be undone.
![Screenshot 2025-12-02 121855.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32233367348125)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360005058217-Calculation-of-daily-and-weekly-working-hours.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005058217-Calculation-of-daily-and-weekly-working-hours -->

# Calculation of daily and weekly working hours

Overtime is accumulated on a daily basis, not per event, meaning all accrued overtime is summed together. After this, it is interpreted according to the settings whether it is 50% or 100% overtime. If rounding applies to the overtime, the rounding is formed temporally to the last overtime period. The exception to this is the 'Agreed 100% Overtime', which rounds independently and does not affect the other overtime calculations of the day.
A person’s daily and weekly working hours are determined based on the settings group associated with the person and the person’s work time percentage. The length of the working day and week used can be seen in the **Events Calendar** or in the **Events in table** view by clicking on the date.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20545516878365) ![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20545516879133)
When calculating working hours, regular working hours for a person are formed from those time entries that fall below the length of the workday and the workweek. In interpretation, regular working hours are scheduled so that they are compensated starting from the beginning of the workday as set in the settings. Regular working hours are compensated for subsequent events in chronological order. The scheduling of regular working hours can be directed by entering [assumed working hours](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558617-Expected-work-times>) into the service.
The settings mentioned below can be found in the settings under **Work Hours > TES**.
For the portion exceeding regular working hours, the calculation first examines the length of the workweek. Working time is treated as exceeding the weekly working hours to the extent that it exceeds the value of the ‘TES work week length’ setting but still falls below the length of the workday.
Time exceeding the length of the workweek can be allocated to accruals or paid as overtime. If the time exceeding the workweek is compensated as overtime, then the time is compensated as weekly additional work up to the 'TES maximum hours of work per week**'** setting. See a more detailed description of additional work [here.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559438-Additional-work-formation>) Weekly 50% overtime is compensated up to the 'TES maximum weekly 50% overtime hours' setting. After this, the resulting weekly overtime is compensated with a 100% increase.
When the maximum weekly working hours have not been reached, weekly overtime can be set to accrue with the setting**'** Weekly overtime threshold if earned before TES max week length**'.** In this case, work that exceeds the weekly working hours is compensated as TES overtime when the threshold amount of work for the week is exceeded. In this case, no weekly additional work is formed. Threshold value must be smaller than TES work week length for it to have effect. This setting can be used in accumulating of overtime for part-time employees.
Working time is treated as exceeding the daily working hours to the extent that it exceeds the ‘length of the workday’ setting. Time exceeding the length of the day can be allocated to accruals or paid as overtime. If the time exceeding the workday is compensated as overtime, then the time is compensated as daily additional work up to the ‘TES maximum work day length’ setting. See a more detailed description of additional work [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559438-Additional-work-formation>). Daily 50% overtime is compensated up to the 'TES daily 50% overtime compensated hours**'** setting. After this, the resulting daily overtime is compensated with a 100% increase.
Setting "Earn 100% overtime after weekly overtime" can be used to set when 100% overtime earning begins. If the setting is set to:  
-"No", overtime earning goes as per the settings.  
-"Yes", 100% overtime earning starts immediately after weekly overtime has been earned, regardless of the amount. For example if on Wednesday 3 hours of weekly50% has been earned, will all overtime be 100% on Thursday.  
-"TES maximum weekly 50% overtime hours" 100% overtime earning starts after the maximum amount of weekly 50% overtime has been earned. For example, if the maximum amount of weekly 50% overtime is 8h, will 100% overtime earning begin after the 8 hours of 50% weekly overtime has been earned. 
When the maximum daily working hours have not been reached, daily overtime can be set to accrue with the setting 'Daily overtime threshold if earned before TES max day length**'.** In this case, work that exceeds the daily working hours is compensated as daily TES overtime as soon as the time to be compensated for the day exceeds the threshold. In this case, no daily additional work or weekly overtime is formed. Threshold value must be smaller than maximum work day length for it to have effect. This setting can be used in accumulating of overtime for part-time employees.
The compensation for event types and their consideration in the calculation of the actual weekly working hours can be changed in the settings under **Work Hours > TES > Event types that contribute to work week.**
Note! By default, only paid event types are counted towards the workweek
If event type-specific settings have not been changed, the following paid event types are not counted towards the workweek:
  * Training
  * Union steward work
  * Travel time
  * Health care
  * Workplace health and safety work


## Reducing the maximum weekly working hours
The maximum weekly working hours can be reduced when there is a public holiday during the week, or when the person has absences. Absences that reduce the maximum weekly working hours are defined in TES settings under the title 'Extra time to be deducted from max week length on absence days' .
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20547615083293)
For example, if you want sick leave to reduce the workweek by 7 hours and 30 minutes according to the entry and to reduce the maximum working hours for the day by a total of 8 hours, the setting value for sick leave would be given as 30 minutes.
## Reducing the length of the workweek on a public holiday week
A public holiday can be set to reduce the weekly working hours as follows:
  1. According to the daily obligation. In this option, one day reduces the workweek by a maximum of 8 hours, even if the length of the day is longer
  2. According to the weekly obligation. In this option, the length of the workweek is divided by five (5). For example, with a 30-hour workweek, each public holiday reduces both the weekly working hours and the maximum weekly working hours by 6 hours. Additionally, in the TES settings, the setting Public and annual leaves shorten whole week first must be defined as ‘Yes’ so that the reducing effect of the public holiday is also processed on the weekdays preceding the public holiday
  3. According to the maximum weekly working hours. In this option, both the length of the workweek and the maximum weekly working hours are divided by five (5). For example, if there is a 30-hour workweek and a 40-hour maximum weekly working hours, then each public holiday reduces the weekly working hours by 6 hours and the maximum working hours by 8 hours.


The method of reduction can be defined in the settings of the work community or settings group under **Work Hours - > Public Holidays -> Public holidays shortens work week by**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20550623302301)
In addition to the method of reduction, it must be defined how the weekly working hours are shortened. The reduction can affect the length of the workweek (TES work week length) and the maximum weekly working hours
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20550609007645)
Weekly overtime is compensated as additional work if the length of the workweek is exceeded, but the maximum weekly working hours are not exceeded. If the maximum weekly working hours are not shortened, weekly overtime is paid as additional work up to the maximum working hours, after which weekly overtime is paid. Detailed instructions for defining additional work can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559438-Additional-work-formation>)
## Weekly Overtime Formation Before Completion of Weekly Hours
The collective agreement (TES) may interpret that weekly overtime is accrued even before the completion of weekly hours. With the setting ‘threshold for the formation of weekly overtime’, it can be directed that after a set amount of work, weekly overtime is earned regardless of the length of the workweek.
The collective agreement (TES) may also interpret that when certain event types occur, no weekly additional work is formed, but work done on a day off is compensated as weekly overtime. With the setting 'Collective labour agreement for the salaried employees in the real estate sector' > 'Event types which cause overtime on days off to be compensated as weekly overtime', these event types can be selected. In addition, the same functionality can be chosen for public holidays that shorten the workweek.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20550623304221)
If overtime according to the collective agreement (TES) is accrued before the completion of weekly hours, this overtime can be set as separate from the weekly overtime with the setting 'TES overtime earned separately to weekly overtime'**.** In this case, overtime according to TES is calculated separately from weekly overtime, and it is possible to first earn overtime according to TES up to the weekly threshold and correspondingly weekly overtime.
When 'TES overtime earned separately to weekly overtime**'** is set to 'Yes' and there are absence days during the week that trigger overtime on the weekend according to the real estate sector TES rules, overtime for the weekend would be calculated as follows:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20598137640605)
## The length of the workday/week and the maximum working hours
In interpretation, the length of the workday or workweek is considered fulfilled when the maximum working hours are filled, even if the length of the workday or workweek has not yet been met. After this, the working time is interpreted as overtime.
If the maximum working hours per day/week in the settings are shorter than the length of the workday/week, the maximum working hours are increased to match the length of the workday/week.
## Hour to hour -overtime contributes towards weekly obligation
By default no hour to hour time contributes to weekly obligation.
Also if the event type is set to not contribute towards weekly obligation then its hour to hour time won't contribute either regardless of what is set to these settings.
If needed, this setting can specify that hours exceeding regular time, which are compensated hour to hour, are counted toward weekly obligated work time in one of the following ways:
  * Both week and max work week length
  * Only work week length
  * Only max work week length
  * Only on non obligated days (with this setting, the hour to hour interpreted time is considered only in max work week length)

![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32136911681309)
The week and max work week length are defined in the TES section under the following settings:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32136925198877)
