# Calendar Synchronisation

Keep your personal or work calendar up to date with Nepton regarding your meetings, shifts and holidays. Events marked on Nepton (as selected) are automatically transferred to your calendar. This feature is only available if your non-Nepton calendar supports synchronization of events from an external service.
Note that only 7 days from the past and the next 3 years of future events are synchronized.
## Enabling Calendar Synchronisation
1\. Go to Worktime -section and choose events in calendar. On the top right corner of the page, click Calendar Sync. Choose the right calendar: 
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4412300264977/mceclip0.png)
2\. Choose, which event types you wish to export from Nepton:
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4412293673489/mceclip1.png)
3\. A link is created automatically. Copy the link.
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4412300281617/mceclip2.png)
## Setting the link to an external calendar 
If your calendar supports syncing events from an external calendar, you should be able to create a new calendar from your calendar with options that resemble "Import by URL" or "Import by iCal (ics)". The link you copied can be set with this function.
**Outlook**
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360005534497/mceclip0.png)
The added calendar and selected events should now appear on your external calendar. Events are updated on your calendar about every hour. If the update does not take place, set the link again to update the events.
**TIP** : In Outlook, you can use the Overlay feature to bring Nepton and Outlook calendar views together.
![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4412309556625/mceclip3.png)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-recording/4687116906141-Calendar-view-presentation.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4687116906141-Calendar-view-presentation -->

# Calendar view presentation

The calendar view can be found in the menu **Worktime > Work hours > Events in calendar**. The Events in calendar view always shows the current calendar month and the logged-in user's calendar by default.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33208374259869)
By clicking on the date row, you can change the view's time period to the desired time period, either by selecting the days manually or moving forward/backward by using the arrow buttons.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33208374260765)
In the example below, only one day, January 5, 2026, has been selected as the view using the date search function.
## Day's basic information
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33208374261149)
**The Week** row shows the week number, year and date. By clicking on the date you can[ add a new event](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002596797>) to the day. The Total column shows the total data per week for the period searched in the calendar view.
**The Events** row shows all[ event types](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002520778>) recorded for the day. In the example, the added event "Work" is marked for the time period 08:00-17:30. This event is assigned to the project "Varasto (warehouse)". The event includes an automatically generated[ lunch break](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558757>) from 11:30-12:00. In addition, there is another work event during the day from 19:00-20:00.
**Worked time incl. absences** indicates the recorded working time after deducting unpaid events. In this example, the lunch break of 30 mins has been subtracted from worked time including absences value. If roundings are in use, any time created due to rounding up is not shown on this row. NOTE: Accrual leaves are not shown on this line, even though they are paid absences.
In the example, **regular time is** filled by the Work event. Regular working hours are filled when work has been done for the [length of the working day](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>), i.e. in this case 07:30 hours. Regular working hours could also be filled from an [accrual](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005073918>), if the work obligation isn't fulfilled. Any hours targeted "hour to hour to salary" are also shown on this line.
**The Overtime** row appears in the calendar if overtime has been earned during the week. The [overtime portion of an event](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002481617>) can be handled in many different ways, depending on what is defined in the [settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4417295059985>). In this example, the time exceeding regular working hours of the event is allocated with Overtime - Salary target. The portion exceeding regular working hours, 02:30, is overtime. Under the Overtime heading, you can see that it has been allocated to salary. By clicking on the triangle next to it, you can open an even more detailed breakdown of overtime:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33208358067997)
After overtime, **supplements** are shown, if any have been recorded. [Supplements ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559637>)are one-time compensations that are added manually. In the example, the supplement Asuntonäyttö ilta has been added to the event once.
Next any automatically generated increments, i.e. [work rises](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560978>), are shown. In the example image, 1 hour of evening increment (iltalisä) has been generated. Work rises can be accrued based on the time of day, event type, and event type compensation type.
The bottom row shows all displayed **accruals** in use. In the example, the accrual types used are balance, bank, holiday pay, kausiainsainta, testikertymäl, weekly rest and work time shortening leave. If there is an event on the day that affects the accrual, the negative or positive balance for the accrual on the day is displayed.
## Worktime calculation criteria
Clicking on the date in the calendar view opens the view below, worktime calculation criteria. The view tells you the settings the interpretation of the work day is based on.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33208941320093)  
  
The [work day obligation](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>) in the example is defined in the settings as 7 hours and 30 minutes, meaning the person's regular working hours are 7 hours and 30 minutes per day.
The[ work week obligation](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558537>) in the example is defined as 37 hours 30 minutes, meaning the person's regular weekly working hours are 37 hours 30 minutes.
[Expected working hours](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558617>) affect the interpretation of overtime. Using expected working hours can enable overtime to be earned even before the actual work shift or established working hours. In this example, the expected working hours are 00-24:00.
[Permitted working hours](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558597>) define the hours outside of which work performed is not considered working time. In this example, the permitted working hours are 06:00-20:00. If the Work event in the example had been started before 06:00, the time before 06:00 would not have been considered working time. If the Work event in the example had been finished after 20:00, the time after 20:00 would not have been considered working time.
## Event's basic information
By clicking on a registered event in the calendar, more detailed information about that event will open in a new window.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33208941323165)
The information displayed about the event includes the total duration of the event, overtime earned from the event, recorded supplement, and the event creator.
[The Event edit history](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002521298>) feature allows you to view the original entry of the event and other older versions if it has been edited since creation.
[The Event listing report](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548877>) shows all recorded and deleted events.
[The Copy event ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002521078>)function allows you to copy an event to multiple times and people.
[The Related Events](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002521118>) function allows you to mass delete copied events from the calendar view as long as the events have not been edited or approved.
The event can be [deleted](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002520978>).
Events for the period searched for in the calendar view can be [approved ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519197>)directly from the calendar at the end of the week or for the entire calendar view. The right to approve events depends on the rights granted by the [worktime roles](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554338>).
## Summary
  
At the bottom of the calendar view is a summary of the hours in the entire view. Below is an example of a summary of an entire month.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33208957549981)
In addition to the information displayed in the calendar view, the summary shows the event types used, the number of public holidays, annual leave days used, and public holiday compensation.

# Calibrate terminal screen (For Nepton Touch devices before September 2022)

**Whoops!**
This article has not been translated yet.
Huomioithan, että kaikkien työaikapäätteiden näyttöä ei voi kalibroida vaan kalibroinnin mahdollisuus riippuu työaikapäätteen tyypistä. Tämä ohje korkee Nepton Touch -palvelusopimuksella toimitettuja OLink-laitteita. Lisätietoja saadaksesi olethan yhteydessä organisaationne palvelun pääkäyttäjään.
**1\. Jotta laitteen näyttö voidaan kalibroida uudelleen, tulee ensin poistua kirjausnäkymästä.**
\- Tarkista, että laitteessa on virrat päällä.
\- Paina sormella tai kosketusnäyttökynällä laitteen kosketusnäytön jokaista neljää kulmaa kerran jämäkästi mahdollisimman läheltä reunaa järjestyksessä**vasen yläkulma - oikea yläkulma - oikea alakulma - vasen alakulma.**
\- Näkymän pitäisi poistua ja nyt pitäisi näkyä perinteinen Windows-työpöytänäkymä, jolla erilaisia kuvakkeita.
**2\. Näytön kalibrointi**
Kalibrointiasetuksiin pääset valitsemalla M**y Device - Control Panel - Stylus - Calibration - Recalibrate.** Klikkaa kaikkia viittä rastia, jotka ilmestyvät näytölle. Kun viimeinen rasti katoaa, paina mistä tahansa kohtaa näyttöä. Tämän toimenpiteen saattaa joutua toistamaan, mikäli osut liian kauas jostain näytölle ilmestyvistä rasteista.  
  
Tarvittaessa laitteeseen on mahdollista kiinnittää myös USB-näppäimistö, jonka avulla voit navigoida työpöytä-näkymän valikoissa.
**3\. Palaaminen kirjausnäkymään, jotta työaikaa voi taas kirjata.**
\- Kun halutut asetukset on määritelty tulee Terminal Launcher käynnistää uudelleen, jotta työaikaa voi taas kirjata. Työpöytänäkymästä löytyy **Nepton Terminal Launcher -kuvake** , jota tuplaklikkaamalla palvelu käynnistyy. Kun palvelua käynnistetään saattaa se käynnistyä itsestään useamman kerran uudelleen. Tämä on normaalia ja saattaa kestää jopa 10 minuuttia. Odota rauhassa, että palvelu käynnistyy.  
  
\- Joissain laiteversioissa Terminal Launcher ei ole työpöydällä, vaan se tulee käynnistää valitsemalla työpöydältä kansio **My device**. Kansiosta valitaan **Storage Card - Release - Työteho** (tuplaklikataan). Kirjausnäkymä avautuu automaattisesti ja laite on valmis vastaanottamaan kirjauksia. Tässäkin tapauksessa palvelu saattaa käynnistyä uudelleen useita kertoja ja käynnistyksessä saattaa kestää useita minuutteja.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360017272298-Camp-work.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360017272298-Camp-work -->

# Camp work

## Background
Nepton service can be configured to automatically compensate holiday time to employees for performing camp work based on their TES agreement. Holiday time is earned in the form of days based on the length of the Camp work and can be paid into their bank or balance.
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360016222317/mceclip1.png)
## How to configure Camp working hours compensation
Two steps are required for configuring camp working hours compensation.
  1. Setting camp work holiday earning and maximum earned work on first camp work day
  2. Setting work rises to handle worked time earning from camp work


### Holiday earning and maximum earned work on first camp work day
The compensation settings can be configured in:
Worktime > Administration > Working community settings (or Setting groups > select Setting group > select Setting group settings) > Work hours > TES > Camp work
  * "Maximum earned work on first camp day" - Total amount of time that can be earned for the first day of camp when setting up.
  * "Holiday day length earned from camp work" - The number of holiday days earned are based on the duration of the Camp work. This setting dictates how many hours and minutes each day will pay once paid into an accrual.
  * "Earn camp work holidays to accrual" - Which accrual should the earned camp work holiday compensation be paid into.
  * "Rule for earning holiday from camp work" - Different compensation can be earned for being on camp work for different lengths of time, these can be configured using up to 10 rules with each setting meaning the following: 
    * "Holidays earned if camp work length at least" - Total duration of camp work required to earn the number of days specified in the next setting.
    * "Holiday days earned" - Number of holiday days earned for meeting the threshold in the previous setting.
    * "Camp work has to start on Friday or Saturday" - Some rules require that the holiday days are only earned if the camp work started on a Friday or Saturday, this can be configured here.


### Work rises
This step is required for correct earning of worked time from recorded camp work event.
**First work rise - remove camp work earned time that is not regular time**
  * "Name" - Descriptive work rise name
  * "Visible in week panel" - it is recommended to not show this work rise in week panel as it will make the view more unclear
  * "On public holidays earning is calculated according to day" - set this to be Sunday
  * "Compensation types that earn work rise" - should be earned from all other types than "Regular time"
  * "Event types that earn work rise" - should be only earned from "Camp work" event type
  * "Periods of validity" - set this to be 00:00 - 24:00 on all week days, Monday to Sunday
  * "Force time earned during work rise to overtime" - set all of them to be "Not compensated"


**Second work rise - worked time from camp work during weekends**
  * "Name" - a descriptive name, for example "Camp work on weekends"
  * "Maximum amount compensated" - the maximum amount of worked time that you want to be earned from camp work on days during weekend and public holidays
  * "Visible in week panel" - it is recommended to display this in week panel
  * "On public holidays earning is calculated according to day" - set this to be Sunday
  * "Compensation types that earn work rise" - should be earned from all types
  * "Event types that earn work rise" - should be only earned from "Camp work" event type
  * "Periods of validity" - set this to be 00:00 - 24:00 on Saturday and Sunday
  * "Force time earned during work rise to overtime" - if you for example want camp work to be compensated to work hour bank on weekends, set all of them to be "Hour to hour - Bank"


### Camp work event types
Also ensure the travel time, and camp event types are visible to the relevant users. You may also want to create a dedicated type for "Camp preparation / clearance" to record time setting up and clearing the camp in 
Worktime > Administration > Working community settings (or Setting groups > select Setting group > select Setting group settings) > Work hours > Event types
## How to record your hours during Camp work
  * Use "Travel time" to record your travel to and from the camp
  * Use "Camp preparation / clearance" to record the time it takes to set up and clear the camp if required
  * Use a continuous "Camp work" marking to record the rest of your time during the camp.


##

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Salary systems | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Salary-systems/5358790925853-CGI-Prima-salary-data-for-pricing.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/5358790925853-CGI-Prima-salary-data-for-pricing -->

# CGI Prima salary data for pricing

# File format
Transfer file is a delimited text file in CSV format where the fields are separated with a semicolon (;). Line break is CR+LF. Strings are not enclosed with quotation marks. Character encoding is ISO-8859-1. Header row is not generated in the file but instead data content starts from the first row. Decimal numbers use a dot (.) as decimal separator.
# File fields
Column | Field | Ruleset field name | Format | Description  
---|---|---|---|---  
1 | Social security number or personnel number | OverrideUserIntegrationId | string | By default Finnish social security number. Can be overridden with a ruleset.  
2 | Start date | OverrideStartDate | date | Format dd.mm.yyyy  
3 | End date | OverrideEndDate | date | Format dd.mm.yyyy  
4 | Salary code | OverrideSalaryCode | string | Mandatory, salary code in Prima. Fetched from settings.  
5 | Hours | OverrideAmount | string | Optional, format 5.2, e.g. 4.00, no leading zeros; if a salary type does not use units, empty in file. Can be overridden.  
6 | Multiplier | Multiplier | decimal | Optional, format 5.2, e.g. 4.00, no leading zeros; if a salary type does not use units, empty in file. Can be overridden.  
7 | Price per unit | PricePerUnit | decimal | Optional, e.g. 234.56, no leading zeros. Can be overridden.  
8 | Identifier | EmploymentIdentifier | string | Optional, unique identifier for service period. Can be overridden.  
9 | Account | Account | string | Optional, if transferred, should match Prima accounting, if accounting from service period and/or salary type for pricing can not be used. Can be overriden

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / Terminal administration | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/Terminal-administration/360002593558-Change-terminal-time-and-or-date.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002593558-Change-terminal-time-and-or-date -->

# Change terminal time and/or date

Please note that the instructions may differ slightly depending on the type of terminal, but in general the logic is the same in the devices. Please contact your organization’s administrator if you need further assistance.
In most cases, the reason for events being logged at strange times is an incorrect time on the terminal. This may be caused by Internet connection problems or summer / winter time changes for example.
The time and / or date of the terminal can be changed as follows:
**1\. To reset the device time, you must first exit the logging view.**
\- Check that the device is turned on.
\- Use your finger or stylus to firmly press each of the four corners of the device's touch screen once as close to the edge as possible **in this order** :  
upper left corner - upper right corner - lower right corner - lower left corner.  
\- The view should disappear, and you should now see the traditional Windows desktop view with different icons.
**2\. Changing time and date**
\- This step is easiest done by connecting a separate USB-connected mouse to the USB port on the device. You can also make configurations with your finger or with the stylus that comes with some devices (in small black device inside the back panel of the device, can be detached by pulling up).
\- Double-click the Windows icon at the bottom left of the desktop view and click Settings - Control panel - Date & time
\- You should now have a calendar view where you can change the date and time.
\- You can edit the date first. If the date is incorrect, click on the date / month / year and edit the values ​​correctly. Then click **Apply**.
-Next, you can edit the time. Select the correct time and click **Apply**.
\- Lastly, make sure you have the correct time zone. The time zone should be +2, Riga, Helsinki, etc (If you are in Finland). Make sure you click **Apply** after the correct time zone is selected.
\- Please consider when changing settings that, for example, the time and time zone cannot be adjusted at the same time, but you must first adjust another, then select Apply - Ok, and then return to change the other setting and save it again in the same way. We recommend that you check after each save that the previously changed value has remained correct.
\- When the settings look right, select Ok in the top corner and the settings are now saved. After that, please check one more time that the changes were saved correctly.
**3\. Returning to the logging view so that events can be logged again.**
\- Once the desired settings have been defined, the Terminal Launcher must be restarted so that events can be logged again.
-In the desktop view, you will find the Nepton Terminal Launcher icon, which you can double-click to launch the service. When the service is started, it may restart itself several times. This is normal and may take up to 10 minutes. Please give the device the time it needs to start and wait patiently.
\- In some device versions, Terminal Launcher is not on the desktop, but can be found in the folder “My device” on the desktop. Select Storage Card - Release - Work Capacity (double click) from the folder. The logging view opens automatically, and the device is ready to receive new entries. Again, the service may restart several times and it may take several minutes to start.

# Changing your password

## Changing your password when logged in
If needed a user can change their own password in **Employees** -section under **Own info** >**Personal information**.
The password can be changed at the bottom of the page.

1\. Enter your current password  
2\. Type in the new password

![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33235108678557)
## Ordering a new password
If you have forgotten your current password and can't log in, you can order a new password from your deployment's login page by clicking "**Forgot password** "-link.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33235108679453)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / Example APIs and method descriptions | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/Example-APIs-and-method-descriptions/6919474574237-ClearVisibleProjectsForUser.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6919474574237-ClearVisibleProjectsForUser -->

# ClearVisibleProjectsForUser

A newer version of this method exists. If you are currently using this method, we recommend that you will look at the instructions of the next method for changes required to update to the next version. You can find the instructions for the next version [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/36506225707677>)
## Interface overview
The web service allows you to remove all user-level project visibility from a specified person. This does not affect projects defined through a person group.
The WSDL schema of the web service is publicly available [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). The interfaces are described in general [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).
The occurrences column in the description determines whether a piece of information is mandatory in the call or not. Occurrences 0 means that the information in question does not need to be passed in the call. Occurrences 1 means that the information must appear once in the call. Occurrences 0..n means that the information in question can appear any number of times in the call. Occurrences 1..n means that the information in question must appear in the data at least once, but can appear more often.
## User identifiers
The target user can be identified by a unique Nepton ID, employee number, or a username. One of these must be provided. The service returns an error if no username has been specified or no user matching the identifier was found.
## Data to be sent
LEVEL | FIELD NAME | FORMAT | OCCURRENCES | DESCRIPTION  
---|---|---|---|---  
0 | ParametersForClearVisibleProjectsForUser | XML element |  | Root,  
below SOAP body  
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | Authentication details. See more [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019983978>).  
1 | ClearVisibleProjectsForUserList | XML element | 1 |   
2 | ClearVisibleProjectForUser | XML element | 1..n |   
3 | UserId | integer | 0..1 | Target user's Nepton ID.  
3 | PersonnelNumber | string | 0..1 | Target user's personnel number.  
3 | UserName | string | 0..1 | Target user's username.  
### Call example
[code]
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">
      <soapenv:Header/>
      <soapenv:Body>
        <tyo:ParametersForClearVisibleProjectsForUser>
          <CallerAuthentication /> <!-- Autentikointi vaaditaan, mutta on jätetty pois tästä esimerkistä -->
          <ClearVisibleProjectsForUserList>
            <ClearVisibleProjectForUser>
              <PersonnelNumber>54236</PersonnelNumber>
            </ClearVisibleProjectForUser>
          </ClearVisibleProjectsForUserList>
        </tyo:ParametersForClearVisibleProjectsForUser>
      </soapenv:Body>
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]

# ClearVisibleProjectsForUserV2

## Interface overview
The web service allows you to remove all user-level project visibility from a specified person. This does not affect projects defined through a person group.
The WSDL schema of the web service is publicly available [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). The interfaces are described in general [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).
The occurrences column in the description determines whether a piece of information is mandatory in the call or not. Occurrences 0 means that the information in question does not need to be passed in the call. Occurrences 1 means that the information must appear once in the call. Occurrences 0..n means that the information in question can appear any number of times in the call. Occurrences 1..n means that the information in question must appear in the data at least once, but can appear more often.
## Changes to previous version ([ClearVisibleProjectsForUser](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6919474574237>))
V2-version adds the following field
Field | Description  
---|---  
PersonExternalIdentifier | Allows identification of a person using an external identifier  
## User identifiers
The target user can be identified by a unique Nepton ID, employee number, external identifier, or a username. One of these must be provided. The service returns an error if no username has been specified or no user matching the identifier was found.
## Data to send
LEVEL | FIELD NAME | FORMAT | OCCURRENCES | DESCRIPTION  
---|---|---|---|---  
0 | ParametersForClearVisibleProjectsForUserV2 | XML element | 1 | Root, below SOAP body  
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | Authentication details, see more [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019983978>)  
1 | ClearVisibleProjectsForUserList | XML element | 1 |   
2 | ClearVisibleProjectForUser | XML element | 1..n |   
3 | UserId | integer | 0..1 | Target user's id  
3 | PersonnelNumber | string | 0..1 | Target user's personnel number  
3 | PersonExternalIdentifier | XML Element | 0..1 | NEW in V2 - Target user's external identifier  
4 | Identifier | string | 1 | Value of external identifier  
4 | FieldName | string | 1 |  Field name of external identifier. Supported values:
[code] 
    ExternalIdentifier1
[/code]

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / General information on integrations | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/General-information-on-integrations/360002489417-Common-principles-on-implementing-integrations.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002489417-Common-principles-on-implementing-integrations -->

# Common principles on implementing integrations

Integration refers to the method of transferring data either from Nepton to another system or from another system to Nepton. The available integration methods are:
[File-based SFTP transfer](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003762477>)
[Using an API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861518>)
The principle of file-based SFTP transfer is that the source system generates the data on a scheduled basis and uploads it to an SFTP server. The target system then retrieves and processes the data on a separate schedule. Typically, data is transferred during nighttime, with enough buffer time between generation and retrieval to ensure the source system has completed the file.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29108382197021)
The API integration is based on requests, where the external system calls Nepton’s API to obtain the desired information. The capabilities available via Nepton’s API are described in the following articles:
  * [Worktime API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>)
  * [HR API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004855857>)


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29108414553117)
File-based SFTP transfers are more schedule-oriented and often involve transferring a larger volume of data at once (e.g. importing new personnel and updating personal information). API integrations are used when data needs to be transferred quickly and made available in Nepton immediately (e.g. importing or exporting project data).
When implementing integrations, the following operational principles should be considered:
## Problem detection and resolution
[Potential issues should be anticipated and handled](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/9056347382813>) already during the integration implementation phase.
## Scheduling
Integrations operating through the SFTP server can be scheduled in Nepton. Learn more about:
  * [Scheduled task - Person import](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002489317>)
  * [Scheduled task - Person export](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002489357>)
  * [Scheduling worktime import/export integrations](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/10510800700573>)


Additionally, there are some near real-time integrations that run once per minute. These include integrations to phone exchange and presence systems such as:
  * [Elisa Ring (eIPKulva)](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004522538>)
  * [Mitel Aastra and Telia Merex](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360013422917>)


## Identification of the person being transferred
An employee number can be assigned to the individual, which is used in all transfers. If multiple identifiers are in use, a system-specific identifier can be set in the person's Employees-section. This identifier will be used for transfers related to that specific system.
The code '0' (zero) is a special code used to exclude the individual’s data from being transferred. This code should be used as the identifier only when the person's data or events are not to be transferred.
## Integration user
A dedicated user account that only executes transfers must be created in Nepton. This user is granted the required permissions for the integration tasks.
To transfer personnel data, the user must have administrator rights.
To transfer worktime data, the following additional permissions may be required (depending on the type of data):
For exporting data:  
Can view events of all personnel
For importing data:  
Can edit and approve all users events  
Can lock event dates  
Can unlock locked dates  
Can administer balances  
Can edit approved events  
Can view external identifier of events  
Can edit external identifier of events
For transferring project data:  
Can manage projects and project relations  
Can manage persons' settings and projects
For modifying person groups, setting groups or worktime roles:  
Can manage person groups  
Can manage person setting groups  
Can manage worktime roles

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/360007613717-Competencies.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007613717-Competencies -->

# Competencies

Adding and managing competency requirements in HR solutions and utilizing them in shift planning is only included in the Pro and Complete service levels.  
Competencies represent a person's capabilities and/or certifications that enable them to perform related work tasks.
  * For example, to work with a forklift truck, you would need the necessary certification and license to drive the forklift truck.
  * Although competencies can be used purely for HR data purposes, they can also be used in shift planning to ensure the most suitable staff are used. The "assign people to needs automatically" tool can also benefit from this.


## Creating a new competency
Competencies are configured in the **Employees** section. The Competency list shows a list of already added competencies in the service.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28026500002205)
To add a new competence, select **Add new competence** , enter a name and description for the competence, and press Save.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28026451572893)
**Competencies related** to each other indicate that if a person for example has a Truck driving license, he can also drive lighter vehicles, such as a car and a tractor.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28026451575069)
The **distance** between two competencies is a number that shows how desirable or practical it is for a person to perform tasks related to the other competency.
Competencies can be related to each other and tasks. Competencies can be used for more detailed scheduling of shifts using tasks, of which you can find more information in the [Tasks](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360010504757>) article.
**An example:** A Secretary's competencies might be related to both a Cleaning and a Shift planning competencies. However, the distance to Cleaning is much larger than to Shift planning, indicating that the Secretary can do Cleaning if necessary, but that it would be preferable for a person with this skill to do Shift planning instead.
A distance of zero indicates that the related competence is just as desirable as the one it is related to.
## Adding a competence to a person
Person's Competencies tab shows you a list of persons who have the specific competence in their details.
Competence can be added to a person either through competencies by searching for "Persons without competence " and then adding it to them.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28026451579805)
Alternatively, you can add competencies from the person's own information on the competencies tab (**Employees > Persons > Open the person's ID card from the magnifying glass image > Competencies**).
## Deleting a competence
A competence can be deleted in Additional actions tab.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28026500014621)

# Competitiveness Agreement

**Sorry!**
This article has not been translated yet. We will do that as soon as possible, please check back later.
Kilpailukykysopimuksia (kiky) aletaan pikkuhiljaa purkaa eri aloilla ja sopimuksen mukaiset työaikaan vaikuttavat säännöt voidaan poistaa palvelusta.
Voidaksesi poistaa säännöt, sinun tulee ensin tietää, miten kiky on työyhteisössänne toteutettu. Onko työpäivän pituutta lisätty 6 minuuttia, onko saldosta vähennetty 2 tuntia kerran kuussa vai jokin muu tapa.
## Esimerkkejä kiky-sääntöjen poistamisesta
Jos kiky toteutettiin työpäivän pituutta muuttamalla, katso alla olevista linkeistä ohjeet työpäivän ja työviikon pituuden muuttamiseksi. Muistathan tehdä muutokset voimassaolotoiminnon kautta käyttäen voimassa alkaen ja voimassa saakka kenttiä, ettei laskenta muutu takautuvasti.
Jos kiky toteutettiin ylimääräisillä työpäivillä, esim. lauantaitöillä, katso alta ohje, kuinka määrität työvelvoitteen juhlapyhille tai lauantaille. Näissä tapauksissa on mahdollista, että muutokset on tehty aina vasta ko. päivän varmistuttua ja että tarvetta muutoksiin ei ole.
Jos kiky toteutettiin saldon tai työaikapankin arvon muutoksella, ei sinulta edellytetä mitään toimenpiteitä. Näitä ei voi automatisoida, vaan ne on tehtävä aina manuaalisesti.
## Esimerkkejä kiky-sääntöjen lisäämisestä
Kilpailukykysopimuksen mukaisesti vuosittaista työaikaa pidennetään 24 tunnilla. Työajan pidennysten toteuttamistapa voi vaihdella työyhteisön mukaan. Kerromme tässä vaihtoehtoisia tapoja toteuttaa muutokset Nepton-palvelussa.
## Työpäivän ja työviikon pituuden muutos
Jotta vuosittainen työaika pitenisi 24 tunnilla, tulee jokaisen viikon työaikaa pidentää 30 minuuttia eli 6 minuuttia päivässä, mikäli työntekijä työskentelee viitenä päivänä viikossa. Mikäli päivittäinen työaika on aikaisemmin ollut esimerkiksi 7h 30 minuuttia, on se muutoksen jälkeen 7h 36 minuuttia.  
  
Mikäli päivittäinen työaika pitenee 7h 30 minuutista 7h 36 minuuttiin, pitenee näin ollen myös viikottainen työaika 37h 30 minuutista 38 tuntiin.  
  
[Katso tästä ohje työpäivän pituuden muuttamiseksi](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002558417>)  
[Katso tästä ohje työviikon pituuden muuttamiseksi](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002558537>)  
  
Muutos tulee tehdä joko Työyhteisön tai kaikkien niiden asetusryhmien asetuksissa, joissa on määritetty jotakin ylemmästä asetusryhmästä poikkeavaa työpäivän tai työviikon pituuden osalta. Esimerkiksi osa-aikaisten asetusryhmälle tulee aina määrittää työpäivän pituus, jotta työajan laskenta toimisi oikein. Muutosten tekemisen laajuus riippuu siitä, miten työyhteisön asetukset on perustettu ja millä tasoilla työpäivän ja työviikon pituus on määritetty.  
  
[Katso tästä ohje asetusten hierarkiasta ja periytymisestä Nepton-palvelussa](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002559178>)
## Muutoksen tekeminen saldon muutoksella
Mikäli työyhteisöllä on käytössä saldolaskenta, muutos voidaan tehdä myös vähentämällä tuntimäärä työntekijän työaikasaldosta. Tunnit voidaan vähentää kertaluontoisesti sovittuna ajankohtana vuosittain tai esimerkiksi kuukausittain pienemmissä erissä vuoden aikana.
Huomioittehan ympäristössänne mahdollisesti määritetyt saldorajat!
[Katso tästä tarkempi ohje saldomuutoksen tekemisestä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002481797>)
## Muutoksen tekeminen työaikapankin arvon muutoksella
Niissä työyhteisöissä, joilla on käytössä työaikapankki, muutos voidaan toteuttaa myös työaikapankin arvon muutoksella. Tällöin tuntimäärä vähennetään työntekijän työaikapankin saldosta sovittuna ajankohtana.  
  
[Katso tarkempi ohje työaikapankin arvon muutoksen tekemisestä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002485598>)
## Työvelvoitteen määrittäminen juhlapyhille tai lauantaille
Työajan pidentäminen voidaan toteuttaa myös kokonaisina työpäivinä, jolloin järjestelmään määritetään työvelvoite aikaisemmin juhlapyhäksi määritetylle päivälle kuten esimerkiksi loppiaiselle tai helatorstaille, tai vaihtoehtoisesti jollekin tietylle yrityksessä sovitulle lauantaipäivälle vaikka se ei normaalisti ole työpäivä.  
  
  
[Katso tästä tarkempi ohje juhlapyhien asetusten käsittelystä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002558797>)  
[Katso tästä tarkempi ohje työvelvoitteen määrittämiseksi lauantaipäivälle](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002560737>)

# Configure a custom email server for Nepton (SMTP)

Palvelussa voidaan määritellä palvelusta lähetettävien sähköpostiviestien lähettämiseen mukautettu sähköpostipalvelin. Nepton käyttää oletuksena Mailjet-sähköpostipalvelinta. Jos haluatte muokata käytettäväksi sähköpostipalvelimeksi mukautetun palvelimen, on siitä esimerkiksi seuraavat hyödyt:

IP-osoite tai sähköpostipalvelimen nimi (esimerkiksi smtp-mail.outlook.com)
  * Portti


Portin numero. Jos kenttä jätetään tyhjäksi, käytetään arvoa 25.
  * Käytä (SSL) salattua yhteyttä


Suosittelemme aina käyttämään salattua yhteyttä kaikille sähköposteille.

Salasana, määritellään palveluntarjoajan asetuksissa
  * Testaa lähetysasetusten toimivuus

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Login / Single Sign-on (SSO) / SAML Login | path: en-gb/Support/Login/Single-Sign-on-SSO/SAML-Login/360005242897-Configure-ADFS-server.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005242897-Configure-ADFS-server -->

# Configure ADFS server

Below are detailed technical instructions for configuration of a customers' ADFS server (Active Directory Federation Services) for SAML based SSO (Single Sign On) with the Nepton platform. These instructions are intended for individuals with experience in the area of ADFS server.
Please see other articles under the [Configuring SSO](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590097>) section for more information on the topic of SSO configuration.
Nepton SP (Service Provider) metadata can be found here:
<https://go.nepton.com/externallogin/metadata/EntityDescriptor_SP_go.nepton.com_V7_27_Apr_2025_26_Apr_2026.xml>
## Configure the Relying Party Trust (Service Provider)
choose one of the two options below:
### Import data online or on a local network 
  * Login to the ADFS server and open the management console.
  * Right-click on "Relying Party Trusts" under "Trust Relationships" > Add Relying Party Trust... > Start
  * Select "Import data about the relying party published online or on a local network"
  * Enter: 
    * https://go.nepton.com/externallogin/metadata/EntityDescriptor_SP_go.nepton.com_V7_27_Apr_2025_26_Apr_2026.xml
  * Next
  * Enter a Display Name, eg: "go.nepton.com" > Next
  * Click Next to skip the Multi-factor Authentication
  * Select "Permit all users to access this relying party" (you can change this later) > Next
  * Click Next to continue
  * Uncheck "Open the claim rules dialog..." > Close
  * Right-click the new trust you just created > Properties
  * Advanced tab > Choose the desired algorithm, which will be set up also in Nepton
  * Click OK 


### Enter data manually
  * Login to the ADFS server and open the management console.
  * Right-click on "Relying Party Trusts" under "Trust Relationships" > Add Relying Party Trust... > Start
  * Select "Enter data about the relying party manually" > Next
  * Enter a Display Name, eg: "go.nepton.com" > Next
  * Click "AD FS 2 (or 3)" profile > Next
  * Click Next to skip the Token encryption certificate
  * Click Next to skip the Configure URL section
  * Enter following as the "Relying party trust identifier" 
    * **https://go.nepton.com/ExternalLogin/Saml**
  * Add > Next
  * Click Next to skip the Multi-factor Authentication
  * Select "Permit all users to access this relying party" (you can change this later) > Next
  * Click Next to skip
  * Uncheck "Open the claim rules dialog..." > Close
  * Right-click the new trust you just created > Properties 
    * Monitoring tab 
      * Enter following as Relying party's metadata URL 
        * <https://go.nepton.com/externallogin/metadata/EntityDescriptor_SP_go.nepton.com_V7_27_Apr_2025_26_Apr_2026.xml>
        * Add > Next
      * Check "Monitor Relying Party"
      * Check "Automatically update relying party"
    * Advanced tab > Choose the correct algorithm and **send the hash algorithm to Nepton**
    * Enter following on Endpoints tab > **SAML Assertion Consumer** , with **POST** binding 
      * **https://go.nepton.com/ExternalLogin/Saml2Consumer.aspx**
    * Click OK


## Ensure required certificates are set up
  1. Login to the ADFS server and open the management console.
  2. Ensure you have the **VRK Gov. Root CA - G2 **and **VRK CA for Service Providers - G4** Certificates installed in the Trusted Intermediate & Trusted Root stores. These certificates are available from <https://dvv.fi/en/ca-certificates>
  3. Import the go.nepton.com certificate 
     1. Right-click the Relying Party > Update from Federation Metadata 
        1. If this doesn't work, please check if you can from ADFS server access the metadata URL. If this is blocked, you might need to open the firewall accordingly.
     2. Verify the certificate's path is valid in the "Certificate Path" tab under the certificate's properties.
  4. Configuring the Claim Rules 
     1. Right-click the new trust you just created > Edit Claim Rules...
     2. Add Rule > **Send LDAP Attributes as Claims** > Next 
        1. Claim rule name > enter "Get LDAP Attributes"
        2. Attribute store > select Active Directory
        3. LDAP Attribute > Email Addresses
        4. Outgoing Claim Type > Email Address
        5. Finish
     3. Add Rule > **Transform an incoming claim** > Next 
        1. Claim rule name > enter "Convert Email to Name Id"
        2. Incoming claim type > Email Address
        3. Outgoing claim type > Name ID
        4. Outgoing Name ID format > Transient Identifier
        5. Finish
     4. Apply > OK


## Collect the Token-Signing Certificate
  * Login to the ADFS server and open the management console
  * Browse to Service > Certificates > Right-click the Token-Signing Certificate > View Certificate > Details Tab > Copy to File > Next 
    * Click "No, do not export the private key" > Next
    * Select "Base-64 encoded X.509" > Next
    * Pick a location to save the file > Next > Finish
    * You will need the certificate file on next step


## Creating the settings in Nepton
  * Add the SSO settings and certificate to Nepton. Guidance can be seen [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590097>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Login / Single Sign-on (SSO) / SAML Login | path: en-gb/Support/Login/Single-Sign-on-SSO/SAML-Login/23063634766493-Configure-Entra-ID-service.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/23063634766493-Configure-Entra-ID-service -->

# Configure Entra ID service

This approach should only be used if you can't use the recommended [Microsoft Login](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590137>) method.
Below are detailed technical instructions for configuration of a customers' Entra ID service for SAML based SSO (Single Sign On) with the Nepton platform. These instructions are intended for individuals with experience in the Entra ID service.
Please see other articles under the [Configuring SSO](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590097>) section for more information on the topic of SSO configuration.
## Entra ID configuration
1) Nepton SP (Service Provider) metadata can be found from the link below. Download this XML file and save it to your computer.
<https://go.nepton.com/externallogin/metadata/EntityDescriptor_SP_go.nepton.com_V7_27_Apr_2025_26_Apr_2026.xml>
2) Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center with your admin credentials.
3) Go to Identity, Applications, Enterprise Applications, New application, Create your own application
4) Add a new application called "SSO Nepton SAML 2". Select the "Integrate any other application you don't find in the gallery (Non-gallery)". Click Create.
5) Go the "SSO Nepton SAML 2" application. Select Manage, Single-sign-on, and select the SAML method. In the "Set up Single Sign-On with SAML" select "Upload metadata file" and upload the the XML file you downloaded in step 1. Review settings. Save.
6) Copy following values to notepad:
  * App Federation Metadata Url
  * Login URL
  * Microsoft Entra Identififier


7) Go the "SSO Nepton SAML 2" application. Select Manage, Properties, and check that "Assignment required" is set to "No". Click Save.
## Nepton configuration
8) Sign in to Nepton with your admin credentials
9) Go the Employees, Administration, Single Sign-On (SSO)
10) Click "Add" to create new SSO
  * Management: manual
  * Entity Id: The "Microsoft Entra Identifier" value you copied to notepad in step 6
  * Sign on service Url: he "Login Url" value you copied to notepad in step 6
  * Sign on service url binding: HTTP-POST
  * Certificate hash-algorithm: SHA-256
  * Name id format: unspecified
  * Use NameId for person identification: Yes
  * Identify person by: Email


11) Save
12) Find the "App Federation Metadata URL" address you copied to notepad in step 6. Open this address. Look at the long text string between ds:X509Certificate tags and copy this long text string to notepad. Add the missing certificate (this long text string) to Nepton and save it.
