<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Setting exceptions | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Setting-exceptions/360005052857-Day-level-worktime-exception.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005052857-Day-level-worktime-exception -->

# Day level worktime exception

Daily exception settings in mass can be defined using [this guide](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560817>).
It is possible to set a daily exception for some worktime settings in**Events in calendar** and **Events in table** views. Without exceptions, the service uses settings inherited from the Working community settings and Setting group settings. The set exception overrides other definitions related to that setting. A daily exception can be used, for example, when an agreement has been made with an employee for an interpretation of working hours that differs from the norm for one day.
The current settings ([length of the workday](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>), [length of the workweek](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558537>), [permitted work times](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558597>), [expected work times](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558617>), and daily exceptions) can be viewed by selecting the desired date from the person’s calendar. The settings and their editing options that a person sees depend on their [work](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554338>)[time role](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554338>).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/21154811510813)
A daily exception can be set by selecting the specific setting and assigning it the desired value. The set exception applies only to the person and the day for which the change is made. Daily exceptions do not appear in the setting group or work community settings. After setting the change, the active change is displayed on the info board by selecting the date of the respective day from the calendar.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/21675877652765)
Please note, if the permitted work times come from Shift Planning and there is a day level exception set that overlaps with it, the day level exception will not be considered.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event types and absence types | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-types-and-absence-types/360002558717-Default-event-types-and-assumed-event-types.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558717-Default-event-types-and-assumed-event-types -->

# Default event types and assumed event types

The service can be used to define what kind of assumed, i.e. automatic, events are created in different situations.
Default event types can be defined in the Work Time section in either the Working Community Settings or Setting Groups level settings in **Work time > Administration > Working community / Setting group settings > Work hours > Event types. **The configuration can also be done at person level (**Work Time > Administration > Persons**). However, we do not recommend making configurations on person level, as managing them is challenging.
Configurations can be made for two different functions:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32927233128349)
**1\. Default event type when creating a new event**  
Specifies which event type is displayed by default when a new event is recorded. If this settings has not been set, the default event type is Work. This default event type is also mobile quick start event type in addition to the Lunch Break. Read [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360009193677-How-to-edit-mobile-start-page->) for more instructions on how to customize your mobile view quick start.
**2\. Assumed event type on empty work days**  
Defines which event type is created in the person's worktime calendar on days, when the person has a work obligation (length of working day) but the person has not recorded any events. NOTE: The assumed event type can't be automatically formed on public holidays, even if the day has work obligation. The automatic event is created with start and end times defined in the [Rendering Options](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360008777997>). If nothing is specified in the rendering options, an automatic event will occur between 8:00 and 16:00.
The assumed event type on empty business days can be used in the following situations, for example:
  * Individuals who do the same task at the same time every day. In this case, the person does not have to make entries manually, but they are automatically added to the person's calendar.
  * Individuals whose work time isn't monitored, but all work done needs to be reported.
  * Individuals who work part-time in such a way that they have full-day absences during the week and the day of absence varies. In this case, it can be set that an 'Part-time off' event, for example, is added to the days not worked automatically. More about part-time options [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559018>).


In case a different assumed event type is needed for certain days, an exceptional setting can made:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32927171527453)
In this example. on Saturdays and Sundays Remote Work is the assumed event type. More about exceptional entries [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560618>). NOTE: The assumed event types can't be automatically formed on public holidays, not even using exceptional settings.
It is also possible to use planned work shift as the base for default event type:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32927233133469)
In this case, the default event is created with work shift begin and end times and the planned event type is used as the event type. Setting exceptions can also be used to specify that the assumed event type only comes from certain types of shifts. The determination can be made based on the shift alias or the planned event type.
If the **Assumed Event Type on empty work days** is set from the start of a person's work contract, some sort of entry must be made in the calendar (such as work or balance reset) to start the calculations. In other words, if you want the assumed event type on empty working days to be valid from 15.5.2024, you can for example, enter work from 08:00 to 08:00, and the default event types are now entered for empty work days, from this day onwards.
We recommend that you perform all configurations in all situations through the [validity control function](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358-Using-the-validity-control-in-Worktime>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Setting groups / Examples for setting up setting groups / Leveling period | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Setting-groups/Examples-for-setting-up-setting-groups/Leveling-period/14849123960989-Defining-levelling-period-for-part-timers.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/14849123960989-Defining-levelling-period-for-part-timers -->

# Defining levelling period for part-timers

Levelling periods can be configured to consider the worktime percentage of part-time employees. This scales the additional work-earning threshold according to the set percentage. It can be defined in settings at Worktime > Settings > Work hours > Leveling period:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/14870728392861)
For example, if an employee is a part-timer with a 60% worktime percentage and the limits of the one-week levelling period in settings are as follows:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/14870748814237)
The limits of the employee's entire period would be as follows:
  * Maximum working hours: 22.5 hours
  * Maximum additional work: 17.5 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime: 10 hours


If worktime percentage is not used to calculate additional work earning threshold, the limits for the entire period would be as follows:
  * Maximum working hours: 37.5 hours
  * Maximum additional work: 2.5 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime: 10 hours


## Differentiating additional work between 0% and TES additional work rise percentage
Service can be configured to differentiate calculation of additional work so that 0% additional work is earned until full-time obligation is reached and after that additional work is earned based on TES additional work rise percentage. This is achieved by defining both "Use work time percentage to calculate additional work earning threshold" and "Part-time workers should earn additional work 0% under their full-time threshold"-settings to be set as "Yes".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/17293510458909)
Example: In a two week levelling period, additional work is earned after 72 hours. A part-time workers work time percentage is 60%. Part-time worker starts to earn additional work after 48 hours, and will earn 0% additional work until 72 hours, the threshold for full-time workers additional work. So for example if part-time workers maximum working hours in the period are 45 hours and they have worked 79 hours during the levelling period, they will earn 30 hours worth of 0% additional work and 4 hours of additional work with their TES additional work rise percentage, as they have worked for 4 hours after fulfilling full-time workers additional work threshold, i.e. 79 h - (45h +30h) = 4h.
## Defining the amount of reduction from absences
Absences shorten the maximum work hours of the levelling period depending on the work obligation on the days of absence.
For example, if the length of the work day (Mon-Fri) is set to 7:30, with a 60% working time percentage, absences would reduce the maximum work hours by 4.5 hours on weekdays.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/14870748814621)
If you want to define which three days are absence days in the week, you can do so by setting work day length exceptions to the days.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/14870728393885)
## Defining the amount of reduction from public holidays
As with absences, public holidays shorten the levelling period according to the worktime percentage. So, for example, with a worktime percentage of 60%, a public holiday would shorten the maximum work hours of the levelling period by 4.5 hours.
You can also define how much holiday shortens the levelling period by setting work day length exception for the day.

# Defining subordinate

Adding or replacing a subordinate for a user requires certain types of [roles](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002425637>) from the administrator.
You can add a subordinate to a user through the person's information card in the **Employees** section. A person may have several subordinates.
In order to add a subordinate, the subordinate must have an Employee Number.
A subordinate can be assigned to an employee as follows:
Open the **Employees** section and choose Persons -> **Persons**.  
Open the desired person's information from the magnifying glass.  
From the menu, select **Organization > Subordinates > Add**. Start typing the name of the subordinate in the opening box and select the desired person as the subordinate from the results.
You can add more than one subordinate to a person.
Once you have selected the subordinates, select **Done**.  
Always remember to save the changes from the **Save** button at the bottom of the page.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29074913271837)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002558417-Defining-the-length-of-work-day.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417-Defining-the-length-of-work-day -->

# Defining the length of work day

The length of the work day can be set in Worktime section either in Working community or Setting group level. The settings can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Working community / Setting group settings > Workhours > Length of work day.**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34553925403037)
## Set length of work day
The length of the workday is defined by each weekday separately. If you do not want to specify the length of the workday for the day (for example, in situations where a person never works on Saturdays), you can leave the setting empty for that day.
It is recommended to set the length of the working day via the validity function (small calendar button next to the setting). This allows you to set the Valid from and Valid until dates.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34553927759517)  
If this is the first time setting the workday length, it can be set without start date (always valid) or from wanted date onwards.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34553927762589)
If an existing value is to be changed, you must first end the old value by setting the date to Valid to -field. To add a new value, click Add setting value. The new value automatically takes effect on the day following the end of the previous value. In this way, the changes do not affect the past worktime calculations.
If you want to set an exception to the length of the working day, for example a shorter day than usually on New Year's Eve, you need to add a setting exception for that day. More detailed instructions and examples can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560677>).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34553925411485)
A workday length exception setting can also be set by [mass entering](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560837>).
## Planned shift determines the length of the workday
The Planned event types that override workday length setting allows you to specify that the planned shift determines the workday length on days when a shift is planned for the day. This setting can be set at the Working Community level in the menu **Work time > Administration > Working Community Settings > Shifts.** If the workday length comes from the planned shift, there is no need to specify the length of day in the setting group.
## Day-level exception also sets maximum work day length
The setting "Day-level exception also sets maximum work day length" can be used to determine whether the daily TES maximum work time changes in a situation where an exception has been made to the length of a person's working day in the calendar view for one day. If the setting is "yes", the TES maximum working time changes by the amount of the exception made.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002558537-Defining-the-length-of-work-week.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558537-Defining-the-length-of-work-week -->

# Defining the length of work week

The length of the work week can be defined in the Worktime section in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings / Setting group settings > Work hours > TES.**
If the length of the working week is not specified at all in the setting ‘TES work week length’, the default value is 0.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33384068995869)  
  
The length of the work week is defined in settings **TES work week length** / **TES work week length is based on the duration of planned shifts** and **TES maximum hours of work per week / TES maximum hours of work per week are based on the duration of planned shifts**. 
The length of the work week is defined as either a fixed amount or it is based on the duration of planned work shifts. Only one of these settings should be used at a time. If both settings have a valid value, the setting "TES maximum hours of work per week are based on the duration of planned shifts" overrides the fixed value set in the setting "TES maximum hours of work per week".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33384040766877)
TES maximum hours of work per week are defined in the settings under the workweek. The fixed TES maximum hours of work per week is often greater than the length of the workweek, in which case the difference between the two is formed as additional work, unless otherwise specified in the settings. TES maximum hours of work per week can also be formed by planned work shifts, in which case this setting overrides any fixed value that may have been set.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33384069000733)
It is recommended to use the [validity tool](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358>) when defining the length of work week.  
  
Please also check if you need to make any changes to the [length of work day](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>) settings.
### Setting an exception to work week length in calendar view
An exception to the length of the work week can be set directly in the person's calendar for one week at a time. An exception made in calendar always overrules a setting coming from setting group, regardless if the setting says the work week length is fixed or is formed by planned shifts.
In the person's calendar, press the date for the week which length you want to change. The date button opens a separate pop-up window, where one of the options is the length of the work week. By pressing that, you can set an exception to the length of the work week.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33384040772253)
Set the exceptional length and press 'Save':
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33384069008541)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360007557338-Defining-Work-week-starting-time.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007557338-Defining-Work-week-starting-time -->

# Defining Work week starting time

Work week starting time can be defined in Nepton. Work week starting time affects [work rises](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560978>), [Weekly rest time compensation](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007389978-Weekly-rest-time-compensation>) and how overtime is calculated.
Setting can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings / Setting groups > Work hours > TES**
**Work week starting day –** setting defines, what day starts the week. If no value is set, the default is Monday.
**Work week starting time** – setting defines, what time the work week begins. It also defines what time the day changes to next. 
**![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20998076555037)**  
If work week starting time is set to ‘00:00’ the work week and each day of the work week starts always at 00:00. Then also each day is considered to start at 00:00 and finishes at 24:00.
Monday 00:00 – 24:00
Tuesday 00:00 – 24:00
Wednesday 00:00 – 24:00
Thursday 00:00 – 24:00
Friday 00:00 – 24:00
Saturday 00:00 – 24:00
Sunday 00:00 – 24:00
= 1 week
If work week starting time is set to '07:00', the calculation is considered as follows:
Monday 07:00 – 07:00 (at Tuesday morning)
Tuesday 07:00 – 07:00 (at Wednesday morning)
Wednesday 07:00 – 07:00 (at Thursday morning)
Thursday 07:00 – 07:00 (at Friday morning)
Friday 07:00 – 07:00 (at Saturday morning)
Saturday 07:00 – 07:00 (at Sunday morning)
Sunday 07:00 – 07:00 (at Monday morning)
Depending on if day starts before or after the noon (12:00), also affects to the **Work week/day starting time.**
If your work week starts on Sunday at 22:00 for example, then:
  * Your first day of the week is MONDAY/next day (because the start time is after noon), but your Monday starts at 22:00 on SUNDAY and finishes on Monday 22:00.
  * The second day of the week is Tuesday but starts on Monday at 22:00 and ends on Tuesday at 22:00. And so on…
  * So, shifts starting on Sunday at 23:00 will display on Monday and calculated as a Monday shift and the week just starting.
  * Shifts starting before 22:00 on the Sunday will display on Sunday and calculated as a Sunday shift for the week just ending.


If your work week starts on Sunday at 04:00 then:
  * Your first day of the week is SUNDAY/same day (because the start time is before noon) and is from Sunday 04:00 to Monday 04:00.
  * Your second day of the week is Monday, starting from Monday 04:00 to Tuesday 04:0 And so on…
  * So, shifts starting on Sunday before 04:00 will be displayed and calculated as Saturday shifts for the week ending.
  * Shifts starting on Sunday after 04:00 will be displayed and calculated as Sunday shifts for the week starting.
  * Shifts starting on Monday before 4AM will be displayed and calculated as Sunday shifts.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management / Person details management | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/Person-details-management/360002424617-Delete-person.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002424617-Delete-person -->

# Delete person

Please note that deleting (and restoring) persons is only possible with 'Administrator',  
'HR management' and 'Salary management' roles.  
It is recommended to delete a person when an employee's working contract has ended. Separate instructions on what steps to take when an employment relationship ends can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575438>).
Deleting the person does not delete any information saved for the person, or persons events or interpretation. When person is deleted they no longer can log into the service.
A person can be removed from users as follows:
  1. In the Employment section, go to the list of persons.
  2. Open the person card of the person you want to remove by clicking on the magnifying glass next to the person’s name.
  3. On the Person's Information tab, add the employment end date.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33247383521565)
Then delete the RFID tag and the PIN code if they are in use:  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33247388556189)
4\. Save the changes at the bottom of the page.  
5\. Move to additional functions tab and delete the username from Remove-button.   
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33247383523997)  
6\. After removal you will be redirected to the person's information page. At the top of the page you will see a notification confirming that the username has been deleted. There is also a Restore-button.  
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4412315743505)
If only the employment end date is added, the person will still be able to log in to the service.
Please note that removing a user in the Employment section does not completely delete the person or the events stored for them. For example, the person appears in reports and in the calendar view if you are looking at a time period in when the person has been active. Always remember to mark the start and end dates of employment to all users.
Deleted person can be [restored](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002424957>).
## A total removal of person's information
Individuals, all their data on the Employees side and worktime records can be permanently deleted from the service by Nepton's product development team. In this case, all information about individuals in Nepton's database will be deleted in accordance with GDPR requirements and the information in question can no longer be restored. We ask our customers to contact Nepton's customer service to perform a complete deletion of individuals. In connection with the deletion request, we ask you to submit a list of individuals to be deleted and the desired deletion time. It is the customer's own responsibility to recover the necessary information before performing a complete deletion.

# Deleting settings group

Settings groups can also be deleted. If a person’s settings group is deleted, the person’s calculations for the entire period they were in the deleted settings group will be removed.
We always recommend creating a new settings group and then, instead of deleting, modifying the name of the settings group, e.g., ‘Hourly Workers’ -> ‘Hourly Workers NOT IN USE’. This way, the person’s calculations will also be preserved in the past. You can find instructions for modifying the settings group [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558758-Edit-the-name-code-and-description-of-a-setting-group>).
A settings group can be deleted as follows: Select **Worktime > Administration > Setting groups > Setting Groups: Group to be deleted > Delete Settings Group **
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/21132039022109)  
The service will confirm if you are sure. Select **Yes**. The service will then confirm the deletion of the settings group.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/21132039026589)

# Deprecated ruleset examples

**Sorry!**
This article has not been translated yet.
# Varallaolo vähennettynä varallaoloaikana tehdyllä työllä
[code] 
    SELECT OnCall.*, OnCall.SumAmount, - IFNULL(OnCallWork.SumAmount, 0) AS OverrideAmount,
    substring_part(Oncall.ActivityTypeCode, '/', 2) AS OverrideSalaryCode
    
    FROM (SELECT *, SUM(Amount) SumAmount 
    FROM UserSalaryData
    WHERE CompensationType = 'MarkedTime'AND BasePartTarget IS NULL AND ActivityTypeCode = '33'GROUP BY SalaryRenderingDate) 
    OnCall
    
    LEFT JOIN (SELECT *, SUM(Amount) SumAmount
    
    FROM UserSalaryData
    WHERE ActivityTypeCode IN ('1') -- jatka tähän listaan ne kaikki tapahtumat joiden päällekkäisyys vähennetään varallaolona poimittavasta arvosta  
    AND 
    (OverlapsUnderlyingActivityTypeIds LIKE '%,33,%' OR OverlapsUnderlyingActivityTypeIds LIKE '%,VARA%,%')
    AND CompensationType IN ('BasicTime', 'AdditionalWork', 'OvertimeDaily50', 
    'OvertimeDaily100','OvertimeWeekly50', 'OvertimeWeekly100', 'OvertimeSunday50', 
    'OvertimeSunday100')
    GROUPBY SalaryRenderingDate) 
    OnCallWork 
    
    ON (OnCallWork.SalaryRenderingDate = OnCall.SalaryRenderingDate)
    
    GROUPBY OverrideSalaryCode, Oncall.SalaryRenderingDate, Oncall.ProjectCode1, Oncall.ProjectCode2, Oncall.ProjectCode3,
    Oncall.ProjectCode4, Oncall.ProjectCode5, Oncall.ProjectCode6, Oncall.Comment
[/code]
Yllä olevaa mallia suositeltiin aiemmin käytettäväksi varallaoloaikojen laskemiseen palkkaliittymissä. Mallissa vähennetään varallaoloaika-tapahtuman kestosta tietyt tapahtumat, jotka on kirjattu sen päälle.
Tällainen laskenta lisättiin myöhemmin osaksi järjestelmää (tarkemmat tiedot [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/8040695057821>)).
Mallin mukainen kysely toimii edelleen mutta mikäli haluat käyttää järjestelmän sisäistä laskentaa ja asettaa sen arvot esille kalenterinäkymään on vahvasti suositeltavaa, että palkkaliittymiin välitetään sama arvo sen sijaan että se lasketaan erikseen sääntöjoukossa. UserSalaryData taulu sisältää nyt erilliset rivit varallaoloajalle kts. päivitetty esimerkki [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360008045337-S%C3%A4%C3%A4nt%C3%B6joukon-mallit-palkkaliittym%C3%A4#360008045337-toc-13>)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / General information on integrations | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/General-information-on-integrations/9056347382813-Detecting-and-resolving-integration-problems.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/9056347382813-Detecting-and-resolving-integration-problems -->

# Detecting and resolving integration problems

When integrating with Nepton, ensure that possible problems will be detected and resolved. This is especially important when integration is synchronizing data between external system and Nepton by sending only the changes in the data instead of sending all the data including non-changed data periodically. In these types of integrations, the data will get out of sync potentially permanently unless the potential problems are detected and resolved.  
To ensure this we recommend to:
  1. Identify and agree the ways potential problems will be detected.
  2. Agree how to resolve the detected problems.


To help with these goals Nepton provides tooling and related process examples. These tools are:
  * [Service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002575478>)
    * Logs detected integration related problems
  * Nepton API responses 
    * Contains information about problems API call encounter 
      * [HR API result codes](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406446686609>)
      * [Worktime API result codes](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019841477>)


## Using service log in integration problem handling
Integration related problems detected by Nepton can be found in the service log. Here are some examples of how service log can be used in process of detecting and resolving the integration problems.
### Example 1
  1. Customer detects an integration problem during regular routine service log check.
  2. Log details tell that there is a problem in the integration file content sent nightly to Nepton, so the customer fixes the data in the HR system where the data is being sent from.
  3. The corrected data will be sent to Nepton automatically the next night.


### Example 2
  1. Customer detects an integration problem during regular routine service log check.
  2. Log details show that one of the calls to Nepton API adding a new project failed because of a missing project name.
  3. The customer asks the person responsible for the project to fill in the project name and save the changes to get the changes re-sent to Nepton.


## Using API call results in integration problem handling
The Nepton API call responses tells the caller if the API call was successful. If the call was not successful, the response describes what the detected problems were.
### Ensuring data doesn't get out of sync
On integrations implemented using Nepton API it is more common to sync only the changes in the data between Nepton and external system. In these cases, if problems occur, to avoid the systems getting out of sync it is important to ensure there is a way to re-send the data. Examples of ways to ensure data can be synchronized after possible API call fail:
  * Resaving the data in originating system to trigger resending of data
  * Capability of triggering a resynching of all the data including unchanged data
  * Periodical scheduled resynching of all the data including unchanged data


Here is an example of how API call response can be used in the process of detecting and resolving potential integration problems.
  1. The sending system gets a response from Nepton API that tells that adding a project to Nepton failed.
  2. The sending system informs designated person at customer about the problem by email containing the problem details from the API response.
  3. The person who got the email instructs how to correct projects details causing the problem and resave the changes to get the changes re-sent to Nepton.


It is also good to notice that the failed API calls are also shown in the [Service log.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002575478>)
Additional info:
[HR API result codes](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406446686609>)
[Worktime API result codes](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019841477>)
## Integration problem handling using other methods
In addition to the integration problem detection Nepton can offer by provided tooling, it is important to notice that often additional integration problem detection is needed. For example:
  * In case external system fails on connecting Nepton API for a reason or another, Nepton can't know about the failed API call attempt
  * In case there are problems on creating the data to be transferred to Nepton, Nepton can't be aware of the problems

# Digia Enterprise

Nepton can be configured to export payroll data interpreted from recorded events, in a format the Digia Enterprise system can understand. It is possible to request this as a downloadable file or to schedule and send the information to a Digia Enterprise end-point automatically.
## Setup instructions
**1\. Set person identifiers (Employee number)**
Data in the export is identified by a person's Employee number. Employee numbers can be set by editing persons' information in Employees > Person's information view, under the Identifiers heading.
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360008596217/mceclip0.png)
**2\. Create an integration ruleset**
An integration ruleset must be configured in order to export the data. You can read more about what an integration ruleset is, and how to define one [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002489257>).
## File format
The used file format is text data where columns separated by a space. Row separator is `CR` & `LF` and character encoding is UTF-8.
The column types are formatted as follows:
  * **String (Text)** \- Enclosed within double-quote characters (`"`), even when a string is empty (e.g.`""`). Double-quote characters in these strings are escaped with double-quote character (e.g.`"She said """hello world""" out loud"`)
  * **Integer (Whole number)** \- Without enclosing. Empty values are exported as a zero (`0`)
  * **Decimal** \- Without enclosing, with a precision of two decimal places. The decimal separator is a comma character (`,`). Empty value is exported as a zero (`0`)
  * **Date** \- Without enclosing, format `DD-MM-YYYY`. If empty, it is exported as a question mark character (`?`). E.g. the date 31.1.2019 would be formatted as 01-31-2019


## Limitations
Persons with Employee number "0" (zero) will not be included in the export data.
## Data columns
Column | Field | Format | Notes  
---|---|---|---  
A | Salary pay group | string | Empty as default string, can be overridden with rule field `DigiaEnterpriseSalPayGrp`  
B | Salary period | integer |  `0` as default, can be overridden with rule field `DigiaEnterpriseSalPeriod`  
C | Personnel number | integer | Person's personnel number. Can be overridden with rule field `OverrideUserIntegrationId`  
D | Salary type | string | Salary type code  
E | Time quantity | decimal | Hours as decimal when the row unit type is seconds or hours. Can be overridden with rule field `OverrideHourAmount`. When overridden, the amount will be shown regardless of the row unit type.  
F | Time quantity unit | string | If the row unit type is seconds or hours, the default value is `H`, otherwise, the default value is an empty string. Can be overridden with rule field `DigiaEnterpriseTimeUnit`  
G | Unit price | decimal |  `0` as default, can be overridden with rule field `UnitPrice`  
H | Total price | decimal |  `0` as default, can be overridden with rule field `TotalPrice`  
I | Quantity | decimal | Amount as decimal when the row unit type is not seconds or hours. Can be overridden with rule field `OverrideUnitAmount`. When overridden, the amount will be shown regardless of the row unit type.  
J | Quantity unit | string | If the row unit type is not seconds or hours, the default value is `kpl`, otherwise, the default value is an empty string. Can be overridden with rule field `DigiaEnterpriseQuantityUnit`

L | Event date | date | Row's salary date (SalaryRenderingDate).

AF | Event time | integer |  `0` as default, can be overridden with rule field `DigiaEnterpriseEventTime`  
AG | End time | integer |  `0` as default, can be overridden with rule field `DigiaEnterpriseEndTime`

# Digital accessibility in Nepton

Nepton takes accessibility and equality very seriously and as such we are constantly improving and updating the platform to do better. It is important to us that everyone can use Nepton, regardless of disabilities or assistive devices used. We want to hear from you if there is something specific we can improve.
## Worktime clocking for users with disabilities
We offer a dedicated view for users with disabilities to clock their work hours. It is simplified for disability tools such as screen readers and is suitable for desktop and mobile use. If you would like to enable this feature for your users, please [get in touch](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7077076926237>).
If a mobile link is already visible in your Nepton environment (in section Employees - Persons - View info - Additional functions), you can activate the feature by following [this instruction](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002425577>) without contacting us separately.
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8917942773021)
## We're always improving
We consider accessibility and equality every day and we are actively working to modernise our whole user interface. As such, our modernised pages should work with many disability tools and should have sensible language and terms. We recognise that some of the older pages and features do not yet meet all accessibility requirements, and we are actively working to improve them. If you see something specific you'd like us to change or improve, please [get in touch](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7077076926237>).
## Accessibility statement
The accessibility status of our service is described in the accessibility statement, which you can find attached below.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Reporting / Worktime reports | path: en-gb/Support/Reporting/Worktime-reports/360002548278-Dining-reports.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548278-Dining-reports -->

# Dining reports

Dining reporting relates to supplement markings made by employees either using Nepton terminal software in cafeteria mode, or via a browser, to indicate the kind of purchases they have made. Below are details of the various types of reports and the information available within them.
## Dining by person
Report can be used to report lunch supplements that are recorded in dining events. The report shows persons dining events on a daily level by each lunch supplement type. The report can be printed and saved as a spreadsheet file.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25731656210077)
## Dining totals by person
Report displays each persons total amount of lunch supplements grouped by supplement type.
The report can be printed and saved as a spreadsheet file.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25731656214685)
## Dining report for restaurant/cafeteria staff and other third parties
It can be beneficial for third parties, that do not have access to the Nepton service, to still get a report of the supplements which have been recorded, whilst avoiding any other personal or sensitive data.
This is achieved by configuring a recurring scheduled [custom export](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/10758741671581>) that emails the report to the third party as a spreadsheet.
  1. Create an integration ruleset with an integration rule that exposes only the data the third party needs. Below is a recommended query which does not include any sensitive employee information:  

[code] SELECT   
         s.startDateTime, s.WorkIncrementName as SupplementName, s.Amount, s.UnitType, e.TerminalId   
         FROM UserSalaryData s   
         INNER JOIN UserEventData e ON s.activityId = e.activityid   
         WHERE s.CompensationType = 'WorkIncrement'   
         and TerminalId IS NOT NULL 
[/code]
  2. In the same ruleset you will need to define which columns to export based on the data you are querying and to include the headers in the file. Below is a recommended example, detailed instructions can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/10758741671581>).  
![d1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/10868083208093)
  3. Finally, a schedule can be created to export the data on a daily basis to the email addresses of the 3rd parties. More information on creating schedules can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/10510800700573>).

# Direct login links for SAML SSO and Microsoft login (Hash login)

If you use a SSO (single sign on) login to the service, then the login can be made easier by using the direct login link.
You can save the link to your browser as a bookmark or as a shortcut on your desktop.
Instructions for creating a SAML SSO direct sign-in link can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590097>).
Instructions for creating an Microsoft login direct login link can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590137>).

# DL Prime salary events

**Sorry!**
This article hasn't been translated yet
Nepton voidaan määrittää tuottamaan kirjatuista tapahtumista tulkittu palkka-aineisto DL Prime järjestelmään.
Aineistomallit ja siihen liittyvät asetukset löytyvät Neptonista nimellä "DL Software"
## Määrittäminen
**1\. Henkilöiden tunnusten määrittäminen**
Henkilöiden henkilötunnisteet voidaan määrittää muokkaamalla henkilötietoja Työsuhde > Henkilön tiedot > Tunnisteet -näkymässä.
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29395754407325)
Jos henkilön DL Software -tunnusta ei ole asetettu, käytetään henkilön henkilönumeroa.
**2\. Sääntöjoukon luominen**
Liittymässä voidaan käyttää integraation sääntöjoukkoja. Sääntöjoukon poiminnan ohje löytyy artikkelista [Sääntöjoukon poimintasääntöjen käsittely](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002489257-S%C3%A4%C3%A4nt%C3%B6joukon-poimintas%C3%A4%C3%A4nt%C3%B6jen-k%C3%A4sittely>).
## Tiedostomuoto
Siirtotiedosto on UTF-8 muotoista positioeroteltua tekstimuotoista dataa. Aineisto ei sisällä otsikoita. Numeerisia kenttiä **ei** täytetä etunollilla, tyhjät merkit täytetään välilyönneillä oikeasta laidasta, jollei kentässä ole toisin mainittu.
## Rajaukset
Työntekijät työntekijänumerolla 0 eivät tule osaksi aineistoa.
## Aineistomuodot
Nepton tukee kahta DL Prime aineistomuotoa:
  * DL Prime 2000 - DLWPLPT3
  * DL Prime 3000 - DLWPLPT8


DL Prime 3000 aineistomuoto on laajennettu versio DL Prime 2000 aineistomuodosta.

# Document folder management

Document folders provide a convenient place to store additional information about personnel that is contained or archived in files. e.g. PDFs, Excels, Word documents, or any other file types.
By default, there are three document folders types; Work contracts, Salary slips, and Other documents.
Work contracts and Salary slips folder types are related to other features described below, and should not be removed if you are using them. However, removed folders can be returned at a later date.
  * **Work contracts folder** \- Required by the Online work contract features, for storing signed work contract PDFs and attached materials. The folder can also be used for storing any other working contract related materials. e.g. scanned copies of written contracts, etc.
  * **Salary slips folder** \- Required by the Salary advance request features, for storing approved requests as PDF. Can also be used for storing other manually created materials related to salaries.
  * **Other documents folder** \- A general-purpose folder for storing any other files related to a user


### Create or edit folders
The document folders are managed from the **Employees - > Administration page**, under the **Document folders** heading. From here you can adjust all aspects to the folders.
  * **Add a folder** \- To add a new folder, simply click the 'Add folder' button and fill the related fields. You can create as many folders as you feel necessary to organise your person information.  
An example of this can be seen in the screenshot below, called _Custom folder_.  
When adding a folder, the 'Type' dictates whether it is used by other features in the platform and the file types it permits. Please see the **Folder types, default folders and related features** heading above for more information.
  * **Remove a folder** \- Clicking the 'X' next to a folder, will mark it removed. Removed folders will no longer be accessible for anyone, but this can be reversed after clicking the 'Show deleted document folders' check box above the management panel.
  * **Edit a folder** \- By clicking the 'Pencil' icon next to a folder, you can edit its details. Here you can change its name, description, type, and permissions. Folders permissions dictate roles who have access to that folder for employees they also have permissions to.
  * **Change order** \- The arrow buttons beside the document folders, allow you to change the order in which they are displayed to end-users.  

Please note that changing a document folders 'Type' is not recommended after it has been created


![mceclip4.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360010972058/mceclip4.png)
## Viewing and editing a person's documents
### I can't see any document folders?
If your administrator has not yet configured any document folders, or you lack the permissions to view them for the person in question, then you will see a notification instead. If you think this is incorrect, please contact your administrator.
_Example: When no document folders are configured_
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360010897317/mceclip0.png)
### Person documents
If you have permissions to see a persons information, and permission to at least read one of the related document folders, it is possible to see the uploaded documents by visiting the person's information page and the Documents tab - **Employees - > Persons -> Person information**.
Depending on your folder permissions, you may then view, upload and even delete documents within each folder.
New documents can be uploaded either using the browse harddisk dialogue or by dragging and dropping the document to the intended folder.
![mceclip5.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360010972078/mceclip5.png)
### Document Permissions
Access to documents is restricted to individuals with authorized privileges, determined by both user role and document folder permissions. This chapter describes how document permissions are applied.
  * If document is not associated with any user, access to the document is based only on read permission granted to the folder for particular role.
  * Work contracts which are not associated with any user can only be read by Administrators, HR Management and Salary Management.
  * Persons holding the roles mentioned below are not able to access their own documents without employee role read access.


#### Permissions by Role
Below is a list of documents that can be accessed by different roles if read permission is set for their roles:
  * **Administrator, HR Management and Salary Management** \- All documents regardless of the user associated with the documents.
  * **Unit Manager** \- Documents which belong to users in the same unit as the Unit Manager.
  * **Supervisor** \- Documents of subordinates.
  * **Employee** \- Own documents.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Accruals | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Accruals/360019742118-Edit-or-set-accrual-value-to-multiple-people-at-once.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019742118-Edit-or-set-accrual-value-to-multiple-people-at-once -->

# Edit or set accrual value to multiple people at once

It is possible to set or change an accrual value for multiple persons at once using [event import](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002868137>). This may be necessary, for example, when the service is first taken into use and the starting balances need to be set for all employees.
The accrual is changed or set by using the Accrual Reset event type. At least the following columns must be imported:
  * Employee number
  * Event type code. Must be set before import in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Integrations > Event import**.
  * New value for accrual. Can be moved either in HH:MM format or in decimals.
  * Start date
  * Start time
  * End date
  * End time


The data fields (columns) and their technical requirements as well as an example file are described in more detail [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002868137>).

# Edit the name, code, and description of a setting group

The name, code and description of a setting group can be changed.  
  
Note that if changing the name or code, the changes need to be reflected in possible person imports.
Choose **Worktime - Administration - Setting groups - Setting group: Setting group to be modified - Action: Setting group information**  
  
![20210107-support-system-identifier-1-en.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015671577/20210107-support-system-identifier-1-en.png)  
Information can be changed by clicking input field and editing the text. Remember to save the changes by clicking the **Save** -button. Setting group can be deleted by clicking the **Delete setting group** -button.
Setting group information also shows a system identifier which is used if the current setting group needs to be copied as a template to another deployment. Read more about this in the article [Add a setting group](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002557537>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event management | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-management/360002520998-Editing-and-deleting-events.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002520998-Editing-and-deleting-events -->

# Editing and deleting events

Events recorded to calendar in **worktime** can be flexibly edited. Events can be edited in calendar and table view or individually in [mobile view.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002602658-Edit-events-using-Nepton-mobile>)
In this article, editing a single event is guided. If you need to edit multiple events at one time, please see [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002521038>).
If there is a need to change an already recorded event afterwards, this is possible. Rights to edit events are given by the worktime role, so depending on the policies, different users may have different rights to edit the event. The most common policy is that employees can edit events until they are approved by a supervisor. After approval, the supervisor can edit events until the days are locked. After locking, only the administrator can edit events. If a person has the right to edit an event, they can also delete events.
Calendar view can be found in **Worktime > Work hours > Events in calendar**.
## Editing an event
To edit an event, click on the event in the calendar, and the menu below will open:  
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35048097358109)  
Click **Edit** and the event edit window will open in a separate window:   

![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35048114081437)
The event can be flexibly edited:   
  
\- Used Event type  
\- Start and End time of the event  
\- How to process overtime after regular worktime  
\- Supplements  
\- Project targets  
\- Attachments (if enabled for deployment)  
\- Comments  
  
Editing options change between different event types, depending on if the event is for example Work - or Absence event type. Also company specific configurations might affect to the editing options.
Note that after editing or saving a new event, if the event would have a potential issue like e.g. it overlaps another event or its project hours are not allocated correctly within the event's duration, a warning will be displayed when saving the event. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35048114084125)
Event may be saved with these warnings by clicking "Yes" or the event can be modified/updated based on the details related to these warnings by clicking "Cancel" and then editing the event details. If an event is saved despite the warning, a yellow warning triangle will appear in the calendar view, indicating an exceptional entry. Exceptional entries can be managed and turned on or off [in the settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560618>).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35048097366941)
All event editing data is saved to [history data.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002521298-Event-edit-history>)
## Deleting an event
Events can be deleted in the calendar view through the same menu as when editing them. Click on the event to open the menu. From the menu, press "delete":
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35048393674397)
After clicking on this, you will need to confirm the deletion via a new pop-up window:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35048386149917)
Once an event is deleted, it disappears from the calendar view. Deleted events can still be viewed and restored to active status via the [Event Listing report](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548877>).

# Editing events in Nepton mobile

It is possible to edit previously created events on mobile.  
  
From the top menu of the page, choose the day on which the event has been saved on. You can view more days from the calendar icon at the top right corner of the page.   
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33723724566045)  
  

Click on the title of the event to open the edit view for that event. In this example case, the title Work is selected.
In the edit view, you can edit the event the same way as in the desktop version of the calendar. You can edit event type, start and end times, notes, projects (if enabled), overtime targeting (if the person has rights to specify overtime targeting), and supplements (if enabled).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33723709144093)
When the wanted changes are made, click Save. The changes are now saved.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Person groups | path: en-gb/Support/Person-groups/360002554377-Editing-moving-and-deleting-a-person-group.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554377-Editing-moving-and-deleting-a-person-group -->

# Editing, moving, and deleting a person group

Editing person groups, moving them within the person group structure, and deleting them is carried out in the Worktime section under **Administration - > Person Groups**. For all of the above actions, click the person group in the person group main view that you want to modify. 
Instructions for creating a person group in the service can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554498-Creating-a-new-person-group>).
# Editing a person group
In the following example, the settings of the person group “**Suomi / Finland”** are edited.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469658652189)
When you click the person group “**Suomi / Finland** ”, the view that opens on the right-hand side of the service, on the “Main” tab, allows you to edit the person group’s settings: **name, code, parent group (i.e., the person group’s position within the structure), and description.**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469658654365)
**NOTE!** The person group code is used as an identifier in person data integrations, so any changes to it may affect the transfer of person data.
Save the changes using the **Save** button.
# Moving a person group
The position of existing person groups within the person group structure can be changed by moving a person group under a new parent group. In the following example, the person group **“New Person Group A”** is moved from the root to under the **“Hallinto** ” person group by selecting “**Hallinto”** as the new parent group.  
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469658658077)
If it is necessary to return a person group to the root, making it its own parent group, select “**Root”** as the new parent group for the person group being edited. In the following example, the person group **“New Person Group A** ” is moved to become its own parent group by selecting **“Root”** as the new parent group.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469680329501)
Members of the person group at the time of the transfer remain members of the moved person group.
**NOTE!** In some cases, the entire person group structure is imported for individuals via the person data integration. In such situations, changes to the person group structure in the service may affect the transfer of person data.
# Deleting and restoring a person group
Deleting person groups is done by selecting the desired person group and then clicking the “Delete” button in the view that opens on the right-hand side of the service.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469658663453)
If the person group to be deleted has subgroups, you must choose what happens to them during the deletion process. If the subgroups are retained, they will be moved to the root in the person group structure, becoming person groups without a parent group.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469658667293)
If the person group being deleted has members, they will become ungrouped persons.
Restoring a person group is done by first activating the “Deleted” option from the main view of person groups. This view lists all deleted person groups.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469658673309)
To restore a person group, first select the person group you want to restore from the list. Then, in the view that opens on the right-hand side of the service, on the “**Main** ” tab, click the “**Restore”** button. 
The person group will then become an active person group at the root of the person group structure. If necessary, the restored person group should be moved back to the correct position in the structure.
When restoring, the individuals who were previously members of the person group will be reinstated as members, unless they have been moved to another person group after deletion.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32469680336669)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Salary systems | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Salary-systems/360003273378-eFina-Administer-salary-data-CSV.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003273378-eFina-Administer-salary-data-CSV -->

# eFina Administer salary data, CSV

## File format
The transfer file is text-based data separated by semicolons. Line breaks are CR & LF. Character encoding is UTF-8.
### Limits
Employees with an employee number of 0 are not included in the data.
### Data records
Column | Field | Integration query field | Format | Notes  
---|---|---|---|---  
A | Personnel number | Set automatically, cannot be overridden | number | Mandatory, maximum length 8  
B | Social security number | Set automatically | string | Can be overridden with `eFinaSocialSecurityNumber`. Maximum length 11  
C | Salary code | SalaryCode | number | Mandatory, maximum length 3  
D | Amount | Amount | decimal | Comma (`,`) as decimal separator. Maximum length 9  
E | Unit price | UnitPrice | decimal | Comma (`,`) as decimal separator. Maximum length 9. Can be overridden with `UnitPrice`  
F | Total price | TotalPrice | decimal | Comma (`,`) as decimal separator. Maximum length 9. Can be overridden with `TotalPrice`  
G | Comment | Comment | string | Maximum length 58 (automatically limited in file)  
H | Project Code 1 | ProjectCode1 | number | Maximum length 6. Populated from `ProjectCode1`  
I | Project Code 2 | ProjectCode2 | number | Maximum length 6. Populated from `ProjectCode2`  
J | Project Code 3 | ProjectCode3 | number | Maximum length 6. Populated from `ProjectCode3`  
K | Employee Name | eFinaEmployeeName | string | Person's first and last name. Can be overridden with `eFinaEmployeeName`  
L | Project Code 4 | ProjectCode4 | number | Maximum length 6. Populated from `ProjectCode4`  
M | Project Code 5 | ProjectCode5 | number | Maximum length 6. Populated from `ProjectCode5`  
N | Project Code 6 | ProjectCode6 | number | Maximum length 6. Populated from `ProjectCode6`

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Events | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Events/360004522538-Elisa-Ring-status-information.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004522538-Elisa-Ring-status-information -->

# Elisa Ring status information

**Sorry!**
This article has not been translated yet.
Palvelusta voidaan lähettää henkilöiden tilatiedot Elisan kulunvalvontapalveluun. Tilatietoja käytetään hyväksi Elisa Ring -puhelinjärjestelmässä, esimerkiksi ohjaamalla saapuvat puhelut paikalla oleville henkilölle. Liittymä ja sen käyttöönotto on vakioitu.
## Kuvaus liittymän toiminnasta
Kun liittymä on määritelty käyttöön, Nepton lähettää tilatiedot koko henkilöstöstä Elisa Ringiin. Liittymä siirtää tietoa kerran minuutissa ja mikäli henkilöllä on alkanut tai päättynyt tapahtuma Neptonissa, niin henkilön uusi tila siiretään Elisa Ringiin. Esimerkiksi jos henkilö on työssä ja on kirjannut koulutuksen alkamaan 11:00 niin tällä ajankohdalla Elisa Ringiin siirretään tieto siitä että henkilön tila on koulutuksessa.
Liittymä siirtää jokaiselle henkilölle tilatiedon siten, että henkilön tilaa kuvaa koodi. Koodit määritellään Neptonin käyttöliittymässä ja siirretään sellaisenaan Elisa Ringiin. Eri tapahtumatyypit voivat jakaa saman koodin. Esimerkiksi sairauslomat voidaan siirtää poissaolo-koodilla, jotta ei välitetä sellaita henkilöön liittyvää tietoa, jota Elisa Ringissä ei hyödennetä.
## Elisa Ring liittymän käyttöönotto
Liittymän käyttöönotto tehdään seuraavalla tavalla.
### 1\. Määrittele henkilöiden tunnisteet
Henkilöiden Elisa Ring -tunnisteet määritetään muokkaamalla henkilötietoja **Työsuhde** \- **Henkilön tiedot** \- **Tunnisteet**. Mikäli Elisa Ring tunnusta ei määritetä käytetään siirrossa henkilön henkilönumeroa. Tunnisteet voidaan päivittää myös massana palveluun käyttäen [henkilöiden tuonnin](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360003762577>) toiminnallisuuksia.
![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360005568998/mceclip3.png)
### 2\. Määrittele tapahtumatyyppien koodit
Tapahtumatyyppien koodit määritetään työyhteisön asetuksista, **Työaika** \- **Hallinta** \- **Työyhteisön asetukset** \- **Ulkoiset palvelut** \- **Elisa Ring (eIP Kulva)**
![mceclip7.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360005482757/mceclip7.png)
Määritettävät koodit ovat ne, mitä Elisa Ring -järjestelmään siirretään ja niiden tulee vastata Elisa Ringin liittymään määritettyjä koodeja. Usealle tapahtumatyypille on mahdollista asettaa sama koodi.
Koodi määritetää myös sille, kun henkilöllä ei ole meneillään olevaa tapahtumaa. Tämä koodi lähetetään liittymällä silloin kun henkilöllä ei ole meneillään olevaa tapahtumaa.
![mceclip6.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360005569058/mceclip6.png)
### 3\. Määrittele liittymän asetukset 
Liittymän siirto aktivoituu kun Neptoniin määritellään alla olevat asetukset. Nämä määritellään työyhteisön asetuksista, **Työaika** -**Hallinta** -**Työyhteisön asetukset** -**Ulkoiset palvelut** -**Elisa Ring (eIP Kulva)** \- **Kokoonpano**
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360005482737/mceclip2.png)
  * Elisan integraatiopalvelut toimittaa seuraavat tiedot, jotka tulee asettaa Neptoniin: 
    * Web servicen päätepiste
    * Web servicen käyttäjätunnus
    * Web servicen salasana
    * asiakastunniste
  * Laitetunniste on informatiivinen tieto, joka esitetään Elisa Ringissä. Tällä tiedolla vaihteenhoitaja tietää mistä palvelusta tilatieto on siirretty. Tähän määritetään arvo 'NEPTON'
  * Lähetettävien tilapäivityksien maksimimäärään ei tehdä muutoksia. Asetus on käyttöliittymässä sellaisia tilanteita varten, että teknisistä syistä liittymän siirtonopeutta tulee rajata. Esimerkiksi vanhemmat puhelinvaihteen tietoliikennelaitteet voivat aiheuttaa rajoitetteita.

## Liittymän tekninen toiminta
## Rajoitukset
  * Työntekijät henkilönumerolla 0 eivät tule osaksi aineistoa


## Lähtösanoma
Muuttuneet tilatiedot lähetetään minuutin välein. Lähetettävät tiedot ovat kuvattu alla. Liittymä on vakioitu eikä tietosisältöön ole tarvetta tehdä muutoksia.
Taso | Kentän nimi | Formaatti | Esiintymiskerrat | Selite  
---|---|---|---|---  
Juuri,  
SOAP body:n alla | Stamps | XML element | 1 |   
1 | entries | XML element | 0..1 |   
2 | Entry | XML element | 0..n | Yhden henkilön uusi tilatieto  
3 | Identity | XML element | 1 |   
4 | ClientId | string | 1 | Tietojen lähetysasetuksissa määritetty asiakastunniste  
4 | DeviceId | string | 1 | Tietojen lähetysasetuksissa määritetty laitetunniste  
3 | CardId | string | 1 | Henkilön Elisa Ring -tunnus / henkilönumero  
3 | ReasonCode | string | 1 | Elisa Ring asetuksissa määritetty tapahtumatyypin koodi  
3 | OccurredTime | datetime | 1 | Aika milloin henkilön tilatieto on muuttunut. Formaatti: `YYYY-MM-DD'T'HH:MM:SS[Z|(+|-)hh:mm]`  
3 | EndTime | datetime | 0..1 | Jos on etukäteen tiedossa, mihin asti tietty tila on voimassa (esimerkiksi paikalla, eli töissä), päättymisaika lähetetään. Formaatti: `YYYY-MM-DD'T'HH:MM:SS[Z|(+|-)hh:mm]`  
Kyselyn esimerkki:
[code]

              <a:Identity>

              </a:Identity>  
              <a:CardId>2222</a:CardId>  
              <a:ReasonCode>1</a:ReasonCode>  
              <a:OccurredTime>2015-04-15T18:11:26+03:00</a:OccurredTime>  
              <a:EndTime i:nil="true"/>  
            </a:Entry>  
            <a:Entry>  
              <a:Identity>  
                <a:ClientId>F9E2348B-C20E-4A0E-B2D5-725DC34B9230</a:ClientId>  
                <a:DeviceId>NEPTON</a:DeviceId>  
              </a:Identity>  
              <a:CardId>1111</a:CardId>

## Paluusanoma
Liittymä odottaa suoraa vastausta paluusanomana. Paluusanoman muoto on seuraava:
Taso | Kentän nimi | Formaatti | Esiintymiskerrat | Selite  
---|---|---|---|---  
Juuri,  
SOAP body:n alla | StampsResponse | XML element | 1 |   
1 | StampsResult | XML element | 0..1 |   
2 | GenericResult | XML element | 0..n | Yhden henkilön tilatiedon päivityksen tulos  
3 | DeviceId | string | 1 | Lähetetty laitetunniste  
3 | CardId | string | 1 | Lähetetty henkilön Elisa Ring -tunnus / henkilönumero  
3 | Code | integer | 1 | Paluukoodi 
  * 0 = OK
  * 1 = ClientId puuttuu
  * 2 = DeviceId puuttuu
  * 3 = CardId puuttuu
  * 4 = ReasonCode puuttuu
  * 10 = Tallennus epäonnistui

  
3 | Message | string | 1 | Tarkempi selitys tapahtumalle  
Sanoman esimerkki:
[code] 
    <s:Envelope xmlns:s="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/">  
      <s:Body>  
        <StampsResponse xmlns="http://www.elisa.fi/kulva">  
          <StampsResult xmlns:a="http://schemas.datacontract.org/2004/07/KulvaWCF" xmlns:i="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">  
            <a:GenericResult>  
              <a:DeviceId>NEPTON</a:DeviceId>  
              <a:CardId>2222</a:CardId>  
              <a:Code>0</a:Code>  
              <a:Message>OK</a:Message>  
            </a:GenericResult>  
            <a:GenericResult>  
              <a:DeviceId>NEPTON</a:DeviceId>  
              <a:CardId>1111</a:CardId>  
              <a:Code>0</a:Code>  
              <a:Message>OK</a:Message>  
            </a:GenericResult>  
          </StampsResult>  
        </StampsResponse>  
      </s:Body>

# EmCe work time management  - realized work hours and holidays

**Sorry!**
This article has not been translated yet.

## Määrittäminen
**1\. Henkilöiden tunnusten määrittäminen**

Siirtotiedosto on puolipisteellä (`;`) erotettua tekstimuotoista dataa. Rivinvaihto on `CR` & `LF` ja merkistökoodauksena on ISO-8859-1.
Siirtotiedostossa ei ole otsikkoriviä.

# Employers

Employers contain information about personnel’s employer. This can be especially useful when managing a group of personnel having varying employers due to corporate structure. Information related to employers can be freely defined. This is done by adding related additional information fields to the employer information. You can set employers in **Employees > Employers**.
Employers-field can be used with [Visma LTR integration](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/11166111654685>).
## Managing employers
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28250746151581)
Employer can be added by selecting "Add new employer". By default employer has "Name" and "Code" fields. Employer can also have customizable employer info, which can be added by clicking "Add employer info" button. Employer info will have a field name and a value. Employer info values are shown as hidden by default as they might contain passwords or other sensitive information.
![e1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/10849249748381)
Employer can be edited by clicking edit-icon on the left of the employer in employer list.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/10847617086621)
## Adding employers for persons
Employers can be added for persons by editing their person information
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/10847673245853)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / HR data / Person import fields | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/HR-data/Person-import-fields/9003095125149-Employment-duration-in-person-imports.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/9003095125149-Employment-duration-in-person-imports -->

# Employment duration in person imports

Employment duration information can be imported in [person imports](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003762577>) and the fields related to it are part of [person import fields](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015933397>).
"Default"-person import type doesn't update employment dates according to the rules described below.
On "Default"-person import type, employment dates will be imported exactly as the values are in the import data. In case you need to import using rules and possibilities of "Default"-import, but you want the import to only make the employment date range longer, use the import type "Extend working contract dates".
Employment days are updated in person imports following these rules:
  * Employment start date
    * If employment start date is not already set for a person, new date value is saved.
    * When employment start date has already been set for a person, it is only replaced if the new date is smaller than the set date or an empty value.
  * Employment end date
    * If employment end date is not already set for a person, new date value is saved.
    * When employment end date has already been set for a person, it is only replaced if the new date is greater then the set date or an empty value.


This restriction ensures that persons with multiple Employment start days are handled and showed correctly in Nepton.
If users are imported via the user interface, Employees->Persons->Import persons, any empty values in these fields are ignored, unless "Delete existing field values (Strict)" is chosen for "Empty values in import file"-selection.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Project management | path: en-gb/Support/Project-management/360002562418-End-project.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002562418-End-project -->

# End project

To end a project so that no more work can be targeted to it, you must add an **end date** to the project. 
Go to **Worktime - > Projects -> Project administration.**  
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4414929725073/mceclip2.png)  
Choose the right project from the **Projects** menu.  
![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4414935325457/mceclip3.png)  
Add the ending date to **Project ends** field.  
Save changes by clicking **Save project** at the bottom of the page.
NOTE! If a project has been set as a person's default project, they can still record hours to it even after the project has ended.
If start and/or end times have been set to a parent project, they will be copied to all sub-projects. If these dates are removed from the parent project, they will not be removed from sub-projects automatically but they need to be manually removed from each project.

# EnsureProjectsExist

This article has not been translated yet.
A newer version of this method exists. If you are currently using this method, we recommend that you will look at the instructions of the next method for changes required to update to the next version. You can find the instructions for the next version [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360005783318>)
## Rajapinnan yleiskuvaus
Verkkopalvelua käytetään siihen, että kutsussa annettu lista projekteista päivitetään Neptoniin. Mikäli projekti on olemassa niin sen tietoja päivitetään. Mikäli projektia ei ole olemassa niin se luodaan. Projektin olemassaolo todetaan joko kutsussa määritetyn Nepton tunnisteen (Id) perusteella tai projektin koodin perusteella (code).
Verkkopalvelun WSDL-skeema on julkisesti saatavilla [täällä](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). Rajapinnat ovat yleisellä tasolla kuvattuna [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>).
Kuvauksessa oleva sarake esiintymiskerrat määrittää sen onko jokin tieto pakollinen kutsussa vai ei. Esiintymiskerrat 0, tarkoittaa että kyseistä tietoa ei tarvitse siirtää kutsussa. Esiintymiskerrat 1 tarkoittaa, että tiedon tulee esiintyä kutsussa yhden kerran. Esiintymiskerrat 0..n tarkoittaa, että kyseinen tieto voi esiintyä kutsussa minkä tahansa määrän. Esiintymiskerrat 1..n tarkoittaa että kyseinen tieto tulee olla aineistossa ainakin kerran, mutta voi olla useamminkin.
## Lähetettävät tiedot
Taso | Kentän nimi | Muoto | Esiintymiskerrat | Selite  
---|---|---|---|---  
Juuri,  
SOAP body:n alla | ParametersForEnsureProjectsExist | XML element | 1 |   
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | Lisää tietoa autentikoitumisesta [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>)  
1 | ProjectList | XML element | 1 | Listaus projekteja  
2 | Project | XML element | 1..n | Yhden projektin tiedot. Yleisten elementtien sisällön näkee [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>).  
3 | Id | unsignedInt | 0..1 | Neptonin antama yksilöllinen projektin tunniste.   
3 | Name | string | 1 | Projektin nimi  
3 | Deleted | boolean | 0..1 | Onko projekti poistettu vai ei. Poistetut projektit säilyvät tietokannassa, mutta niiden palauttaminen ei ole mahdollista tämän rajapinnan kautta.  
3 | Active | boolean | 0..1 |  Jos kentän arvona on `true`, projektin päättymispäivä tyhjennetään. Jos kentän arvona on `false`, päättymispäiväksi asetetaan eilinen päivä. Jos `EndDate` kentällä on arvo, tämän kentän tiedot sivuutetaan.  
3 | Code | string | 0..1 | Projektin koodi, jota voidaan myös käyttää projektin tunnisteena  
3 | TypeInternalName | string | 0..1 | Projektin tyypin sisäinen tunniste. Arvo täytyy antaa projektia luodessa. Jos erillisiä projektityyppejä ei ole asetettuna, arvona on `project_work`  
3 | Description | string | 0..1 | Projektin kuvaus  
3 | StartDate | date | 0..1 | Projektin alkamispäivä. Projektia ei voida asettaa tapahtumien kohdisteeksi tai projektin tunteja raportoida ennen tätä päivää. Arvona voi myös olla `null`, esimerkiksi: 
[code]
    <StartDate xsi:nil="true" />
[/code]  
3 | EndDate | date | 0..1 | Projektin päättymispäivä. Projektia ei voida asettaa tapahtumien kohdisteeksi tai projektin tunteja raportoida tämän päivän jälkeen. Arvona voi myös olla `null`, esimerkiksi: 
[code]
    <EndDate xsi:nil="true" />
[/code]  
3 | ParentProjectId | unsignedInt | 0..1 | Projektin yläprojektin Neptonin yksilöllinen tunniste. Arvona voi myös olla `null`, esimerkiksi: 
[code]
    <ParentProjectId xsi:nil="true" />
[/code]  
3 | ParentProjectCode | string | 0..1 | Projektin yläprojektin projektikoodi. Arvona voi myös olla `null`, esimerkiksi: 
[code]
    <ParentProjectCode xsi:nil="true" />
[/code]  
3 | Left | unsignedInt | 0..1 | Tietoa ei käytetä  
3 | Right | unsignedInt | 0..1 | Tietoa ei käytetä  
3 | ChildProjects | XML element | 0..n | Tietoa ei käytetä  
### Kyselyn esimerkki
[code] 
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance">  
      <soapenv:Header/>  
      <soapenv:Body>

      </soapenv:Body>
