<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002558617-Expected-work-times.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558617-Expected-work-times -->

# Expected work times

Expected work times determine the hours when overtime can be formed, for example in situations where a person leaves for sick leave in the middle of the day, or if work has been done before the start of the actual work hours. In the worktime calculations, regular working hours fall inside the expected work times. The worked time that is outside expected work times is interpreted with the overtime settings. The excess time is compensated based on the [overtime target](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002481617-Event-overtime-targeting>) on the event.
## Setting up Expected work times
Expected work times can be defined in Worktime section either on working community or setting group level: Worktime > Administration > Working community / setting group settings > Work hours > Expected work times. Please note, that all setting changes should be made using [validity control](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358-Using-the-validity-control-in-Worktime>).
In order to turn the expected work times on, first set 'Yes' to the setting 'Use expected working times'. After this you can define the expected work times for each day individually, Mon-Sun. It is possible to set two values for each day. This might be necessary when work is done overnight. 
In the example below the excepted work times have been set from 8am to 4pm from Monday to Friday.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19949811109533)
If expected work hours are in use, they can be seen in the person's calendar view when clicking on the date:  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19949843379485)
### Setting expected times for one person for one day
Sometimes it is necessary to modify the expected working hours in a certain situation. Exceptional expected working hours for a day can be set for a single person. This can be done in the person's calendar view, when clicking on the correct date. After that, click on the expected work times. This opens a new window where you can define exceptional expected work hours for the day in question, to apply only to the person in question.
## Expected work times and overtime interpretation
Now that the settings are set, a person can earn overtime even if regular work hours aren't filled. Below are examples of situations where expected work hours are set to 8-16:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19949811113501)
Tuesday 4.6. Work has been done from 6am to 3pm. Overtime target is "overtime to salary". Because the expected work times start at 8am, the first two hours are interpreted as overtime. Regular working time starts at 8am. As the work was finished at 3pm, the regular working hours haven't been filled, but are one hour short. Therefore that one hour is borrowed from balance at the end of the day.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19949811116061)
Wednesday 5.6. The work done is the same as previous day, but this time the overtime target is "hour to hour - balance". Therefore no overtime is formed, but at the end of the day one hour is added to balance as work exceeds regular time by one hour.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19949811117597)
Thursday 6.6. Work has been started at 7am with the overtime target "overtime to salary". During the day the person has got sick, and started sick leave at 12pm. As expected work times begin at 8, the first hour is counted as overtime.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19949843392797)
Without expected work hours the week in question would look like this, overtime would not be earned before regular working hours are full:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19949811122333)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / HR data | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/HR-data/8042662966429-Export-HR-data-to-a-REST-API-endpoint.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/8042662966429-Export-HR-data-to-a-REST-API-endpoint -->

# Export HR data to a REST API endpoint

This article describes technical details on how to set up an external REST API endpoint for receiving HR data exported from Nepton via a scheduled person export. Details about setting up a scheduled task for person export including the REST API settings are described in [Scheduled task – person export](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002489357>) page and data format specific pages for [CSV](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/4405423095953>) and [JSON](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/7982660700189>).
# Request message
This section describes the HTTP requests sent by Nepton platform when contacting an external REST API endpoint for exporting HR data. The contents of the data sent – according to selected data format – are described in [Export persons - Default CSV data format](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4405423095953>) and [Export persons - JSON data format](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7982660700189>) pages.
## REST API address
Scheduled person export task is using [HTTP PUT method](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/PUT>) when contacting the REST API endpoint. The endpoint must support [TLS](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/TLS>) protocol (address must be defined with https:// prefix).  
  
![mceclip4.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8043302516765)
## Authentication type
The selected authentication method determines the [Authorization header](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization>) value used when contacting the REST API service.
### No authentication
If "No authentication" is selected as the authentication type, the data is sent to service and no authentication options are expected to be required.
![mceclip6.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8211391152285)
### Basic HTTP authentication
Basic HTTP authentication adds an [Authorization header](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization>) with value "Basic" followed by a space and the "username" and "password" parameter values separated by colon – in username:password format – encoded as [UTF-8](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8>) bytes converted to [Base64](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base64>) string.  
  
![mceclip5.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8043327434013)  
Example:
[code] 
    Authorization: Basic c2FtcGxldXNlcm5hbWU6YW0jbWFhNmZtMjh2bWYmR2xo
[/code]
where c2FtcGxldXNlcm5hbWU6YW0jbWFhNmZtMjh2bWYmR2xo is the _sampleusername:am#maa6fm28vm &Glh_ (parameter values username and password from scheduled task settings combined with colon) converted to Base64 string.
### OAuth 2.0 (Basic HTTP authentication)
OAuth 2.0 authorization contacts the given authorization service with [HTTP POST method](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/POST>) first, using [Authorization header](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization>) similar to Basic HTTP authentication. Authorization server must support [TLS](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/TLS>) protocol (address must be defined with https:// prefix).
  
![mceclip6.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8043606311069)  
A successful response from authorization server should have a [JSON object](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON#Data_types>) as the body of the response. The object should have at least _access_token_ field defined. The format of the response (there may be more HTTP headers):
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    Content-Type: application/json;charset=utf-8
    Content-Length: 119
    
    {
    	"access_token": "secret_access_token_value",
    	"token_type": "token_type",
    	"expires_in": 999999,
    	"scope": "scope"
    }
[/code]
The access_token field value is then passed to the given REST API service in Authorization header:
[code] 
    Authorization: Bearer _secret_access_token_value_
[/code]
where _secret_access_token_value_ is the _access_token_ field value from the authorization server response.
### Token authorization
Token authorization adds the parameter _apikey_ value to [Authorization header](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Authorization>) with TOKEN prefix.
![mceclip7.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8044600701725)
Example Authorization header:
[code] 
    Authorization: TOKEN _secret_api_key_provided_
[/code]
where _secret_api_key_provided_ is the value of the _apikey_ parameter from scheduled task settings.
Scheduled task for person export will contact the service defined in REST API address using [HTTP PUT method](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/PUT>) and adding an authorization header value based on the selected authentication type of the scheduled task.
## Security protocols
Endpoint and possible OAuth 2.0 authorization service must support [TLS protocol](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/TLS>) and their addresses must be defined with https:// prefix. Currently we support TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.1 security protocols.
## 100-Continue behaviour
Before sending data, an initial request with [HTTP PUT method](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Methods/PUT>) is made with an [Expect header](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Expect>) with value "100-continue", with all the other request headers included but without data as request body:
[code] 
    Content-Length: 25959
    Expect: 100-continue
[/code]
A [HTTP response 100](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/100>) (continue) is expected as indication for successful authentication and acceptance of the details in the headers before sending the actual data:
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 100 Continue
[/code]
If the server cannot accept the request, it can respond with [HTTP response 417](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/417>) (expectation failed):
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 417 Expectation Failed
[/code]
or another appropriate response, e.g., [HTTP response 401](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/401>) (unauthorized):
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
[/code]
## Content type
Content type of the request is presented as [Content-Type header](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Type>) value as the [media type](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/MIME_type>) of the contents to be sent ("application/json" for [JSON](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7982660700189>) format, "text/csv" for [CSV](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4405423095953>) format), followed by ";charset=" and the encoding of the contents (either "utf-8" for [UTF-8](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8>) (Unicode character set) encoding or "iso-8859-1" for [ISO-8859-1](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_8859-1>) ("Latin 1") encoding).
Examples:
[code] 
    Content-Type: application/json;charset=utf-8
[/code]
[code] 
    Content-Type: text/csv;charset=iso-8859-1
[/code]
## Content length
The length of the exported HR data file in bytes is sent as [Content-Length header](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Length>) value.
Example:
[code] 
    Content-Length: 3909
[/code]
# Response message
This section describes the HTTP responses expected by Nepton platform when it has exported HR data to an external REST API endpoint.
## Responses for sending a JSON file
### Transport was successful – reports by individual entries
Nepton platform expects an [HTTP response status code of a success](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#successful_responses>) (status code in range 200 – 299) (e.g. status code 200: OK), if the service handling the remote endpoint received the transported data successfully.
The response body must be [a JSON object](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON#Data_types>) – and the object must contain statuses for the individual person entries in the export message. The key names expected in the JSON object response:
  * "Status" key. It should have a matching value with text "Success" to indicate the export file could be processed – there could still have been problems in handling individual persons' information entries. If the Status value is "Error" – or anything else than "Success" – then it is reported to platform that no information could be processed.
  * "StatusByEmployee" key as an array of JSON objects matching each individual person included in the person export file. Each person JSON object should then contain the following key names:  

    * "EmployeeNeptonId" – mandatory key with a matching string value containing the [Nepton Id](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/8017902121885>), NeptonPersonGUID field value from the person export file.
    * If the handling of the individual person's information was successful, there should be **one or more of the following key names** in the StatusByEmployee object so that the individual person export is considered a success. The values for these keys should be JSON objects with at least one key name. Format of information of the values is currently not limited: 
      * Added
      * Modified
      * NoChanges
      * RemovedInfo
    * If the handling of the individual person's information was a failure or there were any kinds of warnings, one or both of the following key names should be included. Their values are logged in the [service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575478>) warning entry and the export for the individual person is considered a failure: 
      * FatalError (errors preventing the whole handling)
      * Warnings
  * There may be other keys included either in the main object or within the StatusByEmployee objects. This information is not currently handled, but _any_ information in the response may end up in a corresponding [service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575478>) entry.


Example (there may be more HTTP headers):
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
    Content-Length: 917
    
    {
    	"Status": "Success",
    	"StatusByEmployee": [
    		{
    			"EmployeeNeptonId": "206894AF-E2E6-5F11-B988-DD9E52BD067A",
    			"Added": {
    				"Field1": "Success",
    				"Field2": "Success",
    				"Field3": "Success"
    			},
    			"Modified": {
    				"Field4": "Success"
    			},
    			"NoChanges": {
    				"Field5": "Success"
    			},
    			"RemovedInfo": {
    				"Field6": "Success"
    			},
    			"AnyInformation": "There may be additional member fields - they won't interfere with the interpretation"
    		},
    		{
    			"EmployeeNeptonId": "D9D6AA30-58A9-43E4-A66A-12193A71C25E",
    			"Modified": {
    				"Field1": "Success"
    			},
    		},
    		{
    			"EmployeeNeptonId": "2CA5D9DF-5B57-446A-879B-FC8F704FA0F7",
    			"FatalError": "Mandatory field missing: \"Personal identity code\" is required by the XX system",
    		},
    		{
    			"EmployeeNeptonId": "FEE31CF4-B4BF-4DDF-ADAD-5ACB1B8CD130",
    			"Warnings": "Invalid value: \"Additional administrative information\" (\"1CC\")"
    		}
    	]
    }
[/code]
### Transport failed
It is recommended that a [HTTP response status code of a success](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#successful_responses>) (status code in range 200 – 299) is sent if there was no transport related error and inform about the specific details in the format described below. If the server just needs to inform that receiving failed or the service could not process information at all, it may alternatively send an error response – [HTTP client error response](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#client_error_responses>) (status code in range 400 – 499), a [HTTP server error response](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#server_error_responses>) (in range 500 – 599) or any other response classified as an error – and it will be logged in [service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002575478>) error entry.
If the response body consists of a JSON object with "Status" key name with matching value of "Error" – or anything else than "Success" – or if there is a message included in the matching value for "ErrorMessage" key name, the whole export operation is considered as failed. Any error message in "ErrorMessage" value will be logged in [service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002575478>) error entry.
Example (there may be more HTTP headers):
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
    Content-Length: 64
    
    {
    	"Status": "Error",
    	"ErrorMessage": "Error message for log"
    }
[/code]
Errors and warnings for individual person entries within the person export file should not be reported as a failure in general but using the "FatalError" and "Warnings" keys within "StatusByEmployee" array objects, see Transport was successful – reports by individual entries.
## Responses for sending a CSV file
### Transport and handling were successful
If the service handling the remote endpoint received and could process the contents like expected, an [HTTP response status code of a success](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#successful_responses>) (status code in range 200 – 299) is expected (e.g. status code 200: OK. No other information than the successful HTTP status code is required for a successful response when the contents were sent in CSV format. If any information is provided in the message body, it is logged as informational message in [service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002575478>) success entry.
Example (there may be more HTTP headers):
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 200 OK
    Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
    Content-Length: 2
    
    OK
[/code]
### Transport or handling failed
A non-success HTTP code is expected in case there was any problem either in transporting to or handling of the data in the service handling the remote endpoint. That code may be a [HTTP client error response](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#client_error_responses>) (status code in range 400 – 499), a [HTTP server error response](<https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status#server_error_responses>) (in range 500 – 599) or any other response classified as an error. The response code and any information received in the body of result is then included in [service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002575478>) error entry.
Example (there may be more HTTP headers):
[code] 
    HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
    Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8
    Content-Length: 54
    
    An unexpected error occurred while processing the data
[/code]

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management / Exporting and importing data | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/Exporting-and-importing-data/360002430478-Export-person-data-to-Excel.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430478-Export-person-data-to-Excel -->

# Export person data to Excel

You can export person data to an Excel sheet if you have rights to access other people's data using the persons search. For example, supervisors can export their own data and the data of their subordinates to for reporting purposes, storing the addresses and working contract details etc. You can also use the export functionality to edit certain details for many users at once in Excel and then import the updated data into Nepton or an external system.
Due to technical limitations, there are differences between the data fields supported by the person export and import. Please check the documentation carefully for the latest information.
## Export to Excel
  1. Navigate to **employees, persons, persons** -page,
  2. Filter the persons list by search terms and search for the persons whose data you want to export.
  3. Select Export to Excel to save the results to your computer.
  4. You can open the saved Excel file on Excel, LibreOffice or another spreadsheet program. 


## Export to importable Excel
  1. Navigate to **employees, persons, persons** -page.
  2. Filter the persons list by search terms and search for the persons whose data you want to export.
  3. Select **Export to importable Excel** to save the results to your computer.
  4. You can open the saved Excel file on Excel, LibreOffice or another spreadsheet program.
  5. Edit existing data and/or add new data.
  6. Navigate to **employees, persons, import persons** -page.
  7. Import the modified file into Nepton.


## Columns in importable Excel file
The name of the export file is including the date and time first, followed by "PERSONS" and the name of the working community - in the format: YYYYMMDD_HHMM_PERSONS_COMMUNITY.xlsx. All persons are on the first sheet/tab. The name of the sheet is "Henkilölista".
The columns are displayed in the following order. The column title is displayed on the first row, other rows contain information for one person each.

# Export persons - Default CSV data format

Person data can be exported from Nepton into an external service. This article describes Default format person export fields. A detailed description about person export can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360002489357>).

## Data format details
  * Default CSV format contains 61 standard fields.
  * In addition, all the [persons additional fields](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430918>) are included in the export.
  * If the fields are not in use or not set yet the value in the export file will be empty.
  * The separator character used between fields in CSV file is semicolon (;).
  * Line separator is standard Windows line separator (CR+LF 0x0D 0x0A).
  * The first row of the export file includes the column titles listed in the table above.
  * Username and employee number are both unique fields within the working community and can be used to identify the person.
  * Date fields are using the format DD.MM.YYYY - day, month and year separated by dots (.)
  * Possible [additional fields](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430918>) of type Date and time are using the format DD.MM.YYYY HH:MM - day, month and year separated by dots (.), a space, hours and minutes separated by colon (:)
  * Decimal number fields are using comma (,) as decimal separator.
  * Fields combining multiple values are using pipe (|) separating each value.

## Data format details
  * Character encoding of the exported file is always [UTF-8](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8>) (a common Unicode encoding).
  * Line separator is standard Windows line separator (CR+LF 0x0D 0x0A).
  * In [JSON](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON>) data format person information is exported as an array of person objects.
  * Each person object represents one person.
  * Person object consists of name–value pairs where each name represents field name and value is an array of one or more value objects.
  * Each value object consists of three name–value pairs:
**Name** | **Value**  
---|---  
Valid from | null or date "YYYY-MM-DD" of first date the value was or is valid  
Valid to | null or date "YYYY-MM-DD" of last date the value was or is valid  
Value | Decimal number or boolean value (true/false) without quotes or any other value enclosed in quotes (")  
  * If a field is not in use or not set yet the field is not included at all.
  * [Nepton Id](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles//articles/8017902121885>) (field name NeptonPersonGUID), External Identifier 1, Username, and Employee number are all unique identifiers for a person and can be used to identify an individual. We recommend using the Nepton Id, as it is guaranteed not to change. All of the other identifiers—except for the field **“External Identifier 1”** —will always have a value in the export data.
  * Date fields are using the format "YYYY-MM-DD" (year, month and day separated by hyphens (-), enclosed in quotes).
  * Possible additional fields of type Date and time are using the format "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" (year, month and day separated by hyphens (-), a space, hours, minutes and seconds separated by colon (:), enclosed in quotes).
  * Decimal number fields are using dot (.) as decimal separator when the decimal part is not zero. Otherwise value is only integer number. Negative numbers are prefixed with hyphen (-).
  * UUID fields are represented as strings consisting of 32 hexadecimal digits separated by four hyphens: 8 digits - 4 digits - 4-digits - 4 digits - 12 digits. Letters are in upper case. The code is enclosed in quotes (").
  * Any other values than true, false, null or decimal numbers are always enclosed in quotes. Certain characters are escaped with a backslash (\\):
**Escaped character** | **Original character**  
---|---  
\" | "  
\\\ | \  
\/ | /  
\b | backspace  
\f | form feed  
\r | carriage return  
\n | line feed  
\u hexadecimal code | any Unicode character out of valid range 0x0020 - 0x10FFFF is displayed with \u prefix and hexadecimal code of 4 digits or more

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / HR data / System specific person imports | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/HR-data/System-specific-person-imports/13129687045789-Extend-employment-dates-length-in-person-import.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/13129687045789-Extend-employment-dates-length-in-person-import -->

# Extend employment dates length in person import

This article explains how employment dates for people are updated in person imports. Also, this article explains how to correct if employment start date or end date is imported incorrectly.
Note that employment dates extension logic works the same in all person import types except Default mapping.
## How it works?
  * If a person has an existing employment start date, imported start date can zero out (empty) the existing start date value, or change the start date value to an earlier date, but start date value can't be changed to later date
  * If a person has an existing employment end date, imported end date can zero out (empty) the the existing end date value, or change the end date value to later date, but end date value can't be changed to earlier date
  * These limitations ensure persons who have multiple employment dates can be viewed and managed properly in the service
  * At a later date, full support for multiple contracts per person will be added
  * Examples: 
    1.        1. No existing employment dates  
imported values  
Employment start date : 01.05.2021  
Employment end date : 31.08.2022  
result: 01.05.2021 - 31.08.2022 (new dates can be added when there are no existing dates)
       2. Existing employment dates 01.05.2021 - 31.08.2022  
imported values  
Employment start date : 01.01.2021  
Employment end date : 31.12.2021  
Result: 01.01.2021 - 31.08.2022 (start date can be changed to an earlier value but end date cannot)
       3. Existing employment dates 01.01.2021 - 31.08.2022  
imported values  
Employment start date : 01.01.2022  
Employment end date : 31.12.2022  
Result: 01.01.2021 - 31.12.2022 (end date can be extended to a later value but start date cannot)
       4. Existing employment dates 01.01.2021 - 31.12.2022  
imported values  
Employment start date : ""  
Employment end date : ""  
Result: no working contract start or end dates (working contract start date and end date can always be cleared)


## How to fix if you make a mistake while importing employment dates?
  * We want to import "01.01.2021 - 31.12.2023" as employment dates for a person  

    * We set by mistake the values as following  
Employment start date : 01.01.2022  
Employment end date : 31.12.2022  
Result: 01.01.2021 - 31.12.2023
  * Now we can fix the contract start date by performing following steps 
    1. First import values  
Employment start date : ""  
Employment end date : 31.12.2022  
Result: "" - 31.12.2023
    2. Now import the values  
Employment start date : 01.01.2021  
Employment end date : 31.12.2022  
Result: 01.01.2021 - 31.12.2023


  *

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / HR data / Field validities in person imports | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/HR-data/Field-validities-in-person-imports/360015807338-Field-validities-in-person-imports.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015807338-Field-validities-in-person-imports -->

# Field validities in person imports

It is possible to define for which time period a certain field value is valid for person information. This makes it possible e.g. to save future person information changes advance (more about [validities](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004856937>)). Importing validity information makes it also possible to correctly import the data even if there are delays in the import because of connection problems or service interruptions. This is very important for fields like work time percentage or worktime setting group, where the validity plays a crucial part.
We recommend that a new person imported to Nepton platform is imported without validity information.
Use the _Employment start date_ field to indicate the date the person starts/has started working.
The method used for importing validity information depends on the source system of the imported data. All source systems do not support importing data with validity information.
There are three different methods of import concerning validity information:
  * [Without validity information](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015741097>)
  * [With Valid from information](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015754117>)
  * [With Valid from and Valid to information](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015842238>)


The "Default" person import type which can be used, for example, in [manual person import](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003762577>), supports importing [without validity information](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015741097>) and [with Valid from information](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015754117>). The support for methods of validity information import varies depending on person import type and the source system of the imported data. You can find more detailed information about supported methods of validity information import in the person import type specific guidance.
There must be values for [mandatory fields](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015933397>) for all times even after person imports.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Reporting / Reporting in general | path: en-gb/Support/Reporting/Reporting-in-general/360004437597-Filtering-persons-in-worktime-and-project-reports.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004437597-Filtering-persons-in-worktime-and-project-reports -->

# Filtering persons in worktime and project reports

In all time work time and project reports, as well as integration data, various user selection options can be used to limit the information contained in the reports.
User selection is made directly from the opening view under **Person selection options**. Additional filters can be applied from the gear icon in the upper right corner. To filter users, the report creator must have at least the rights to view subordinates’ events.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25731153155869)
## Additional search filters
When any of the filters below have been applied, the selection is confirmed by clicking the **Save** button, which updates the user list according to the filter.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25731178258077)
## Load users for period
With the filter, you can search for users whose employment ended before the actual reporting period selection.
**Example:** The person’s employment is set to have ended on 15.1.2025. The actual reporting period is 1.2.2025 - 28.2.2025. If for filter Load users for period also January is chosen, the person will be selectable in the Select person section even though their employment was not active during this period.
## Group by
By default, user selections for reports are made based on **P****erson group**. By changing the filter to**Setting group** , user selections can be made based on work time forms. By changing the filter to **Payment Group** , user selections can be made based on payment groups.
**Example:** Reporting is desired to focus on employees working flexible hours. The selection can then be made based on the setting group(s).
## Filter to supervisor's subordinates
User selections can be limited to subordinates of a specific supervisor.
**Example:** Reporting is desired to focus only on the subordinates of Supervisor A.
## Filter users
**All users:** All possible selectable users will be available for selection. At the administrator level, this practically means all active users. At the supervisor level, it means all subordinates of the supervisor.
**All subordinates** : All subordinates for whom the report creator is the primary or secondary supervisor will be available for selection.
**Primary subordinates:** Only those subordinates for whom the report creator is the primary supervisor will be available for selection.
**Secondary subordinates:** Only those subordinates for whom the report creator is the secondary supervisor will be available for selection.
## Filter by salary type
User selection will include those whose setting group has a salary type defined as **Monthly wage** or **Hourly Wage** (in the setting group’s settings under Work hours -> TES -> Salary type).
**Example:** The Hours by salary type report is intended to focus only on hourly wage employees. The employees belong to a setting group where the salary type is defined. Only those who meet this filter criterion, i.e., hourly wage employees, will be available for selection.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / Terminal administration | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/Terminal-administration/360007577678-Find-or-edit-a-terminal-s-network-information.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007577678-Find-or-edit-a-terminal-s-network-information -->

# Find or edit a terminal's network information

Terminals will automatically acquire suitable network configuration and no action is usually needed. However, in some specialised environments it can be necessary to report on, review, or manually configure a terminal's network settings.
## Reporting on terminals
Basic network information of terminals linked to a customer environment can usually be reported by an admin by visiting Employees > Administration > Terminals.
Information that can be viewed here is:
  * Nepton terminal Id
  * IPv4 and IPv6
  * Computer name
  * Last polled (Last time network connectivity was confirmed between the terminal and the Nepton platform)


Please note that in some special cases, terminal network configurations cannot be retrieved remotely.
![Capture201.JPG](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360007754817/Capture201.JPG)
## Advanced details & editing network settings
To view or edit advanced terminal network settings, it is necessary to physically visit the device in question.
The following information can be obtained in this manner;
  * MAC / Physical address
  * IPv4 and IPv6 address
  * DHCP server
  * Default gateway
  * Subnet mask
  * DNS Servers


An administrator must shut down the terminal software to allow administrative actions on the device. In quick succession, touch the screen in the bottom right corner, followed by bottom left corner, the top left corner, and the top right corner, clockwise one after another.
The network information can be viewed and edited using the desktop shortcuts on newer devices. Instructions for changing the IP address settings of a new device can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7132764025373>).
or by clicking the network icon in the bottom right corner on older devices.

## File type  
Export file is in XML form. See file structure below.
## Limitations
  * Fivaldi Business ID must be set in Nepton in _Worktime - Administration - Working community settings - Integrations - Fivaldi - Payroll system ID._
  * Persons with personnel number 0 will not be exported.

          <!-- optional, may be set with SQL, value 0 or 1 -->
          <SalesOrderRowStatisticsRow Value="0"/>  
          <!-- optional, may be set with SQL -->

        </SalesOrderRow>  
      </SalesOrder>  
    </FivaldiXML>

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Salary systems | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Salary-systems/360003272618-Fivaldi-salary-export-CSV.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003272618-Fivaldi-salary-export-CSV -->

# Fivaldi salary export, CSV

Nepton can be configured to export salary data from recorded events to Visma Fivaldi-system.
## Configuration
**1\. Configuring person identifiers**
Person identifiers can be configured by editing person information in Employees > Person's information > Identifiers view.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/13988909138589)
If person does not have Fivaldi identifier set, personnel number is used as an identifier.
**2\. Creating a ruleset**
Integration supports the use of rulesets. Instructions on creating rulesets can be found in [Setting up integration rulesets](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002489257>).
## File format
Transfer file is text data separated with a semicolon (`;`). If some field contains special characters, it will be surrounded by double quotes (`"`). Line break is `CR` & `LF`. Character encoding is in UTF-8.
Column A will contain the identifier of the export batch (`FivaldiBatchIdentifier`), which has the value in format 'Palkat dd.mm.yy'. Date comes from the first date of the selected period. E.g data is selected from period of 1.1.2022-15.1.2022 and the value for column A will be 'Palkat 01.01.22'.
File contains the following header row:
[code] 
    ERA;PVM;HENKILO;PALKKALAJI;MAARA;SK1;SK2;SK3;SK4;KERROIN;HINTA;KULUTILI;SELITE;PAIVITYSTAPA;LOMA_ALKUPVM;LOMA_LOPPUPVM
[/code]
## Limitations
  * Fivaldi Business ID must be added to Nepton in _Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Integrations > Visma Fivaldi_.   
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/11466940097309)
  * Persons with employeenumber 0 are not included in the transfer file


## Transfer file columns
Column | Field | Ruleset field name | Format | Description  
---|---|---|---|---  
A | Batch identifier | FivaldiBatchIdentifier | string | Can be overridden in ruleset with field `FivaldiBatchIdentifier`.  
B | Date | SalaryRenderingDate | date | Format: `DD.MM.YYYY`.  
C | Person identifier | OverrideUserIntegrationId | string | Fivaldi identifier or employee number of person. Can be overridden in ruleset with field `OverrideUserIntegrationId`.  
D | Salary code | SalaryCode | string |   
E | Amount | Amount | decimal | Amount in two decimal precision. For example pieces or hours in decimal. Decimal separator is comma (`,`).  
F | Project 1 code | ProjectCode1 | string | Project code 1. Note that if only 1 project is set up with '/' separator it will be split to other project codes.  
G | Project 2 code | ProjectCode2 | string |   
H | Project 3 code | ProjectCode3 | string |   
I | Project 4 code | ProjectCode4 | string |   
J | Multiplier | Multiplier | decimal | Empty by default. Can be overridden in ruleset with field `Multiplier`. Decimal separator is comma (`,`).  
K | Unit price | UnitPrice | decimal | Empty by default. Can be overridden in ruleset with field `UnitPrice`. Decimal separator is comma (`,`).  
L | Expense account | ExpenseAccount | string | Empty by default. Can be overridden in ruleset with field `ExpenseAccount`.  
M | Comment | Comment | string | Description of related event.  
N | Update method | FivaldiUpdateMethod | character | Default value is 1. Can be overridden in ruleset with field `FivaldiUpdateMethod`.  
O | Vacation start date | FivaldiVacationStartDate | date |  Empty by default. Can be overridden in ruleset with field `FivaldiVacationStartDate`. Format: `DD.MM.YYYY`. Information is used in reporting absences to Incomes Register.  
P | Vacation end date | FivaldiVacationEndDate | date |  Empty by default. Can be overridden in ruleset with field `FivaldiVacationEndDate`. Format: `DD.MM.YYYY`. Information is used in reporting absences to Incomes Register.  
### Example
[code] 
    ERA;PVM;HENKILO;PALKKALAJI;MAARA;SK1;SK2;SK3;SK4;KERROIN;HINTA;KULUTILI;SELITE;PAIVITYSTAPA;LOMA_ALKUPVM;LOMA_LOPPUPVM  
    Palkat 01.01.12;08.12.2011;78050;101;3,50;63111;81323;;;;;;"TT Iltavuoro";1;;  
    Palkat 01.01.12;08.12.2011;78050;101;1,00;63111;81323;;;;;;;1;;  
    Palkat 01.01.12;05.12.2011;78055;101;4,00;63111;81333;;;;;;"TT Iltavuoro";1;;  
    Palkat 01.01.12;07.12.2011;78055;200;16,00;63111;81333;;;;;;;1;07.12.2011;08.12.2011
[/code]

# Fivaldi Salary export, XML 

**Sorry!**  
This article has not been translated yet.
## Tiedostomuoto
Siirtotiedosto on XML-muotoista tietoa.
<PayrollBatchId> arvo on 'Palkat pp.kk.vv'. Päivämäärä tulee poimintajakson ensimmäisestä päivästä. Esim. poimitaan jaksolta 1.1.2022-15.1.2022 on ko. arvo 'Palkat 01.01.22'. Ko. arvon voi korvata poimintasäännössä kentällä FivaldiBatchIdentifier. Tämä vastaa csv-muotoisen aineiston Erä-kenttää.
## Rajaukset 
  * Fivaldi Business ID tulee olla syötetty Nepton-palveluun valikossa _Työaika - Hallinta - Työyhteisön asetukset - Liittymät - Visma Fivaldi.![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/11467184356509)_
  * Työntekijät työntekijänumerolla 0 eivät tule osaksi aineistoa


## Aineiston rakenne 
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="ISO-8859-15"?>
<FivaldiXML xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="https://asp.fivaldi.net/fivaldi/FivaldiXMLv1_7.xsd">
<FVBusinessId>01010ÄÄ1-1</FVBusinessId> //Fivaldi businessId setting is used. Can be overridden with SQL rule.
<FVCreationTime>2017-12-13T14:15:16+02:00</FVCreationTime> //file creation time
<Payroll>
<PayrollBatchId>Palkat 12.04.16</PayrollBatchId> //always contains text palkat and salary range start date
<PayrollRow>
<PayrollEmployeeId></PayrollEmployeeId>
<PayrollDate>2016-05-11</PayrollDate> //Fetched from SalaryRenderingDate
<PayrollSalaryType>200</PayrollSalaryType>
<PayrollAmount>8.00</PayrollAmount>
<PayrollFollowUp1> // up to 4 elements from PayrollFollowUp1 to PayrollFollowup4
<FVFollowUpId>PROJ</FVFollowUpId> //project code
</PayrollFollowUp1>
</PayrollRow>
</Payroll>
</FivaldiXML>

# Generic settings

General settings (Employment > Administration > Settings > General) can be modified by Administrators. This article describes those settings in more detail. Please note that settings related to [work time calculations](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/sections/360000707378-Worktime-calculations-and-management>) can be found on the Worktime section.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32263242611997)
**Default worktime role:**[Worktime role](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554338-Worktime-roles>) is a mandatory field for each person. If a person is brought to Nepton without worktime role, the role set in this setting will be his/her worktime role. One person can have multiple worktime roles.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32263226899997)
**Default worktime setting group:** Default [worktime setting group](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002557357-Add-person-to-a-setting-group>) is not a mandatory field. It can be empty when a new person is added manually or via integration to Nepton. When a new person is created via the UI, or a user import, and a setting group is not provided, the new person is set to the default setting group. An exception to this is when the RESET keyword is used, then they do not get a setting group.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32263226901149)
**Nepton version** : The link will guide you to the Release notes article in Support Portal, where you can read about newest published changes in Nepton.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / Example APIs and method descriptions | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/Example-APIs-and-method-descriptions/6913825701277-GetAccrualValuesForUser.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6913825701277-GetAccrualValuesForUser -->

# GetAccrualValuesForUser

## Interface overview
The service retrieves the values ​​of a person's accruals from a specific date. The accruals returned are those that have been specified to be calculated for the person.
Some of the accruals are enabled by default for every customer. These include "balance", "flexible bank" and "bank". Customers can also define their own custom accruals. The names of these accruals are visible in the query results, if they are enabled. All accruals are returned by the call. In addition to the accrual value, the method also returns the change in the accrual for that day.
The WSDL schema of the web service is publicly available [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). The interfaces are described in general [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).
The occurrences column in the description determines whether a piece of information is mandatory in the call or not. Occurrences 0 means that the information in question does not need to be passed in the call. Occurrences 1 means that the information must appear once in the call. Occurrences 0..n means that the information in question can appear any number of times in the call. Occurrences 1..n means that the information in question must appear in the data at least once, but can appear more often.
## Sent data
**Level** | **Field name** | **Format** | **Occurences** | **Description**  
---|---|---|---|---  
0 | ParametersForGetAccrualValues | XML element | 1 | Root element below SOAP body  
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | Authentication details. See [authentication in worktime API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019983978>).  
1 | UserPersonnelNumber | string | 1 | Personnel number of the person, whose accruals are being retrieved.  
1 | SalaryDate | date | 0..1 | Date on which the accrual values ​​are returned, in the format YYYY-MM-DD, e.g. "2016-12-31". Note: returns accrual values ​​at the end of all shifts on that day.  
### Call example
[code] 
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">  
      <soapenv:Header/>  
      <soapenv:Body>  
        <tyo:ParametersForGetAccrualValuesForUser>  
          <CallerAuthentication /> <!-- Authentication is needed but not shown in this example -->  
          <UserPersonnelNumber>2345</UserPersonnelNumber>  
          <SalaryDate>2020-01-01</SalaryDate>  
        </tyo:ParametersForGetAccrualValuesForUser>  
      </soapenv:Body>  
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]
## Response
**Level** | **Field name** | **Format** | **Occurences** | **Description**  
---|---|---|---|---  
0 | ReturnValueForGetAccrualValues | XML element | 1 | Root element below SOAP body  
1 | ResponseCode | int | 1 | A code that describes the success or failure of the request  
1 | ResponseString | string | 1 | A string description of the success or failure of the request  
1 | AccrualList | XML element | 1 | List of accruals  
2 | Accrual | XML element | 0..n | Accrual  
3 | InternalName | string |  | Internal string ID of the accrual  
3 | Name | string | 1 | The name of the accrual defined for the customer/according to the language used  
3 | Amount | string | 1 | Accrual value  
3 | ChangeAmount | string | 0..1 | Amount of change in the accrual from the previous day's value (not returned if there is no change)  
### Response example
[code] 
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">  
      <soapenv:Header/>  
      <soapenv:Body>  
        <tyo:ReturnValueForGetAccrualValuesForUser>  
          <ResponseCode>?</ResponseCode>  
          <ResponseString>?</ResponseString>  
          <AccrualList>  
            <Accrual>  
              <InternalName>bank</InternalName>  
              <Name>pankki</Name>  
              <Amount>18</Amount>  
              <ChangeAmount>10</ChangeAmount>  
            </Accrual>  
          </AccrualList>  
        </tyo:ReturnValueForGetAccrualValuesForUser>  
      </soapenv:Body>  
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]

# GetActivities

This article has not been translated yet.
Tästä metodista on uudempi versio. Mikäli käytät jo tätä metodia, niin suosittelemme että tarkastelet seuraavan version ohjeesta, mitä muutoksia vaaditaan uuden version käyttöönottamiseksi. Seuraavan version ohjeen löydät [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360020751677>).
## Rajapinnan yleiskuvaus
Verkkopalvelua käytetään tapahtumatietojen noutoon Neptonista. Verkkopalvelu palauttaa tapahtumat myös deaktivoiduille henkilöille.
Verkkopalvelun WSDL-skeema on julkisesti saatavilla [täällä](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). Rajapinnat ovat yleisellä tasolla kuvattuna [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>).
Kuvauksessa oleva sarake esiintymiskerrat määrittää sen onko jokin tieto pakollinen pyynnössä vai ei. Esiintymiskerrat 0, tarkoittaa että kyseistä tietoa ei tarvitse siirtää pyynnössä. Esiintymiskerrat 1 tarkoittaa, että tiedon tulee esiintyä pyynnössä yhden kerran. Esiintymiskerrat 0..n tarkoittaa, että kyseinen tieto voi esiintyä pyynnössä minkä tahansa määrän. Esiintymiskerrat 1..n tarkoittaa että kyseinen tieto tulee olla aineistossa ainakin kerran, mutta voi olla useamminkin.
## Lähetettävät tiedot
Taso |  Kentän nimi |  Muoto |  Esiintymiskerrat |  Selite  
---|---|---|---|---  
0 |  ParametersForGetActivities |  XML element |  1 |  Juurielementti,  
SOAP body:n alla  
1 |  CallerAuthentication |  XML element |  1 |  Lisää tietoa autentikoitumisesta [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>)  
1 |  FilterByUserIds |  string |  0..1 |  Suodatus henkilöiden yksilöllisten Nepton-tunnisteiden mukaan. Voit antaa useamman tunnisteen erottamalla ne pilkulla.  
1 |  FilterByUserNames |  string |  0..1 |  Suodatus henkilöiden käyttäjätunnuksien mukaan. voit antaa useamman käyttäjätunnuksen erottelemalla ne pilkulla  
1 |  FilterByActivityTypeIds |  string |  0..1 |  Suodatus tapahtumatyyppien yksilöllisten Nepton-tunnisteiden mukaan. Voit antaa useamman tunnisteen erottelemalla ne pilkulla.  
1 |  FilterPeriodBeginDateTime |  string |  0..1 |  Suodatus tapahtumiin, jotka päättyvät annetun päivämäärän ja ajan jälkeen. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PP HH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18 12:30:00`.

1 |  OrderResultsFirstBy |  string |  0..1 |  Tapahtumien ensisijainen lajittelukriteeri. Seuraavat arvot ovat tuettuja:
  * `ActivityId` \- Tapahtuman yksilöllinen tunniste Neptonissa
  * `ActivityBeginDatetime` \- Tapahtuman alkupäivä ja -aika
  * `ActivityEndDatetime` \- Tapahtuman päättymispäivä ja -aika
  * `UserId` \- Henkilön, jolla tapahtuma on, tunniste Neptonissa
  * `ActivityTypeId` \- Tapahtumatyypin tunniste Neptonissa

  
1 |  OrderResultsSecondBy |  string |  0..1 |  Tapahtumien toinen lajittelukriteeri. Tuetut kriteerit ovat samat kuin ensisijaisessa lajittelukriteerissä.  
1 |  OrderResultsThirdBy |  string |  0..1 |  Tapahtumien kolmas lajittelukriteeri. Tuetut kriteerit ovat samat kuin ensisijaisessa lajittelukriteerissä.  
### Kyselyn esimerkki

3 |  PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetStartInMins |  integer |  0..1 |  Tämä tieto löytyy myös ActivityDetailsin alta. Tämä elementti poistuu uudemmissa versioissa   
3 |  PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetEndInMins |  integer |  0..1 |  Tämä tieto löytyy myös ActivityDetailsin alta. Tämä elementti poistuu uudemmissa versioissa   
3 |  PlannedWorkActivityGroupPublicInfo |  string |  0..1 |  Tämä tieto löytyy myös ActivityDetailsin alta. Tämä elementti poistuu uudemmissa versioissa

  * `1` \- palkallinen
  * `2` \- palkaton
  * `3` \- vähennetty palkka

5 |  PlannedWorkColor |  string |  0..1 |  Työvuoron toimipisteen suunnittelutason tunnusväri. Tunnusvärin voi asettaa Vuorosuunnittelussa: Toimipisteet > Valitse suunnittelutaso > Suunnittelutason asetukset > Suunnittelutason väri

5 |  PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetStartInMins |  integer |  0..1 |  Työvuorosta tulevan sallitun työn aloitusajan aikasiirtymä minuutteina. Arvo lisätään tapahtuman alkuaikaan, jota käytetään sallitun työn aloitusajan asettamiseen. Nolla-arvo asettaa sallitun työn aloitusajan tapahtuman aloitusajaksi.

5 |  AssumedLunchInMinutes |  integer |  0..1 |  Työvuorosta tulevan oletetun ruokatauon pituus minuutteina  
5 |  PlannedWorkActivityGroupPublicInfo |  string |  0..1 |  Työvuoron ryhmän tietoihin annettu julkinen tieto  
4 |  SickLeaveDetails |  XML element |  0..1 |  Sairausloman lisätiedot  
5 |  CompensationTypeId |  integer |  0..1 |  Sairausloman korvaustyypin tunniste. Mahdolliset arvot:

# GetActivitiesV2

This article has not been translated yet.
Tästä metodista on uudempi versio. Mikäli käytät jo tätä metodia, niin suosittelemme että tarkastelet seuraavan version ohjeesta, mitä muutoksia vaaditaan uuden version käyttöönottamiseksi. Seuraavan version ohjeen löydät [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360020751677>).
## Rajapinnan yleiskuvaus
Verkkopalvelua käytetään tapahtumatietojen noutoon Neptonista. Verkkopalvelu palauttaa tapahtumat myös deaktivoiduille henkilöille.
Verkkopalvelun WSDL-skeema on julkisesti saatavilla [täällä](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). Rajapinnat ovat yleisellä tasolla kuvattuna [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>).
Kuvauksessa oleva sarake esiintymiskerrat määrittää sen onko jokin tieto pakollinen kutsussa vai ei. Esiintymiskerrat 0, tarkoittaa että kyseistä tietoa ei tarvitse siirtää kutsussa. Esiintymiskerrat 1 tarkoittaa, että tiedon tulee esiintyä kutsussa yhden kerran. Esiintymiskerrat 0..n tarkoittaa, että kyseinen tieto voi esiintyä kutsussa minkä tahansa määrän. Esiintymiskerrat 1..n tarkoittaa että kyseinen tieto tulee olla aineistossa ainakin kerran, mutta voi olla useamminkin.
## Muutokset aiempaan versioon ([GetActivities](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6580727241501>))

### Poistuneet elementit
Aiemmassa versiossa vastaus sisälsi seuraavat elementit kahdesti, ensin Activity-elementin alla ja sitten myös ActivityDetails-elementin alla:
  * PlannedWorkCalculationUnit
  * PlannedWorkColor
  * PlannedWorkUseForWorkDayLengthCalculations
  * PlannedWorkCanBeCancelledUntil
  * PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetStartInMins
  * PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetEndInMins
  * PlannedWorkActivityGroupPublicInfo


Nämä löytyvät jatkossa ainoastaan ActivityDetails-elementin alta.
Seuraava kenttä oli merkitty vanhentuneeksi jo aiemmassa versiossa ja on nyt poistettu vastauksesta:
  * ActivityList/Activity/RelatedActivityId


### Uudet ominaisuudet ja elementit
  * Hakumahdollisuus henkilönumeroiden perusteella (FilterByPersonnelNumbers-elementti kutsussa)
  * Hakumahdollisuus ulkoisen tunnisteen perusteella (FilterByExternalIdentifiers-elementti kutsussa)
  * Rajapintavastaus sisältää henkilönumeron tapahtuman henkilölle (UserPersonnelNumber-elementti)
  * Rajapintavastaus sisältää henkilönumeron tapahtuman hyväksyjälle (ApproverPersonnelNumber-elementti)
  * Rajapintavastaus sisältää tapahtuman ulkoiset tunnisteet (ExternalIdentifiers-elementti)

---|---|---|---|---

1 | FilterByActivityTypeIds | XML element | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumatyyppien yksilöllisten Nepton-tunnisteiden mukaan.

1 | FilterPeriodEndDateTime | dateTime | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, jotka alkavat ennen annettua päivämäärää ja aikaa. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.  
1 | FilterModifiedBeginDateTime | dateTime | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, joita on viimeksi muutettu annetun päivämäärän ja ajan jälkeen. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.  
1 | FilterModifiedEndDateTime | dateTime | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, joita on viimeksi muutettu ennen annettua päivämäärää ja aikaa. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.

1 | IncludeDeleted | boolean | 0..1 | Sisällytetäänkö poistetut tapahtumat (`true`) vai ei (`false`). Poistettuja tapahtumia ei oletusarvoisesti sisällytetä.  
1 | OrderResultsFirstBy | string | 0..1 |  Tapahtumien ensisijainen lajittelukriteeri. Seuraavat arvot ovat tuettuja:
  * `ActivityId` \- Tapahtuman yksilöllinen tunniste Neptonissa
  * `ActivityBeginDatetime` \- Tapahtuman alkupäivä ja -aika
  * `ActivityEndDatetime` \- Tapahtuman päättymispäivä ja -aika
  * `UserId` \- Henkilön, jolla tapahtuma on, tunniste Neptonissa
  * `ActiviTytypeId` \- Tapahtumatyypin tunniste Neptonissa

  
1 | OrderResultsSecondBy | string | 0..1 | Tapahtumien toinen lajittelukriteeri. Tuetut kriteerit ovat samat kuin ensisijaisessa lajittelukriteerissä.  
1 | OrderResultsThirdBy | string | 0..1 | Tapahtumien kolmas lajittelukriteeri. Tuetut kriteerit ovat samat kuin ensisijaisessa lajittelukriteerissä.

5 | PlannedWorkColor | string | 0..1 | Työvuoron toimipisteen suunnittelutason tunnusväri. Tunnusvärin voi asettaa Vuorosuunnittelussa: Toimipisteet > Valitse suunnittelutaso > Suunnittelutason asetukset > Suunnittelutason väri  
5 | PlannedWorkUseForWorkDayLengthCalculations | boolean | 0..1 | Tuleeko työpäivän pituus työvuorosta (`true`) vai ei (`false`)  
5 | PlannedWorkCanBeCancelledUntil | string | 0..1 | Päivämäärä ja aika, mihin asti varattu vuorotarve on mahdollista perua. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.  
5 | PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetStartInMins | integer | 0..1 |  Työvuorosta tulevan sallitun työn aloitusajan aikasiirtymä minuutteina. Arvo lisätään tapahtuman alkuaikaan, jota käytetään sallitun työn aloitusajan asettamiseen. Nolla-arvo asettaa sallitun työn aloitusajan tapahtuman aloitusajaksi.  
5 | PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetEndInMins | integer | 0..1 |  Työvuorosta tulevan sallitun työn lopetusajan aikasiirtymä minuutteina. Arvo lisätään tapahtuman loppuaikaan, jota käytetään sallitun työn lopetusajan asettamiseen. Nolla-arvo asettaa sallitun työn lopetusajan tapahtuman lopetusajaksi.  
5 | AssumedLunchInMinutes | integer | 0..1 | Työvuorosta tulevan oletetun ruokatauon pituus minuutteina  
5 | PlannedWorkActivityGroupPublicInfo | string | 0..1 | Työvuoron ryhmän tietoihin annettu julkinen tieto  
4 | SickLeaveDetails | XML element | 0..1 | Sairausloman lisätiedot  
5 | CompensationTypeId | integer | 0..1 |  Sairausloman korvaustyypin tunniste. Mahdolliset arvot:
  * `1` \- palkallinen
  * `2` \- palkaton
  * `3` \- vähennetty palkka

  
5 | CompensationTypeName | string | 0..1 | Sairausloman korvaustyypin nimi  
5 | EarnsVacationDays | boolean | 0..1 | Ansaitaanko poissaolosta vuosilomapäiviä (`true`) vai ei (`false`)  
5 | SickLeaveTypeId | integer | 0..1 |  Sairausloman tyypin tunniste. Mahdolliset arvot:
  * `1` \- sairas
  * `2` \- lapsi sairas
  * `3` \- työtapaturma
  * `4` \- työmatkatapaturma
  * `5` \- vapaa-ajan tapaturma

  
5 | SickLeaveTypeName | string | 0..1 | Sairausloman tyypin nimi  
5 | MedicalCertificateGiven | boolean | 0..1 | Onko lääkärintodistus luovutettu (`true`) vai ei (`false`)  
5 | SupervisorsPermission | boolean | 0..1 | Onko sairauslomalle esimiehen hyväksyntä lääkärintodistuksen sijaan (`true`) vai ei (`false`)  
5 | ReasonCode | string | 0..1 | Sairausloman syykoodi  
3 | ExternalIdentifiers | XML element | 0..1 | Tapahtuman ulkoiset tunnisteet  
4 | ExternalIdentifier | XML element | 1..n | Tapahtuman ulkoinen tunniste  
5 | Identifier | string | 1 | Ulkoinen tunniste  
5 | IdentifierType | string | 1 | Ulkoisen tunnisteen tyyppi  
3 | IsDeleted | boolean | 0..1 | Onko tapahtuma poistettu (`true`) vai ei (`false`)

# GetActivitiesV3

This article has not been translated yet.
Tästä metodista on uudempi versio. Mikäli käytät jo tätä metodia, niin suosittelemme että tarkastelet seuraavan version ohjeesta, mitä muutoksia vaaditaan uuden version käyttöönottamiseksi. Seuraavan version ohjeen löydät [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/27551218873757>).
## Rajapinnan yleiskuvaus
Verkkopalvelua käytetään tapahtumatietojen noutoon Neptonista. Verkkopalvelu palauttaa tapahtumat myös deaktivoiduille henkilöille.
Verkkopalvelun WSDL-skeema on julkisesti saatavilla [täällä](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). Rajapinnat ovat yleisellä tasolla kuvattuna [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>).
Kuvauksessa oleva sarake esiintymiskerrat määrittää sen onko jokin tieto pakollinen kutsussa vai ei. Esiintymiskerrat 0, tarkoittaa että kyseistä tietoa ei tarvitse siirtää kutsussa. Esiintymiskerrat 1 tarkoittaa, että tiedon tulee esiintyä kutsussa yhden kerran. Esiintymiskerrat 0..n tarkoittaa, että kyseinen tieto voi esiintyä kutsussa minkä tahansa määrän. Esiintymiskerrat 1..n tarkoittaa että kyseinen tieto tulee olla aineistossa ainakin kerran, mutta voi olla useamminkin.
## Muutokset aiempaan versioon nähden ([GetActivitiesV2](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6580610511133>))
### Rakenteelliset muutokset
Vanha | Uusi | Lisätiedot  
---|---|---

      ...
    </tyo:ParametersForGetActivitiesV2>
[/code]  
|

    <tyo:ParametersForGetActivitiesV3>
      ...
    </tyoParametersForGetActivitiesV3>
[/code]

      ...
    </tyo:ReturnValueForGetActivitiesV2>
[/code]  
|

    ...
    </tyo:ParametersForGetActivitiesV3>
[/code]
| Juurielementin nimi vastauksessa muuttunut  
### Uudet ominaisuudet ja elementit
  * Tapahtumatyypin koodi lisätty rajapintavastaukseen
    * ActivityTypeCode-elementti lisätty vastaukseen


## Lähetettävät tiedot
Taso | Kentän nimi | Muoto | Esiintymiskerrat | Selite  
---|---|---|---|---  
Juuri,  
SOAP body:n alla | ParametersForGetActivitiesV3 | XML element | 1 |   
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | Lisää tietoa autentikoitumisesta [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>)  
1 | FilterByUserIds | XML element | 0..1 | Suodatus henkilöiden yksilöllisten Nepton-tunnisteiden mukaan.  
2 | UserId | integer | 1..n | Yhden henkilön yksilöllinen Nepton-tunniste.  
1 | FilterByUserNames | XML element | 0..1 | Suodatus henkilöiden käyttäjätunnuksien mukaan.  
2 | UserName | string | 1..n | Yhden henkilön käyttäjätunnus.  
1 | FilterByUserPersonnelNumbers | XML element | 0..1 | Suodatus henkilöiden henkilönumeroiden mukaan.  
2 | PersonnelNumber | string | 1..n | Yhden henkilön henkilönumero.  
1 | FilterByActivityTypeIds | XML element | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumatyyppien yksilöllisten Nepton-tunnisteiden mukaan.  
2 | ActivityTypeId | integer | 1..n | Yhden tapahtumatyypin tunniste.  
2 | ActivityTypeCode | string | 0..1 | Tapahtumatyypin koodi  
1 | FilterByExternalIdentifiers | XML element | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumien ulkoisten tunnisteiden mukaan.  
2 | ExternalIdentifier | XML element | 1..n | Yhden tapahtuman ulkoinen tunniste.  
3 | Identifier | string | 1 | Ulkoinen tunniste  
3 | IdentifierType | string | 1 | Ulkoisen tunnisteen tyyppi. Tällä hetkellä ainoa tuettu tyyppi on `External`  
1 | FilterPeriodBeginDateTime | dateTime | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, jotka päättyvät annetun päivämäärän ja ajan jälkeen. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.  
1 | FilterPeriodEndDateTime | dateTime | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, jotka alkavat ennen annettua päivämäärää ja aikaa. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.  
1 | FilterModifiedBeginDateTime | dateTime | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, joita on viimeksi muutettu annetun päivämäärän ja ajan jälkeen. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.  
1 | FilterModifiedEndDateTime | dateTime | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, joita on viimeksi muutettu ennen annettua päivämäärää ja aikaa. Muotona on `VVVV-KK-PPTHH:MM:SS`, esimerkiksi `2021-02-18T12:30:00`.  
1 | FilterIsApproved | boolean | 0..1 | Suodatus tapahtumiin, jotka ovat hyväksyttyjä (`true`) tai eivät ole hyväksyttyjä (`false`).  
1 | IncludeDeleted | boolean | 0..1 | Sisällytetäänkö poistetut tapahtumat (`true`) vai ei (`false`). Poistettuja tapahtumia ei oletusarvoisesti sisällytetä.  
1 | OrderResultsFirstBy | string | 0..1 |  Tapahtumien ensisijainen lajittelukriteeri. Seuraavat arvot ovat tuettuja:
  * `ActivityId` \- Tapahtuman yksilöllinen tunniste Neptonissa
  * `ActivityBeginDatetime` \- Tapahtuman alkupäivä ja -aika
  * `ActivityEndDatetime` \- Tapahtuman päättymispäivä ja -aika
  * `UserId` \- Henkilön, jolla tapahtuma on, tunniste Neptonissa
  * `ActiviTytypeId` \- Tapahtumatyypin tunniste Neptonissa

  
1 | OrderResultsSecondBy | string | 0..1 | Tapahtumien toinen lajittelukriteeri. Tuetut kriteerit ovat samat kuin ensisijaisessa lajittelukriteerissä.  
1 | OrderResultsThirdBy | string | 0..1 | Tapahtumien kolmas lajittelukriteeri. Tuetut kriteerit ovat samat kuin ensisijaisessa lajittelukriteerissä.

[code]
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">

            </ExternalIdentifier>
            <ExternalIdentifier>

              <IdentifierType>External</IdentifierType>
            </ExternalIdentifier>
          </FilterByExternalIdentifiers>
          <FilterPeriodBeginDateTime>2021-01-01T00:00:00</FilterPeriodBeginDateTime>
          <FilterPeriodEndDateTime>2021-01-31T23:59:59</FilterPeriodEndDateTime>
          <IncludeDeleted>false</IncludeDeleted>
          <OrderResultsFirstBy>ActivityBeginDatetime</OrderResultsFirstBy>
        </tyo:ParametersForGetActivitiesV3>
      </soapenv:Body>
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]

# GetActivitiesV4

A newer version of this method exists. If you are currently using this method, we recommend that you will look at the instructions of the next method for changes required to update to the next version. You can find the instructions for the next version [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/36508618065565>)
## Interface overview
The web service is used to retrieve event information from Nepton. The web service also returns events for deactivated people (those deleted in Nepton using the Remove User function) when a user filter (e.g. personal identification number) is included in the query.
The WSDL schema of the web service is publicly available [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). The interfaces are described in general [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).
The occurrences column in the description determines whether a piece of information is mandatory in the call or not. Occurrences 0 means that the information in question does not need to be passed in the call. Occurrences 1 means that the information must appear once in the call. Occurrences 0..n means that the information in question can appear any number of times in the call. Occurrences 1..n means that the information in question must appear in the data at least once, but can appear more often.
## Changes from the previous version ([GetActivitiesV3](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360020751677>))
### New features and fields
  * Accrual and annual leave reset values are returned
    * ResetValue-element added to the response
  * Accrual and annual leave change values are returned
    * ChangeValue-element added to the response


## Sent data
Level | Field name | Format | Occurences | Description  
---|---|---|---|---  
Root,  
below SOAP body | ParametersForGetActivitiesV4 | XML element | 1 |   
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | More information about authentication [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).

2 | ActivityTypeId | integer | 1..n |  The identifier of a single event type. The ActivityTypeId can be checked in SQL by adding ActivityTypeId AS Aid to the SELECT clause. This will add the Aid column, where the Id is displayed. If the Id is not found, an empty query is returned.

1 | OrderResultsFirstBy | string | 0..1 |  The primary sorting criteria for events. The following values ​​are supported:

  * `ActivityBeginDatetime` \- Event start date and time

  * `UserId` \- User ID of the person who's registered the event
  * `ActiviTytypeId` \- Event type ID in Nepton

  
1 | OrderResultsSecondBy | string | 0..1 | A secondary sorting criteria for events. The supported criteria are the same as the primary sorting criterion.  
1 | OrderResultsThirdBy | string | 0..1 | A third sorting criteria for events. The supported criteria are the same as the primary sorting criterion.

# GetActivitiesV5

## Interface overview
The web service is used to retrieve event information from Nepton. The web service also returns events for deactivated people (those deleted in Nepton using the Remove User function) when a user filter (e.g. personal identification number) is included in the query.
The WSDL schema of the web service is publicly available [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). The interfaces are described in general [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).
The occurrences column in the description determines whether a piece of information is mandatory in the call or not. Occurrences 0 means that the information in question does not need to be passed in the call. Occurrences 1 means that the information must appear once in the call. Occurrences 0..n means that the information in question can appear any number of times in the call. Occurrences 1..n means that the information in question must appear in the data at least once, but can appear more often.
## Changes from the previous version ([GetActivitiesV4](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/27551218873757>))
### New features and fields
  * Events can be filtered with person's external identifiers
    * FilterByUserPersonExternalIdentifiers - element added to the request
    * FilterByUserPersonExternalIdentifiers contains PersonExternalIdentifier - elements
    * PersonExternalIdentifier - element contains elements Identifier and FieldName

# GetActivityTypes

## Overview of the interface  
Interface is used in retrieving event type information from Nepton.
Web service WSDL-schema is available publicly [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). Interfaces are described generally [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360004861558>).
Occurrences - column in request description defines whether a field is mandatory in a request or not. 0 occurrences means that field is not mandatory in the request. 1 occurrence means that the field must be present in the request once. 0..n occurrences means that the request may contain any number of those fields or none at all. Occurrences 1..n means that the request may contain any number of those fields but there must be at least one instance of that field.
## Request data
LEVEL | FIELD NAME | TYPE | OCCURRENCES | DESCRIPTION  
---|---|---|---|---  
0 | ParametersForGetActivityTypes | XML element | 1 | Root element under SOAP body  
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element |  | More information about authentication [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360004861558>)  
1 | FilterByIds | XML element | 0..1 | Filter by Nepton unique identifiers of event types  
2 | Id | integer | 0..n | Nepton unique identifier  
1 | FilterByInternalNames |  | 0..1 | Filter by event type internal names  
2 | InternalName | string | 0..n | Event type internal name  
### Request example
[code] 
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">  
      <soapenv:Header/>  
      <soapenv:Body>  
        <tyo:ParametersForGetActivityTypes>  
          <CallerAuthentication / > <!-- Authentication is required but is omitted from this example -->  
          <FilterByIds>  
            <Id>1</Id>  
          </FilterByIds>  
          <FilterByInternalNames>  
            <InternalName>work</InternalName>  
          </FilterByInternalNames>  
        </tyo:ParametersForGetActivityTypes>  
      </soapenv:Body>  
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]
## Response

---|---|---|---|---

1 | ResponseCode | integer | 1 | Response code of handling the request. List of response codes can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019841477>).  
1 | ResponseString | string | 1 | Response description  
1 | ActivityTypeList | XML element | 1 | List of event type  
2 |  ActivityType |  XML element |  0..n | Element containing information of single event type  
3 |  Id |  integer |  1 |  Nepton identifier of event type  
3 |  InternalName |  string |  1 |  Internal name of event type  
3 |  TranslatedName | XML element | 0..n | Translated names for event type. The number of elements is the same as the number of supported languages in Nepton. See supported languages and their codes [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6904407712413>).  
4 |  Locale | string | 1 | Language code for translation  
4 |  Name | string | 1 | Translation of event type name  
3 |  Code |  string |  0..1 |  Event type code  
3 |  Visible |  boolean |  0..1 |  true if event type is set as visible in Nepton, false if not  
3 |  CanAssignWorkIncrements |  boolean |  0..1 |  Can supplements be assigned for event type (true/false)  
3 |  CanHaveRelatedProjects |  boolean |  0..1 |  Can projects be targeted for event type (true/false)  
3 |  CategoryInternalName |  string |  0..1 |  Event type category internal name  
3 |  TranslatedCategoryName | XML element | 0..n | Translated names for event type category. The number of elements is the same as the number of supported languages in Nepton. See supported languages and their codes [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6904407712413>).

4 |  Name | string |  1 |  Translation of event type category name

---|---  
mandatory | Mandatory  
  
optional | Optional  
  
disabled | Not in use  
  
3 |  EndDateTimeInput |  string |  0..1 |  Setting for inserting end time for event type. Options are same as with BeginDateTimeInput - element.

# GetProjectsV2

## Overview of interface
The interface is used for exporting project information from Nepton.
Web service WSDL-schema is available publicly [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>).
Occurrences - column in request description defines whether a field is mandatory in a request or not. 0 occurrences means that field is not mandatory in the request. 1 occurrence means that the field must be present in the request once. 0..n occurrences means that the request may contain any number of those fields or none at all. Occurrences 1..n means that the request may contain any number of those fields but there must be at least one instance of that field.
## Changes to earlier version ([GetProjects](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6913429557405>))
### Structural changes
Old | New | Information  
---|---|---
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForGetProjects>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForGetProjects>
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForGetProjectsV2>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForGetProjectsV2>
[/code]
| Root element name in request has changed
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForGetProjects>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForGetProjects>
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForGetProjectsV2>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForGetProjectsV2>
[/code]
| Root element name in response has changed  
### New properties and elements
  * Projects can be filtered by an external identifier 
    * Added FilterByExternalIdentifiers element to the request
  * The projects' external identifiers are available in the response 
    * Added ExternalIdentifier element to response


## Request data
Level | Field name | Type | Occurences | Description  
---|---|---|---|---  
0 | ParametersForGetProjectsV2 | XML element | 1 | Root element under SOAP body  
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | Authentication details. More information about authentication [here.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019983978>)  
1 | FilterByProjectIds | string | 0..1 | Filters by Nepton identifier (can be seen in the Project details URL). Multiple indentifiers can be given separated by a comma (,).  
1 | FilterByExternalIdentifiers | string | 0..1 | Filters by external identifier. Multiple indentifiers can be given separated by a comma (,).  
1 | FilterByProjectName | string | 0..1 | Filters by project name, an asterisk '*' can be used.  
1 | FilterByProjectCode | string | 0..1 | Filters by project code, an asterisk '*' can be used.  
1 | FilterByUserGroupId | integer | 0..1 |  Filters projects attached to a person group, filtering by person group identifier (can be seen in the Person groupinformation URL).

1 | FilterByProjectTypeInternalName | string | 0..1 | Filters by project type name.  
1 | FilterActiveProjectsByStartDate | date | 0..1 | Use this with the FilterActiveProjectsByEndDate element to filter out projects which have not been active during the selected period.  
1 | FilterActiveProjectsByEndDate | date | 0..1 | Use this with the FilterActiveProjectsByStartDate element to filter out projects which have not been active during the selected period.  
1 | OrderResultsFirstBy | string | 0..1 |  The primary ordering basis for results. The options are:
  * projectid
  * left
  * right
  * name
  * code
  * internaltype

  
1 | OrderResultsSecondBy | string | 0..1 |  The 2nd ordering basis for results. Same options as in the primary ordering.  
1 | OrderResultsThirdBy | string | 0..1 |  The 3rd ordering basis for results. Same options as in the primary and 2nd ordering.  
1 | ReturnFormat | string | 0..1 |  Result format. The only option at the moment is the default format, flat_list.  
### Request example
[code] 
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">
