# Heeros ePalkat, salary integration

**Sorry!**
This article has not been translated yet.
Nepton voidaan määrittää tuottamaan kirjatuista tapahtumista tulkittu palkka-aineisto Heeros ePalkat -järjestelmään.
Huom! Aineiston nimi on Neptonissa aiemmin ollut Aboa
## Määrittäminen
**1\. Henkilöiden tunnusten määrittäminen**
Henkilöiden henkilötunnisteet voidaan määrittää muokkaamalla henkilötietoja Työsuhde > Henkilön tiedot > Tunnisteet -näkymässä.
Jos henkilön Heeros -tunnusta ei ole asetettu, käytetään henkilön henkilönumeroa.
**2\. Sääntöjoukon luominen**
Liittymässä voidaan käyttää integraation sääntöjoukkoja. Sääntöjoukon poiminnan ohje löytyy artikkelista [Sääntöjoukon poimintasääntöjen käsittely](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002489257>).
## Tiedostomuoto
Siirtotiedosto on tabulaattorilla erotettua tekstimuotoista dataa. Rivinvaihto on CR & LF. Merkistökoodaus on UTF-8.
Muodostettava aineisto on aina ryhmitelty per henkilö, per projekti, per palkkalaji
## Rajaukset
Työntekijät työntekijänumerolla 0 eivät tule osaksi aineistoa
## Aineiston tietueet
Sarake | Tieto | Sääntöjoukon kentän nimi | Muoto | Kuvaus  
---|---|---|---|---  
A | Henkilönumero | OverrideUserIntegrationId | merkkijono | Henkilön Heeros-tunniste tai henkilönumero. Arvo voidaan myös antaa sääntöjoukon kentällä.  
B | Palkkalajikoodi |  _Saa arvonsa sääntöjoukon yksittäisen säännön Koodi-kentästä ja voidaan korvata käyttämällä kenttänimeä_ OverrideSalaryCode | merkkijono | Palkkalajin koodi, esimerkiksi `412`  
C | Määrä | Amount | desimaali | Määrä desimaalina. Luku on kahden desimaalin tarkkuudella ja desimaalierottimena on pilkku (`,`).  
D | Rivi | RowDescription | merkkijono | Oletuksena tyhjä, arvo voidaan antaa sääntöjoukon kentällä.  
E | Hinta | UnitPrice | desimaali |  Oletuksena tyhjä, arvo voidaan antaa sääntöjoukon kentällä. Luku on kahden desimaalin tarkkuudella ja desimaalierottimena on pilkku (`,`).  
F | Kerroin | HeerosMultiplier | desimaali |  Oletuksena tyhjä, arvo voidaan antaa sääntöjoukon kentällä. Luku on kahden desimaalin tarkkuudella ja desimaalierottimena on pilkku (`,`).  
G | Työnumero | HeerosJobNumber | merkkijono | Oletuksena tyhjä, arvo voidaan antaa sääntöjoukon kentällä.  
H | Projekti |  | merkkijono | Jos projekteja on yksi, sen projektin projektikoodi. Jos projekteja on enemmän, projektikoodit järjestetääm aakkosjärjestyksen mukaan ja järjestyksessä viimeisenä oleva otetaan projektikoodiksi.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Rulesets | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Rulesets/360009018778-Helper-functions-for-rulesets.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360009018778-Helper-functions-for-rulesets -->

# Helper functions for rulesets

When writing ruleset extraction rules, in addition to SQL Lite functions, auxiliary functions implemented for the service are available. With helper functions, it is easier to handle, for example, strings in SQL Lite.
### List of available helper functions and their operation
  * **substring_part**. Parameters: (sourceString, separator, index). The function splits the given string sourceString with the given separator string separator. The return value consists of as much data content as the index value indicates. If the string does not contain this element, NULL is returned. A negative index returns the element pointed to by the index calculated from the last results. -1 returns the last element, -2 returns the second to last, and so on.  

  * **substring_index()** <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/string-functions.html#function_substring-index>  

  * **sql_left()** <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/string-functions.html#function_left>  

  * **sql_right()** <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/string-functions.html#function_right>  

  * **concat()** <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/string-functions.html#function_concat>  

  * **if()** <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/control-flow-functions.html#function_if>  

  * **timestamp()** <https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/date-and-time-functions.html#function_timestamp>  

  * **strftime(format,timestring)** Returns the 'timestring' formatted according to the 'format' string provided. For example, strftime('%Y %m %d', 'now', 'localtime') would extract the Year Month and Day for the current date.  

  * **curdate()** Returns the current date according the server's local timezone (Finland). Format YYYY-MM-DD  

  * **curtime()** Returns the current time according to the server's local timezone (Finland). Format H:i:s  

  * **now()** Returns the current date and time according to the server's local timezone (Finland). Format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS  

  * **weekday(date/datetime/timestamp)** Returns the day of the week as a number based on the provided date or time. 0 (for Monday) through 6 (for Sunday). For example, if you want to filter out Saturdays and Sundays, you can add the following line to the code: AND weekday(salaryrenderingdate) NOT IN (5, 6)  

  * **ceil(decimal)** Round a decimal up to the nearest whole number  

  * **floor(decimal)** Round a decimal down to the nearest whole number  

  * **round(decimal)** Round a decimal to a specific amount of digits.  

  * **minutesToHHMM(decimal)** Converts the amount of minutes to HH:MM format. The value is not rounded. For example `minutesToHHMM(270.8)` would return 04:30. If rounding is needed, it needs to be done specifically, for example `minutesToHHMM(round(270.8))`  

  * **minutesToHHMMSS(decimal)** Converts the amount of minutes to HH:MM:SS format. For example `minutesToHHMMSS(270.8)` would return 04:30:48.  

  * **secondsToHHMM(decimal)** Converts the amount of seconds to HH:MM format. The value is not rounded. For example `secondsToHHMM(16248)` would return 04:30. If rounding is needed, it needs to be done specifically, for example `minutesToHHMM(round(16248 / 60.0))`  

  * **secondsToHHMMSS(decimal)** Converts the amount of seconds to HH:MM:SS format. For example `secondsToHHMMSS(16248)` would return 04:30:48.  

  * **isAnniversary(**  
<currentDate>,  
<date to test e.g. birthday, contract start date, etc>,  
<years as string CSV that you want to match e.g. "5,10" for 5th and 10th anniversary>,  
<number of days to match beforehand e.g. 14 could be used to remind about anniversaries 2 weeks before the anniversary> **)**  
It will return the matching year e.g. if the current date is the 5th anniversary of the contract start date it returns 5, if not, it returns null.   
**Example:**  
**![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33078355689757)**

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002559178-Hierarchy-of-calculation-settings.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559178-Hierarchy-of-calculation-settings -->

# Hierarchy of calculation settings

The settings in the service work based on different setting levels, so that the setting levels have a hierarchy according to which the settings are inherited from top to bottom. The initial settings are already made during implementation, i.e. they are customized for your own working community and only need to be changed when necessary.
The hierarchy and inheritance of settings are described below.
## Settings in Working community level
The most common rules can be set in the working community level, aka the highest level, for all users. From here they are inherited downwards to setting groups and individual users. You can find these settings in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings**.
## Settings in setting group level
Settings group settings can be used to make exceptions to working community settings. The setting groups are often made, for example, according to the different TES’ used, in which case each setting group has settings according to the TES. Usually, there is also one highest level setting group, for example 'Finland', where you can define rules that affect all users instead of using the working community level.
The settings made in a setting group apply to all its members, unless they have different settings on a lower level (user settings). Settings are inherited from the upper setting group level to the lower setting group, unless otherwise specified on a lower level. The setting group hierarchy is displayed in the setting group list with the lower setting groups indented below the upper. In the example image below you can see upper setting group level "Finland", under which is "7.5h monthly paid, from hour to hour to balance" and then below it three separate part-time setting groups (osa-aika 50%, 60%)".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28386807397917)
In the example picture, the settings flow from the upper setting group to the Part-time groups, unless different settings have been defined in these setting groups. The setting group "8h monthly paid Mon-Sun" is on the same level as "7.5h monthly paid, hourly to balance" and the rest of the setting groups in the list, so the settings are not inherited from each other. The upper level of all these setting groups is Finland and then Working Community level. The settings group settings can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Settings groups > Function: Settings group settings**.
## Settings for persons
It is not recommended to make too many settings behind individual users as it is easier to manage settings from one location (setting group / working community level). Most settings should come from user's setting group. Settings should be made for a single user only in specific situations, such as a lower accrual limit or different annual leave calculations at the beginning of the employment or a temporarily agreed shorter work obligation. All settings must be made using [the validity tool.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358>) User settings can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Persons > Function: Person settings**.
Inheriting settings according to the hierarchy described above works in practice so that when the service checks the settings, it first looks for a setting on the user level. If no setting is defined for the user level, the service switches to the setting group level. If there is no setting on the setting group level, the setting used comes from the working community level.
## Preventing inheriting
Inheritance can be prevented in many different ways, depending on the setting.
  * "Enabled" setting: Some settings have an "enabled" setting. This can be used to prevent settings from being inherited from a higher level by setting the "Enabled: No" in the actual setting group. For example: Allowed working hours are enabled at a higher setting group level, but you do not want them to be valid at a lower setting group level. In this case, you can specify that they are not enabled at that setting group level.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29757335523613)
  * Some settings have an option to select "Do not use parent group setting":  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29757309896989)
  * A text field setting can be prevented from being inherited by storing an empty value in the field header. For example, if you want to prevent the name of a work rise from being inherited to a lower level, you can write some other text in the name field on the lower level, or save an empty field:  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29757309898525)


The exception is integration rules (External Services), where inheritance is prevented by saving an empty value in all three fields: Description, Salary code, and Integration rule.
  * Inheritance of numeric fields can be prevented by clicking the cross icon that appears in the field. For example, inheritance of the length of work day can be prevented this way. In the example in the image, a cross is displayed for Monday, which can be clicked to prevent inheritance. Thursday shows what the setting looks like when inheritance is prevented.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29757309899421)


Please always use the [validity tool](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358>) when making changes in the settings.
If inheritance is prevented, the setting uses the default value in the service. The default value depends on which field is in question. The default value can be a numeric value (for example, the default working day length is 0 hours, unless otherwise specified), or it can mean that the setting is not valid at all. Several default values comply with the Working Time Act. Please note: Default value is not always 0.
## Exceptional settings inheritance
If a setting has been made on the top level with an exception rule, both of these are inherited to the setting groups below. Inheritance continues until something else is saved in the setting on one of the levels - that is, if something is saved in the main setting, the inheritance is broken, and the exception setting is also not inherited. Inheritance continues only as long as nothing is saved in the same setting on a lower level.
If only an exception setting has been made on the top level, this will be inherited downwards. If an exception setting has also been made on the bottom level, this will not prevent the exception from being inherited from the top level, but both exceptions (both the inheritable and the setting made at the setting group level itself) will be valid at the bottom level. Inheritance can only be prevented by giving the main setting a value, or by overriding the exception from the top level by setting the same exception with a different value at the bottom level.

# How can I target overtime basic part and increment part to different overtime targets?

The time exceeding regular work time can be allocated in different ways. Targets can be, for example, compensation hour to hour, overtime to salary or an accrual.
The targets to which the work time will be allocated need to be set visible. This is done either in the worktime setting group settings or working community settings: **Work hours - Accruals and overtime hours - Calculation settings - Overtime - Visible overtime options on event creation**
For example, if you want to target the basic part of overtime hours to **Overtime balance** and the increment part of overtime hours to **Salary** , then you need to set the following option visible by selecting **Yes** to the setting:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20555480239517)
When your desired option has been set visible, it will appear in the list of overtime targets in event creation.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20555480243741)
More information about targeting overtime hours can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002481617>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Event-recording/360002573157-How-do-I-add-an-event-type-that-is-not-on-the-list-of-event-types.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002573157-How-do-I-add-an-event-type-that-is-not-on-the-list-of-event-types -->

# How do I add an event type that is not on the list of event types?

Nepton has a comprehensive selection of [event types](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002520778>). It is possible to define the use and visibility of these event types both in Working community settings and at a setting group level. However, your work community may use event types that cannot be found ready in the service. In such situations, you can [add your own event type](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519157>) to the service, and define its behavior logic. 
A new event type is added through the menu**Work time > Administration > Working community settings > Work hours > Event types** by choosing **Add event type**. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20411875294621)
In the pop-up window, enter a **name** and a **code** for the new event type, and select its **behaviour** logic from the drop-down menu (Behaviour). The behaviour defines that the new event type behaves in the work time calendar in the same way as one of the existing event types. It for example accumulates working hours or is counted as an unpaid absence. 
You should not change the behaviour of an added event after creation.  
Although it is technically possible, the changes also have a retrospective effect and all already saved events using the event type may have to be saved again.
Note! It is not possible to create a new event type that would behave like Lunch or Travel invoice.
It is possible to add translations of a created event type by selecting 'Other languages'. You can add a translation for all the languages supported by the system.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20413135078557)
The added event can be found in the list of event types. **The pen icon** in front of the event type indicates that it is an added event type.
After adding the event type, define also where and to whom the new event type will be visible. In the **Event type administration** settings, you can define if the total time marked for the event type is shown in the calendar view summary, if the event type is shown in shift planning and if overtime pay is targeted exceptionally.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20413135081629)
If you make changes to the event type settings in the working community settings where the new event type was added, the settings apply to the entire working community by default. You can define setting group specific exceptions to event type visibility and other settings in the settings of each setting group. More detailed instructions for enabling and modifying the visibility of an event type can be found in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519157>).

# How do I check a person's balance on a particular day?

If you want to check the balance of a person/persons on a certain day, you can do it using the **Hours by pay salary type** report. The report can be found in **Work time - > Work hours -> Reports ->** select the report **Hours by salary type**. Set the **time period** for the day of which you want to see the balance.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25734715722781)
After this, you can select either one person or several people whose balance you want to check.
After selecting people, click **Show report**.
In the report, the **Balance** field tells the person's balance at the end of that period. It is possible to download the report to Excel, where extra fields can be removed if only the person's balance accumulation is to be displayed on the report.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25734725402653)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Workshift planning | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Workshift-planning/360002575538-How-do-I-create-a-new-location-that-is-used-for-shift-planning.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575538-How-do-I-create-a-new-location-that-is-used-for-shift-planning -->

# How do I create a new location that is used for shift planning?

In order to use shift planning, at least one unit must be established in the service and that unit needs to have at least one location. Once a shift planning location is established, it forms a project to the Worktime section with the corresponding name and code.
This instruction describes a situation in which a completely new location is established under a unit, where the employees work in shifts, and thus there is a need to plan shifts for them to the location.
### Adding a location
**1\. Choose Locations from the main menu.**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20857868896925)  
**2\. Choose the right unit**
Select the unit under which the new location belongs, from the Change Unit section. Once you have selected the corret unit, click the Continue button. If several units have already been established for the service, they can be selected from this list
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20857889383325)
**3\. Locations view and the locations tree**
You can see all the locations that may already be under the unit. If the unit does not yet have a single location, you will only see the New location line.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20857868903709)
Add the new locations by giving the location **a name** , **a calculation unit (code), validity dates** and if necessary, **a category**. Confirm the addition of the location with the Save button.
The category defines the placement of the new location in the location tree. In the example above, the locations Espoon keskus and Leppävaara are under the category Espoo, which means that they are sub-locations of category Espoo. On the right side of the page, you can see the real-time tree structure of the locations:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20857889392797)
It is possible to edit the name, category, calculation unit and validity periods of all locations from the pen button next to each location. If, for example, the category information is incorrect for the new location, it can be corrected. After this, the location also moves to the right place in the location tree.
After adding a new location, always check the location tree on the right side of the page and make sure the location is in the right place.
When a new location has been added, you still need to connect the persons working for the location to it. Follow the instructions of the following article [Why is an employee not visible in the planning view?](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575598>) to make sure that all necessary people are visible in the planning view of the new location.
### Location and the Worktime section projects
The location added under a unit always forms a project with the corresponding name and code to the Worktime section. In the example below, a new location has been created under the name Leppävaara, in the category Espoo.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20858471270301)  
In the Worktime section, by clicking the Projects menu and choosing Project list, the location in question is shown as a project. Work time can be allocated to the project, for example when logging work events.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20858471275293)
If the location and the cost center/project where the actual work events are allocated to are the same, it is therefore not necessary to set up a separate corresponding project on the side of the Worktime section.
  
**Important note: Changes made to locations must always be made on the Locations section using the pen button in front of each location. Changes to locations are automatically updated in the corresponding project in the Worktime section.**

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/360002575558-How-do-I-define-a-setting-that-is-effective-retrospectively-or-in-the-future.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575558-How-do-I-define-a-setting-that-is-effective-retrospectively-or-in-the-future -->

# How do I define a setting that is effective retrospectively or in the future?

In Nepton, it’s possible to define a setting change to take effect not only from the current moment but also retroactively from a past date or in the future. This enables that changes and corrections affecting employees' working hours can be made retroactively. In addition, an employee's transition from one setting group to another can be set in advance for a specific day. When a change is set to take effect on a certain date, it won’t disrupt previous work hour calculations.
## Worktime section
Most of the Worktime settings can be modified retroactively or in the future with [the validity function](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358>) represented by a small calendar icon next to each setting.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20192309641117)
For example, if you want to set the assumed lunch break duration to 1 hour starting from August 1, 2024 (replacing the previous 30 minutes), follow these steps:
  * Click the validity function next to the **Assumed Lunch Break Duration** row.
  * Set an **end date** for the old value (30 minutes).
  * **Add a new setting value** (1 hour) with the desired **start date**.
  * Save your changes in the editing window (saving again on the main settings page **is not necessary**).


**![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20192357804701)**
It is always a good idea to make setting changes using the validity control so that any previous setting history is preserved, and the corresponding calculation does not go wrong due to changing new settings.
When a person's work time changes, for example from part-time to full-time, the person's setting group must be changed. If you want to change the setting group to another starting from a specific day (past or future), you can make this change either in the Worktime or the Employees settings.
In the Worktime settings, the setting group is changed under **Worktime - Administration - Setting groups - Action: Setting group members**. Choose the validity function image next to the person in question and mark the end date for the old setting group and the new date for the new setting group in the window that opens.
## Employees section
In the employees section, a person's setting group can also be defined to change on a specific date by using a similar validity function:
  1. Open the details of the person in question using the magnifying glass icon.
  2. The current setting group can be seen under **employment information**. When you click the setting group menu you can add a new setting group from a date of your choice by choosing **Add**. ![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20194952220189)![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20194952225565)
  3. Save the changes by clicking **Done**.
  4. Confirm the changes with the **Save** button in the lower left corner.


When the change date of the setting group is defined this way in advance, the change takes place automatically on the desired day.
If a retroactive change is made to someone's worktime calculations, the person's balance may not be up to date after the change. This may be alerted by a warning triangle in the person's calendar, which tells them that the balance does not match. In such a situation, the person's calendar should be updated on a day that has already passed, so that the balance is retroactively calculated. The easiest way to do this is to create a Notes event in the person's calendar for the day before the change. Once this is done, the event can be deleted. This is enough to update the calendar calculation to match the retroactive changes made and have the balance displayed correctly. More detailed instructions for updating balances can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4411220910865>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Workshift planning | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Workshift-planning/360002575518-How-do-I-give-a-person-rights-to-plan-shifts.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575518-How-do-I-give-a-person-rights-to-plan-shifts -->

# How do I give a person rights to plan shifts?

The role "Supervisor" or upper role in Employees permissions, gives a person rights to plan work shifts in Planning. Upper roles are Unit manager, Salary management, HR management and Administration. In order to be able to plan shifts, a person must belong to at least one unit and to at least one location of the unit.
### If person needs rights to plan shifts, check the following things:
#### 1\. Person's unit
You can add a unit to a person in the Person's information settings in the Employees section, if he or she doesn't already have it. A person can have several units: one unit is primary and others are secondary. The primary value is only informative.
#### 2\. Person's role in Employees tab
You can define a person's role in the Employees section in the person's information settings. If a person needs only rights to plan work shifts, define role as a "Supervisor". 
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407787602705)
A person's role can be "Supervisor" even if the person does not actually work in supervisor tasks. If the person has subordinates, they need to be defined separately according to [this article's instructions](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005113898>).
When you have defined "Supervisor" or some other upper role for the person, the shift planning tab becomes visible in Nepton.
#### 3\. Person's membership in location of the unit
  1. Go to the shift planning tab and select the unit to which the supervisor belongs to.  
  
![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407795437585)  
  
Unit selection is not shown if there is only one unit in your environment, then page is redirected straight to the location selection.   
  

  2. Select Locations tab from top of page.  
  
![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407788311057)  
  

  3. Select Location, for which the person is to plan shifts.   
  
![mceclip4.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407795999761)  
  

  4. Open the Location Persons menu  
  
![mceclip5.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407796160401)  
  

  5. Add person to the previously selected location using the Add button. You can change the location from top of page using Select location. The person was successfully added, once person's name moves up, underneath 'Location Persons'. Adding person is not needed to save separately.  
  
Location tree follows same principle of inheritance than other settings in Nepton. If a person works in two different Locations, the person can be added to the higher level Location above these two locations. The person is then shown in both location's shift planning view.   
  
The person who is planning shifts might not be intended to be resourced to the planned shifts themselves. This can be bypassed by selecting **No** to the Location resource.  
  
![mceclip6.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407789230097)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / HR management | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/HR-management/360002572937-How-do-I-give-access-to-a-unit-s-work-time-calendars-for-the-unit-manager-or-equivalent.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002572937-How-do-I-give-access-to-a-unit-s-work-time-calendars-for-the-unit-manager-or-equivalent -->

# How do I give access to a unit's work time calendars for the unit manager (or equivalent)?

A supervisor or unit manager gets visibility in the individual employee's work calendar when he is marked as the employee's supervisor. This is done in the **Employees** section by opening the employee's information and selecting the desired supervisor from the **Supervisors** menu.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20523797953181)
If you want to give the unit manager visibility into the calendar of**several employees at once** , you can do this by marking him as a **deputy** for all supervisors in the unit. You can also assign a deputy for the unit manager/supervisor. The deputy gets the same visibility in the employees' work time calendars as the person being substituted has. In this way, the unit manager can see the information of all the persons who are marked as subordinates to the Supervisors and he does not have to be marked as the supervisor individually for each employee.
You can define the deputy in the **Employees** section by opening the information of the desired supervisor and then the Deputy tab. Search for the desired substitute (unit manager) in the Deputy field by name.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20523797961373)
Visibility to the subordinates' work time calendars is always defined for a limited time since you need to choose also the start and end time for the deputy role. Save the changes with the **Save** button.
More information about assigning a deputy can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430678>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Accruals and overtime hours | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Accruals-and-overtime-hours/360002573137-How-do-I-reset-a-person-s-balance.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002573137-How-do-I-reset-a-person-s-balance -->

# How do I reset a person's balance?

The balance is set for example, when the service is first taken into use. The setting can also be made in other situations as needed. The value can be set to any, such as zero or the balance reading accrued from a previous balance value. The balance setting is done on the same day on which it should come into effect. Thus, if the service is taken into use for example, on the 1st of the month, the balance is set for the same day.
Setting a balance gives the service a base value for calculations starting that day.
The balance is set by:
  1. Going to the right person’s calendar view and creating **a new event** for the desired day.
  2. Selecting **"Balance Reset"** as the event type.
  3. Entering the balance by typing it in the New value field. Add a note if needed and press save.


**![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20602988664221)**
Note that in the summary at the end of the week where the balance setting has been made, the balance change shows the difference caused by the change in the balance setting.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20602977101597)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Accruals and overtime hours | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Accruals-and-overtime-hours/360002575698-How-do-I-update-a-person-s-annual-holiday-balance-to-Nepton.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575698-How-do-I-update-a-person-s-annual-holiday-balance-to-Nepton -->

# How do I update a person's annual holiday balance to Nepton?

Usually, the settings for earning annual leave are defined in the Working community settings and employees earn annual leave days automatically according to these settings. The amount of annual leave days earned from previous holiday years or before deployment are **set** according to [this](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002481737>) instruction. The instruction in question is used, for example, when annual leave calculation is deployed in the middle of the year and the accumulated annual leave days from previous holiday years are to be taken into account in the service.
If you want**to add** a person's accumulated annual leave days from the previous holiday year (which they can use during the current holiday year), the change must be made for the last month of the previous holiday year, i.e. 31.3.
  1. Select 31.3. in the person's calendar. **Add Event**.
  2. Select the event type **Annual leave earning change**
  3. Enter the desired number of annual leave days to the **Change amount** , half a day is entered as 12 hours
  4. It is possible to write an explanation for the change in the **Notes** field
  5. **Save** the change


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20767723831581)
After this, the added number of annual leave days can be seen, for example, in the report **Annual leave, usage follow-up**. In the report, the annual leave days added by changing the annual leave balance are now included in the total number of earned annual leave days on April 1st and are available for the employee's use in the current holiday year.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / HR management | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/HR-management/360002575458-How-to-act-if-a-former-employee-returns-to-work.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575458-How-to-act-if-a-former-employee-returns-to-work -->

# How to act if a former employee returns to work?

When a person who previously worked at the company returns to work, their previous credentials should be **restored** for their use. Currently, it is not possible in Nepton to mark multiple separate consecutive employment relationships for one person; the system only supports one employment relationship per person.
You can restore the person’s previous credentials in the **Employees** section:
  1. Enter the person’s name in the search function and select the option **Show deleted** or **Show only deleted** from the Deleted persons field. The person’s information should then be found when you select **Search**. The deleted person’s information will appear in grey.  
  

  2. You can view the person’s information by clicking the magnifying glass icon, or alternatively, you can directly select the red **Restore** button in the list view. After selecting this, the person will be restored as an active user again.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20546355767453)  
  

  3. Remove the end date of the person’s employment (or add a new end date in the future if it is already known) and keep the start date of the original employment. This way, the information from the previous employment will not be lost but will be found in the person’s history and will appear in reports and materials taken from these time periods.  
  

  4. Update other personal information, such as **the setting group** , to match the new employment details. Add the correct setting group to the person’s information with the start date of the new employment. Also, insert an empty value to the setting group for the period when the person was not employed, if this was not already done when the previous employment ended. This way, it will be clear when the employment was not active. Additionally, work time calculations are halted during the period when the setting group value is empty.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20545766658333)  
  

  5. When a person is restored to active status, **the accrual statuses must be checked** in the person's work time calendar. For example the balance may be distorted due to the restoration of the user account. If necessary, you can reset the person's balance by selecting **Add event** at the start date of the new employment in the person's calendar, and selecting**Balance reset** as the event type. Under **New value** , enter 00:00 and click **Save**.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20546355768477)


After restoring the employee's profile, they can log into the system again with their previous credentials. If necessary, you can change the [username](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430838>) or [password](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7025290536989>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Setting groups / Examples for setting up setting groups | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Setting-groups/Examples-for-setting-up-setting-groups/360002559018-How-to-define-settings-for-part-time-work.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559018-How-to-define-settings-for-part-time-work -->

# How to define settings for part-time work

## Different types of part-time work and how to define the settings in Nepton
In Nepton, different types of part-time work can be divided into three categories. However, these three categories can include an endless variety of work obligations. The options on how to define settings for these different kinds of part-time employees are:
  * Utilizing the work time percentage. A separate article about work time percentage can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003961118>).
  * A new setting group for employees who work **shorter days**
  * A new setting group for employees who work **irregular** **shorter weeks**
  * A new setting group for employees who work **regular shorter weeks**


If the current setting group is using [Nepton's shift planning](<https://nepton.com/workshift-planning/>), check paragraph 6.
## Employees who work shorter days
This is a form of part-time work in which a person works the same working days as if they were working full-time, but works shorter days.
An example of this type of part-time work:  
  
The weekly working time of the working community is 37.5 hours and the daily working time is 7.5 hours per day, from Monday to Friday. A part-time worker working 80% of the hours, working a shortened day, therefore works 30 hours a week, six (6) hours a day, from Monday to Friday. The working days are the same as for a full-time employee, the length of the working day is shorter.
This type of part-time work can be defined in the following two ways:
### Work time percentage
You can set a work time percentage for a part-time worker who works shortened days. The work time percentage is set with [the validity function](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004856937>). An empty field is interpreted as a value of 100 %, i.e. full working time.
When the work time percentage is set, Nepton automatically calculates the percentage of daily and weekly work time from the settings of the setting group. The work time is calculated to be evenly distributed over the workind days of the week.
Absences and the minus and plus balance are compared to the person's shortened day and compensated in proportion to the person's work time percentage. The processing of absences and balance hours for those working a shortened day is automatic.
Read more about the work time percentage [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003961118>).
### A new setting group for employees working shorter days
You can create a new setting group for part-timers working shorter days. Instructions for creating a new setting group can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002557537>) (1 Add manually). It is recommended to place the new setting group below the full-time setting group, so that the same settings affecting the interpretation of work time are also inherited to the lower level part-time setting group. Make sure that the correct values ​​are set for the length of the working day ([instructions here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>)) and the length of the working week ([instructions here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558537>)) in the new part-time settings group.
## Employees who work irregular shorter weeks
This is a form of part-time work where a person only works part of the working days that they would work if they were full-time. In an irregular week, the work days are not agreed in advance, or the agreed days vary from week to week.
In Nepton, the work time settings for part-timers who work an irregular shortened work week can be defined in two ways, with the work time percentage or by creating a new setting group:
### Work time percentage
You can set [a work time percentage](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003961118>) for a part-time worker who works irregular shorter weeks. The work time percentage is set with [the validity function](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004856937>).
A recorded absence or balance is compared to the person's shortened day and compensated according to the person's work time percentage. The amount of absence and balance to be compensated at the end of the week is correct if the length of the work week calculated using the working time percentage has been met or hasn't been exceeded.
If the person is absent for a whole week, Nepton calculates a minus balance for the whole week.If the person does double the weekly workload the following week, the minus balances from the previous week are reset and the balance equalizes.
The person in the example below works an irregular 7.5-hour work week. According to the working time percentage, the length of a work day is 1 hour 30 minutes and the length of a work week is 7 hours 30 minutes. The balance is 0 minutes at the beginning of the week.
![osa-aikainen.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20217818894109)
  * The work event on Monday is from 08:00 to 10:30. Work time is two hours. Since he work day length is 1h 30min, 30 minutes is added to the balance.
  * There is no work event on Tuesday. Since the work day length is 1h 30min this 1h 30minutes is deducted from the balance.
  * The work event on Wednesday is from 08:00 to 10:30. Work time is two hours. Since the work day length is 1h 30min, 30 minutes is added to the balance.
  * There is no work event on Tuesday. Since the work day length is 1h 30min this 1h 30minutes is deducted from the balance.
  * The work event on Friday is from 08:00 to 12:00. Work time is four hours. Since the work day length is 1h 30min, 2 hours and 30 minutes is added to the balance. At the end of the work week, a total of 30 minutes has accumulated to the balance.


### A new setting group for employees who work irregular shorter weeks
You can also create a new setting group for part-timers working irregular shorter work weeks. Instructions for creating a new setting group can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002557537>) (1 Add manually). It is recommended to place the new setting group below the full-time setting group, so that the same settings affecting the interpretation of work time are also inherited to the lower level part-time setting group.
[Length of work day](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>) and l[ength of work week](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558537>) are defined for the part-time setting group, and t**he person's work time percentage is not changed**.
The same length of work day is set for all weekdays. In addition, the event type "Weekly leave" should be set as [the assumed event type](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558717>) so that this event will be automatically added to work days without any event. This ensures that the work time calculations are correct in the work time calendar and the part-time worker doesn't get a negative balance.
At times, it may be necessary to use a setting that deducts the difference between the hours worked on a week and the length of work week from balance. 
This setting is '**Borrow at the end of the week if weekly obligation not fulfilled** '. and can be found the setting group setting in **Work hours - Accruals and overtime hours - Calculation settings: Balance**.
Here's an example of a week like this, when a part-timer has two "extra" absence days and these absences should be deducted from the balance:  
  
![FuVVu2qfnQ.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20219880338589)  

If this setting isn't in use, the assumed event "Weekly leave" causes absence days not to be deducted from balande.
## A new setting group for employees who work regular shorter weeks
This is a form of part-time work in which a person works only part of the working days that they would work if they were full-time. In a regular week, the working days are agreed in advance, meaning that the person has an agreed work rhythm. 
[A new setting group](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002557537>) (1 Add manually) is created for employees who work regular shorter weeks. The new setting group is created below the full-time setting group, so that the same settings affecting the interpretation of work time are also inherited to the lower level part-time setting group.
[Length of work day](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>) and l[ength of work week](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558537>) are defined for the part-time setting group and are the basis of the calculation for regular working hours, absences and public holidays. **The person's work time percentage is not changed**. When defining the length of work day and work week:  

  * Length of work day is the same as with full-time workers'. Weekdays that are not work days are set as 0 minutes long.
  * Length of work week is set according to the part-time worker's work week length.


After creating the part-time setting group, it is recommended to test how the public holiday settings and annual leave settings that are inherited from the full-time setting group work for the part-timers. It may be necessary to change some settings for the part-time setting group, in which case the necessary instructions can be found in the articles [Public holiday management](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558797>) and [Setting up annual leave earning](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560698>).
## This to consider when interpreting annual holidays when a person has days without a work obligation
For those working a shortened work week, zero minutes will probably be marked as an obligation for some of the workweek days, i.e. people have days where they do not have a work obligation. These days must be taken into account for annual holidays, because annual leave is not taken if there is no obligation on the working day. Check out the separate instructions for earning annual leave [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560698>), in section 4.4 of the instructions.
## Person's work time when shift planning is in use
A person's work obligation can also come directly from shift planning. In this case, a new setting group is not created, but the published shift list is the basis for calculating absences and work days. By defining [the minimum and maximum obligations](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004769718>) of a person's weekly working time from the employment section, how many hours a person can work per week is defined. Minimum and maximum obligations can be used in shift planning as target numbers to support planning.
## Changing the work week hours in the middle of the work week
If a person's work week obligation changes in the middle of the work week, the service does not automatically identify which work time obligation it should follow in its calculation. Because of this, the correct length of the work week must be calculated and entered manually.
For example: a person works part-time, 80 % of the working time, from Monday to Wednesday. The length of the work day is 6 hours/day. From Thursday, the person will return to working full time (work obligation is 100 %), so the length of the working day is 7.5h/day on Thursday and Friday. So add up the hourly obligation of the working days to get the work obligation for the entire working week, according to the previous example like this:
Monday - Wednesday: 3 x 6h = 18h
Thursday - Friday: 2 x 7.5h = 15h
The total work week obligation is therefore 33 hours, when the work obligation has changed in the middle of the work week.
You can set an exception to the total work week obligation by pressing the date icon in the person's working time calendar and selecting the length of the work week. The "Edit length of work week" view opens in a new window, where you can set an exception setting for the length of the work week.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20221375275805)
## Changing settings for the past
If setting group settings are changed retroactively, the person's accrual values may not be up-to-date in the work time calendar after the change. This may be alerted by a yellow triangle in the work time calendar. In these cases, the work time calendars must be manually updated. Instructions for updating the accruals for one person or multiple people can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4411220910865>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Event-recording/360019808377-How-to-set-event-default-project-to-be-the-planned-shift-s-location-instead-of-the-person-s-default-project.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019808377-How-to-set-event-default-project-to-be-the-planned-shift-s-location-instead-of-the-person-s-default-project -->

# How to set event default project to be the planned shift's location instead of the person's default project?

When an event is created based on a planned work shift, the default project for the event can be set to be the [work shift's location](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015675918>) instead of the person's [default project](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002563098>).
Instructions for creating an event based on the planned work shift can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019808237>).
In [project targeting settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002562658>) you can configurate if events are targeted to a work shift's location or to person's default project.
Configuration can be done either at the **Working community** level or at a **setting group** level.
  1. Select the level where you want to define the settings.
  2. Select **Projects**.
  3. Select the desired setting for '**Target the worktime event to the project of the planned work shift. If "no" is selected, the person's default project is used** '.  
When defining settings, use the validity function (calendar icon), through which you can activate the setting from a date of your choice.


If setting is set to 'No', Nepton uses the default project set in the person's information page in Employees-section.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20440982486557)
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20440998712861)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / Terminal use | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/Terminal-use/24730505042077-How-to-use-Nepton-Flexim-terminal.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/24730505042077-How-to-use-Nepton-Flexim-terminal -->

# How to use Nepton Flexim terminal

This article guides you through how to use Nepton Flexim terminal.
## Main display
By default, the terminal screen is displayed in Finnish. The language can be changed to English or Swedish with the admin PIN code from the terminal's settings (see instructions at the end of this article). When a person logs in, the terminal uses the language set for the person in Nepton.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25046505072797)
On the terminal, the top bar shows Nepton logo, question mark symbol and the current time. Clicking on the question mark opens additional information about the terminal; Terminal ID, software version, QR code for instructions on the support website and the option to restart the device. The Settings button is introduced at the end of this article.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25046492159517)
  
In the middle of the screen, the enabled login options are presented. Login methods are explained in more detail in the next section of this article.
## Logging in
There are different ways to login to Nepton Flexim terminal:
### Logging in with RFID-tag
The tag is shown to the reader, and the user is logged in. Then they can register work time. The tag number must be saved under person's information. A person can have multiple RFIDs saved in their information.
### Logging in with PIN-code
When logging in with a PIN code, the user keys in their own PIN code on the number board, after which they are logged in and can register working hours. The PIN code must be saved in the person's information. Logging in with a PIN code can also be blocked on each terminal, in which case the terminal log in mode would look like this:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25046505090205)
### Quick clocking
Terminals can be set to offer quick clocking mode at the login screen. Quick clocking mode is intended for situations where there are large volumes of people, or where editing of events isn't necessary at the terminal. When quick clocking mode is on, showing your tag to the reader starts a work event from that moment on. If the person has an open event, it ends when a new quick registration starts. If a default project has been set for the person, the work is automatically assigned to this project. When the quick clocking function is enabled, each user can determine whether it is in use or not from the terminal's home screen. Quick clocking method can be used also when the terminal is offline.
## Screen view after logging in
If there already is an active event, it is highlighted in the event menu in blue. This event ends automatically if another event is selected from the terminal and "Start" is pressed.
If nothing is done after logging in, the user is automatically logged out after a 20-second delay. The length of delay can be adjusted in the terminal settings. The delay is shown as a decreasing bar at the bottom of the screen. Above the bar, the current value of two accruals is displayed. There is also a Cancel button at the bottom of the screen, which allows you to return to the previous view, and an Exit button, which allows you to log out of the terminal.
A menu appears at the top of the screen; the first is the event selection, next is the adding work supplements, after that is target for possible overtime and the last is project targeting. The upper right corner shows which user is logged in and what time it is at that moment.
## Adding an event
Once a person is logged in on the device, predetermined events are shown. A maximum of eight events are shown on the screen. If more events have been set to be displayed, the view is split on multiple pages, and the side arrow is used to move to the next page. A new event is started by clicking on the desired event type and then the "start" button. When the event is started, the user is automatically logged out of the terminal. If the terminal is in offline, only quick recording events will be registered.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25047288224669)
### Adding an event with start and end times
The terminal can also be used to add events to the future by giving them a start and/or end time. In order for this to be possible, this option must be enabled for the event type in the user's setting group in Nepton. When an event is activated on the terminal, the "Edit" button appears next to the "Start" button.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25050679289373)
When clicking this a new menu opens, from which you can select the start and end time for the event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25050704703389)
After the dates have been chosen, the next view will let you set the times.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25050679297565)
## Targeting overtime
In the overtime tab the target for overtime can be changed. The options shown are determined in setting group settings. The number of currently active selections is displayed next to the name of the tab.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25047348289565)
## Adding a supplement
Supplements can be added when an event has been started. The supplements tab shows four supplements per page. The side arrow can be used to move to the next page, if there are more than four supplements.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25051729451421)
The type and default values ​​of the supplements come from the settings in the settings group. You can reduce or increase the amount of the supplement either by pcs or by 15 min at a time with quick dials. If necessary, a more precise value can be given by pressing the pencil icon.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25050704711197)
The number of currently active selections is displayed next to the name of the tab.
## Project targeting
From the Projects tab, you can select which project the event is assigned to. The view shows 8 projects on one page. If there are more projects, you can move to the next page with the side arrow. The user is offered the most recently used ones, i.e. the same projects that are offered to the person when creating an event in the browser. With the search function, you can also find other projects by using the project name or code.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25051754348061)
### Project targeting with bar code reader
The project can also be selected with a barcode scanner after the person has logged in on the terminal. After reading the barcode, the event with the project starts and the person logs out of the terminal. The screen shows that event has started successfully.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25052088604317)
If an event is started with a barcode reader with a project that is not yet in Nepton, and the user has the necessary rights, the project will automatically be created as a new project in Nepton (the project will be in the root of the project tree). The necessary rights for this are given by the mid-level rights in the worktime roles "Can create missing projects via terminal barcode reader":
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25051729456029)
## Changing the settings on the terminal
Some terminal settings can be changed directly from the terminal. For this, a management PIN code is required. The settings can be accessed from the terminal's home screen by clicking on the question mark symbol, and from the screen that opens, the "settings" button. At this point, the terminal will ask for a PIN code. If you do not know the PIN code for managing your terminals, please contact Nepton's customer service.
Once the PIN code has been entered, the following management menu opens (please note, the admin menu is only in Finnish):
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25052088605469)
Terminal information is displayed at the top of the screen; serial number, software version and IP address.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25052088606621)
In the menu, you can change the device's local network settings, configure an encrypted server connection, and restart the device. Encrypted server connection is only needed in situations where there is a firewall in use that reopens the connection. On the next page, you can change settings related to the user experience:
Automatic logout delay  
Automatic restart cycle  
Allowing login with a PIN code  
Allowing quick clocking  
Terminal language

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Event-recording/360009227298-How-to-use-Temporary-lay-off-event-type.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360009227298-How-to-use-Temporary-lay-off-event-type -->

# How to use Temporary lay-off event type

The 'Temporary lay-off' event type behaves like an absence. It fulfills the missing work obligation up to the length of the working day but does not accumulate overtime, balance, or other accruals.
## Getting started
When Temporary lay-offs are started, either part-time or full-time, it is usually not necessary to change the length of the work day to reflect the reduced work obligation. This way it is easy to see work and Temporary lay-off in calendar and reports.
## Best practices
We recommend the following approaches for dealing with temporary lay-offs. The examples below handle the most common cases.
If it is necessary to get overtime or accumulated balance recorded during Temporary lay-off, a new event type must be created that behaves like the 'Work' event type. Follow this link for full instructions on how to [Manage and edit event types](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519157>).
The order of events in the calendar impacts how working time is interpreted. If the day starts with a 'Temporary lay-off' event and continues with a 'Work' event, the work will accrue balance/overtime if desired. If the order of these events was reversed, there will never be balance/overtime.
If you use a custom event type, e.g. 'Temporary lay-off in flexitime', which behaves like 'Work', the order of the events does not matter.
The annotated screenshot below shows different examples of Temporary lay-off and their behavior.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20521781565085)
  1. Temporary lay-off in flexitime \- custom event type that behaves like work
  2. Temporary lay-off \- the default service event type that behaves like an absence
  3. Overtime option Overtime - Salary
  4. Overtime option Hour to hour - Balance
  5. Nothing is accrued because the 'Temporary lay-off' event ends the business day and only fills up to the daily obligation
  6. Overtime option Overtime - Balance


If desired, 'Temporary lay-off' events can be reported with, Hours by event type.
![Lomautus_3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360008760198)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/4419112526865-How-to-write-a-good-support-request.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4419112526865-How-to-write-a-good-support-request -->

# How to write a good support request?

Please not, that only organization's Nepton-certified Administrators are entitled to use Nepton's Customer Support services. If you are not your organization's trained admin user, please contact your supervisor or your organization's human resources to clarify the matter.
Nepton Customer Service is available on weekdays from 08:00 to 16:00 at asiakaspalvelu@nepton.fi. A support request can also be sent through our [support pages](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406611917841>) at support.nepton.com (separate registration to the support portal is required).
If you are a certified admin user and about to send a support request to Nepton's Customer Service, please provide us at least the following in your request:
  1. Example person (if possible), in whose Nepton calendar the situation occurs
  2. Example date, when the situation occurs
  3. Description of what happened, what is wrong
  4. Description of how the calculation or situation should be instead
  5. Whether the situation concerns multiple people or just one person
  6. Possible screenshot of the situation


For example:
  * Example person: Adam Smith (you may also provide us user personnel number i.e 123456)
  * Date: Sunday 9.1.2022
  * Description of the situation: Adam has accumulated 5h of evening bonus on 9.1.2022
  * Description how the situation should go instead: Adam should have accumulated 7h of evening bonus on 9.1.2022


This way, we can provide you with the most straightforward assistance possible in interpreting and resolving the situation in our customer service. Remember, that you may never provide us too many details. Giving us too little information may lead into extra questions, which could be avoided by giving extensive amount of information on your first message.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / HR API | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/HR-API/360004855857-HR-API-general-description.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004855857-HR-API-general-description -->

# HR API general description

## Production API description
<https://go.nepton.com/API/SOAPWebService.asmx>
Please also ensure that the necessary IP addresses are opened. Instructions [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360009237257>).
The HR API provides external systems access to certain features and data from Nepton. The WSDL for the API can be found at <https://go.nepton.com/API/SOAPWebService.asmx?wsdl>.
Request are passed as a SOAP request using the POST method. The Content-Type HTTP header is required with value of "text/xml; charset=utf-8".
Guidance for individual topics is provided in the following articles:
  * [Authentication in HR API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406441875089>)
  * [Responses and result codes of HR API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406446686609>)
  * [Persons API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406271660945>)
  * [Units API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406271664273>)


Please note that:
  * The sent XML has to be valid XML
  * Used character encoding is UTF-8
  * API-calls are case-sensitive. Make sure you have typed all upper case letters in a correct way.


The best way to ensure the validity of XML is to use a SOAP library to handle requests and responses. For example [SoapClient](<https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.soapclient>) in PHP and [WCF Web Service Reference](<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/additional-tools/wcf-web-service-reference-guide>) in .NET are viable options.
If you are generating XML without the help of an XML library, you need to keep in mind that the following characters need to be represented as entities:
Character | Entity  
---|---  
`&` | `&amp;`  
`<` | `&lt;`  
`>` | `&gt;`  
If you want to represent password "_HpR9cHN &f8C<_" in XML, it should be done the following way:
[code] 
    <UserPassword>HpR9cHN&amp;f8C&lt;</UserPassword>
[/code]

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Nepton Payroll | path: en-gb/Support/Nepton-Payroll/4408264552977-HR-data-for-payroll.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4408264552977-HR-data-for-payroll -->

# HR data for payroll

The Nepton Payroll service uses personal data entered in the "Employees" section. By adding and maintaining this data, Nepton Payroll operates smoothly and salaries can be paid. Edits are synchronised in real-time, including changes based on validity date (e.g. changes that occur in the future).
## Payment groups
[Payment groups](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406602996625>) are required for Nepton Payroll to function correctly. They are used to automatically generate payroll lists during the payroll process.
Define in Nepton's Employees section:
  * Payment groups - Separate groups for at least monthly and hourly employees, more separation if you wish. 
    * A name for easy identification
    * Code - Provided by the payroll specialist. It links the payment group with payroll ("Payroll template ID" in Palkat)
    * (optional) A supporting description of the group
  * Payment group periods - Each represents a payment to employees 
    * The date range the payment is for
    * The date employees in this payment group will be paid
    * (optional) The date on which this payment is considered in bookkeeping
    * Coming soon: To help with the payroll flow, we plan to add a new date field which represents when events and approvals should be finalised so that payroll specialists can finalise a payroll.
    * Please note: Additional one-off payments are handled by payroll specialists and should not be added to payment group periods.
  * Payment group memberships for the employees 
    * These can be added manually via the person information pages, or with the person import feature, manually or via scheduled integration.


## Person information
The following information is used in payroll processing. These fields must be filled in Nepton for payroll to function correctly. It is recommended to use all the following fields, even if they are not marked as mandatory.
In Nepton's payroll processing, Nepton is considered the master data system. These fields should always be kept up to date in Nepton's Emplyees section, either manually or via integration from another HR system.
Although it is important to keep all personal information up to date at all times, when taking Nepton payroll into use, please make sure that Employment dates, Employee numbers, and Payment groups, are correctly set for everyone, **including past and deleted employees**. This information is used to determine which employees should be included in payroll calculations.
People with employee number 0 (Zero) will not be synchronised for Payroll. This employee number is reserved for special cases, such as accounts used for automation or administration, who do not need to be considered in payroll. It is **not** intended for deleted or past employees. Please read more about deleting people [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002424617>).
**Infromation group  
** | **Field name  
** | **Mandatory** | **Notes**  
---|---|---|---  
Basic information | First name | x |   
Last name | x |   
Email | x |   
Phone number |  |   
Street address |  |   
Postcode |  |   
City |  |   
IBAN | x | Used for payments.  
Personal identity code | x |   
Employment information | Job title |  | Shown on the payslip.  
Classification of occupation | x | Needed for insurance purposes in Payroll.  
Contract type | x |  Monthly salary OR Hourly salary Used for automatic calculations in Payroll.  
Employment start date | x |   
Employment end date |  | If set, employment in Payroll will be ended.  
Work time percentage |  |  Not synced yet! Coming in future release. Used for automatic calculations in Payroll.  
Monthly salary | x | Both monthly and hourly salary are needed for monthly paid persons. Hourly is used for monthly salary employees when hourly deductions and corrects are needed etc.  
Hourly salary | x | Required for hourly paid contracts  
Organization | Payment group | x | Will define which payroll the person belongs to. Used for generating payrolls and defining payment periods.  
## Troubleshooting
If a person's HR data is missing the required information for payroll, that will be indicated as a warning in the [Service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575478>). A full list of the required fields is detailed in the table above.
In the event of missing, invalid, or rejected, values being reported for some fields, all valid information about a person will still be used by Payroll.
If the service log reports an error regarding permissions, such as "Unauthorised" or "Write denied", it indicates the service has not been correctly configured. Please contact customer service and provide them with the date and time of the log indicating the problem.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Salary systems | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Salary-systems/360003501757-IFS-event-approvals.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003501757-IFS-event-approvals -->

# IFS event approvals

## About
Nepton can be configured to send event approvals to IFS. Data is sent when approving or unapproving events. Approval or unapproval will not be saved unless IFS returns a positive response.
A SOAP web service on IFS (or an intermediate system such as BizTalk) is required to send the data to. The WSDL schema for this web service is described below.
## Setup instructions
**1) Set up employees**
The person IDs for the export can be configured in Employees by editing a person's information and clicking on the Identifiers tab and then editing the IFS field. Note that if person's IFS ID is not set, personnel number is used instead.
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/11562524707485)
**2) Configure sending data to the web service**
The used web service end point and company name / identifier sent in the web service request can be configured in Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Integrations > IFS Event approval. If API key authentication is used in the integration, it is set in the same place.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/11562499034909)
Web service endpoint and API key can be set on setting group level as well, from Worktime > Administration > Setting group > Setting group dronpdown: Desired setting group > Action drondpon: Setting group settings > Integrations > IFS Event approval.
## Limitations
  * Persons with personnel number 0 will not be included
  * If approving or unapproving a person's hours could not be processed by receiving end, action is not done in Nepton for that person
  * Single event approvals are not supported as approved / unapproved days are sent instead. To disable approval / unapproval of single events you can turn "Approve events by day" on from Worktime -> Administration -> Working community settings -> Work hours -> Event locking and approval.


## Export trigger
The export is not scheduled but is triggered in real-time when approving or unapproving events. Export is not triggered when approving single events.
## Sent data
Level | Field name | Format | Occurs | Notes  
---|---|---|---|---  
Root,  
under SOAP body | AUTHORIZE_REPORT | XML element | 1 |   
1 | COMPANY | string (20) | 0..1 | Company name / identifier which is given in integration settings  
1 | EMP_ID | string (11) | 0..1 | Employee ID of the employee approving / unapproving events  
1 | AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTIONS | XML element | 1 |   
2 | AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTION | XML element | 0..n |   
3 | START_DATE | date | 1 | Approved from date, format `YYYY-MM-DD`  
3 | END_DATE | date | 0..1 | Approved to date, format `YYYY-MM-DD`  
3 | STATE | string (1) | 1 | Approval state: 
  * 1 - approved
  * 0 - not approved

  
3 | AUTH_ID | string (20) | 1 | Employee ID of the employee whose events are being approved / unapproved  
Request example:
[code] 
    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>  
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:wo="WO.fi.TyoTeho.Schemas.AuthorizationFromTyoTeho">  
      <soapenv:Header/>  
      <soapenv:Body>  
        <wo:AUTHORIZE_REPORT>  
          <wo:COMPANY>CompanyID</wo:COMPANY>  
          <wo:EMP_ID>1230</wo:EMP_ID>  
          <wo:AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTIONS>  
            <wo:AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTION>  
              <wo:START_DATE>2019-06-01</wo:START_DATE>  
              <wo:END_DATE>2019-06-30</wo:END_DATE>  
              <wo:STATE>1</wo:STATE>  
              <wo:AUTH_ID>1240</wo:AUTH_ID>  
            </wo:AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTION>  
            <wo:AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTION>  
              <wo:START_DATE>2019-06-01</wo:START_DATE>  
              <wo:END_DATE>2019-06-30</wo:END_DATE>  
              <wo:STATE>1</wo:STATE>  
              <wo:AUTH_ID>1250</wo:AUTH_ID>  
            </wo:AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTION>  
          </wo:AUTHORIZE_TRANSACTIONS>  
        </wo:AUTHORIZE_REPORT>  
      </soapenv:Body>  
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]
## Expected response
This API requires a direct response for the sent request. Request format is the following:
Level | Field name | Format | Occurs | Notes  
---|---|---|---|---  
Root,  
under SOAP body | Response | XML element | 1 |   
1 | Success | boolean | 1 | Whether sending approvals / unapprovals was successful or not  
1 | Message | string | 0..1 | Optional message, used for error message in case of a failure or returning a list of IFS IDs / personnel numbers for persons whose event approval / unapproval was successful. Personnel numbers are comma separated.  
Response example:
[code] 
    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>  
    <SOAP-ENV:Envelope xmlns:SOAP-ENV="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:ns1="http://WO.fi.TyoTeho.Schemas.TimeReportResponse">  
      <SOAP-ENV:Body>  
        <ns1:Response>  
          <Success>true</Success>  
          <Message>1011,2011,3011</Message>  
        </ns1:Response>  
      </SOAP-ENV:Body>  
    </SOAP-ENV:Envelope>
[/code]
