# Project targeting settings

Project settings can be managed both on **Working community** and **Setting group** levels.
## Settings in Working community level
### Working community level
All other project-related settings in Working community level are under "projects" (Worktime > Administration > Working community level > Projects).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/36217009558429)
**Service enabled** \- Defines whether project targeting is in use. When the service is enabled, Projects menu will appear in the Worktime section.
**How many levels of parent projects are included in the project name** \- If the value is for example 2, are the projects parent and the parent project's parent project names shown.
Below is an example of how the parent projects are shown:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19182786907293)
**Show the project description in the interface** \- Project description is visible both in adding a new event view and when viewing an existing event.  
**Include the project code in the project name** \- Parent and child project codes are shown before the project name as in the picture below:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19183397590813)
**Show only projects assigned to person in the worktime** \- When adding an event, only the projects related to the user or his/her person group are shown. Instructions: [How to add a project to a person or person group.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360006776758-Adding-projects-to-person-or-person-group>)
  * If the value of the setting is "No", all projects are visible to the user, if there are 50 or less projects in total. If there are more than 50 projects, the most recently used ones are displayed.
  * A default project can only be a project that is attached to the person or his/her person group. Instructions: [Setting a person's default project](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002563098-Adding-default-project-to-a-person>).


**Stop active projects when logging out from the terminal** \- The project is terminated when logging out via terminal, and the same project will not continue automatically when starting a new event. If this setting is set to "No", either the default project or the project that was in the last entry will continue in the next event, regardless of who made the entry and whether it was done via terminal or another way.
**Target the worktime event to the project of the planned work shift** \- If the setting is set to "no", the person's default project is used.
**How near to the scheduled shift the event must be recorded in order to use the project of the planned work shift -** When a new real-time event is created, the person's default project is automatically added to it. With this setting it can be set so, that the project added to the event is the project for which the person's working time is planned for, when the person starts their work shift in close enough time to the planned shift. The project will then come from the shift. The amount of time within the work needs to be started before the shift is set in the setting.
The value of his setting doesn't matter, if the setting "Target the worktime event to the project of the planned work shift" has been set to "no". 
**Minimum number of projects users must select for events-** If this is set to bigger than 0, is adding a project to every event mandatory. More about setting projects mandatory in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002561457-Making-project-mandatory-for-events>).
**Maximum number of projects users can select for events-** defines, how many projects can be added to each event.  
**Show the project duration input -** Defines, whether project length can be added to events. Length can be given both in hours/minutes or percentages: ![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19188579174557)
Further instructions for targeting event to multiple projects can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4411705615377-Targeting-events-to-projects-general>).
### Project types
Instructions for Project types and adding new project types are in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002562338-Project-types>).
In this section, each project type can be given a translation to any Nepton use language. Additionally a hint text can be given to project types. The text is shown to users under the heading "projects" when adding or editing an event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/36217009560477)
## Settings in setting group level
Project settings in setting group level can be found: **Worktime > Administration > Setting groups > *select wanted setting group* > Setting group settings > Projects.**
In setting group settings the settings of the projects are narrower than the settings in the working community. In the settings group in the project settings, the number of parent projects displayed in the project name, targeting the event to the project of the work shift, and the accuracy with which the event recording is assigned to the project of the planned work shift can be defined.
Minimum and maximum numbers of required projects and the option for adding the length of the project can also be set for each setting group.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/36217070346653)
## Current Status
The setting for displaying projects on terminals and the Current status view can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Current status.** When this is set to Yes, all new events are automatically targeted to the user's default project, or alternatively by the scheduled shift's project if it is set to be on.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/31526827552541)

# Project types

By default, two project types are available in the service: Customer and Projects. With the help of these default project types work can be allocated based on whether the nature of the work is actual project work (e.g. projects) or, for example, customer-specific billable work. More project types can also be created as needed.
The functionality of project targeting can be used with Pro and Complete service levels.
The various project types can be used when exporting data from Nepton. Such data could be, for example, salary data, absence data or other reports used to monitor worktime. By utilizing the project type, only the necessary data can be reported, depending of course on the final use of the data.
## Adding a new project type
Project types can be managed in Worktime section: Projects > Project type administration.   
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19088203045405)
New project type can be added by selecting "add new project type". Then a project type name is given before clicking "Save". After saving the new project type it is ready to be used.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19088203050781)
## Adding new project type to a project
Instructions for adding new projects can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560877-Add-project>).
When a new project is added it can also be added to a project type. In the example below, a project called Testi2 is added to a project type Demo types. This can be done in Work time > projects > project administration.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19088176480285)

# Project visibility

By default, projects added to the service are visible to all users. Projects can be made visible individually or by person group. This way, you can say that only certain projects are visible to members of certain groups of individuals. To enable this, the setting "Show only projects assigned to person in the worktime" must be enabled in the **Worktime > Administration > Working Community / Setting group Settings > Projects** section:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29888736944157)
If you want all individual projects to be automatically available when they are added to the project structure, only the top-level project is added to the person or person group. If a subproject in the project structure is added manually, the new subprojects are not automatically updated to be visible to the person.
## Setting a project visible to a person
A project can be added to the person in **Worktime > Administration > Persons**. Select the person and Person's projects as action. In the left window, select the projects you want to attach to the person and click **Save**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29888733596189)
## Setting a project visible to a person group
A project can be set visible to an entire person group at a time, in which case it will be visible to all members of the person group. Go to **Worktime > Administration> Person groups > Person group projects**. Select the person group and select Person group projects as the action. Click on the projects you want to assign to the person group in the left window and press **Save**. Please note that the visibility of projects works on the same principle as [inheritance of settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559178>). A project set for a parent person group is inherited downwards in the person group structure until something else is defined for the subgroup, which blocks the inheritance.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29888733596701)
When user adds a new event both person and person group projects will be shown to them in the menu. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29888733599005)

# Providing a mobile link to a person

The instructions below are only for organizations that still use old mobile link to record events. All organizations are recommended to follow new [Login to Nepton mobile](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002602598>) -instructions.
Only admin users can see mobile links in Nepton. Mobile links are personal and they can not be changed. 
Only send links to persons who have the right to record events in mobile. 
1\. You can find user's mobile link in Employees section in Persons. Open the person's details from the  
magnifying glass and open additional functions tab. 
2\. Click on the mobile link.
3\. Copy the user's personal link from the address bar.
4\. Send the link via e-mail to the user.
5\. The user opens the e-mail in mobile and can then save the link to the mobile device as a bookmark or shortcut.
6\. The user can now use mobile link to record events. ![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4412308749841/mceclip0.png)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002558797-Public-holiday-management.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558797-Public-holiday-management -->

# Public holiday management

The service allows you to configure settings for each holiday. In the settings, you can determine whether the holiday is displayed in the calendar and whether it has calculated effects on working hours or compensation.
## Defining settings
Settings can be configured in **Worktime > Working community/Setting group settings > Work hours > Public holidays**. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815153260957)
### General settings
The first settings define how public holidays affect working hours.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815128299677)
The "Treat working on public holidays that shorten the week as" setting determines what happens if work events are recorded on a public holiday.
**Normal day** = All work recorded to the public holiday is handled as it would be normal working day. Calculations are done according to work day length and balance is deducted when working less than the work day length. In shiftwork shifts can occur on public holidays and should be treated as normal working days.  
**Additional work** = All work recorded on public holiday is handled as additional work, however depending on defined [additional work settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559438>).   
**Daily- / weekly overtime** = All work recorded on public holiday is first weekly overtime, and then daily overtime, once TES maximum work day length has been crossed.  
**Daily overtime** = All work recorded to the public holiday is directly daily overtime. 
It is important to notice which overtime target is used when calculating work on public holiday. Such as if work which is targeted as "Hour to hour - Balance", overtime is not automatically interpreted by increment percentage.
If work recorded on public holiday is wanted to be compensated hour by hour, 'Treat working on public holidays that shorten the week as' should be set as "Daily / weekly overtime" or "Daily overtime", depending on how work on public holiday should be compensated if work is targeted as overtime to salary. 
With setting "**Public holidays shorten work week by** " you can define, whether public holiday should shorten work week length by daily obligation, weekly obligation or maximum weekly obligation. The setting is described in more detail [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005058217>).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815128301085)
Please note! Public holiday shortens work week max 8 hours per one day.   
  

The setting "**Show public holiday compensation** " defines whether a possible compensation is shown on it's own row in calendar view or not. The compensation is determined by the settings in "Public holidays: Show/Earn compensation/Shorten workweek". The compensation is based on length of work day.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815153265053)
### Fixed compensation
The settings in this section allow you to define a fixed compensation for public holiday compensation. The first setting determines whether the fixed compensation is in use, and the second determines the amount of the compensation. Exception settings can also be used in both settings, for example if fixed compensation is not in use at all on a certain day, or there is a different amount of compensation on a certain public holiday. The compensation is linked to the "compensation is earned" setting in the public holiday table. For example, if you want to earn 8 hours of public holiday compensation for every public holiday on weekdays, regardless of work obligation, the settings would be set as follows:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29941749970461)
And in addition, for each holiday that constitutes compensation, "Earn compensation: Only on weekdays".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29941739136029)
In this case, an 8-hour compensation will appear on every public holiday that falls on a weekday:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29941739136925)
The image above shows that a 12-hour fixed compensation is created for public holidays that fall on a weekday, but no compensation is created for Boxing Day, which falls on a Saturday.
### Public holidays that shorten work week, shorten...
You can also define how work week shortening on public holidays behave and which determination of the length of the working week they shorten.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815153265309)
**Shortening of work week and border of overtime**
If work week is wanted to be shortened, but not the border of the overtime, then values should set as:
  * TES work week length = Yes
  * TES maximum hours of work per week = No


If also the border of overtime is wanted to be shortened, then values should be set as:
  * TES work week length = Yes
  * TES maximum hours of work per week = Yes


All these three settings can have [exceptions,](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560677>) which are valid only on certain days.
The third setting, "Weekly overtime threshold if earned before TES max week length" does not matter, if it is not set in the TES settings (Work hours > TES). 
### Public Holidays
The section lists the days in the service that can be defined as public holidays. There are three separate settings for each holiday; "Show", "Earn compensation" and "Shorten work week".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815128306589)
The setting "Show" defines, how the day is shown in the worktime calendar.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815128307357)
If set to **No** , the day in question will be displayed in the calendar like any other day (white background).  
If set to **As important day** , the day in question will be displayed in the calendar with a red title highlighted (white background).  
If set to **As public holiday** , the day in question will be displayed in the calendar with a red title and a red background.
The picture below displays first a day set as "no" (normal day), then a day set as important day, then a day set as public holiday:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815153271325)
**Earn compensation** setting defines, whether a compensation is paid for said day. The options are:  
No  
Only on weekdays  
Only on days with work obligation  
Only when public holiday shortens work week  
Always
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815128311837)
In order for the compensation based on the selected settings to be displayed in the calendar, the "show public holiday compensation" setting must also be set to "yes". The compensation is based on length of work day.
**Shortens work week** setting defines if the work week shortens during the week in which the public holidays falls. The options are:
No  
Only on weekdays  
Only on days with work obligation  
Always  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26815153274397)
Other settings related to shortening the work week can be found above the table.
## Shortening work week length in the beginning of the week 
Public holidays and annual leave can shorten work week already in the beginning of the week. Then for example if public holiday or annual leave is on Friday, the work week is shortened on Monday. 
The setting can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Working community level/ Setting group settings > Work hours >****TES.** ******  
**
![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4418085218193)
## Public holiday settings for planning
If the planning is in use, the settings for the public holidays can be defined in the **Employees** section. Planning settings can be found from **Employees > Administration > Settings > Planning**. A shortened length can be specified for the public holiday and whether a daily work obligation is added in addition to the planned work. You can find more detailed description of the shift planning public holiday settings and calculation in the planning view [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360017908457-Planning-view-calculations>).
[code] 
    ![Screenshot 2024-05-24 133249.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/19084930368285)
[/code]

# Public key-authentication

If Public key authentication is used, the username/password login method is not available.
**NOTE: Following are not possible via Public key -authentication**
  * **Import of personnel information to Nepton**
  * **Export of personnel information from Nepton**
  * **Export of payment groups from Nepton**


Other data transfers can utilize RSA public key authentication. In this case only Nepton service can connect to SFTP server.
Define suitable username and leave password undefined.
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360013442138)
Both public and private keys have already been created by Nepton Service. You can download the public key from the bottom of this article. Please note that there are several versions of the public key in different formats. You must select the public key version based on the target system or application requirements.
Deliver the public key and your defined username to SFTP service administrator.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Servers and data protection | path: en-gb/Support/Servers-and-data-protection/18904657842973-Public-Testing-Servers-aka-PTS.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/18904657842973-Public-Testing-Servers-aka-PTS -->

# Public Testing Servers (aka PTS)

Not to be confused with a Customer testing environment, which is your own dedciated space for tests and practice. Public Testing Servers (aka PTS) are intended for cooperating with invited stakeholders on the development of features, and the testing of more complex changes that require external services (e.g. SSO). To facilitate specific goals, data and software versions in PTS often change between sessions and as such they are considered volatile. They are not suitable for everyday customer testing needs.
If you are invited to use these servers, it will be for a specific time period, and you will be given detailed instructions on how to gain access.
If you're interested doing testing or practice of your own, please see the Customer testing environment article for more details.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event types and absence types | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-types-and-absence-types/7074461491101-Quick-start-events.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7074461491101-Quick-start-events -->

# Quick start events

Quick start events are a customisable, convenient, and quick way for employees to record fully or partially prefilled work events in Nepton Mobile. Available at working community and/or setting group levels they can be used by all employees in a single click.
## Configuration
If quick start events are not configured, quick start shows by default the users default event type and lunch if user is permitted to record those types of events.
Quick start events are configured for Working community and/or Setting group levels, and can make use of inheritance. See the related settings respectively in **Worktime > Administration > Working Community / Setting group Settings > Work hours > Quick start events.**
Note that when configuring quick start events, the fields and options available are context-sensitive, and therefore might be different when configured at the working community level vs. setting group level. For example if working community level has a quick start event configured which includes a supplement that is not available for certain setting group, the members of this setting group can record an event based on the quick start event but are not able to use the supplement they are not permitted to set.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32929142855837)
A new quick start event is added by clicking "Add quick start event". This opens up the event editing form, but instead of recording an event, this is used to save the event as a template that people can use when they quick start that event.
Each quick start event requires a title, which is used for displaying it when listing quick start events. Titles should be descriptive so that people can recognise and distinguish them without reviewing all their details.
If projects are enabled, a selection is visible for whether the quick start event should include default project. If this is checked, then recording an event from the quick start event will automatically include the recording user's default project to the recorded event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32929132213789)
"In use" - columns selection defines whether quick start event is enabled or not. Newly added quick start events are in use by default. If it is required to disable a quick start event, it can be set by selecting "No" in the "In use" - column. "In use" supports setting inheritance so if a quick start event should be shown for a parent setting group but not shown for a child setting group, "In use" can be set to "Yes" for parent setting group and then "No" for child setting group to achieve this.
Quick start event can be deleted by clicking the X button in the "Delete" column.
If a travel invoice quick start event is created, if you want to add trip dates and durations, and the quick start event will have the travel and trip dates prefilled based on the current date and the saved duration. If trip dates and durations are not meaningful for the quick start event, they can be left empty.
![20221129-quickstart-events-guidance-e3.PNG](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7985939150621)
Note that some event types like event requests, travel invoices, and administrative ones, can not be directly started even if they are in the quick start menu because they always have more details needed from the person recording them. The "Start" button is not shown for these, instead they can be opened by clicking "Add" button for editing before being saved/started.
Also if a quick start event has something configured that the person is not permitted to add, quick starting is not possible but instead a work recording based on the event can be done by clicking "Add", where user is asked to check the items that were present in the quick start event that could not be used in their event. See troubleshooting - chapter below for more info.
### Languages
The name of the quick start event can be translated into languages used in the organization. This way, the quick start event is displayed according to the user's language preference. When editing the quick start event, a 'Other languages' button appears next to the Name field, allowing you to create translations for different languages.
![quick-start-language.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32028611863325)
### User permissions
The permissions assigned to the work time role of the user affect the way events can be created using the quick start events. The minimum permissions required for a user to create an event with a quick start option, is the permission to review own events and the permission to record real time events (both basic level permissions). The permission to edit events allows user to modify the entry during creation or after starting it. You can read about the worktime roles [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002554338>)
## Use
Quick start events are shown both in mobile and calendar view.
### Mobile view
Quick start events are shown in user's mobile view where they can:
  * Record an event based on it by clicking "Start" if the event can be clocked by the person
  * Click the quick start event name which opens the event editing form and person can record their event having prefilled values from the quick start event.
  * If an event can not be quick-started, a recording based on the event can be added by clicking "Add"


![20221129-quickstart-events-guidance-e4.PNG](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7985902575005)  
_Quick start shows a list of configured quick start events. Events can be quick started by clicking "Start" or opened for editing by clicking the quick start event title._  

![20221129-quickstart-events-guidance-e5.PNG](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7985940809501)
 _Event editing form opens with prefilled values based on the quick start event._
### Calendar view
Quick Start events can be used in calendar view by clicking on the date. A new window will pop-up with the quick start events under the Add event function. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32929142860573)
When clicking on the quick event, a new event editing window will pop up. The event is already pre-filled with the quick start event information, but it can also be manually edited or directly Saved.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32929132215709)
Alternatively a quick start event can be started by clicking on "Start":
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/32929132217117)
In which case the pre-made event starts from that second and is active until ended.
## Troubleshooting
If a quick start event is set up in a way that it is set for a person, but includes preset values that are not available for the user to set (such as a supplement that is set to be not used anymore, overtime target that is set to be not in use anymore or a project that has already been completed), quick start view will indicate this with an info icon and an event can't be clocked based on it. The event can still be opened for editing with "Add" button. The values that could not be set for the user are defaulted, i.e. if there was an overtime target not available, it uses default overtime target and if there was a supplement that could not be set, it is not included in the event editing form.
![20221129-quickstart-events-guidance-e6.PNG](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7985941262493)
_If event can not be quick started, it will have an info-icon next to it. It can be opened for editing by clicking "Add" - button._
![20221129-quickstart-events-guidance-e7.PNG](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7985904113949)
_When opening an event, person is informed of fields they should check before saving the event._

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-recording/16574372856221-Real-time-event-recordgins.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/16574372856221-Real-time-event-recordgins -->

# Real-time event recordgins

Events can be recorded in Nepton in real-time or before/after the time of the event. Events recorded in real-time are distinguished from events recorded in advance and afterwards by the Building and Clock icons. The icons are displayed in connection with the event in the Events in calendar view and in the approval of events.
If the real-time recording has been done with a Nepton Touch or Nepton Flexim work time terminal, this is indicated by the Building icon. If the real-time recording has been done on another device (e.g. a mobile phone, via a browser or with a Nepton Rugger work time terminal), the Clock icon is displayed.
If the event has not been recorded in real-time, the icons will not be displayed regardless of the device on which the recording was made. Accepting the event or editing the data (excluding the time) does not affect whether the event is interpreted as real-time. If the time of a real-time recorded event is changed afterwards, the recording is no longer real-time and icons are not displayed in connection with it.
## Event recorded in real-time with a terminal
If an event is recorded in real-time with a terminal, the event will have a Building icon next to it, such as in the image below:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/16574746111773)
By clicking the event more information is displayed such as description that the event is recorded in real-time with a terminal.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/16574746122397)
## Event recorded in real-time with other device than terminal
If an event is recorded in real-time with some other device than a terminal, a Clock icon will be displayed next to the event, such as in the image below:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/16574746134685)
By clicking the event more information is displayed, such as description that the event is recorded in real-time.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34907298021277)
There must be at least 1 minute between events recorded in real time, in order for them to be interpreted as separate events.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Reporting / Worktime reports | path: en-gb/Support/Reporting/Worktime-reports/360016836978-Realized-work-hours.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360016836978-Realized-work-hours -->

# Realized work hours

The report Realized work hours is created according to model 2 found on the online service of the Finnish Occupational Safety and Health Administration, in which the effect of holidays and vacations raising the maximum amount of working hours has been eliminated.
Report for realized work hours can be located in **Worktime > Work hours > Reports > Realized work hours.**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27329625164829)
Report time period is set by adding the dates into the Time period - fields and the time period is freely selectable. The report calculation adjusts to the selected time period. The period must have at least one day between Monday and Friday. Users are selected with the Select users - tool. The report can have multiple users or user groups. The report is generated by clicking "Show report".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27329625166877)
The report shows the realized work hours per day for the report period and also provides a breakdown of additional information that is described in the next paragraph.
The day columns show the realized work hours for that day. Absences are presented with a letter code, the letter codes are:
PH = Public holiday  
SL = Sick leave  
AH = Year leave  
A = Absence  
WSL = Work time shortening leave
Note! Travel time outside regular working hours is not included in the hour amounts shown in the report.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27329636849437)
**Total hours worked** \- column shows the compensated working hours of the report's time period.  
Any event type that is paid,
including
  * paid absence hours with reduced salary,
  * additional work,
  * overtime (including time that is compensated to balance or another accrual),
  * sick leave and
  * absences


but excluding
  * unpaid absence hours, 
  * public holidays (paid days off on Mon-Fri) or annual leave
  * time borrowed from balance or other accrual.


**Regular time without absences** \- column shows all regular time without absences in the report period. This includes paid time during normal daily or weekly working hours according to employment contracts. This also includes hour to hour if it's targeted to salary. This excludes any paid time recorded with event types under absences event type category.
For example, these are _not included_ : 
  * Paid time with reduced salary
  * Time automatically borrowed from accrual, such as borrowing from balance because person didn't record enough time for the day
  * Public holidays (paid days off on Mon-Fri)
  * Annual leave


**Total overtime** \- column shows the total overtime of the report period. Only overtime and additional work where the increment part is paid to salary is included. Hour to hour is not considered overtime so it is not counted here.
**Holidays equal to work time** \- column shows the amount of annual leave that is equal to work time in the report period. Report will count the work day lengths from holidays and show them on the report. If workday length for a day is more than 8 hours, only 8 hours are calculated.
**Time equal to work time** \- column shows the sum of Total hours worked and Holidays equal to work time. The column can be used in checking that the maximum amount of work in working time law is not exceeded.
**Average time equal to work time per week** \- column is calculated by dividing the time equal to work time by the amount of 5-day weeks in the report period. Public holidays that are on weekdays are taken into the calculations. For example if a report period has four full weeks and one weekday, the time equal to work time is divided by 4,2.
**Amount of absence days** \- column shows the amount of days in the reporting period which have working obligation and an absence. Even if a day has only a short absence, it is calculated as one absence day.
**Amount of work days** \- column shows the amount of days in the reporting period which have working obligation.
**Accrual balance value on xx.xx.xxxx** \- column shows the persons accrual balance on the final day of the reporting period.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27329625170589)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-recording/33334659658525-Recording-absences.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/33334659658525-Recording-absences -->

# Recording absences

Absences are added to Nepton in the same way as other events. Depending on the settings, absences can be added in the worktime calendar, in the current status, on mobile or on worktime terminal. Some absences can be recorded in advance also on the terminal, depending on the settings. Some absences may be event requests that require approval before the entry is created in the calendar.
## Recording absences in calendar view
Absences are recorded in the calendar in the same way as Work entries. Click on the date and select “add event”. Select the correct event type from the Add event window. The event types are divided into the categories “Work”, “absence” and “administration” in the menu, the latter of which is only visible to the administrator or other person who has been granted rights to administrative events. Basic users usually see events in the “Work” and “absence” categories. Select the correct absence event from the menu and save it like any other event. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047306248989)
Long absences can be marked by start and end dates, and there is no need to make separate entries for each day. Absences only cover the regular time of the day (or how each absence is defined to behave), so even if the absence entry itself is longer than the work obligation of the day, it will not earn, for example, balance or overtime. Long absences appear in the calendar as a daily entry with the start and end days times. By clicking on an event, its total duration is shown.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047322855453)  

## Sick leave
Some ansences, like Sick leave, have additional fields that appear when the absence type has been selected. The right to edit these fields depends on the person's worktime role and permissions. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047306260125)
In the **Additional info** field you can choose the type of the sick leave. The options are Sick, Child sick, Accident at work, Accident while commuting and Accident in free time. These default fields can't be modified.
In the **Medical certificate** field you can enter the status of medical certificate: Not known, Not received, Received, Permission from supervisor. These default fields can't be modified. Medical certificate - field is visible for only roles that have the permissions to see or edit this field. Usually these roles are for payroll and administrative personnel. 
In the **Reason code** field you can enter for example doctor's given reason code or other code used in your company. Reason code - field is visible for only roles that have the permissions to see or edit this field. Usually these roles are for payroll and administrative personnel. 
**Compensation** field is used to define the compensation of the absence. 
**Earns vacation days** is chosen as a default, but it can be unticked.
**Notes** field can be used to write a message to the supervisor or person who approves the absence.
Sick leave hours can also be targeted to a project like any other event when creating or modifying the event.
Sick leave certificates cannot be saved in Nepton. This is because the certificates contain health information, which is considered special personal data according to the GDPR and the Finnish Data Protection Act.
## Annual leave
Annual leave can also be found in the menu under the Absence category, and it is recorded in the same way as other events. When recording annual leave, the service calculates by default how much of the annual leave balance is used by the absence in question, and how much is left after the event. The calculation can be turned off in the [annual leave settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560698>).
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047306261277)
The entire holiday period is recorded as one event. The event must include the last Saturday used. Sundays do not consume the accrual if the settings have defined Mon-Sat as annual holiday days. If a day does not consume the accrual, it will be displayed in gray colour in the calendar:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047322862365)
The accrual value is only displayed if the annual leave is registered for the future. The value of the Annual Leave accrual is not displayed in connection with an Annual Leave event that is scheduled for the past or for the same day, or is already in the calendar. A person can view their available annual leave days using the 'Annual Leave Usage by Season' report.
Annual leave hours can also be targeted to a project like any other event when creating or modifying the event.
### Working during annual leave
Sometimes it is necessary to work during annual leave. Working during annual leave is generally interpreted as overtime.
If work during annual leave should be interpreted as overtime, the work event must be recorded at the same time with Annual leave in calendar. For example, if Annual leave event is recorded 8:00-16:00, Work event needs to be recorded between 8:00-16:00, for example 12:00-13:00. Then the work event is targeted automatically to person's default overtime target.
In this example person's overtime target is 'Hour to hour - Balance', so one hour moves to balance as a result.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047322864413)
If the work event is recorded outside of the Annual leave event (partly or entirely) Nepton interprets that work is done and the annual leave for the day is ignored. Then person earns minus balance, because person's daily working hours (work obligation) are not met. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047306272925)
If a workday has both annual leave and work events that are equal in lengths, the recording that was first made will be interpreted.
Please note: If a clocked event is logged at the same time as annual leave (or any other absence), the annual leave event will end as the clocked event begins. If Emergency Work is recorded on annual holiday, it is always interpreted as 100% overtime.
### Getting sick during Annual leave
According to the Annual Leave Act, there are six deductable days of sick leave during annual leave. If you become ill during annual leave, the annual leave event is shortened so that the days of sick leave remain as annual leave. The days of sick leave are not considered annual leave for the purposes of interpretation. The remaining time is recorded as sick leave.
## Accrual leaves
An event type "accrual leave" has been automatically created for each accrual in use. For example, if balance accrual is used in the settings group, the event type menu also includes the events balance leave (as well as the administrative events balance setting and balance change). When accrual leave is used, the work obligation is fulfilled for the duration of the event/ length of work day from the accrual. The administrator can change the [settings ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005073918>)to specify which event types are in use and how they behave, as well as which days are considered accrual leave.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35047322869917)
When you record accrual leave, the service calculates the impact of using the accrual leave on the accrual balance according to your settings. The value of the accrual leave is only displayed if it is recorded for the future. The value is not displayed for accrual leave that is scheduled for the past or the same day, or for an accrual leave that is already in the calendar.
## Absence requests
Some absences may have been set as event requests. In this case, the person can record the absence as an event, but it will wait for approval from a supervisor before it becomes a confirmed event. More about event requests in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360017787717>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / Terminal use | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/Terminal-use/360002593398-Recording-an-event-with-a-project-using-the-terminal.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002593398-Recording-an-event-with-a-project-using-the-terminal -->

# Recording an event with a project using the terminal

## Recording an event
  1. Identify by showing your tag to the RFID-reader or entering your PIN-code to the terminal. Terminal displays the login methods selected in the Working community settings. 
  2. Select the event type you want to start. Event type changes from grey to blue once it is selected.![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4408164721937/mceclip0.png)


## Recording a project
  1. Select 'Target' from top of the page to access project list.
  2. Terminal shows the available projects as a list. Select the wanted project. You can also search for the project with 'Search'-function from the bottom of the page. Terminal shows only those available project which are set to be viewed with terminal.
  3. When you have selected the project, click blue 'Select' button from bottom right corner.
  4. Selected project will move to list. With 'Select' button from bottom of the list you can add other projects to the event, then event is targeted to multiple different project simultaneously. 
  5. When you have selected wanted project or projects you can click 'Start' button.
  6. After clicking 'Start' - button, event is started with wanted projects and terminal is ready to use for next person. 


![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4408172028561/mceclip2.png)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Event recording | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Event-recording/360017110497-Recording-events-general.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360017110497-Recording-events-general -->

# Recording events - general

This article is about general principals about recording events to Nepton when work time is performed unequivocally. 
Recording events can be descripted as follows:  
1\. Start work day, record event type Work-Start  
2\. Go to lunch, record event type Lunch break-Start  
3\. Continue work day, record event type Work-Start  
4\. Finish work day, record event type Work-Stop
In the beginning of the work day record Start and at the end of the work day record Stop. All other events of the day can be done with Start record. Nepton ends the previous event automatically when new event is started.
This is how continuous event chain is gained and work time can be interpret unequivocally. If events are not in continuous chain, for example automated lunch break does not form right. 
The easiest way to use event recording is to use above descripted real time recording. There are several options to use real time event recording: [mobile](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002602638-Add-an-event-using-Nepton-mobile>), [terminal](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002593338-Start-an-event-using-the-terminal>) and [Current status](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002603258-Recording-events-in-current-status-view-or-terminal>) -view. Events can be also recorded real time in Events in Calendar or Events in table view.
Note: Events should not be saved more than four years into the future, or there may be errors in recording real-time events or event requests.
## New event start time logic
You can set a default Start and End time for an event in the [Rendering options](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360008777997>). When adding the first event for any day, whether in mobile or calendar, Nepton will suggest a default start and end time for the event based on the rendering options. If no default start and end times are set, Nepton will suggest a default times of 0800-1600 for the event.
If there is already an event on the current day and another event is added to the same day, Nepton will suggest the current time as the default start time for the event.
If there is already an event on the day in the past or future and another event is added to the day, Nepton will suggest the end time of the previous event as the default start time for the event.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/29995759457821)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / Terminal use | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/Terminal-use/360021083038-Recording-overtime-using-a-terminal.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360021083038-Recording-overtime-using-a-terminal -->

# Recording overtime using a terminal

This article contains instructions which will take effect when the terminals of your company have been updated to version 2.14 (on Week 6/2024 or later).
Work time exceeding regular time can be targeted to one of the accruals or to salary in the same way as in worktime calendar view.
Under heading **Work hours - > Accruals and overtime options -> Calculation settings -> Overtime** the setting _Can set overtime target on terminals_ must be set to "Yes" on either the working community or setting group settings.
![Can set overtime target on terminals setting under Calculation settings and Overtime titles](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15872112509341)
The compensation can be set either as hour by hour or as overtime and offer different kinds of combinations of targeting base hours and overtime hours to accruals in use or to salary. These options are under the **Visible overtime options on event creation** subtitle (note that the picture below does not list all of the possibilities).
![Example of available overtime targeting options like](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15874065697821)
In addition to these settings the accruals selected must also be in use under **Work hours - > Accruals and overtime hours -> Accrual is in use** title.  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879925507869)
It is possible to set different default overtime options for different event types under **Work hours - > Event types -> Exceptional overtime pay target default** title for _Base part (Terminal)_ and _Increment report (Terminal)_.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879948749213)
In addition, in the worktime role the person logging in has should have the correct settings for setting the overtime targets _Hour to hour_ and/or _Overtime_ for their own events. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879925524125)
When the settings have been made in worktime, there will be a new tab "Overtime" on the Terminal when a person is starting or stopping activity.
When starting activity, the overtime tab appears after the activity type has been selected:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879925531933)
Similarly, when stopping activity, the overtime tab appears after the activity type has been turned off:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879948775197)
In the overtime view the overtime can then be targeted to one of the options available for the selected activity type.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879948782237)
When switching from one activity to another, it is important to look at which of the activities the selected overtime target option is targeting. It is stated above the options either for the ending activity:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879948791965)
or the starting activity:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/15879948796317)
To make sure the overtime is targeted for the correct activity, **it is recommended that the ongoing activity is first stopped** settings its options and **pressing the Stop button** , log in again and set the options for the starting activity only after that.
As an alternative, the overtime options can be targeted for both activities separately during the same login session in the following order:
  * unselect the stopping activity
  * select Overtime tab
  * check and, if necessary, select the overtime target for the **ending** activity (check from the title)
  * (select possible time options, project targets and supplements)
  * _recommended step:_ press Stop and log in again to make sure only the ending activity is targeted
  * select Work tab again
  * select activity type for the starting activity
  * select Overtime tab again
  * check and, if necessary, select the overtime target for the **starting** activity (check from the title)
  * (select possible time options, project targets and supplements)
  * press Start

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Setting groups / Examples for setting up setting groups / Leveling period | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Setting-groups/Examples-for-setting-up-setting-groups/Leveling-period/4410641911825-Reductions-for-public-holidays-that-shorten-the-work-week-during-the-levelling-period.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4410641911825-Reductions-for-public-holidays-that-shorten-the-work-week-during-the-levelling-period -->

# Reductions for public holidays that shorten the work week during the levelling period

These instructions explain how public holidays falling within the levelling period are interpreted in work time calculations. Similar to other working time arragements, it is possible t o define how public holidays are treated when they fall within the levelling period. The settings for interpreting public holidays in the levelling period can be found under setting group settings **Work hours - > Accruals -> Levelling period hours -> Reductions to levelling period limits on public holidays**.
The interpretation of public holidays is usually already defined in working community settings, but if needed, it can be specified separately in the levelling period settings group under **Work hours - > Public holidays section**, with instructions available [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558797>).
Public holidays that shorten the work week can be set to reduce the following levelling period limits:
  * Maximum regular working time
  * Maximum additional work
  * Maximum 50% overtime


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28583919038749)
More detailed instructions on configuring overtime calculation in the levelling period can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4410630282257>).
### Example 1
A two-week levelling period with the following limits:
  * Additional work is earned after a total of 75 hours
  * 50% overtime is earned after a total of 80 hours
  * 100% overtime is earned after a total of 100 hours
  * Hours are no longer compensated after a total of 300 hours


And the following public holiday reductions:
  * Maximum regular working time: 7,5 hours
  * Maximum additional work: 0,5 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime: 2 hours


The levelling period includes two public holidays that shorten the workweek, for example, Good Friday and Easter Monday. The public holidays would reduce the levelling period limits as follows:
  * Additional work earned after: 60 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 7,5 hours
  * 50% overtime is earned after: 79 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 0,5 hours
  * 100% overtime is earned after: 96 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 2 hours


### Example 2
A two-week levelling period with the following limits on work days in period:
  * Average length of work day: 7,5 hours
  * Maximum additional work compensated per day: 0,5 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime compensated per day: 2 hours
  * Maximum 100% overtime compensated per day: 10 hours


And the following public holiday reductions:
  * Maximum regular working time: 7,5 hours
  * Maximum additional work: 0,5 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime: 2 hours


The limits for the entire two-week period would be:
  * Maximum regular working time: 75 hours
  * Maximum additional work: 5 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime: 20 hours
  * Maximum 100% overtime: 100 hours


The levelling period includes two public holidays that shorten the work week, for example, Good Friday and Easter Monday. The public holidays would reduce the levelling period limits as follows:
  * Maximum regular working time: 60 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 7,5 hours
  * Maximum additional work: 4 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 0,5 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime: 16 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 2 hours


### Example 3
If the outcome of Example 1 is to be aligned with Example 2, the public holiday reductions must be set as follows:
  * Maximum regular working time: 7,5 hours
  * Maximum additional work: 8 hours
  * Maximum 50% overtime: 10 hours


Then the public holidays would reduce the levelling period limits as follows:
  * Additional work earned after: 60 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 7,5 hours
  * 50% overtime earned after: 64 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 8 hours
  * 100% overtime earned after: 80 hours, holiday reduction 2 x 10 hours

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: HR management / Person details management | path: en-gb/Support/HR-management/Person-details-management/9001809419037-Reform-of-personal-identity-codes-on-1-9-2023.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/9001809419037-Reform-of-personal-identity-codes-on-1-9-2023 -->

# Reform of personal identity codes on 1.9.2023

Effective 1.9.2023, [**personal identity codes are being reformed**](<https://dvv.fi/en/reform-of-personal-identity-code>) by the **[Digital and population data services agency](<https://dvv.fi/en/individuals>).** The reform requires new intermediate characters as indicated below:
  * For those born in or after 2000, the current A or the new B, C, D, E, F.
  * For those born in the 20th century, the current hyphen (-) or the new letters Y, X, W, V, U.


Personal identity codes that have already been issued will remain unchanged.
Nepton has enabled new intermediate characters in the personal identification code field. 
Nepton allows different character strings to be saved but gives a warning/notification about a potentially incorrect format. If the personal identity code itself is correct, this warning can be ignored.
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/9034345193757)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/10067038494621-Regular-time-over-work-day-length-earning-threshold.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/10067038494621-Regular-time-over-work-day-length-earning-threshold -->

# Regular time over work day length earning threshold

In Nepton's settings, under [the length of work day](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558417>), there are settings "Regular time over work day length earning threshold" (Worktime > Administration > Working community/Setting group settings > Work hours > Length of work day), which can be defined according to [event types](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002520778>). The setting's is typically used with event types that normally accumulate only regular work hours up to the length of the work day, for example sick leave and travel time. The setting can for example, allow 9 hours of working time to be earned from sick leave, even if the length of the work day is 7 hours 30 minutes. The setting limits the maximum amount of work time that can be earned. Another typical use for the setting is Travel time, when time exceeding regular work hours needs to be [directed in the balance](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559737>).
## Settings
The setting will display a field for each event type that is in use in the deployment.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22005059119645)
**Regular time over work day length earning threshold - "Event type"** \- Enter the value that
is the maximum work time threshold for earning with this event type. For example, if 2 hours worktime should be earned from travel time after the regular time is filled, would the value be 2 hours + the length of the workday (7,5 hours in this case) = 9,5 hours. In this case, travel time can be earned until the day's work hours have reached 9.5 hours. 
**Of which is unpaid** \- the value defines, how many hours are unpaid before worktime is earned after the length of work day.
The setting doesn't enable earning a set amount of hours per event type, but it limits earning per event type when the day's work hours have reached set limit. If there are also hour to hour work done on top of regular hours, earning for event type decreases accordingly.
## Use case examples
Few examples of how this setting can be used can be found below.
### Travel time
By default, "travel time" only accumulates regular hours. If work time should also be earned after the day's obligation has been fulfilled, you must set the correct value for the setting. As an example, a case where you can earn 3 hours of travel time on weekdays and 12 hours on weekends to balance. The length of the working day is 7.5 hours, so the settings would be set as follows:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22005059125917)
Then, on work days travel time can't earn worktime after the work hours have reached 10,5 hours and at the weekends 12,5 hours.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22005029209373)
  * Thursday 10.10.: First a full work day of 7,5 hours has been done, which follows by 2 hours of travel time. No hours have been limited, because the total hours of the day don't exceed 10,5 hours.
  * Friday 11.10.: First a full work day of 7,5 hours has been done, which follows by 5 hours of travel time. Only 3 hours are earned from travel time, because by then the maximum hours of 10,5 have been reached.
  * Saturday 12.10.: The day has only travel time 14h. Only 12 hours go to balance as that is the maximum set in the setting.


### Sick leave
By default, "sick leave" only accumulates regular hours. If work time should also be earned after the day's obligation has been fulfilled, you must set the correct value for the setting. As an example, a case where the length of the work day is 7,5h, but sick leave can be earned up to 9 hours. One hour is unpaid time.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22005715543197)
  * Regular time over work day length earning threshold = 9:00
  * Of which is unpaid = 1:00


Sick leave earning would go as follows:
  * 07:00 - 15:00 -> 7,5 regular hours (includes 30 min unpaid lunch break)
  * 15:00 - 16:00 -> 1h unpaid time as set
  * 16:00 - 17:00 -> 1h regular time over work day length earning. Worktime can be earned up to 9 hours.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22005715545245)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Workshift planning and Work schedules / Units | path: en-gb/Support/Workshift-planning-and-Work-schedules/Units/360019523197-Removing-a-unit.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019523197-Removing-a-unit -->

# Removing a unit

## General
Units are used in many parts of Nepton service and removing a unit might have undesired effects. Please check all the related information mentioned in this guidance before removing a unit.
## Check locations
A unit should not be removed if there are any locations under it that have not been removed. You can check if there are any locations for the unit from Locations. Select Change Unit tab, select the unit from Unit Selection and click Continue. You should now see the locations of the unit. If there are locations for the unit, you should check for each location if the location is still needed. The locations are displayed as a hierarchy tree:
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360019349497)
If you plan to remove a location, you should make sure no location under it is needed either. Existing locations under a location can be moved under another location by changing the category. However, locations cannot be moved to another unit, so if any of the locations are needed, the unit cannot be removed.
### Locations in workshift planning
If your working community is using [workshift planning](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/sections/360000934137>), the location may be needed to group people to plan shifts for in [shift planning by location](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360015675918>). You can check if there are people assigned to a location from Planning > select Change Unit > select the unit from Unit Selection > Continue > select the location from Location selection > Continue > select Locations tab > select Location Persons. If there are any persons under Location Persons heading, you should check if they should be assigned to another (unit and) location.
## Check Worktime projects
If a unit has locations created under it, there are corresponding projects automatically created to Worktime matching the names and codes of the units and locations (for locations the project code matches the calculation unit of location). These projects may be used like any other projects to target work to and the may have been assigned project managers - [see more information about Project management](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/sections/360000707398>). When deleting a location, the corresponding project will also be deleted and it cannot be used to target work to. Also, after the project has been deleted any work targeted to it cannot be retrieved from Worktime using project reports. You can check if there is work targeted to a project using different reports under **Worktime > Projects > Reports**.
## Check persons in unit
You can check if the unit has been assigned for persons as their unit from **Employees > Units > select unit > Unit Persons**. Before removing persons in this view you should consider adding the persons to another unit. See [Add persons to the unit](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002595478>).
## Release the unit code for future use
We strongly recommend changing the code of the unit before removing the unit. You can use a format that would never be used for normal unit codes. For example, you could prefix the code with REMOVED_, e.g. REMOVED_1000.
## Removing unit
After resolving all the possible issues that might prevent removing the unit (see previous steps) and after you've renamed the unit code (see last step before this), you can remove the unit via **Employees > Units > select Unit > (check that you've selected the correct unit) > Additional functions > Remove**.
After removing the unit a message 'The unit has been deleted' is displayed. If at this point you notice you've pressed the Remove button accidentally or there is still some additional checks you've not done, you can click **Restore**. The unit will be restored to use.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Events | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Events/360003135257-Removing-events-created-with-integration-file-import-or-by-copying.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003135257-Removing-events-created-with-integration-file-import-or-by-copying -->

# Removing events created with integration, file import or by copying

In this article, events imported via file refer to events that have been imported using the _Tools > Import events _functionality.  
Events imported or copied via file can be deleted in bulk if the data is incorrect or the same data has been imported multiple times. Deletion is carried out using the **Related events** function or by selecting the events you wish to delete.
1\. Navigate to **Worktime > Work hours > Events in calendar.**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34350069202973)
2\. Select the event you wish to delete.
3\. Select **Related events** , which will display the events that were created at the same time as the selected event. With the top checkbox (next to the Event ID field), you can select all events at once. The name of the import file is also displayed if the events were imported via _Tools > Import event data_.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/34350069203613)
4\. **Delete events** deletes the selected events.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360008777997-Rendering-options.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360008777997-Rendering-options -->

# Rendering options

Rendering options can be set either in working community level or setting group level. Settings can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings / Setting groups > Work hours > Rendering options. **
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33609136850589)
The following settings can be configured here:
  * Whether basic pay information is shown in the calendar or not (working community level only). By default, the setting is always on. If this is set to no, the calendar view is simplified and the interpretation of working time is not displayed in the view.
  * On which calendar day the events and the interpretation of working hours are shown. Options are:
    1. Salary is shown on the day it is earned.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33609122675485)
    2. Salary earned is shown on the day the shift starts.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33609122677021)
    3. Salary earned is shown on the day the shift ends.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33609136854557)
Default value for setting is 'Salary earned is shown on the day the shift starts'. If day has planned work shift it is used when determining on which day events are shown. In the example below setting value is 'Salary earned is shown on the day the shift ends'. Work event continues to the next day but planned shift determines on which day events are shown.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33609136857373)
It is worth noting that the selected setting also affects the day on which the weekly rest compensation is calculated. If the setting 'Salary earned is shown on the day the shift ends' is used, the interpretation of events recorded at the end of the week will always be transferred to the following day - and following week. In order for such event entries to be taken into account in the calculation of the weekly rest compensation, the weekly rest compensation is not formed until the following week (usually on Monday).
  * In addition, you can specify the default business hours that the service suggests when creating a new event. When a new event is created, it automatically has the start and end times set here. The user can change the default times for each event. Unless otherwise specified, the service suggests a default start time of 08:00 on current day and an end time of 16:00 on current day.
  * Default business hours can be set for each event type separately. This can be done by setting the hours for each event type in the Event type specific default start and end times - section. First the event type that requires to have specific business hours is selected from the dropdown and Add - button is clicked. After that specific start and end times can be set for this event type.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33609122680605)

# Reporting a problem with a terminal

**Sorry!**
This article has not been translated yet.
Pahoittelemme, mikäli työaikapäätteenne on vikaantunut. Pyydämme tekemään vikailmoituksen, jotta asia saadaan kuntoon mahdollisimman pian. Vikailmoituksen voitte tehdä asiakaspalveluumme ([asiakaspalvelu@nepton.fi](<mailto:asiakaspalvelu@nepton.fi>)) tai sopimusyhteyshenkilöllenne.
Vikailmoitus tulee tehdä yhteisöllenne toimitettujen ohjeiden mukaisesti joko pääkäyttäjille, palveluntarjoajallenne, yhteisönne IT-osastolle tai suoraan Nepton-asiakaspalveluun. Varmistathan oikean toimintatavan yhteisönne pääkäyttäjältä tai esimieheltäsi.
Vikailmoitusta tehdessä pyydämme ilmoittamaan seuraavat tiedot:**  
**
**\- Laitteen ID-numero tai sarjanumero**  
Laitteen ID-numeron saat selville laitteen näytöltä. Jos laitteen näyttö on pimeänä, ei ID-numeroa välttämättä pysty toimittamaan. Tällöin pitää toimittaa laitten sarjanumero, joka löytyy Nepton Touch -pääteistä laitteen takapuolella olevasta tarrasta (659-alkuinen numero). Idesco-päätteissä sarjanumero on laitteen sisällä, emolevyllä olevassa tarrassa (nelinumeroinen).  
  
**\- Laitteen fyysinen sijainti**  
Laitteen sijainti on hyvä toimittaa. Yhteisöllänne saattaa olla käytössä useampi työaikapääte, joten pyydämme ilmoittamaan mahdollisimman tarkan sijainnin. Sijainti on hyvä ilmoittaa esimerkiksi muodossa  _Kotikatu 1 A, 00100 Helsinki, 3. kerros, sisääntuloaula.  
_  
**\- Milloin vikatilanne on alkanut?  
** Ilmoitathan mahdollisimman tarkasti ajankohdan, jolloin laitteessa havaittiin vikatilanne ensimmäisen kerran. Tämä auttaa selvittämään voisiko vikatilanne liittyä esimerkiksi palvelun päivitykseen tai muuhun vastaavaan.  
  
**\- Tarkka vikaseloste**  
Millä tavalla laite on viallinen? Alkoiko vikatilanne yllättäen vai pikkuhiljaa? Onko vikatila jatkuva, vai toimiiko laite välillä normaalisti?   
  
**\- Oletteko tehneet toimenpiteitä laitteelle tai ympäristöön, jossa laite on  
** Ilmoitathan myös, jos olette jo tehneet jonkinlaisia toimenpiteitä laitteelle, esimerkiksi jos laite on käynnistetty uudelleen. Myös esimerkiksi mahdolliset yhteisönne omaan verkkoympäristöön tehdyt muutokset on hyvä huomioida ja ilmoittaa meille. Tämä auttaa meitä selvittämään vikatilan juurisyytä.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Reporting / Worktime reports | path: en-gb/Support/Reporting/Worktime-reports/4410571913873-Reporting-Accruals.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4410571913873-Reporting-Accruals -->

# Reporting Accruals

In the service, various [accruals](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005073918-Implementation-of-Accruals>) (e.g., balance, working time shortening leaves) can be tracked. Accruals can be reported using various reports. This article describes the different possibilities for reporting accruals.
## Reporting Balance
Balance can be reported using [ Managerial balance changes](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548917-Balance-event-report>) report.
The total amount of balance at the requested time can be seen in several different reports, such as the [Realized work hours report](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360016836978-Realized-work-hours>)
See also the instruction [how do I check a persons balance on a particular day](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575818-How-do-I-check-a-person-s-balance-on-a-particular-day>)
More information about the reports used for balance reporting can be found [in this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548557-Worktime-reports>)
## Reporting Worktime shortening leave
Worktime shortening leaves can be reported using the [Worktime shortening leave](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548777-Work-time-shortening-leave-report>) report.
## Reporting Annual leave
Reporting the amount of annual leave is possible using the [Annual leave ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548717-Annual-leave-reporting-aka-Holiday-or-Year-leave-report>)reports.
## Reporting all Accruals in one view
If a report of **all available accruals** is needed, it can be done using the [Realized work hours ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360016836978-Realized-work-hours>) report. This report shows the status of all accruals on the last day of the selected reporting period.
You can also see the value of all accruals in the [Event request](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360017787717-Event-requests>) view. This view also shows the value of the annual leave.
