<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002559637-Supplements.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559637-Supplements -->

# Supplements

Supplements can be used to record various lump sums or reimbursements. These are configured as items that can be recorded and reported in pieces, time, or decimals, which are then [recorded as part of an event](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002596797>). Reimbursement of[ travel invoice](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004773818>) expenses and kilometer reimbursement of the travel invoice route are handled with work supplements.
##  Inheritance and deactivation of work supplements
Each work supplement has its own number. It should be noted that if, for example, settings are made in work supplement 1, they will be inherited according to the normal hierarchy of settings. Inheritance can be prevented and the work supplement disabled.
This is done by setting Enabled for the work supplement to be "No" in the desired setting level (e.g. working community, setting group hierarchy, or at user level)
## Setting up work supplements
Work supplements can be set up in Worktime section at either the **Administration > Working community settings > ****Work hours > Supplements** or **Administration > Settings groups > ****Work hours > Supplements**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35339999687581)
From the Supplement settings, you can review the configured work supplements. For each supplement that is in use, a name is shown. Supplements without a name are not in use. If the name is in italics, at least _some_ of its settings are inherited from the upper-level setting group. If the name is shown in bold, all related settings are configured at the currently viewed setting level.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35339999693213)
## Supplement settings
The purpose of the work supplement and more detailed information are configured in the work supplement's settings. The settings control the visibility of the work supplement in event recording.  
Below is a list of the work supplement settings and their effect upon the platform.
**Enabled**  
Whether a work supplement is enabled or not. This setting can be used to prevent the settings from being inherited from a higher level.  

**Name**  
Work supplement's name, free text. The name is displayed in the person's user interface as well as in reports. 
**Salary code**  
The salary code of the work supplement. The salary code can be exported in integrations and it can also describe, for example, the accounting account of the expense item of the travel invoice.
**Visible in week tables**  
Determines whether the supplement is visible in user's 'Events in calendar' and 'Events in table' view. The supplement is always visible in the reports. If supplement is not displayed, it can still be recorded normally and exported with integrations.
**Visible in terminal**  
Determines whether supplement can be recorded with the work time terminal.
**Unit type**  
Work supplement's unit. The unit can be hours, pieces, decimal, currency or days. In addition to the user interface, the information affects in which column the information is exported in integrations.
**Default value when added**  
The default value that the work supplement has when it is selected for the event. If you are recording the event in Current Status view or Terminal and the Supplement has a default value, Supplement is automatically added to the event.
NOTE. If the supplement is used for lunch supplement and it is possible to choose from several options, this setting must be left blank.
**Unit name**  
The unit of the work supplement that is displayed in the user interface. The value of the setting overrides the default of the platform unit and the given unit is displayed in user interfaces and reports. If the unit name is not specified, the fixed unit name of the platform is used.
**Supplement input interval**  
Define in which parts the work allowance should be recorded. For example, for a time-based supplement, it can be specified that the data is recorded in full 15 min increments. The input interval is used for recordings made with the current status view or the working time terminal.
**Increase accrual with duration**  
If the recorded supplement is to affect the accruals, the accrual to which the effect is applied is selected.
**Increase accrual in accordance with rate of increase**  
Set the percentage of the increase of recorded supplement in the accrual value. The percentage can also be negative, reducing accrual as supplement is recorded.
**Supplement is used**  
Set in which context supplement is used. The options are:
**Not set** \- If the setting is not inherited from upper levels then the work supplement is used as a 'normal work supplement'.
**As a normal supplement** \- Work supplement is available for events other than correction, lunch and travel invoice events.
**In correction events** \- Work supplement is available for correction events.
**As a lunch supplement** \- Work supplement is available for lunch recordings on a cafeteria terminal.
**Travel invoice trip reimbursement** \- Work supplement is available for travel invoice events as an expense line.
**Travel invoice travel day allowances** \- Work supplement is available for travel invoice events as a travel day allowance. For example, daily or partial daily allowance.
**Travel invoice other expenses** \- Work supplement is available for travel invoice events as route compensation. For example, own car kilometer allowance alone or company car limited benefit kilometer allowance.
**Supplement comment field**  
It is possible to choose whether a comment field is displayed when entering the work supplement and whether the comment is mandatory. For example, the comment field can be used to describe the explanation of a receipt in the expense line.
**Supplement date field**  
It is possible to choose whether a date field is displayed when entering the work supplement and whether the date is mandatory. For example, the date field can be used to describe the transaction date of the expense receipt.

# Supported browsers

Nepton service works on all modern browsers. Nepton does active development regarding new browser versions so that the service will always work as well and as fast as possible.
To get the best experience from the Nepton service and to maintain your security, you should always use a modern, actively maintained and developed browser with it's newest product version.
Nepton tracks service usability specially across these browsers:
  * Apple Safari
  * Google Chrome
  * Microsoft Edge
  * Mozilla Firefox
  * Opera


Service does not support Internet Explorer browser. Usage of this browser is not recommended.
Service does not use Flash or Java applets.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / Events | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/Events/360003736798-Sympa-sending-absences.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003736798-Sympa-sending-absences -->

# Sympa sending absences

Absences from Sympa can be imported to the service. A csv-file must be created on the SFTP server. Creation timestamp must be in the file name. Timestamp is added to the end of the file name. This ensures that the previous file will not be overwritten for example when receiving end is not run according the import schedule.
The file is saved in UTF-8 encoding. Records are separated by semicolons (`;`). The line feed character is a UNIX line feed character `LF`. By default, this line break consists of almost all information systems.
The data does not contain a title row. In the data, one absence and its validity periods are presented on one row. The absence file must be generated from Sympa so that only new absences (type uusi) and/or deleted absences (type poisto) that have been created since the last absence import are present on the file as their own rows. The setting "Amount of days to rewrite in the past" has no effect when using Sympa absence import, as all the absences on the file are handled according to their type (poisto/uusi).
Rows in the file are processed in _sequential_ order. For example if the first row inserts a new absence on Jan 1st and then the second row removes an absence on Jan 1st, then it will remove the absence it had just created. For this reason, if the import data is spread across multiple files you should ensure that users don't exist in multiple files at the same time, or if they do, that those files are in the correct order (we process the files from the SFTP server in the _chronological_ order they were created in).
## Configuration
**1\. Setting person identifiers**
Person's identifier can be set by editing person's employee number in **Employees** \- **Person's information** \- **Identifiers**
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22448508792477)
**2\. Setting event start and end times**
Events created by the Sympa import will be created with the dates specified in the file import and the times as specified in the Worktime settings (Worktime > Administration > Working community settings/Setting groups-Setting group settings > Work hours > Rendering options > Work hour event default start time/Work hour event default end time). 08:00 - 16:00 will be used if no times are specified.
Note: if [expected work times](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002558617>) are in use, events will be created based on the times of the expected work times.
**3\. Setting absence / holiday codes and SFTP settings**
Absence / holiday codes and SFTP settings can be configured in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings/Setting groups-Setting group settings > Integrations > Sympa**. If an event type has multiple possible codes, these can be set separated by a comma.
Note that SFTP settings are only available in working community settings.
### Import schedule
The schedules for the automatic import can be defined in **Work time > Administration > Working community settings > Integrations > Schedules**. You can read more about the schedules in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/10510800700573>)
### Importing start and end times
It is possible to import the start and end times with the 7th column being the start time and the 8th column being the end time. To enable importing or partial day absences, the following needs to be set in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Integrations > Sympa**:
![sympa-absence-import-settings.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/11161885698205)
#### Event start and end times with partial day absences
If the start/end times are present in the import file, the will be used as the start/end times.
## File format
If the imported file has more than 6 columns, the import will ignore the extra ones. If the
Below is a description of the data and their additional information.
Column | Data | Description  
---|---|---  
1 | Employee number | Employee number  
2 | Absence / holiday code | The codes are defined in the service UI under Sympa settings. If code does not exists then absence is created as holiday.  
3 | Type |  Whether the row is a deletion or a new row. Accepts the following values:
  * `uusi` or `false`
  * `poisto` or `true`

Type 'uusi' will create the absence. Type 'poisto' will remove the absence.  
4 | Vacation period | This is only present in holidays, in absences it is empty. Saved as description. Please surround the column in quotes if there is a risk the value could contain semi-colons.  
5 | Start date | Absence start date, format `DD.MM.YYYY`  
6 | End date | Absence end date, format `DD.MM.YYYY`  
7 | Start time | Optional field, absence start time, format `HH:MM`  
8 | End time | Optional field, absence end time, format `HH:MM`  
Example of the file can be seen below:
[code] 
    445;101;uusi;;02.05.2016;04.05.2016;  
    445;103;uusi;;03.05.2016;06.05.2016;08:00;16:00  
    445;101;poisto;;02.05.2016;03.05.2016;  
    445;200;uusi;"vacation period, something something";01.06.2016;28.06.2016  
    445;200;uusi;"vacation period, something something. Wrong dates on previous one";06.06.2016;02.07.2016  
    445;200;poisto;"vacation period, something something";01.06.2016;28.06.2016
[/code]

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / New terminal setup | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/New-terminal-setup/6231723616925-Take-a-new-terminal-into-use.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6231723616925-Take-a-new-terminal-into-use -->

# Take a new terminal into use

The instructions below will help you get terminals up and running in a customer environment. If you haven't ordered your new terminals yet, please contact your service provider.
Before the terminal arrives you can already save the RFID tag identifier in each employee's information. Please see the guidance [here.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002425517>)
Once your new terminals have arrived, you can follow the steps below to get the device connected, online, and ready for end-users. If any step is unclear, or you simply need some help, please contact your service provider.
## Nepton Touch
### Setup steps
**Before starting:** you will need an active customer environment configured on the Nepton platform. If you need assistance with this, please contact your service provider.
**1)** Unpack the device. You should find the following parts:
  * Quick start guide paper
  * Terminal
  * Power adapter and extension cord
  * Adjustable wall mount & flush wall mounting brackets


**2)** Connect and power on the device
  * Connect an Ethernet cable that provides access to the internet
  * If the device is supplied with an external RFID reader, connect it to the USB connector next to the Ethernet cable
  * Connect the power adapter to the terminal
  * Connect the power adapter to a power source. The terminal will automatically turn on. 
    * There is also a power button on the top of the device if needed


The terminals do not directly support PoE power supply, but the use of PoE requires at least the purchase of a separate PoE splitter, which divides the network cable into a power cord and a network cable. These are connected to the Nepton Touch terminal. In addition, the use of PoE naturally requires that the network cable be powered. This may not be the case by default. To enable this, a PoE injector should be installed. The required equipment according to the PoE+ standard can be obtained directly by the customer or partner or they can be purchased through Nepton.
![20220810_101619s.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/6260761122717)
_Power and Ethernet connections_
![20220810_095248s.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/6260761115421)
_Power button - The terminal powers on automatically whenever a power source is present, even after a powercut_
**3)** The terminal software will automatically start and attempt connecting. Once it has established a connection, it will automatically update to the latest version of the terminal software. If it is necessary to assign a **fixed IP address** to the device, the instructions can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7132764025373>).
  * It is normal for the device to initially appear offline during startup, and also to restart and show multiple different windows during the automatic update and deployment process. New desktop shortcuts will also appear as the first-time setup is carried out. This process can take several minutes.
  * If the device continues to indicate it is offline for more than 15 minutes or encounters other problems, please see the [Connectivity troubleshooting](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002588757>) article and contact your network administrator


The terminal will acquire an IP automatically, but if you need to manually configure a specific one, or find out it's network information, please see the [Find or edit a terminal's network information](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360007577678>) article.
**4)** Once the device has started and updated, it will wait to be linked to a customer environment, by organisation Nepton administrator.  
While waiting, the terminal will show it's assigned terminal Id on the screen. Take note of this number for use in the next step. If at this point there is already a login view on the screen, go to step 7.
**5)** Link the device to the customer environment using the terminal Id.
  * Login to **Nepton as an administrator** , and visit Employees > Administration > Terminals.
  * Under the 'Add' heading, enter the new terminal's Id and click the 'Save' button
  * See [Add a terminal](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004790097>) for more information on this step.
  * If you have any problems with this step, please contact your service provider


**6)** After being added to the customer environment, the terminal will automatically download settings so that it can be used by the end-users. It can take a little time for the terminal to receive this change, and it may automatically restart during this step.
**7)** Once connected to the customer environment, the terminal will show the login screen. It is recommended that the device and software are tested with at least one user. If the terminal is not working as expected, please check out the [terminal troubleshooting articles](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/sections/360005896337-Troubleshooting>).
For end-users to log in to terminals and make records, they must have the method of identification linked to their personnel data in Nepton (PIN code or RFID tag number).
**8)** For the best experience and performance, mount and adjust the angle of the device using the included wall mount, and remove the protective films from the touch screen and reader. These usually come away easily just using your fingers.
It is also possible to install the terminal in a vertical position (Portraid) and the operating system supports this, but the service is not designed to scale to that display format.
If the terminal is supplied with an external RFID reader, attach it with double-sided tape over the device's built-in reader module, the point marked in yellow in the picture.
![Attaching_RFID_reader.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7108911705245)
The terminal is now ready for use! It is configured to automatically update and start the terminal software and will show the terminal login screen when ready.
### Troubleshooting
Having trouble with one of the setup steps? Please check out the [terminal troubleshooting articles](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/sections/360005896337-Troubleshooting>).

# Take a terminal into use (Hardware models before September 2022)

The following instructions are intended for hardware models delivered before September 2022.
For the latest instructions please see the dedicated article [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/6231723616925>)
The instructions below will help you get terminals up and running in a customer environment. If you haven't ordered your new terminals yet, please see [Order a new terminal](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003612837>).
Once your new terminals have arrived, you can follow the steps below to get the device connected, online, and ready for end-users. If any step is unclear, or you simply need some help, please contact your service provider.
## Setup & Getting started
**Before starting:** you will need an active customer environment configured on the Nepton platform. If you need assistance with this, please contact your service provider.
**1)** Unpack the device
  * If you are setting up an Idesco device, you will need to remove the external cover on the rear, and feed cables through the rubber gasket to the inputs inside. See [Idesco hardware setup (Wall mounting)](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003778457>) for more information.


**2)** If you have an external RFID reader, connect it to one of the terminal's USB ports
**3)** Connect an Ethernet cable, that provides access to the internet, to the terminal
**4)** Unless utilising Power over Ethernet (PoE), attach the device to a power source
  * Not all terminals support PoE. Please consult your device's technical documentation. At the moment only Idesco Touch devices support PoE power supply.
  * PoE requires the other end of the Ethernet cable to be connected to PoE switch or injector. Otherwise, the terminal will not get power from the Ethernet cable, even if it does support it


**5)** The device will automatically startup and attempt connecting. Once it has established a connection, it will automatically update to the latest version of the terminal software.
  * It is normal for the device to initially appear offline during startup, and also to restart and show multiple different windows during the automatic update and deployment process
  * If the device continues to indicate it is offline for more than 15 minutes or encounters other problems, please see the [Connectivity troubleshooting](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002588757>) article and contact your network administrator


**6)** Once the device has started and updated, it will wait to be linked to a customer environment.  
While waiting, the terminal will show it's assigned terminal Id on the screen. Take a note of this for the following steps.
**7)** You can now link the device to the customer environment using the terminal Id. Login to Nepton as an administrator, and visit Employees > Administration > Terminals.
  * Under the 'Add' heading, enter the new terminal's Id and click the 'Save' button
  * See [Add a terminal](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004790097>) for more information on this step.
  * If you have any problems with this step, please contact your service provider


**8)** If you have an external RFID reader, contact your service provider to determine the length of the RFID code.
**9)** After having been added to the customer environment, the terminal will automatically download settings so that it can be used by the end-users. It may automatically restart during this step.
**10)** Your terminal is now configured to automatically start and update and will show the terminal login screen. Your device is now ready for use!
  * Depending on your setup, end-users can now use your preferred identification method to log in and make recordings.


For end-users to log in to terminals and make records, they must have the method of identification linked to their personnel data in the Nepton platform (e.g. a PIN number, RFID tag number, or Biometric data).
Unknown RFID tags will allow login and recording data before the tag has been assigned to a person. The recorded data will be attributed to the user when the RFID tag number is added to that person's data
## Switching off the terminal
**Olink**
-To turn off the app, touch the corner of the screen clockwise with your finger from the top left corner, top right corner, bottom right corner, and bottom left corner
\- Press the power button on the right for at least five seconds to turn off the terminal
**Idesco**
\- To turn off the app, touch the corner of the screen clockwise with your finger from the top left corner, top right corner, bottom right corner, and bottom left corner  
\- To turn off the terminal, press the Start button -> Suspend  
\- Disconnect the Ethernet cable (PoE power supply) or power cord

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Project management | path: en-gb/Support/Project-management/4409389747601-Taking-project-targeting-into-use.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4409389747601-Taking-project-targeting-into-use -->

# Taking project targeting into use

It is possible to target all events to projects. 'Project' in Nepton service can be a target, customer, order, unit, etc. Targeted events can be reported in Project reporting and/or in integrations.
Project targeting functionality is included in Pro and Complete service levels.
## Where to start with project targeting feature
To make sure project targeting feature is taken into use as smoothly as possible it's good to make sure following steps has been taken in the organization.
### 1\. Make sure the goal for project targeting is clear
Identify targets to which you want to target events. These can be for example projects, customers, units, orders or other, to which targeting events can produce beneficial data. This data can be utilized for example in reporting, invoicing, payroll or other use.
[Targets are added](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560877>) to Nepton as projects. Projects are shown as a sequenced tree structure, in which the visibility can be defined based on [person group](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002553457>). It may be beneficial to limit visibility of some projects to only for a specfic person groups to make sure events are targeted to correct targets.
### 2\. Familiarize yourself with the project targeting feature in Nepton
To benefit for the feature with it's full potential you need to understand how the feature is planned to be used in Nepton. There are 3 important parts in the feature: Adding and managing projects, targenting events to projects and reporting. Events targeted to projects can also be approved separately from event approval.
Managing project in Nepton is easy. Full description can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002561017>). Different ways of adding and importing projects to Nepton can be found from **Technical implementation: 3. Adding projects to Nepton**).
Targeting work to projects may vary depending on how events are added. Different options for adding events can be found from these articles:
[Targeting event to a project in mobile view](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4410486932497>)
[ Targeting event to a project in calendar view or table view](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002597857>)
[ Recording an event with a project using the terminal](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002593398>)
[Targeting event to project on current status page](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002604478>)
Events targeted to projects can be reported. Data can also be exported as a part of salary data, invoising data or for example to a external reporting service. More info about project reports can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548957>). It is very important to identify if Nepton's standard reports support organization's goals in event targeting process, or should you use external service for project reporting.
It is possible to include project hour approval in the process. Project hours can be approved separately from event hours. This can be done by project manager which [can be set](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360018588898>) to every project. More information about approving project hours can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002561477>).
### 3\. Plan integrations between Nepton and other services
If projects are managed in other service projects and tree structure can be imported to Nepton. It is recommended to plan and identify all services from where data can be imported, or to which data can be exported. If there will be automated and scheduled in use these must be planned beforehand.
If no data is imported to or from Nepton all data can be managed in Nepton.
### 4\. Prepare for launch
When you have defined list of projects, tree structure and possible integrations project targeting can be taken into use. Prepare your organization by deciding suitable date for the launch. Make sure everyone are trained to the processes.
Project targeting can be taken into use by sequencing the launch. For example so one person group uses feature first and later other start using it also.
## Technical implementation
When you are ready to take project targeting unto use you must take following steps in Nepton.
Please note: Even these settings are available in the service project targeting functionality is included in Pro and Complete service levels.
### 1\. Active feature 
Project targeting feature can be activated into use in **Worktime - > Administration -> Working community settings -> Projects -> Service enabled -> Yes.**
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4996773389853/mceclip0.png)
When Projects feature is in use Projects manu will be visible. 
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4996793817629/mceclip1.png)
### 2\. Settings for project targeting 
All setting for the feature can be defined in this same working community level setting menu. It's not mandatory to have all fields filled. Some of the settings can also be defined to the Setting group level but please not not all settings are available on setting group level. 
More information about project settings can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002562658>).
### 3\. Adding projects to Nepton
To target events to projects there must be projects in Nepton. Projects can be added [one by one](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560877>), import to Nepton in bulk [manually](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003737078>), with [scheduled project import](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002492518>), from[ Visma L7](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003751058>) or with [API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360019840237>).
If project hierarchy is important and it needs to be saved when projects are imported or exported we recommend project hierarchy is included in project codes. For example project code could be '10/30', from which '10' would be unit code and '30' would be project code. This way reports can be done based in events targeted to a specific unit. Project code can be as long as needed and it can include as many levels as needed. 
### 4\. Project visibility 
In order to users to be able to target their work to a project you need to make sure they have a visibility to all needed projects. If in project settings it has been defined all projects are not visible to all users and person groups visibility must be defined for users one by one or a person group. More information can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360006776758>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Work events / Travel invoices  | path: en-gb/Support/Work-events/Travel-invoices/360004773818-Taking-Travel-invoice-functionality-into-use.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004773818-Taking-Travel-invoice-functionality-into-use -->

# Taking Travel invoice functionality into use

Travel invoice functionality is included in the **Complete service level**.
Travel compensations with possible attachments can be recorded on travel invoices. The service automatically calculates the daily allowances and suggests the number of kilometers based on the route.
Travel invoices are enabled as follows:
  1. Set the travel invoice event type to be selectable either in the working community settings or for the setting groups where travel invoices are to be used. The visibility of the travel invoice can also be set individually in person settings. Instructions for managing visible event types can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519157>).
  2. Set the rules for automatic filling of daily allowances for travel invoices. Instructions for setting the rules can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559777>).
  3. Set work supplements by using names that are used as travel invoice expense lines, route allowances, or daily allowances. The titles are freely definable. You can also use a pre-defined translation tag in the supplement name. These translation tags present the most common expenses in travel invoices. These translation tags are listed at the end of this guide article.  
Instructions for setting up the supplements can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559637>).


In order for a supplement to be selectable for travel invoices, it must be specified that it is used for travel invoices. The supplement can either be reimbursement of the route (kilometer allowance), reimbursement of the travel day (daily allowances and meals) or reimbursement of other expenses (for example a hotel).![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33718936078237)
If the supplement used is Travel day allowances, also select the correct type of compensation (calculated as).![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33718945869597)
If the supplement is an allowance or other type that has decimals in its value, select the unit type of the supplement as "Decimals".  
  
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/33718936081565)
The pre-defined translation tags to be used in travel invoice supplements are listed below. The translation tag is set as the name of the supplement. The benefit of these translation tags compared to “normal” supplement names is that they respect the language selection in Nepton.
daily_allowance  
partial_daily_allowance  
foreign_daily_allowance  
paid_lunches  
meal_reimbursement  
other_expenses  
telephone_expenses  
car_(alone)  
car_(1_passenger)  
car_(2_passengers)  
car_(3_passengers)  
car_(4_passengers)  
motorbike
  
After defining the supplements, the travel invoices are ready to be used. Instructions for adding a travel invoice can be found [here ](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004788238>)and instructions for approving travel invoices can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360005381337>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / General information on integrations | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/General-information-on-integrations/26861716054045-Target-servers-for-work-time-integrations.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/26861716054045-Target-servers-for-work-time-integrations -->

# Target servers for work time integrations

A separately defined target server must be defined for work time integrations. When the target server has been defined, the same target server can be used in multiple integrations, so you only need to specify the server information once.
Target servers can be managed in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Integrations > Integration target servers**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30716510563613)
## Target server settings
A new target server is added by pressing "Add integration target server", which allows you to fill in the basic information for the target server:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30716541074717)
The target server is given a name, an optional description, and its type is selected from the drop-down menu. The type can be either SFTP (Export), SFTP (Import) or webservice. The type is selected depending on the type of integration the target server is used for. Once this information has been added and "Save" has been pressed, this target server will appear in the target servers menu:
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30716541078557)
In the image above, a new target server called "Absences to Mepco" has been added. The more detailed information about the target server can be filled in by clicking on its name. Note: Each folder structure must have its own defined target server. This means that even if two different files are exported to the same SFTP server, if the target folder is different, separate target servers must be created for them. For example, if a salary export and an absence export were in use and being exported to the server in the folders FromNepton/Salaries and FromNepton/Absences, two target servers should be defined in Nepton.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30716510569885)
Please see [Setting up SFTP data transfer](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003722778>) for general instructions regarding the server address, username, authentication (public key or password), and what kind of path structure the server should have.
If the target server is used for a real-time integration, the "Enable real-time sync (if supported)" setting must be set to Yes.
Once the target server information is specified, it can be selected as the target server for a scheduled export under "Schedules". The same target server can be used for multiple connections.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/30716541080733)
## Buffering real-time exports
Buffering allows the export data to be scheduled rather than being performed when events are saved or approved.
The main benefit of buffering is that downtime on the target server does not result in data not being transferred. Failed transfers are retried as long as they are in the buffer.
The buffer is configured by setting a schedule for the integration target server. In the schedule settings, you must select:
1\. Integration "SFTP file export"  
2\. The desired target server for the integration target server
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27169551827101)
You can read more about scheduling integrations [in this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/10510800700573>).

# Targeting event to a project in mobile view

Project targeting can be taken into use in Pro and Complete service levels.
Start an event by clicking on the orange + sign at the bottom of the page. An Add event window will open. If the event has already been started, click on the event to open an Edit event window.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35277094762141)
The event can be targeted to several projects. Work targeted to several projects can be divided by using percentages or hours. More details about project targeting can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002596797>).
Each project has internal and public notes fields for additional information, if enabled in the settings.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35277094763805)  
Once the correct information has been filled, click **Save**.
Now the event has been started. It shows in mobile front page and the targeted projects are shown below the event name.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35277091189277)
If an assumed lunch break is in use, it will not be assigned a project. If you want to assign a project to lunch break, it must be done manually.

Jokaiseen suunniteltavaan vuoroon voidaan liittää yksi tai useampia tehtäviä. Tehtävä voi olla työohje tai sitä voidaan käyttää varmistamaan se, että vuoroon liitettävän henkilön osaaminen vastaa tehtävän osaamisvaatimusta. Tällä tavalla vuorosuunnittelija ei voi virheellisesti suunnitella sellaisia töitä henkilöille, joilla ei ole vaadittavaa osaamista.
Tehtävät perustetaan tehtävät - valikosta. Tehtävä voidaan perustaa siten, että se on käytettävissä vain osalle yksiköitä. Tehtävää voidaan käyttää kaikissa yksiköissä, mikäli yksikköä ei ole määritetty. Tehtävälle annetaan lisäksi nimi ja kuvaus.
Tehtävän kestoa, tärkeyttä, yhtäjaksoisuutta ja yksikköä käytetään palvelun automaattivälineissä, joilla kapasiteettisuunnittelun perusteella muodostetaan henkilöille työvuorot: Tärkeys määrää tehtävän prioriteetin automaattisesti vuoroja jaettaessa. Jos tehtävä on suoritettava yhtäjaksoisesti, sille varataan merkityn mittainen aika yhdelle päivälle; muuten tehtävä voi jakautua useammalle päivälle. Kappaleina seurattavalle tehtävälle ei tarvitse merkitä kestoa.
Vaadittu osaaminen ohjaa palvelun käyttöliittymää tarjoamaan suunnittelijalle vain kyseiset osaamiset täyttäviä henkilöitä.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002560518-Terminal-and-current-status-view-settings.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560518-Terminal-and-current-status-view-settings -->

# Terminal and current status view settings

Worktime terminal (in Nepton recording terminal) and current status view settings can be defined in working community level and setting group level. Most of the settings are only available on the working community level.
Please note: Event type visibility in terminals and current status is set in event types table. Further instructions [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002519157>).
## Settings
At the working community settings level, the settings can be found in **Worktime > Administration > Working community settings > Current Status.**
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28380483573789)
**Current status page enabled** setting is Yes by default. It indicates whether the [Current State View](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002603258-Recording-events-in-current-status-view-or-terminal>) is active. 
**Current status terminal enabled** is a setting that applies to older implementations. This setting must be set to yes for the web address link on the page to work.
**Web page address** can be used to open the service's Current Status view via aweb address. The link requires that the setting "Current Status terminal enabled" is set to yes. This can be useful, for example, when users need to use the Current Status View on an external device (such as a tablet within the organization’s premises). If RFID authentication or PIN code authentication is required, it must also be done when using this link.
**Log in possible with the Recording Terminal** setting defines if it´s possible to log in using the [PIN code](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430798-Manage-PIN-codes>).
“PIN-code login not in use” = Only RFID login enabled
“PIN-code login in use” = Both PIN code and RFID login enabled 
“Only RFID-login in use” = Only RFID login enabled
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28380473159069)
**Comment input visible in web terminal and current status page** defines, whether a comment can be left when recording events in terminal and current status. It is set to ‘No’ by default.
**Show notifications in the recording terminal and current status page** The option displays notifications created in the Communication section both in the recording terminal and on the Current Status page. The setting is set to 'Yes' by default. The Communication section is not enabled by default. If you would like to enable the Communication section in your organization, please contact your contract contact.
**Ability to edit start and end times in terminal** The setting tells whether a person can edit the start and end times of an event when logging an event using the Current status page or the Current status terminal. This can be useful, for example, if the person is working at a location and then moves to another location for the rest of the day. By default, the setting for editing start and end times is 'No'. Note: This setting does not apply to recording events on[ a terminal](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003685277>) such as Nepton Touch. Instructions on how to set start and end times for chosen events on a terminal can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4406224046097>).
**Input interval of start and end times** setting allows you to define the precision (in minutes) with which start and end times can be adjusted. This can be useful in situations where working hours need to be handled with a minimum accuracy of 15 minutes. Note: This setting does not apply to recording events on a terminal such as Nepton Touch. With terminals you can enter start and end times in 15-minute intervals.
**Show projects** setting determines whether the Project tab is displayed when recording an event on the recording terminal and in the current status view. Enabling this allows [work to be allocated](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002593398-Recording-an-event-with-a-project-using-the-terminal>) to specific projects or targets when using the recording terminal and current status view.
**Has terminals working in cafeteria mode** setting indicates whether the organization uses so-called “lunch terminals” or recording terminals for handling lunch and café payments. This setting is enabled by Nepton or the partner’s contact person if required. It should not be modified.
**Show today's work hours** setting determines whether the person's working hours for the current day are displayed in the current state.
**Show week's work hours** setting determines whether the person's working hours for the current week are displayed in the current state.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28380483576477)
**Go to current status page after log in** If the setting is active, the user will be redirected directly to the current status page after recording events.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / General information on terminals | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/General-information-on-terminals/7611101419037-Terminal-automatic-updates.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7611101419037-Terminal-automatic-updates -->

# Terminal automatic updates

Nepton touch terminals are kept up to date via automatic updates. Generally, these updates will happen overnight and no actions are required from end users. More details about the different kinds of updates are documented below.
# Windows IoT updates
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7610984889757)
Nepton touch devices automatically check for and install Windows updates every night, but in the event that your device shows a blue prompt like this, you can click "Another time" to defer the update until the coming night. By clicking "Restart now", the update will start immediately, during which the terminal will be unavailable for 5-15 minutes and may restart multiple times.
Please do not unplug or interrupt the device whilst it is handling an update.
Please note that Windows updates are published by Microsoft and that we have no control over their timing or content. If you encounter problems during or after a Windows update, please contact [Nepton customer support](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7077076926237>).
# Terminal software updates
Nepton touch devices automatically check for and install terminal software and configuration updates. when needed. These require no action from you and take around 5-10 minutes to complete. During this time the terminal will be unavailable.
Please do not unplug or interrupt the device whilst it is handling an update.

# Terminal does not respond

Sometimes terminal can go into a state where it does not react to anything, i.e. the so-called stuck. This is a computer with an operating system and, like any computer, terminal can stop responding to feeds.
The easiest way to fix this is to [turn off the device](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002588737>). 
If the device does not start operating normally after start-up, contact Nepton Customer Service

**Sorry!**
This article has not been translated yet.
Huomioithan, että ohjeet saattaa poiketa hieman päätelaitteen tyypistä riippuen, mutta pääpiirteissään logiikka on kaikissa laitteissa sama. Olethan yhteydessä organisaationne palvelun pääkäyttäjään, mikäli tarvitset lisäapua.

# Terminal IP address reset (For Nepton Touch devices from September 2022)

1\. Exit the terminal application by clicking from all corners in order upper left corner, upper right corner, lower right corner, lower left corner.
2\. Double-click the Static IP icon on the Windows desktop. If no external keyboard is available, click the Keyboard icon to open the virtual keyboard.
![1_Pikakuvakkeet.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7127415140765)

![MAC_address.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7400533410589)
4\. If you want to change IP address, in the window that opens, select Properties
![2_Static_IP_.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7237569301661)
4\. Click the Yes button
![3_Static_ip_propertises_press_ok.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7127415179933)
5\. Select Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4) and click Configure
![4._Properties.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7127399794845)
6\. Make the necessary settings and click OK
![5_Static_IP_setup.jpg](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/7127399818653)
7\. Close all windows and return to the Windows desktop. Start the Terminal application from the Nepton icon.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / Troubleshooting | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/Troubleshooting/360016976178-Terminal-offline-mode.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360016976178-Terminal-offline-mode -->

# Terminal offline mode

Nepton terminal software can temporarily operate without an internet connection. When a loss of connectivity is detected, the software enters "offline-mode". It allows users to continue marking events with only minor changes and limitations to functionality. When connectivity is restored the terminal will automatically reconnect and synchronise offline markings to the Nepton platform.
This feature is provided to mitigate the impact of short internet interruptions and temporary network problems. Internet connectivity should always be restored as soon as possible.
## Troubleshooting
In exceptional circumstances or at customer request, the offline-mode can be disabled. This will prevent login or markings using the terminal when there is not an active connection to the Nepton platform.
There are many terminal troubleshooting and guidance articles, please use the search, or see the **Terminal Use** section.  
See also: [Terminal remains in offline mode, or cannot connect to the internet (Connectivity troubleshooting).](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002588757>)
## How do I know if a terminal is offline?
Nepton terminal software enters offline-mode when it detects that a connection to the Nepton servers is not available. This functionality is provided to mitigate the impact of short internet interruptions and temporary network problems. Internet connectivity should be restored as soon as possible.
Offline mode is indicated by a red status bar at the bottom of the software.
**![Terminal_offline_2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015697097)**
## Reconnection & synchronisation
Whilst in offline-mode the software frequently checks for connectivity, and when possible, will automatically reconnect. When the terminal re-establishes connection with the Nepton servers it will systematically synchronise any data that was recorded by users in the offline-mode.
The synchronisation of offline markings is fast once reconnected, but please allow some time for events to appear in employee calendars if there are large amounts of data.
When the terminal has good connectivity, normal features are available and the status bar will be green as shown here.
**![Terminal_online_2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015770778)**
## Limitations
### Login
Whilst in offline-mode, logins cannot be authenticated using the Nepton server and therefore an on-board cache is used. Using RFID tags, unknown and first-time users are permitted to login to the terminal software, but will only be able to mark default event types and projects. Depending on your environment's configuration, this might mean that no projects are available. Please see the next heading for more detailed information on event types and projects limitations in offline-mode.
**Important Note:** If markings are recorded with unknown tags and these tags are still not configured for a person in the Nepton platform by the time the terminal reconnects, then the markings **will not** be synchronised to Nepton.
### Event types and projects
When in offline-mode, each terminal relies upon a cache to determine the activity types and projects which should be available to an individual. The cache is updated when a person uses the terminal whilst connected to the Nepton servers, i.e. **not** when in offline-mode.
Providing the terminal has had at least one successful login with connection to the Nepton servers, default event types and projects will be cached, and therefore unknown and first-time users can still record basic markings and projects.
**Important note:** The cache used in offline-mode is device-specific and is not shared between devices. Therefore, depending on when a person used a terminal last, they might see different options between two devices, when both are in offline-mode.
### Marking events & person status
As the terminal software cannot communicate with the Nepton servers a person's current status and accruals information cannot be shown.
As the current status cannot be determined, the terminal cannot intelligently offer or interpret whether a marking should Start, Stop, or Stop and Start an event. Therefore, in offline-mode users must indicate whether their marking is a Stop or Start action. To support this, both options are made available for saving the marking. However, you must first select the event type, i.e. "Work", for the Start button to be activated. If you want to end the ongoing event, you have to press the Work button again so that the Stop button is activated, see images:
**![Terminal_offline_4.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360015697457)**
**![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/9082252631581)**
**![mceclip3.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/9082281621533)**
### Duration of offline mode
It is recommended that terminals are always online. The offline mode is provided to be of assistance during short internet interruptions and temporary network problems. The only restriction of offline mode is the hard disk space of the terminal. If for some reason, the terminal is offline for such a long period of time that the markings made during it will fill up the hard disk space of the terminal, the markings would not be transferred to Nepton once a network connection was re-established. Depending on the usage level and markings made on the terminal, the disk space might run out in a week or two of offline mode. This kind of usage is not recommended.

# Terminal remains in offline mode, or cannot connect to the internet (Connectivity troubleshooting)

**Whoops!**  
This article has not been translated yet. 
Työaikapäätteet reagoivat verkkoyhteyden vikatilanteisiin välittömästi. Nämä vikatilanteet johtuvat usein hetkellisestä katkosta internet-yhteydessä. Usein nämä katkokset ovat niin lyhytaikaisia, ettei käyttäjä ehdi huomaamaan niitä. Katkosten aikana tehdyt kirjaukset jäävät laitteen muistiin ja ne lähetetään palveluun, kun laite on taas internet-yhteydessä.  
  
**Mikäli verkkoyhteys ei palaudu muutamassa minuutissa on hyvä suorittaa/tarkistaa seuraavat asiat.  
**  
-**Laite on hyvä käynnistää uudelleen.** Ohjeet laitteen uudelleenkäynnistykseen löydät [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002588737>).  
\- **Vilkkuuko päätteen ethernet-portissa valo?** Jos ei, on todennäköistä, että portti tai ethernet-kaapeli on vikaantunut, tai verkkoyhteys ei muusta syystä toimi ko. kaapelilla. Suosittelemme kokeilemaan laitteen yhdistämistä toisella verkkokaapelilla.  
\- **Saako toinen laite (esimerkiksi kannettava tietokone) internet-yhteyden samalla kaapelilla?**
Kannettavalla pitää testata yhteys osoitteeseen:
https://go.nepton.com/TerminalUpdateService/TerminalUpdateService.svc
Jos ko. yhteys toimii, tulee näytölle seuraava sivu:
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4407346444689/mceclip0.png)
Mikäli ko. sivu ei avaudu, vikatilanne johtuu todennäköisesti verkkoyhteydestä.  
  
\--  
  
**Alla on kuvattu menettely tilanteessa, jossa työaikapääte ilmoittaa seuraavaa häiriötä:**_**  
**Windows CE Networking  
_ _DHCP was unable to obtain an IP address. If the netcard is removable,__then you can remove/reinsert it to have DHCP make another attempt to_ _obtain an IP address for it. Otherwise you can statically assign an_ _address._
**1\. Jotta vikatilannetta voidaan korjata, tulee ensin poistua kirjausnäkymästä.**
\- Tarkista, että laitteessa on virrat päällä.
\- Paina sormella tai kosketusnäyttökynällä laitteen kosketusnäytön jokaista neljää kulmaa kerran jämäkästi mahdollisimman läheltä reunaa järjestyksessä**vasen yläkulma - oikea yläkulma - oikea alakulma - vasen alakulma.  
  
2\. Vikatilanteen toteaminen ja ratkaisu  
**  
\- Kun työpöytänäkymä on näkyvissä, näkyy Windowsin työkalupalkin vasemmassa reunassa seuraavanlainen kuvake. Tämä kertoo, että laitteessa ei ole verkkoyhteyttä.  
  
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360004646577/mceclip0.png)  
  
\- Klikkaamalla kuvaketta aukeaa ikkuna, jossa on mahdollista päivittää päätteen käyttämät IP-osoitteet.  
  
![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/360004711238/mceclip1.png)  
  
Klikkaamalla **Renew** -painiketta pääte hakee uudet IP-osoitteet. Onnistuneen IP-osoitteiden haun pystyy todentamaan sillä, että aiemmassa kuvassa näkyvän verkkoyhteys-kuvakkeen päällä oleva punainen raksi katoaa. Tällöin verkkoyhteys toimii normaalisti.
**3\. Palaaminen kirjausnäkymään, jotta työaikaa voi taas kirjata.  
**
\- Kun halutut asetukset on määritelty tulee Terminal Launcher käynnistää uudelleen, jotta työaikaa voi taas kirjata. Työpöytänäkymästä löytyy **Nepton Terminal Launcher -kuvake** , jota tuplaklikkaamalla palvelu käynnistyy. Kun palvelua käynnistetään saattaa se käynnistyä itsestään useamman kerran uudelleen. Tämä on normaalia ja saattaa kestää jopa 10 minuuttia. Kannattaa odottaa rauhassa, että palvelu käynnistyy.  
  
\- Joissain laiteversioissa Terminal Launcher ei ole työpöydällä, vaan se tulee käynnistää valitsemalla työpöydältä kansio My device. Kansiosta valitaan Storage Card - Release - Työteho (tuplaklikataan). Kirjausnäkymä avautuu automaattisesti ja laite on valmis vastaanottamaan kirjauksia. Tässäkin tapauksessa palvelu saattaa käynnistyä uudelleen useita kertoja ja käynnistyksessä saattaa kestää useita minuutteja.

# Terminal Services API

This article describes Worktime API methods for handling terminal services. The methods described are technically possible to use in other contexts as well, but they are primarily designed for worktime terminal entries.
## Starting an event
It is possible to start a new event with API. For example a user starts their day by recording a work event.
API methods for starting events:
  * [BeginActivity (obsolete)](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6869807559453>)
  * [BeginActivityV2](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6869562936221>)


## Ending an event
It is possible to end an event with API. For example a user finishes their day by ending a work event.
API methods for ending events:
  * [EndActivity (obsolete)](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6870299031581>)
  * [EndActivityV2](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6870443544477>)


## Päätekirjautuminen
It is possible to obtain information about a specific user at the current time, e.g. information about an open event or the event types that the user can select.
API methods:
  *     * [TerminalLogin (obsolete)](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6887099778333>)
    * [TerminalLoginV2](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360021180898>)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Terminals / General information on terminals | path: en-gb/Support/Terminals/General-information-on-terminals/360003685277-Terminal-Types.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003685277-Terminal-Types -->

# Terminal Types

Below is an outline of the different terminal hardware currently offered by Nepton. If you need information about an older terminal model, please make a support request.
**For marketing information, please visit<https://nepton.com/challenges-and-solutions/terminals/>**
## General information about terminals
Terminals record events in real time.
Real-time recording is displayed in the calendar and table views as an icon between the time and the event type name.
The Event listing report displays the terminal ID if the event was recorded entirely with a terminal. In a situation where recording was started and ended with a different terminal, the ID of the terminal with which the event was started is displayed.
When using Nepton Rugged terminal, there is no icon in the calendar or table view and the Event listing report does not have the terminal ID. This is due to the technology used to communicate with the service, and the technology of Nepton Rugged terminals does not enable the above-mentioned features.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26371303018781)
## Nepton Touch
The device uses modern materials and has a built-in speaker and RFID reader. It replaces the original Nepton Touch devices from September 2022 onwards.
Terminals can be used when offline as they have space for saving thousands of records into memory until they are reconnected. Offline records are transferred to Nepton as soon as the device is back online.
![p__telaite_uusi.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/6388171240989)
### Main features
  * Log in with a PIN or RFID
  * High resolution 10.1" industrial A+ grade LCD touch screen
  * Realtech RTL811E gigabit network card (RJ45/Ethernet)
  * Can be used immediately after being connected to the internet
  * Easy wall mounting with included basic VESA-wall mount kit
  * Windows 10 IOT Enterprise LTSC operating system
  * Onboard SSD hard drive and Intel Celeron CPU for performance
  * Can be used as a cafeteria terminal
  * Existing access control tags can be used
  * RFID reader complying with ISO14443-A and ISO14443-B standards at 13,56 MHz: 
    * Example compatible tags: MIFARE® DESFire: UID + Application files , MIFARE® Classic: UID + Sectors, MIFARE® Ultralight UID + pages, MIFARE® Plus UID security levels 1 and 3, MIFARE® SmartMX (MIFARE® Classic and MIFARE® DESFire EV1 emulation modes), NFC (UID), Mifare Classic 7 Byte UID + sectors, Legic, ISO15693 (UID)
  * Possibility to use external RFID-reader to support a wide range of RFID tags. Guidance to the external readers' supported tags can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/10357648361757>).
  * POE+ and POE++ distribution devices can be used for power supply (30 Watt power requirement). The distribution device must have a separate power output (e.g. Planet POE-172S), which is connected to the device's power connector. If there is no PoE supply in the ethernet cable, a separate PoE injector is still needed (e.g. Ernitec Electra-P2-60W).
  * Rated to operate between -20 to +70 degrees centigrade
  * Constructed from an Aluminum alloy for durability
  * Device measurements:  
Height 19,4 cm  
Width 37,4 cm  
Depth 6 cm


### Cleaning the touch screen
  * Use a soft, clean cloth, a microfiber cloth is recommended.
  * Moisten the cloth lightly with water. You can also use cleansers meant for touch screens. Remember that the device should not get too wet.
  * Wipe the screen carefully using the cloth.


## Nepton-Flexim terminal device
The Nepton-Flexim terminal was introduced as part of Nepton’s device offering in the fall of 2024. The terminals come with their own Nepton software (production release version 5.0.1). The following Nepton-Flexim terminal hardware models already in use can be updated to the software produced by Nepton:
  * SACCTP1_121000 : prox tag reader
  * SACCTM1_121000 : mifare tag reader
  * SACCTC1_121000 : ABLOY SEOS tag reader
  * SACCWPM_121000 (tag reader that supports multiple tags: prox, mifare, SEOS)
  * SACCWPP_121000 (tag reader that supports multiple tags: prox, mifare, SEOS)


Customers using the aforementioned terminal models can check from their terminals whether they can be updated to the new Nepton software as follows: if the serial number found on the device starts with the number three (3), the device can be updated.
New device model SACCWPP_121000 can be obtained from Nepton directly.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497149479325)
Key functionalities:
  * **Login** : With a tag, PIN code (can be enabled/disabled per terminal), or Quick Recording (showing the tag to the reader starts/stops the task. Quick Recording can also be enabled/disabled per terminal).


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497149484829)
  * **Event logging** : In the same way as on the Nepton Touch device.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497133001245)
  * **Selectable buttons on the home screen** : Eight (8) buttons at a time. If more buttons are in use, the page turn arrow acts as an indicator.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497149495837)
  * **Automatic logout** : The terminal logs the user out by default after 20 seconds of inactivity. The logout delay can be changed.
  * **Supplement logging** : Possible after starting an event. 
    * **Supplements tab** : Shows four (4) selectable supplements.
    * **Supplement type and default values** : Come according to the Nepton settings group.
    * **Quick selections** : Supplements can be increased (plus button) or decreased (minus button) at user-defined intervals, for example, 5, 10, or 15 minutes at a time.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497133012125)
  *     *       * **Pen icon (see screenshot above)** : Allows for a more precise, minute-by-minute value alteration


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497149506589)
  * **Overtime target selection** : From the **Overtime tab** , the overtime target can be changed. Options are visible according to the person’s settings group.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497133018909)
  * **Project allocation** : From the **Projects tab** , the desired project allocation for the work can be selected. The last recorded options are shown. Using the search function, options other than the last recorded ones can be displayed. The project can also be selected with a barcode reader, provided the person is logged into the terminal with an identifier. After reading the barcode, the project allocation starts, and the person is automatically logged out of the terminal.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/23497133022109)
  * **Terminal setup** : A new terminal announces its number when it starts, which can be used to connect the terminal to the Nepton environment.

  * RFID reader complying with ISO14443-A and ISO14443-B standards at 13,56 MHz:

  * IP66 case, rated to operate between 0 to +50 degrees centigrade
  * Coloured lights, buzzer and speaker
  * Constructed from plastic for light-weight portability

# TerminalLogin

This article has not been translated yet.
Tästä metodista on uudempi versio. Mikäli käytät jo tätä metodia, niin suosittelemme, että tarkastelet seuraavan version ohjeesta, mitä muutoksia vaaditaan uuden version käyttöönottamiseksi. Seuraavan version ohjeen löydät [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360021180898>)
## Rajapinnan yleiskuvaus
Verkkopalveluita käytetään henkilön nykytilan hakemiseen Neptonista. Verkkopalvelu on suunniteltu käytettäväksi päätelaitesovelluksissa, esimerkiksi näyttämään seuraavat henkilöä koskevat tiedot:
  * Avoimena oleva tapahtumakirjaus
  * Projektit, joita voi tapahtumille kirjata
  * Mitä projekteja käytetään oletuksena uuden tapahtuman aloituksessa
  * Onko projektin kirjaaminen tapahtumalle pakollista vai ei
  * Tapahtumille kirjattavissa olevat työlisät
  * Ylityön oletuskohdenne työtapahtumilla
  * Kirjattavissa olevat tapahtumatyypit
  * Henkilön kertymät ja niiden saldot


Verkkopalvelun autentikoituminen eroaa muista verkkopalveluista sillä tavalla, että onnistuneesti käyttäjätunnuksella ja salasanalla autentikoitunut henkilö voi autentikoitua toisena henkilönä PIN-koodin tai RFID-koodin perusteella. Ensimmäisessä vaiheessa autentikoituneella henkilöllä täytyy olla oikeudet lukea henkilötietoja. Esimerkiksi:
[code] 
    <CallerAuthentication>  
      <CustomerId>1234</CustomerId>  
      <Username>PäätelaiteKäyttäjä</Username>  
      <Password>KuvitteellinenSalasana123</Password>  
      <PinCode>1234</PinCode> <!-- Päätelaitteella syötetty PIN-koodi -->  
    </CallerAuthentication>
[/code]
Jos annetulla PIN-koodilla tai RFID-koodilla ei löydy henkilöä, autentikoituminen epäonnistuu.
Verkkopalvelun WSDL-skeema on julkisesti saatavilla [täällä](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). Rajapinnat ovat yleisellä tasolla kuvattuna [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>).
Kuvauksessa oleva sarake esiintymiskerrat määrittää sen onko jokin tieto pakollinen kutsussa vai ei. Esiintymiskerrat 0, tarkoittaa että kyseistä tietoa ei tarvitse siirtää kutsussa. Esiintymiskerrat 1 tarkoittaa, että tiedon tulee esiintyä kutsussa yhden kerran. Esiintymiskerrat 0..n tarkoittaa, että kyseinen tieto voi esiintyä kutsussa minkä tahansa määrän. Esiintymiskerrat 1..n tarkoittaa että kyseinen tieto tulee olla aineistossa ainakin kerran, mutta voi olla useamminkin.
## Lähetettävät tiedot
Taso | Kentän nimi | Muoto | Esiintymiskerrat | Selite  
---|---|---|---|---  
Juuri,  
SOAP body:n alla | ParametersForTerminalLogin | XML element | 1 |   
1 | CallerAuthentication | XML element | 1 | Lisää tietoa autentikoitumisesta [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360004861558>)  
### Kyselyn esimerkki
[code] 
    <soapenv:Envelope xmlns:soapenv="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/" xmlns:tyo="http://tyoaika.tyoteho.fi">  
      <soapenv:Header/>  
      <soapenv:Body>  
        <tyo:ParametersForTerminalLogin>  
          <CallerAuthentication>  
            <CustomerId>1234</CustomerId>  
            <Username>PäätelaiteKäyttäjä</Username>  
            <Password>KuvitteellinenSalasana123</Password>  
            <RFID>2893789127981239</RFID> <!-- Päätelaitteella luettu RFID-koodi -->          
          </CallerAuthentication>  
        </tyo:ParametersForTerminalLogin>  
      </soapenv:Body>  
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]

4 | Name | string | 1 | Tapahtumatyypin nimi  
3 | Code | string | 0..1 | Tapahtumatyypin koodi

3 | CanHaveRelatedProjects | boolean | 0..1 | Voiko tapahtumatyypille kirjata projekteja (`true`) vai ei (`false`)  
3 | CategoryInternalName | string | 1 | Tapahtumatyypin kategorian sisäinen tunniste Neptonissa  
3 | TranslatedCategoryName | XML element | 0..n | Tapahtumatyypin kategorian käännetty nimi  
4 | Locale | string | 1 | Kielen koodi. Mahdolliset arvot näet [täältä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/6904407712413>)  
4 | Name | string | 1 | Tapahtumatyypin kategorian nimi

  * `disabled` \- Ei sallittu
  * `optional` \- Sallittu
  * `mandatory` \- Aika on pakko antaa

  
3 | EndDateTimeInput | string | 0..1 | Päätettävän tapahtuman aloitusajan syöttö. Mahdolliset arvot samat kuin BeginDateTimeInput-Elementillä  
1 | AccrualList | XML element | 0..1 | Lista kertymistä ja niiden arvoista  
2 | Accrual | XML element | 0..n |

3 | ChangeAmount | string | 0..1 | Paljonko kertymän arvo on muuttunut nykyisenä päivänä. Arvo tunteina ja minuutteina, esimerkiksi `+00:30`

# TerminalLoginV2

## Interface overview
The webservice is used to retrieve a person's current status from Nepton. The web service is designed to be used in terminal applications, to show for example the following user related information:
  * Ongoing event registration
  * Projects that can be registered for events
  * Which projects are used by default when starting a new event
  * Is registering a project for an event mandatory or not
  * Work supplements that can be registered for events
  * Default overtime target for work events
  * Event typess that can be registered
  * Person's accruals and their balances


Authentication in the web service differs from other web services in that a person who has successfully authenticated with a username and password can authenticate as another person based on a PIN code or RFID code. In the first step, the authenticated person must have the rights to view personal data. For example:
[code] 
    <CallerAuthentication>  
      <CustomerId>1234</CustomerId>  
      <Username>PäätelaiteKäyttäjä</Username>  
      <Password>KuvitteellinenSalasana123</Password>  
      <PinCode>1234</PinCode> <!-- Pin code given on terminal -->  
    </CallerAuthentication>
[/code]
If the person cannot be found with the provided PIN code or RFID code, authentication will fail.
The WSDL schema of the web service is publicly available [here](<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>). The interfaces are described in general [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558>).
The occurrences column in the description determines whether a piece of information is mandatory in the call or not. Occurrences 0 means that the information in question does not need to be passed in the call. Occurrences 1 means that the information must appear once in the call. Occurrences 0..n means that the information in question can appear any number of times in the call. Occurrences 1..n means that the information in question must appear in the data at least once, but can appear more often.
## Changes from previous version ([TerminalLogin](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/6887099778333>))
### Structural changes
**Old** | **New** | **Additional information**  
---|---|---
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForTerminalLogin>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForTerminalLogin>
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <tyo:ParametersForTerminalLoginV2>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ParametersForTerminalLoginV2>
[/code]
| The name of the call root element has changed.
[code] 
    <tyo:ReturnValueForTerminalLogin>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ReturnValueForTerminalLogin>
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <tyo:ReturnValueForTerminalLoginV2>  
      ...  
    </tyo:ReturnValueForTerminalLoginV2>
[/code]
| The name of the response root element has changed.
[code] 
    <OngoingActivity>  
      <BeginDateTime>2020-01-01 12:00:00</BeginDateTime>  
      <EndDateTime>2020-01-01 14:00:00</EndDateTime>  
      <ModifiedDateTime>2020-01-01 16:00:00</ModifiedDateTime>  
    </OngoingActivity>  
    
[/code]  
| 
[code] 
    <OngoingActivity>  
      <BeginDateTime>2020-01-01T12:00:00</BeginDateTime>  
      <EndDateTime>2020-01-01T14:00:00</EndDateTime>  
      <ModifiedDateTime>2020-01-01T16:00:00</ModifiedDateTime>  
    </OngoingActivity>
[/code]
| In the response, the date and time elements are now of type datetime, which slightly affects the date format (BeginDateTime, EndDateTime, ModifiedDateTime)  
### Obsolete elements
The following elements were previously in the response twice, first under the OngoingActivity element and the second time under the ActivityDetails element:
  * PlannedWorkCalculationUnit
  * PlannedWorkColor
  * PlannedWorkUseForWorkDayLengthCalculations
  * PlannedWorkCanBeCancelledUntil
  * PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetStartInMins
  * PlannedWorkWorkTimeLimitOffsetEndInMins
  * PlannedWorkActivityGroupPublicInfo


From now on, these elements will only be found under the ActivityDetails element.
RelatedActivityId was already reported as deprecated in the previous version, but now this element has been technically removed from the response.
### New features and elements
  * The response contains the personnel number for the person in the event (UserPersonnelNumber element)
  * The response contains the personnel number for the approver of the event (ApproverPersonnelNumber element)
  * The response contains the external identifiers for the event (ExternalIdentifiers element)

      </soapenv:Body>  
    </soapenv:Envelope>
[/code]

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360003994357-Time-language-and-region.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003994357-Time-language-and-region -->

# Time, language and region

Service can be defined the default language and time zone for a person, setting group or working community. By setting the time zone, real-time job starts and stops functions of service can also be used in organizations, where work is being done in different time zones. When a supervisor or other person views the calendar of a person working in a different time zone, they also see real-time recorded events in that time zone. The calendar does not change the times according to the viewer's time zone.
## Settings
The language and time zone to be used can be defined in the person settings (Worktime -> Administration -> Persons -> Time, language and region), in setting group settings (Worktime -> Administration -> Setting groups -> Action: Setting group settings -> Time, language and region) or in the working community settings (Worktime -> Administration - > Working Community Settings-> Time, language and region).
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4411334332177/mceclip0.png)
## Defaults
The default language in the service is Finnish and the time zone is Finnish time zone.
## Time zones and event creation at the terminal
  * If an event is recorded using a terminal, the start and end times of the event are saved in to Nepton based on the time zone and time set in the posting terminal. If an employee momentarily travels to a different time zone, he or she can log his or her work time according to local time.
  * If an event is recorded via Current Status view or Mobile, the start and end times of the event will be saved in to Nepton according to the settings defined at the Working Community settings / Setting group level. This ensures the correctness of the working time entries. For this reason, it is recommended that the time zone of a person in Nepton always is set to the correct current location.


Note: If you change the time zone retrospectively, the change will not affect events that have already been recorded.
## Restrictions
Only one time zone per day can be valid in one day.
API: If you send times in UTC zero format, they will be converted to local times based on your time zone setting (2019-12-25T10:11:12Z).
When [persons are imported](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003762577-Person-Import>) without a service usage language, the language set in the working community settings does not affect the language of the person's service usage language. If persons are imported without a service usage language, the default language of the customership is used, which is Finnish by default. Changing the default language can be requested from Nepton Customer Service.
