<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/21229494759069-Why-can-t-I-log-in-to-Nepton.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/21229494759069-Why-can-t-I-log-in-to-Nepton -->

# Why can't I log in to Nepton?

This article reviews the most common login problems and solutions.
Instructions for logging in can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002602998>).
### 1\. First, check the following
  * You are logging into the service at **go.nepton.com** (same address on mobile device and computer)
  * You are logging into the right **Company** (your organization’s environment). If necessary, confirm the name of your organization's Nepton environment with your HR department.
  * Is there an outage in the service: We will update in the [Platform status article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360006554777>) if a malfunction affecting login has been detected in the service. The maintenance window is normally active every Tuesday from 19:15 to 19:45. During this time, there may be a short service outage.
  * If a username/email and password are used instead of SSO login, make sure the information is correct and order a new password if necessary.


**Password reset link not received in the user's email?**  
First, check that the user has indeed tried to log in using the same email address that is specified in the person's Employees section information in the service. An extra space at the end of the email can also prevent login. After this, it is advisable to check the spam folder in the email. If these actions do not help, the organization’s Nepton administrator can set a temporary password for the user and ask the user to change the password to a new one after logging into the service (password change instructions [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002596657>)).
### 2\. Check if the problem is browser or device-specific
  * Does logging in work with another browser (Safari/Chrome/Firefox/Edge)?
  * Does logging in work with another device (mobile device, tablet, computer)?


To ensure the login issue is not caused by the browser, please clear the browser’s cache and cookies.
Instructions for clearing the browser’s cache and cookies can be found on the service providers’ own pages (the following links direct to an external site):
[Google Chrome cache clearing](<https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop>)  
[Firefox cache clearing](<https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/how-clear-firefox-cache>)  
[Microsoft Edge cache clearing](<https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/view-and-delete-browser-history-in-microsoft-edge-00cf7943-a9e1-975a-a33d-ac10ce454ca4>)
Also, update your browser to the latest software version if necessary.
### 3\. If the above measures do not help, contact your supervisor, your organization’s HR department, or the Nepton administrator, who can check the following:
  * First, ensure that the login credentials used by the person match the information stored in the service (email address and username). The login identifier is the person's email address or username. An extra space at the end of the email can also prevent login.
  * After this, the Nepton administrator can investigate [the service log](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575478>) to determine any other reasons for the login issue. Only the organization's administrators can access the service log via **Employees > Administration > Service Log**.
If you encounter issues with single sign-on (Microsoft Login, Google Login, SAML), select SSO in the Area field in the service log filters. The service log will describe the cause of the login issue. The most common problems are due to changes in the login details of the person logging in that have not been updated in Nepton (for example, the email address has changed), or the secret value provided by a third party for logging in has expired (for example, Entra ID). We have a separate article in our support service for troubleshooting Microsoft Login issues [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360016233138>).
  * If necessary, the trained administrator user can also contact our [customer service](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7077076926237>). Please include the following information in the support request:
    1. The person affected by the problem, and if the problem affects multiple people
    2. The devices and browsers used to attempt the login
    3. Whether the cache and cookies have been cleared
    4. A video of the login attempt or a clear description of when the problem occurs: For example, does the login page open at all or can the organization's environment be selected?
With this information, we can immediately start investigating the cause of the problem.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / HR management | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/HR-management/360002572877-Why-does-a-person-show-up-in-reports-and-person-listings-when-they-no-longer-work-for-our-company.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002572877-Why-does-a-person-show-up-in-reports-and-person-listings-when-they-no-longer-work-for-our-company -->

# Why does a person show up in reports and person listings when  they no longer work for our company?

If a person who no longer works at your company and whose user account has already been deleted still appears in reports and personnel lists, it is likely that the employment end date information is missing. After deleting the user account, the employee can no longer log into the service, but this does not yet determine the person’s visibility in reports.
The person appears in reports and personnel lists when viewing the period during which their employment contract is active. In addition to deleting the user account, also add the employee’s employment end date to their information so that they appear correctly in reports.
The employment end date is added by opening the person’s information using the magnifying glass icon from the personnel list in the Employees section. The end date is entered in the Employment end date field. Save the information using the Save button at the bottom of the page.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20547509021085)
If the user account has already been deleted, you can find the person's information in the personnel list by selecting either **Show deleted** or **Show only deleted** persons in the Deleted persons field of the search criteria. You can also add the End of employment date to an already deleted user account when you restore the user account to active momentarily.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: FAQ / Workshift planning | path: en-gb/Support/FAQ/Workshift-planning/360002575598-Why-is-an-employee-not-visible-in-the-planning-view.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575598-Why-is-an-employee-not-visible-in-the-planning-view -->

# Why is an employee not visible in the planning view?

This instruction presents the most common situations and reasons why the shift planner does not see all the locations they need or the people working in the locations in the planning view of the Planning section.
## 1\. View filters
Make sure that the view is not unnecessarily filtered in the **View settings**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20768472637341)
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20768472639773)
**\- Person list** : the view is limited according to each person list. If the person missing from the planning view is not a member of the selected person list, the person is not shown in the planning view either.  
**\- Location** : If the highest possible location (category) is selected, all people from lower level locations are also displayed in the planning view. However, if a certain sub-location is selected to which the missing person does not belong, the person will not be shown in the planning view either.  
**\- Primary supervisors** : If a supervisor who is not the primary supervisor of the person missing from the planning view is selected in the primary supervisors field, the person will not be shown in the planning view either.  
**\- Tasks** : If tasks have been added to the service, only the shifts to which the selected task is attached to are displayed. If the person does not have any planned shifts with the selected task, the person will not appear in the planning view either.
## 2\. No unit has been assigned for the person
You can add [the unit information](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002595478>) in the person's information in the Employees section, if the unit information is missing. A person can belong to several units, in which case one of the units is primary and the rest are secondary. However, unit primacy has only informative value.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20769059036701)
## 3\. The person has not been added to the location
Make sure that the person is connected to their shift planning location. Adding people to locations is done from the top bar of the Planning section in the **Locations**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20770539041309)
In the Locations section, first select the location (planning level) where the person works. Under the Location Persons menu in the planning level, you can already see persons attached to the office. Check under the "Available persons" section if there is still a person missing from the planning view in the list. Add a person to the location using the Add button in front of the name. Adding a person to the location does not need to be saved separately.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20770539047197)
The structure of the Locations follows the so-called waterfall model. If a person works in several locations, they can be assigned to the highest location. In this way, shifts can be planned for a person at all sub-locations.  
For example, in the picture above - If a person worked at both locations Espoon keskus and Leppävaara, he could be assigned to the location Espoo.
If a person is missing under the Persons to be added section, there can be two reasons:
1) No unit has been added for the person in the Employees section.  
2) A unit has been assigned to the person, but the location to which the person is being added is under a different unit.
Regardless of which reason it is, the correct unit information must be added to the person's information.

# Work community does not have an active Nepton subscription

![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/5569071660701/mceclip0.png)
If you are seeing this message it means that your contract to use Nepton service has ended with Nepton.
The Scheduled tasks (e.g. integrations) and access to Nepton API are disabled for you work community.
  * Scheduled integration tasks will not be run for your work community.
  * All public Nepton API calls are denied and following error message is returned "Access Denied: A Nepton subscription is required".


In case your Nepton service subscription is active and you are still seeing this message, contact your administrator to solve the situation.

# Work contract notifications

Automatic notifications for online work contracts can be managed on **Employees - Administration - Settings - Automated notifications.** You can choose which events on work contracts will send automatic notification.
To be able to recieve notifications, it requires that email and phone number must have been saved on persons info.
Notificiations can be send on following situations:
  * After creating a first working contract
  * After creating a subsequent working contract
  * After employee accepts a working contract


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20381356319389)
  
  
When the service is selected by clicking the "Send an email to person", more configurations are displayed. Subject and content for email can be added. Email can also be configured to be sent every time to certain email addresses in addition to the persons connected to the work contract.
The email can be configured to use secure email. These services are offered by different service providers. In order for this configuration to work, the secure email sending service must be in use and the service must be defined in Nepton - **Employees - Administration Settings - Change to custom email server (SMTP)**
When secure email is sent, recipient will have notification, which tells "You have had secure email, click this link to open the email". When the link is clicked and recipient chooses "I want to see the concent of message", recipient will get pin-code via text message to open it.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20382994129053)

# Work contract packages

The work contract package can bundle together documents related to the employment contract. The package may include, for example, the work contract, a confidentiality agreement and employee instructions. When creating an online work contract for an employee, an work contract package is always used as the basis for the contract.
## Creating new work contract package
  1. Under the **Employees** section, select **Contracts** and then **Contract Packages**.
  2. At the bottom of the page, write a name and description for the new work contract package in the designated fields.
  3. Press **Add** and the created work contract package will appear in the list.
  4. The name and description of the work contract package can be changed via the **Pencil icon**. Remember to press the**Save button** after making changes.
  5. The work contract templates within the package can be edited through the **Magnifying glass icon.**
  6. In the opening view, work contract templates can be added to the package. This is done by pressing the **Add to package button** from the list of work contract templates. The package can contain only one work contract but several attached files. A work contract template can be removed from the package by pressing the **Remove from package button**. A work contract template can be opened in a separate window for review by pressing the **Magnifying glass icon** from the list of contract templates in the work contract package.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360002560978-Work-rises.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560978-Work-rises -->

# Work rises

Work rises are compensation rules that are automatically calculated based on validity times. If there's a need to let employees add one time compensations themselves, this can be done with [Supplements](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559637>).
Work rises can be used for example to automatically calculate amount of earned evening rise. Work rises can be used for a variety of needs in different industries, but the accumulation of them is always based on time, type of event, and compensation for that type of event.
This article explains the settings behind work rises. At the end of the article, there is guidance on how to create a commonly used evening rise.
## Setting up Work rises
Work rises can be set up in the **Worktime** section of the service at either the **Working community** settings or **Settings group** settings. The determination is made in **Work hours > Work Rises**.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/35449789208349)
If the name is in italics, at least _some_ of its settings are inherited from the upper-level setting group. If the name is shown in bold, all related settings are configured at the currently viewed setting level. If the name is shown both in italics and bold, it has settings on the current level as well as some inheriting from above. A name must always be set to a work rise.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26980943086237)
Different conditions can be defined for the work rise, from the increase method to roundings. You should always read the settings carefully and check that the setting is going as desired.
## Work rise settings
**Enabled:** Setting this to "Yes" will enable a work rise. This setting can be used to prevent the settings from being inherited from a higher level.
**Name** : The name of the work rise that appears on the calendar and in the reports. A name must always be set to a work rise.
**Salary Code** : Salary code associated with earned work rise. This can be accessed with rulesets in table UserSalaryData using field WorkRiseSalaryCode.
**Visible in week panel** : Select whether the work rise is displayed in the 'hours in calendar' and 'hours in the table' views. Even if the work rise does not appear in the weekly tables, it can still be transferred, for example, in integrations.
### Earning times
Determine the times when the work increase is valid, i.e. when it is earned. Earning times can be configured in two different ways, either based on the days the shift overlaps, or on the days the shift belongs to (recommended). More detailed instructions for defining earning times are available [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/25318527637661-Work-rise-earning-times>).
### Earning rules
In this section you can define, through various settings, when a work increase is not earned in certain cases. The settings are:
**Only earn if shift is planned or expected** A work rise is only earned in situations where work is planned with a shift or expected work times.
**Only earn if event types start in validity period** If the setting is set to yes, work rise is earned only in cases where the recorded event has started during the work rise's validity period.
**Work rise not active if work/overtime starts before/after** The setting defines the time of day that recorded event has to start begin/after in order to earn work rise.
**Required duration after which work rise can be earned** With this setting a certain period of work during the validity period of the work rise is needed, before the work rise begins to accrue.
**Do not earn if these work rise(s) have been earned** : If it is desired to prevent earning of a work rise, if some other work increase has been earned, it can be set here. The setting stores a comma-separated list of work rise numbers without spaces.
The setting is suitable for use cases where one work rise is valid earlier than the other and you want to prevent the latter from earning when the previously valid work rise is earned.
The setting can not be used in situations where two work rises are valid for the same time period and you want to prevent one from earning the other. For example, in a situation where there is a need to earn Grand Public Holiday compensation instead of Sunday increase on certain days, the setting "On public holidays earning is calculated according to day" should be set to Monday in Sunday work increase (The setting can be set to any day when it has no validity times). In this way, the Grand Public Holiday increase and the Sunday increase never overlap, and they are not earned at the same time.
### Work rise increment part
A separate increment part can be defined for a work rise. Defining an increment part achieves the same outcome as defining a separate work increase. The function aims to facilitate use cases where, for example, you want to define a separate increment part for Sunday for an evening rise.
**Earn additional increment part** Defines, whether additional increment part earning is in use.
**Name** The name of the increment part.
**Salary code** The increment part's salary code.
**Increase accrual in accordance with rate of increase** If the increment part is directed with the same direction as the recorded work event.
**Increase method:** Options 'percentage' or 'minutes per hour'. The percentage increase can be used to direct the compensation by the selected percentage to the accumulation selected in the work rise settings. The 'minutes per hour' setting can be used to replace the compensation selected from the hourly work during the work rise for the accumulation selected in the work rise settings.
**Minutes in hour increase:** Should be set if the increase method is 'minutes per hour'.
**The percentage increase:** Should be set if the increase method is 'percentage'.
**Earning times:** Work rise increment part's earning times are defined like "days the shift overlaps". Further instructions [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/25318527637661-Work-rise-earning-times>).
### Work rise variable compensation
The compensation for the work rise can be either variable or fixed. Only fill in the settings you need for the desired outcome.
**Increase method** : Options 'percentage' or 'minutes per hour'. The percentage increase can be used to direct the compensation by the selected percentage to the accumulation selected in the work rise settings. The 'minutes per hour' setting can be used to replace the compensation selected from the hourly work during the work rise for the accumulation selected in the work rise settings.
**The percentage increase** : Should be set if the increase method is 'percentage'.
**Minutes in hour increase** : Should be set if the increase method is 'minutes per hour'.
### Work rise fixed compensation 
The compensation for the work rise can be either variable or fixed. Only fill in the settings you need for the desired outcome.
**Fixed compensation amount:** If compensation requirements are met, this set amount will be earned
**Work rise fixed compensation method of pay** :
  * Pay once per day: adds up the events that entitle for the work rise and pays once a day if the conditions are met
  * Pay per event per day: adds up the events that entitle to the work rise and pays each event separately if the total duration of the events entitle to the work rise


In both options, for example, a set maximum earning threshold can prevent earning.
### Work rise compensation calculation criteria
**Increase accrual in accordance with rate of increase:** The setting controls how the earned work rise is compensated. If no value is set, the work rise is compensated in salary. The setting can control the work rise to increase any accrual, or the accrual to be increased can be targeted to the same accrual as selected for the event 'overtime'. If the increase percentage is negative, then the increase can also reduce the accrual.
**Minimum earning threshold** : The work rise will only be earned when it is earned in excess of the minimum earning threshold
**Maximum earning threshold** : The work rise is only earned when it is earned less than the maximum earning threshold
**Calculate threshold based on** : How calculating minimum and maximum earning threshold is done. By default threshold is calculated by all compensation types that earn work rise, i.e. the whole amount of earned rise. It is also possible to set "Regular work hours on the day", which then uses the amount of regular work done on the day for calculating thresholds.
**Work rise earned if** : Will the minimum and maximum threshold be evaluated against the total duration per event or per day. E.g. if there is a maximum threshold, calculation method is daily, and there are two events earning the work rise on a day, the total duration of the events will not be added up, but the work rise duration for each event will be checked to be below the threshold. Then work rise compensation can be earned for each event, even though their total duration would exceed the maximum earning threshold. Setting has no effect if Calculate threshold based on - setting is set to "Regular work hours on the day".
**Minimum amount compensated** : The work rise shall be compensated at least by the amount set, even if less is earned
**Maximum amount compensated** : The work rise shall be compensated up to the amount set, even if more is earned
**Earn from time created due to rounding** : If the value is "Yes", the work rise is earned for both the time worked and the time added due to rounding. If the value is "No", the work rise is earned only for the time actually worked. The default is "Yes" if not set.
**Earn from extra time due to fixed compensation start-up work:** If the value is "Yes", work rise earned from start-up work is earned for both the time worked and the time added due to fixed compensation. If the value is "No", the work rise is earned only for the time actually worked.
**Earn from extra time due to fixed compensation termination work:** If the value is "Yes", work rise earned from termination work is earned for both the time worked and the time added due to fixed compensation. If the value is "No", the work rise is earned only for the time actually worked.
**On public holidays all work is recorded as work rise** : If you select Yes, all work, regardless of time, will earn work rise
**On public holidays earning is calculated according to day** : The setting can be used to control which day's validity periods are used on public holidays. Public holiday-specific validity periods can also be set with an exception to the validity period settings.
**Defer compensation** : This selection can be used to defer compensation of work rise to the last day of the week.
### Compensation types that earn work rise
The setting should be used to set all the compensation types for which a work rise is earned. If no compensation type is set, no work rise will be earned.
### Projects that earn work rise
**Earned from related projects:** If enabled, the work rise can only be earned if the work in the calendar is targeted to a related project. The related projects can be configured from the [Project administration page](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002561017>) next to "Pays work rises".
### Event types that earn work rise
The setting should set all the event types for which a work rise is earned. If no event type is set, no work rise will be earned.
Unpaid absences and unpaid sick leaves do not earn work rise even if these event types would have been set to earn work rise.
### Work rise increase based on weekly rest
This setting can determine that if a work rise is earned on a Sunday, an increase is also earned from it, if weekly rest compensation has formed in that week. A salary code and name can be specified for the increase in the Salary code and Name - fields. The name appears on its own line in the calendar view when the increase has been earned.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22676828104733)
The increase in the work rise can be earned based on the work done during the work rise. The increase is earned on the day the weekly rest allowance is earned. If the weekly rest allowance is shown on Monday, the increase is also shown on Monday. The maximum increase that can be earned is the amount of weekly rest compensation earned in the week. For example, if the weekly rest compensation is 6 hours, and 7 hours and 20 minutes of work has been done on Sunday, an increase of 6 hours is earned.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/22676858629405)
The increase in the work rise is directed to the same target as the work rise itself, it cannot be directed differently. Nor can a different percentage be set for the increase. When the increase needs to picked up for salary integrations, its compensation type is workrise and workriseearnedatcompensationtype is 'WeeklyRestTime'. The salary code is in the field 'workrisesalarycode'. An increase in the work rise is approved if the Sunday event, from which it was earned from has been approved.
### Rounding
**Rounding method** determines whether the sum is rounded down, up, or normally. With the "Up" rounding mode, time is rounded up only once the threshold has been reached. With the "Normal" rounding mode, the time is rounded down only under the threshold, rounded up otherwise. 
**Rounding interval** setting determines the interval at which rounding occurs.
**Rounding threshold** setting determines the threshold after which rounding occurs.
### Force time earned during work rise to overtime
The settings can be used to control the work time on which the work rise is earned in a different way. For example, a work rise could make all overtime 100% compensated during the period of the work rise.
Note: If [work week calculation mode](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559438-Additional-work-formation>) **KVTES** and **Force overlapping regular time to percentage** are both in use, the forcing setting is applied in exceptional way on weeks with weekly leave events. In the example work rise forces regular time to additional work on Saturday and Sunday. Regardless the work rise, regular time is not always forced to additional work if there is weekly leaves on weekdays.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/14198509679901)
The default behavior of work week calculation mode "KVTES" is that regular time is formed on weekends if there is negative balance or weekly leaves during weekdays. Below is an example with balance leave on Monday. Same amount of regular time is formed on Saturday but work rise forces it to additional work and regular time is not indicated in the calendar. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/14198726662045)
Regular time is visible if weekly leave is used. Work rise does not take effect in this case. One weekly leave moves working day to Saturday and work hours are interpreted as regular time. Work rise would take effect on Sunday because Saturday's work has covered skipped working day on Monday.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/14198869467421)
Above-mentioned exceptions are applied on the second last and the last day of the week when amount of weekly leaves on weekdays is evaluated. If there would be two weekly leaves on weekdays, regular time would not be forced to additional work on Saturday nor Sunday. If there would be one weekly leave on weekday and Saturday without work hours, regular time would not be forced to additional work on Sunday because weekly leave is not yet covered. 
## Inheriting and deactivating work rises
Each work rise has it's own number. It should be noted that if, for example, settings are made in Work Rise 1, they will be inherited according to the normal hierarchy of settings, even if the name of the work rise for example, is not marked on another level. So when adding a new work rise to a lower level, always make sure there are no settings set in the setting groups above.
The inheriting can be blocked and remove the work rise from a certain setting group by setting "no" to the first setting, "enabled". 
## Example of setting up Evening rise
Select a work rise which has not been set yet. Also check the other setting levels so that the two work rises do not overlap.
In this example, we create an evening allowance that is automatically earned from work between 6 PM and 10 PM. The value of the work increase is a 20% increase in salary and is earned from selected event and compensation types on all days of the week. Work rise is set to be visible in the calendar of the employees.
Please remember to always configure settings with the [validity](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358>) control.
Set setting as enabled, select a name, salary code if any integrations are in use, visibility in the calendar view and earning times using the method "day the shift belongs to".
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26986765669789)
Select the increase method and give value of "20" to the percentage increase. The increase is directed to salary.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26986735041181)
Select from which compensation types work rise is earned.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26986765672349)
Select from which event types work rise is earned.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/26986735044125)
Exceptions to periods of validity, rounding, or overtime earning do not need to be set up in this example.
The work rise is now set up and will automatically appear in the calendar view if an event is recorded that meets the settings of the work rise.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Workshift planning and Work schedules / Work schedules | path: en-gb/Support/Workshift-planning-and-Work-schedules/Work-schedules/12063496680349-Work-schedules-daily-use-and-follow-up.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12063496680349-Work-schedules-daily-use-and-follow-up -->

# Work schedules daily use and follow up

Below is a collection of useful tips and guidance for the daily use of work schedules by employees, supervisors, planners, and administrators.  
# Using work schedules
## Employees
After becoming a member of a published work schedule group, and possibly also a holiday schedule group, employees will immediately see the related planned events and rest times in their Worktime calendar and mobile.
Employees can record to Worktime normally, and the calculations will consider the planned events vs the recorded ones. 
## Subordinates
Supervisors can see subordinates planned and recorded events and deviations in their Worktime calendar. If the recorded events deviate from the planned ones enough, they are indicated as such in the approval views and reports.
If supervisors should do planning adjustments for their subordinates, they can make Deviations using the Planning section tools. Visit planning and filter to the desired schedule, then edit the subordinates planned events before publishing them. Published deviations appear for the subordinates immediately and can have an accompanying planning note giving a reason for the change, if necessary.
Please also read the "_Planning permission for supervisors heading_ " below.
# Planning permissions for supervisors
Depending on your workflow, supervisors might be required to approve and plan changes to their subordinates' scheduled events, rest times and holidays. In this situation, they will first require planning permissions for the work schedule in question.
To do this, visit Planning > Locations > Choose the desired work schedule "location". Under the heading "Location persons", add the supervisor. If the supervisor is a member of the schedule, then also flag them as a "Location resource".
Please note that access to the Planning section is restricted by role permissions. For more information please check the **[Work schedules requirements& setup](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12039347959581>)** article.
# Reacting to real-world situations
A plan rarely remains unchanged in contact with the real world, so it is essential that teams can react and adapt to changing situations whilst remaining controlled and coordinated.
Below are headings with guidance for handling the most common situations.
## Swapping/Changing planned events
Many situations can result in the need to change a planned event for a person. This is done using the Planning section.
  1. Choose the relevant Unit, and filter the planning view to the related work or holiday schedule.
  2. Browse to the person who's shift you wish to change
  3. Edit the shift as desired. It will appear as a deviation that needs to be published
  4. Publish the change
  5. The affected person's Worktime calendar and mobile will immediately be updated and highlight that there is a deviation to their usual work schedule.


## New employees
When new employees join, they naturally will not be part of any work schedule. They can be assigned to one either via
  * Employees > Person info
  * or, Planning > Work schedules > Desired schedule > Members tab


## Flexible resources
Sometimes it is useful to have some people available as extra resources to a work schedule, even if they do not directly follow it. This means that they will not normally see the planned events from the work schedule, but are still visible in the Planning view as a resource for it, and can be assigned related planned events from there when needed.
To set this up;
  1. Go to, Planning > Locations > Choose the desired schedule "location"
  2. Under the "Location people" heading, add the person and flag them as a Location resource


# Managing group memberships
Please see the "Manage group memberships" heading on the **[Work schedules requirements& setup](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12039347959581>)** article.
# FAQ
We will publish FAQ headings here, as we encounter them.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Workshift planning and Work schedules / Work schedules | path: en-gb/Support/Workshift-planning-and-Work-schedules/Work-schedules/19215744439965-Work-schedules-planning-rights.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/19215744439965-Work-schedules-planning-rights -->

# Work schedules planning rights

When using work schedules, it is important to clearly define who has the right to plan and make changes to work schedules as well as in the planning view. Planning rights should be given to individuals responsible for scheduling shifts in the work schedule and maintaining shifts in the planning view. The most common roles used are Supervisor and Unit manager. This article focuses on these two roles. A more detailed description of other roles and their rights is provided in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002425637-Roles>). 
## Unit Manager role 
The Unit Manager role has very comprehensive rights within the unit to which they are assigned. The Unit Manager can see the work schedules and shifts for the unit they are assigned to. They can also plan new work schedule for their unit. The Unit Manager can plan and publish shifts for all individuals in the unit's work schedules both on the Work schedule page and in the planning view.
## Supervisor Role
The Supervisor role has more limited rights compared to the Unit Manager role. The Supervisor can view the work schedules on the Work schedule page to which they have been added as a location person. The Supervisor can edit and create a new work schedule period for the work schedule to which they have been added as a location person, but they cannot create entirely new work schedules. For person with the Supervisor role to make shift changes in the planning view, they must be added as a location person to the Work schedule (locations) where they need to make changes. [This article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575518-How-do-I-give-a-person-rights-to-plan-shifts>) describes how a person is added as a location person.
## Deputies
A deputy can be assigned to a person, for example, when a supervisor goes on annual leave. Detailed instructions on assigning a deputy can be found in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002430678-Assigning-deputy>). The substitute does not receive the same visibility into shift planning or work schedules as the person being substituted. The substitute must be granted visibility into shift planning in the same way as the person being substituted. [This article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002575518-How-do-I-give-a-person-rights-to-plan-shifts>) provides detailed instructions on how to grant a person the right to plan shifts.
The table presents the most common situations and guidelines on how the Supervisor role and substitution work in connection with work schedules.
Description | Location persons | Location resource | Subordinate assignment  
---|---|---|---  
The person has subordinates assigned and belongs to the same work schedule as the subordinates. | Yes | Yes |   
The person has subordinates assigned but does not have a work schedule group. | Yes | No |   
The person acts as a deputy but does not have a work schedule group assigned and has no own subordinates. | Yes | No | Yes, the deputy is assigned the subordinates they need to see.  
The person has their own subordinates and acts as a deputy for another person who has different subordinates than they do. | Yes | No | Yes, the deputy is assigned the subordinates they need to see.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Workshift planning and Work schedules / Work schedules | path: en-gb/Support/Workshift-planning-and-Work-schedules/Work-schedules/12039347959581-Work-schedules-requirements-setup.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12039347959581-Work-schedules-requirements-setup -->

# Work schedules requirements & setup

Everything you need to know to get up and running with Work Schedules in your environment.
# Requirements
## Planning service
To use the Work schedules features, you must first have access to the Nepton Planning service with an appropriate Nepton Planning service level. For the latest information on Nepton service levels and their pricing, please **[contact support](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/7077076926237>)**.
## Planning permissions
When taking Work schedules into use, you should decide what access is needed for planning and daily operations. Although these decisions largely be dictated by your organisation structure, a recommended configuration is below:
  * Administrative roles (Administrator and Salary Manager) have rights to all aspects of Planning and Work schedules, for the entire environment. This can be very useful for initial setup, troubleshooting, management, and oversight.
  * The Unit manager role has rights to all aspects of Planning and Work schedules for the Units they have a relationship with.
  * People with subordinates (aka Supervisors or team leaders) have the right to see and manage the shifts and work schedules of their subordinates for the work schedule locations they have been linked to. 
    * Please see more about Setting up work shift planning [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360011258978>).
  * Employees do not have access to Planning or work schedules features, but see their work schedule shifts from Worktime.


## Units
To use Work schedules, at least one Unit must be configured via Employees > Units, and the people who will be members of the work schedule(s) should be a member of that Unit.
Units are a core concept that organises the business data (Read more about them **[here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002590317>)**). Work schedules are always linked to a Unit, and therefore it is possible to have different schedules visible only to each Unit.
# Creating a work schedule
For more information on what a Work schedule is, and its related workflow, please see the dedicated article **[here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12038486266909>)**.
## Create a work schedule
  1. To start creating a schedule, visit Planning > Work schedules, and click "Add".
  2. Fill in the basic details of the schedule, choosing the "Work schedule" type, and a unique code it can be identified by, in event and salary exports. Then click "Save" to continue.
  3. Add schedule groups to represent the different groups of people and shift patterns this work schedule will provide. 
     * Providing a unique code for each group is recommended for handling memberships in bulk later on.


Project with name and code of the work schedule will be created automatically. Events of the person following this work schedule can be targeted to this project by using a setting "Target the worktime event to the project of the planned work shift" in the [project targeting settings](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002562658>).
Schedules do not appear in Planning or Worktime sections until at least one Period has been configured and published.
## Create a Holiday schedule
Whenever work schedule groups need to be divided for holiday planning, a dedicated holiday schedule should be created. Planned events from a Holiday schedule override planned events from a work schedule. It is important to note that even rest days on a holiday schedule will override the work schedule. People must become members of a holiday schedule group in addition to their work schedule group for the override to occur.
For example, if an employee would normally follow a shift pattern A A A - - Y - V - - -, but they are also a member of a holiday schedule that had extra rest days and annual leave planned (Where E is an empty day in the holiday schedule, not a rest day) - - E H H H H E E E E. The resulting work schedule for the person would look like - - A H H H H V - - -.
  1. To start creating a schedule, visit Planning > Work schedules, and click "Add".
  2. Fill in the basic details of the schedule, choosing the "Holiday schedule" type, and a unique code it can be identified by, in event and salary exports. Then click "Save" to continue.
  3. Add schedule groups to represent the different groups of people and times that holidays will be planned for 
     * Providing a unique code for each group is recommended for handling memberships in bulk later on.


Schedules do not appear in Planning or Worktime sections until at least one Period has been configured and published.
## Plan the schedule by time period
Schedules are planned and published in advance for a given date range at a time. This date range is known as a schedule period. The schedule period's date range is usually defined by your TES requirements or planning period. Often 6-12 months in length.
After adding a period and its basic information to a schedule, configure the shift and/or absence types, choose the groups of people the period is for, and their repeating shift patterns, and any offset.
At this point, the schedule period calendar will be populated at the bottom of the form, and it is possible to make edits, known as Deviations, and planning notes, before publishing.  
More details on each of these steps are below.
### Define shift types
The different types of planned events that will be part of the schedule are defined for each period. Each planned event requires an alias that it will be referred to as throughout Planning and Worktime. This facilitates quick recognition and planning.
A premade shift type, "-" No shift, is provided for all schedule periods, and should be used to represent rest days.
For example, Alias "A" could represent a morning shift with the name **"Aamu",** a start time of 06:00, end time of 14:00, and additional information and tasks representing the desired morning shift responsibilities.
Assumed lunch reductions for planned events (aka shift types) are based on settings for 
  * The whole deployment - Employees > Administration > Settings > Planning.
  * A specific work schedule - Planning > Locations > "Desired work schedule" > Location settings > Assumed lunch reduction.


### Add groups, repeating shift patterns, and offsets
Add schedule groups for the people who will have planned events during this period, and then define the group's repeating shift pattern based on the Shift types and aliases you defined earlier. The pattern should be separated by spaces.
The offset allows you to use the same pattern for every group, but offset when it starts by a number of days. Value zero starts the shift cycle from the first shift of the pattern. Positive values move the first shift of the pattern later and negative values earlier.
For example, you wish to use a shift pattern of A A A - - Y - V - - - for all 5 groups in a work schedule, each subsequent group staggered to start the pattern 2 days later.
  * **Group, offset = resulting shift pattern from day 1 of the period**
  * Group 1, offset 0 = A A A - - Y - V - - -
  * Group 2, offset 2 = - - A A A - - Y - V -
  * Group 3, offset 4 = V - - - A A A - - Y -
  * Group 4, offset 6 = Y - V - - - A A A - -
  * Group 5, offset 8 = - - Y - V - - - A A A


### Deviations
Deviations are changes from the usual shift and holiday plan for a work schedule group or individual. They can be made in the schedule period calendar and in the Planning view. Deviations are highlighted in purple to ensure they are noticed by planners and employees alike.
Some examples;
  * **A planned maintenance break** \- There will need to be maintenance that affects a production line of one or more of the schedule groups. As such, the expected dates are edited for the affected groups to have an offsite training day instead of their usual pattern. This appears as a deviation for these groups.
  * **An expected increase in demand** \- Due to planned sales and marketing, you expect to need more employees working on a given date. As such, a schedule group that usually has a rest day is edited to have a work shift and a replacement rest day later in the week or month.


### Planning notes
Although planned shifts and holidays can themselves have additional information text, it is sometimes useful to communicate more details about the plan or a special date. In such cases a planning note can be added via the schedule period calendar, for all groups or individual groups.
For example, a planning note could be helpful when you wish to explain why there are deviations on a given date. E.g. Because of a maintenance break or an expected increase in demand.
## Manage group memberships
With a work schedule created and at least one period published, it's time to ensure the right people can see and follow the planned events and shifts from it.
Schedule group memberships can only be managed once at least one period using the groups for the schedule, has been published.
### For new schedules or bulk changes (Using person import)
If you're setting up a new work or holiday schedule, or there are a lot of changes to the people following the schedule, it is recommended to configure group memberships using an Excel import file. Alternatively, the memberships can be managed from the UI, described in the next heading "Via UI".
  1. Create an import file 
     * Either, take an export of the desired people from Employees > Persons > Export to importable excel  
**Note:** When using the importable Excel, you will need to unhide all columns
     * Or, manually create an Excel import file with the desired people and columns
  2. Only include the columns necessary for identifying the person, setting their schedule group membership, and setting the correct validity (start date) of the membership  
i.e. Employee Number, Work schedule group, Holiday schedule group, and Valid from date
  3. Make sure to set the correct Valid from date for each person to preserve their past schedule group memberships.
  4. Import the file in Employees > Persons > Import persons


Full guidance on importing personnel data is **[here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360018767498>)**.
### Via UI & Finding people without a membership
When making small changes to memberships or if you do not have permission to import person data, memberships can be managed via the user interface. Visit Work schedules > Your chosen schedule > "Members" tab. This view also shows people in the Unit, who you have permissions to manage, that do not yet have a membership to a schedule group.
Use the search at the top of the form to find and edit memberships of a person, or browse and expand the schedule groups below, to edit the existing memberships of an individual.
When adding or editing the membership, it is recommended to set valid from date of the membership, so that past planned events from the schedule and group, do not affect the person's worktime calendar and calculations.
## Publishing
With the schedule period configured and any deviations and planning notes added, you can publish the period. Once a period is published, the scheduled events, deviations and planning notes, become visible to all work schedule group members in worktime calendar & mobile, immediately, as well as for planners in the Planning view.
Once published, you can manage, follow up, and react to real-world situations. Please see the [**Work schedules daily use and follow up**](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12063496680349>) article
# Follow-up and daily use
Please see the dedicated article, [**Work schedules daily use and follow up**](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/12063496680349>).

# Work shift planning - General information

Sorry, but this article has not been translated yet.
Vuorosuunnittelunäkymässä suunnitellaan vuorot sekä vuorotarpeet. Vuorotarpeet tarkoittavat vuoroja, joille ei ole määritetty vielä vuoron tekijää. Vuorosuunnittelunäkymässä tehty suunnitelma julkaistaan erikseen, jonka jälkeen vuorot sekä mahdolliset vuorotarpeet tulevat näkyviin työntekijöille. Vuorotarpeet ovat julkaisun jälkeen työntekijöiden varattavissa.
## Näkymän käyttö
### Yleistä näkymästä
Vuorosuunnittelunäkymän käyttöönotto vaatia muutamia [toimenpiteitä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360011258978>), joiden jälkeen vuoroja voidaan suunnitella. Huomaa että:
  * **Jotta henkilö näkyy suunnittelunäkymässä**
    * Henkilöllä tulee olla voimassa oleva työsopimus suunniteltavalla aikavälillä
    * Henkilön tulee kuulua yksikköön, jolle suunnitelma tehdään
    * Henkilön tulee kuulua jollekin toimipisteelle


### Suunnittelunäkymä toimipisteittäin sekä henkilöittäin
Vuorosuunnittelu-näkymä on jaettu kahteen osaan:
  * **Suunnittelunäkymä toimipisteittäin**
    * Suunnittelu lisäämällä vuoroja toimipisteelle
    * Näyttää vuorot selkeästi toimipisteen näkökulmasta
  * **Suunnittelunäkymä resursseittain**
    * Suunnittelu lisäämällä vuoroja henkilöille
    * Näyttää vuorot selkeästi henkilön näkökulmasta


Suunnittelunäkymästä on helppo varmistaa, että suunnitelma toimii toimipisteen ja henkilön näkökulmasta.
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8287660530077)
### Vuorosuunnittelunäkymän työkalut
![mceclip6.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8289140638109)
Vuorosuunnittelunäkymän yläosassa on suunnittelua helpottavia työkaluja:
  * **Päivitä**
    * Päivittää suunnittelunäkymän. Näin voidaan varmistaa, että henkilöiden viimeisimmät tiedot (esim. sairauslomat) ovat näkymässä.
  * **Näkymän asetukset**
    * Rajaa ja määritä mitä suunnittelunäkymässä näet
    * Katso tarkemmat kuvaukset sivulla alempana
  * **Massatoiminnot**  

    *       * Mahdollisuus kohdistaa toimenpiteitä usealle vuorolle yhdellä kertaa. Lisää massatoiminnoista [täällä](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/8271501506973-Massatoiminnot>).


![mceclip1.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8350323097757)
  * **Työkalut**
    * Suunnittelua avustavat toiminteet, kuten vuorojen jako henkilöille automaattisesti.


![mceclip2.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8350296237725)
  * **Julkaise**
    * Vuorojen julkaisu ja niistä kommunikointi. Lue lisää artikkeleista [vuorojen julkaiseminen](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002520077-Vuorojen-julkaiseminen>) ja [vuorotarpeiden julkaiseminen](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002521818-Vuorotarpeiden-julkaiseminen>).
  * **Selite**  

    * Näyttää vuoroja kuvaavien solujen eri värien ja tyylien merkityksen. 
      * Osittain valittu: useasta samanlaisesta vuorotarpeesta on valittu vain osa.
      * Työajasta tai toisesta yksiköstä: Esim. henkilön työaikakalenteriin merkitty sairausloma tai henkilölle toisessa yksikössä merkitty vuoro.  
![mceclip8.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8289296523677)  
  

  * **Kokoruututila**
    * Laajentaa suunnittelunäkymän koko ruudulle ja helpottaa täten kokonaiskuvan muodostamista.


### Näkymän asetukset
#### Rajaukset
Rajausten avulla rajaat näkymässä näkyvää tietoa.
  * Toimipiste 
    * Asettamalla toimipisterajauksen 
      * Ylemmässä toimipistenäkymässä näkyy vain valitsemasi toimipiste sekä sen alla olevat toimipisteet
      * Alemmassa henkilönäkymässä näkyy vain henkilöt, jotka ovat liitettyinä valitsemaasi toimipisteeseen tai sen alla oleviin toimipisteisiin
  * Henkilölista 
    * Henkilölistan valinta rajaa alemman henkilönäkymän henkilöt henkilölistan henkilöihin
    * Rajaus ei vaikuta ylempään toimipistenäkymään
  * Ensisijaiset esimiehet 
    * Ensisijaisen esimiehen valinta rajaa alemman henkilönäkymän henkilöt niihin henkilöihin, joiden ensisijainen esimies on valittu esimies
    * Rajaus ei vaikuta ylempään toimipistenäkymään
  * Henkilöt 
    * Henkilöt valinta rajaa alemman henkilönäkymän henkilöt valittuihin henkilöihin
    * Rajaus ei vaikuta ylempään toimipistenäkymään
  * Tehtävät 
    * Tehtävän valinta rajaa niin ylemmän toimipistenäkymän kuin alemman henkilönäkymän vuorot ja tarpeet niihin joihin on liitetty valittu tehtävä


![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/8350286151069)
### Muut suunnitellut tapahtumat
Vuorosuunnittelussa näytetään myös muita henkilöiden työaikakalenteriin etukäteen merkittyjä tapahtumia, joilla voi olla vaikutusta vuorosuunnitteluun. Tällaisia tapahtumia voivat olla esimerkiksi vuosilomat, pitkään jatkuvat sairauslomat, koulutukset tai kalenteriin lisätyt huomautukset. Vuorosuunnittelussa näytettävät tapahtumatyypit määritellään [tapahtumatyyppien asetuksissa](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/fi/articles/360002519157-Tapahtumatyyppien-lis%C3%A4%C3%A4minen-k%C3%A4ytt%C3%B6%C3%B6notto-ja-muokkaaminen#360002519157-toc-3>). Kaikki poissaolotyypit näytetään tekstillä "Poissaolo", muilta valituilta tapahtumatyypeiltä näytetään tapahtumatyypin nimi. Tapahtumiin kirjatut huomautukset näytetään näkymässä, jos näkymän asetuksissa on valittu näytettäväksi "Julkinen tieto". Huomautuksia ei kuitenkaan näytetä julkisena tietona valituilta poissaolotyyppien eikä terveydenhoito-, luottamusmiestyö- tai työsuojelutyö-tyyppien tapahtumilta.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/360003961118-Work-time-percentage.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360003961118-Work-time-percentage -->

# Work time percentage

If a person has a reduced daily working time, for example 60% of normal, a work time percentage can be set for them. More detailed description about part-time options can be found in [this](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559018-Configure-setting-group-for-part-timers>) article.
If the normal daily working time was 7 hours 30 minutes and the weekly working time 37 hours 30 minutes, 60% of the working time would be
  * 4 hours 30 minutes daily
  * 22 hours and 30 minutes weekly


The work time percentage can be set via **Employees > Persons >** search the person you were looking for and open the person's information from the magnifying glass icon and go to the **Employment information** section.
![mceclip0.png](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/4413353060241)
NOTE! The working time percentage is entered without a percentage sign. An empty field and 100% are both interpreted as full-time (100%). The work time percentage field works with the[ validity function](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004856937>).
The work time percentage does not affect:
  * daily and weekly maximum TES time
  * daily work time interpreted from a shift
  * if the daily or weekly work time comes from a daily exception entry
  * leveling period hours, unless it is [configured that work time percentage considers work time percentage](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/14849123960989>)


## Work time changing in the middle of work week
When employee's work percentage changes during the workweek, the system does not know which percentage to use for calculating the length of work week. In such cases, the balance accrual at the end of the week might be too positive or negative. To address this, manually adjust the balance for the next day using the balance reset or balance change methods, please see instructions [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002481797-Setting-and-changing-the-value-of-balance>).
Alternatively, you can set an exception to the length of workweek in the person’s work calendar. To do this, add up the required hours for different work obligations to determine the total weekly work obligation. For example:
Monday to Wednesday (when person is under 60% obligation): 3 x 6 hours = 18 hours
Thursday to Friday (when person is under 100% obligation): 2 x 7.5 hours = 15 hours
The total work obligation for the week is 33 hours. To set an exception to the length of work week, follow instructions below:
Click on the date icon (1)
Select ‘**Length of work week’** (2)
Set the exception for the work week length. (3)
Save the changes by clicking **‘Save exception.’** (4) You may remove the exception from this same window by clicking **Remove exception**.
These exceptions apply only to the work week you are currently doing modifications to. 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/20197025091229)

# Work time reports

There are multiple standardized reports in Nepton. They can be found in Worktime section under **Work hours > Reports**.
Hours targeted to projects can be reported in **Projects > Reports.** More about project reporting [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548957>). 
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/25732824865821)
There are different reports regarding work time, work time shortening leaves and annual leaves for example. The reports can be searched for a certain time period and filtered users. The reports can be printed and some imported into Excel. If the downloaded report contains too much data (too many users or too long of a time period), the report can only be opened in Excel. Further instructions on how to filter and take out reports can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004437597>).
All articles regarding work time reports can be found [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/sections/360005870318-Worktime-reports>). 
## Reports regarding recorded work time
Reports regarding recorded work time are useful when monitoring for example how works hours are divided between different event types, overtime compensations and absences. More in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548557>).
## Reports regarding sick leaves
The reports regarding sick leave can be used to monitor, for example, the total number of sick leave days (working days/Kela days/calendar days), absences recorded for different reason codes and the number of paid sick leave days.
Reports regarding sick leave include:  
\- Sick leaves by person  
\- Sick leaves by person group
More in [this article](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548797>).
## Reports regarding work time shortening leave
It is possible to activate [work time shortening leave earning](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559837>) in Nepton. After the function is taken into use, it is possible to follow the earning and use of work time shortening leaves via reports. 
There is one standardized report regarding work time shortening leaves:  
\- Work time shortening leaves
More in [this article.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548777>)
## Reports regarding annual leave
It is possible to activate [annual leave earning](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560698>) in Nepton. After the function is taken into use, it is possible to follow the earning and use of annual leaves via reports. 
Reports regarding annual leave include:  
\- Annual leave earning by month  
\- Annual leave usage by month  
\- Annual leave usage by season
More in [this article.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548717>)
## Reports regarding dining events
It is possible to record dining events in Nepton, just like any other events. These dining events can be monitored with the following reports:
-Dining by person  
-Dining totals by person
More in [this article.](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548278>)

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Reporting / Worktime reports | path: en-gb/Support/Reporting/Worktime-reports/360002548777-Work-time-shortening-leaves-report.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002548777-Work-time-shortening-leaves-report -->

# Work time shortening leaves report

It is possible to do [worktime shortening leave](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559837>) calculations in Nepton. When the calculations have been activated, worktime shortening leaves can be monitored with reporting in **Worktime > Work hours > Reports.**
Work time shortening leaves -report can be taken for a calendar year and either selected users (individuals or by user groups) or all personnel at once.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27334869538973)
The report shows two years' (previous and current) worth of data concerning work time shortening leaves. If there are unused work time shortening leaves accrual at the end of the year, they stay in the accrual and can be used the next year. The earning calculations always start from the start at the beginning of the year.
![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/27334893322013)
**Earned** -field shows days/hours earned the previous year, and on current year up to date of reporting.  
**Value changed** -field shows manually done changes to the accrual.  
**Total** -field shows the total sum of Earned and Value changed combined.   
**Used** -field shows the amount of unused work time shortening leaves at the time of reporting.  
**Unit in Collective Agreement -** field shows whether the leave is being earned in days or hours.   
**Collective Agreement** -fields shows the person's collective agreement, if it has been defined in the setting group. 
The report can be printed or exported to Excel.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Worktime calculations and management / Calculation settings / Bulk edit settings | path: en-gb/Support/Worktime-calculations-and-management/Calculation-settings/Bulk-edit-settings/360002560837-Workday-length-mass-entering.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002560837-Workday-length-mass-entering -->

# Workday length mass entering

Mass recording for the length of the workday can be done, for example, when the work obligation of a user changes temporarily. A temporary change does not necessarily need to be made in the working community or setting group settings, but it can be done through mass recording. However, this function should be used only in exceptional cases.
An exception to the length of the workday can also be set by utilizing the exception settings of the [validity function](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002559358>) in the Worktime section. The exception setting described in this article applies only to a specific day, whereas an exception setting made to the working community or settings group can be set to remain in effect indefinitely if necessary.
Select **Worktime > Tools > Mass enter settings**
  * Select the setting for mass recording as **Length of work day**
  * Select the start and end dates for the mass recording from the **Recurring entry** and **Repeat until**.
  * Select the **Frequency** for the mass recording.
  * Insert the desired value in the **Length** field.
  * Select the **users** or **groups** for whom you want to make the change.
  * Finally, select **Perform mass entry**.


![](https://support.nepton.com/hc/article_attachments/28719121800733)
You can first make a mass recording for just one person. This way, you can check that the mass recording is correct.

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Nepton Payroll | path: en-gb/Support/Nepton-Payroll/22125431201693-Workflow-Payslips.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/22125431201693-Workflow-Payslips -->

# Workflow & Payslips

When using Nepton payroll, payslips update automatically based on the data provided by employees, supervisors, and payroll specialists. This allows any potential errors and issues to be identified and corrected before payday.
Our payslips are easy to read, featuring clear terms and logical groupings.
## Workflow: Events, absences, and approvals
When using Nepton Payroll, payslips update automatically based on worktime events. To get the most value from this automation, it is recommended that employees record their work hours and absences as soon as possible, ideally in real-time. Supervisors should regularly review and approve this information, ensuring that all events are recorded and approvals are completed before the end of the payment period cutt-off date.
For clarity, a payslip has different statuses depending on which stage of the payroll process it is on. These statuses are described below.
## Different payslip statuses
### Draft
The payslip is calculated dynamically based on the employee's HR data and relevant Worktime event and absence entries. Payslip recalculates immediately to changes in this data. If the payroll specialist has done manual additions or edits, those are also included.
### Refinement
The cut-off date of the payment period has passed and the payroll specialist has begun reconciling the related payroll.
Edits to HR and event data will only show in "draft" payslips if the payroll specialist has accepted the changes and included them into the draft payroll calculations. This means that the payslip won't update immediately after the changes to Worktime.
### Finalised
The payslip has been finalised by the payroll specialist and flagged for business approval and payment. It is unlikely that further changes will be made, but payroll specialists are informed of any edits made in the Worktime after the fact. They can choose whether to make further amendments, or to handle the changes in the next payslip.
### Paid
The salary has been sent for payment according to the payslip. It can no longer be changed. Any corrections will be handled as part of a new payslip.
## Where can I view the payslips?
A person's payslips can be viewed from three different places
  1. Nepton > Worktime > Work hours > Events in calendar > Salary  
Current and recent payslips including a breakdown for quick reconciliation against marked events by employees.  
  

  2. Nepton > Employees > Own info / Person info  
All payslips for a person can be viewed here.  
  

  3. Nepton > Palkat  
Payroll specialists can view pending, draft, finalised, and paid payslips here.


## Who can see payslips?
See the specific roles that can view the payroll information, including payslips, [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360002425637>).
## Troubleshooting
### My payslip has a mistake
  1. If a payslip seems to be missing salary rows or the amounts doesn't match as expected, please first check that all events have been recorded correctly for the related period.
  2. If the events appear to be correctly recorded and the summary for the day in e.g. events in calendar/table view seems to be right, contact your supervisor to make sure that the [HR information affecting the salary calculations](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4408264552977>) has been correctly set.
  3. In case you can't solve the problem using our guidance, please contact your oeganizations Nepton admin and/or salary contact person to further investigate the issue.


### I don't see my payslip
Payslips are automatically generated in real-time whenever there are edits to work events or relevant HR data for a person. However, this generation only occurs when all information necessary for payroll calculation is present. Below is a list of common causes for pauses in payslip generation:
  * **You have not yet marked work events in the coming payment period** \- Payslips are only shown when there are work events in their payment period. Future payslips are only generated up to two months in advance.
  * **Your payment group has not been set correctly** \- You can check this from the Employees > Own information page. A supervisor can usually change this for you if it is incorrect.
  * **Mandatory HR data is missing from Nepton** \- Your supervisor can check whether all the necessary personal information is saved in Nepton. The supervisor can check the [HR data for payroll](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4408264552977>) article for more information.


### How should corrections be handled?
Any changes to worktime and absence data can be addressed immediately. Depending on the status of payroll processing, the effects will be taken into account in rea-time or in the next payroll. Read more about [handling corrections here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/4412978914065>).

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Reporting / Insights service | path: en-gb/Support/Reporting/Insights-service/26673690781341-Workshift-planning-in-Reporting.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/26673690781341-Workshift-planning-in-Reporting -->

# Workshift planning in Reporting

# Basic Principles
From the data stored for work shift planning, you can add to a query:
  * Planned and published shifts regardless of how they were created
  * Combinations of shifts, for example:
    * Total planned work for Fri–Sat, Sat–Sun, and Sun–Mon combinations
    * Work scheduled on public holidays
  * Data related to rest-time monitoring, such as:
    * Various shift types (only if shift calendars are in use)
      * e.g. how many evening→morning shift combinations occurred
      * If you’re not using shift calendars (traditional mode), no shift types exist and this data can’t be obtained


**Note:** Extracted shift durations do not account for assumed meal breaks from roster planning. For example, a planned 8 h shift with an automatic 30 min break still appears as 8 h, not 7 h 30 min.
## Available Fields
  * Person’s shift-calendar code and name
  * Person’s leave-calendar code and name
  * Shifts planned and published via roster planning and shift calendars (start and end date/time)
  * For each planned and published shift:
    * Planned event type (code)
    * Abbreviation (from the shift calendar)
    * Additional shift-type information
    * Public shift information (cannot extract shift-group public info)
      * You can search within this public info for specific characters or substrings (e.g. a keyword)


## Can not be added to a query
  * Shift-calendar contents (schemas)
  * Leave-calendar contents (schemas)
  * Shift requirements
  * Tasks
  * Competencies
  * Shift-group planning data
  * Shift-group public information
  * Detailed shift-planning notes

<!-- locale: en-gb | category: Support | section: Integration / API / Worktime API | path: en-gb/Support/Integration/API/Worktime-API/360004861558-Worktime-API-in-general.md | source: https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360004861558-Worktime-API-in-general -->

# Worktime API in general

## Production API description
<https://time.nepton.com/WebService.php?WSDL>
Please also ensure that the necessary IP addresses are opened. Instructions [here](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/en-gb/articles/360009237257>).
Maximum POST request data size to worktime API is 128 MB. 
The Worktime API provides external systems access to certain features of Worktime. Guidance for individual topics is provided in the following articles:
  * [Authentication in Worktime API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360019983978>)
  * [Events API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360019840217>)
  * [Projects API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360019840237>)
  * [Accruals API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360019984338>)
  * [Worktime Integrations API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360019840857>)
  * [Terminal Services API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360019841037>)
  * [Response codes of Worktime API](<https://support.nepton.com/hc/articles/360019841477>)


Please note that:
  * The sent XML has to be valid XML
  * Used character encoding is UTF-8
  * Parameters used in the API call are **case-sensitive.** Make sure all upper case letters are used in a correct way when forming the call.


The best way to ensure the validity of XML is to use a SOAP library to handle requests and responses. For example [SoapClient](<https://www.php.net/manual/en/class.soapclient>) in PHP and [WCF Web Service Reference](<https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/additional-tools/wcf-web-service-reference-guide>) in .NET are viable options.
If you are generating XML without the help of an XML library, you need to keep in mind that the following characters need to be represented as entities:
Character | Entity  
---|---  
`&` | `&amp;`  
`<` | `&lt;`  
`>` | `&gt;`  
If you want to represent project name "Project & other work" in XML, it should be done the following way:
[code] 
    <Name>Project &amp; other work</Name>
[/code]
